title: These 4 Ravens Youngsters Must Take The Leap vs Chargers Monday Night
full_text:
The Ravens cannot lose to the Chargers Monday night.
Correction: the Ravens certainly could manage to lose to a previously-winless outfit at home on Monday night, they just can’t expect anything else they do this season to matter if that happens. Given their propensity to choke away games and with just three wins in their last 12 home games and having dropped four in a row in primetime at M&T Bank Stadium, there is certainly reason for concern.
The gravity of the situation weighed on rookie head coach Jesse Minter, who continues to look overmatched, and delivered strange messaging about Lamar Jackson’s thumb surgery . And who seemed to want to embrace being more of a bad cop, but he probably just doesn’t have it in him and he’s been thoroughly runover by a veteran roster to this point, begging questions about him and rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle.
Minter hinted at changes in terms of playing time and roles, and, well, after failing to acknowledge the franchise’s sweeping and overarching roster failures at the trade deadline, stripping underperforming players of their role is about all Minter can do. And that must be happening at critical position groups on both sides of the ball, and a path must be created for more youngsters to make a bigger impact.
“I'm excited for us to sort of re-establish our identity,” Minter said last week. “[With] lineup changes, I think those are all individual basis. But there's certain things that we have to have really high standards for. So, we'll see how it all shakes out."
Let’s hope is shakes out with these young players getting more of an opportunity to impact the football game, starting now.
Feels like a long time ago that he was getting as much pre-season hype as any rookie in the NFL. Oh, it was constant . Keep in mind, the third-round pick was going against one of the most pathetic secondaries in the NFL in practice – no matter how heavily failing general manager Eric DeCosta over-drafted the DBs or overpaid them. So there’s that.
And the Ravens faced some preseason defenses that weren’t doing much. But we all know DeCosta’s track record drafting receivers is abysmal, which is why he’s talked about the need to keep swinging. With Jacoby Brissett at quarterback now, the ability to push the ball deep down the seam is there and Lane has clearly always been crafted to do most of his early damage in the slot. It’s time to see if they can unlock his kid a little bit and give him something positive to take into the offseason.
Injuries to him and to the QBs have sapped that early momentum.
No one stands to gain more than him from Brissett’s arrival. He has some of the attributed Trey McBride had in Arizona and McBride rewrote the NFL history books for TEs with Brissett. He’s back from his hand injury for a few weeks now, and needs to be unleashed from the slot, too. Play action deep shots , go routes, double moves.
This offense is utterly pathetic, it lacks any lack or verve outside of Zay Flowers and this fifth-round pick has some acceleration in his game. He should he unleashed against the Chargers linebackers and a secondary that is without All Pro hybrid defender Derwin James.
The coaching staff loves to hype him, but he’s had to play second-fiddle to $60M alleged-closer Trey Hendrickson ( a bust so far no matter how the Ravens want to couch it ) but he needs to get a real chance to rush from the inside and the outside. Especially if Henrickson is going to have his right hand wrapped up like crazy.
He’s tied for first on the team with 3.5 sacks – with injured Tavius Robinson – and has shown an ability to twist in the A Gap and make things happen. The Chargers interior offensive line is the dregs of the NFL and has been for years. Can we get him unleashed a little bit here in a creative manner?
If the Ravens are going to persists on running $19.3M corner Marlon Humphrey against top outside receivers, only to get shredded, then close up shop. He should have been a slot corner years ago; he can’t win outside and there is reason to think Justin Herbert has hit rock bottom for the Chargers and can only get better from here .
Tampa needs to get a chance to show what he can do. He’s healthy, which has been a real problem, and has the length and levers and profile to fit these zone concepts maybe more than some others who have played in front of him. The Chargers do not have a pass catcher with 300 yards or two touchdowns; seems like the perfect time to make this switch and start riding this kid after hyping him up as some kind of draft steal to the local media for years.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Jacoby Brissett Will Improve  Ravens Offense In These 3 Critical Areas
full_text:
Jacoby Brissett will give the Ravens an opportunity to operate a downfield passing game in ways they never could under Snoop Huntley.
As much as people in Owings Mills have pretended that Huntley is something he’s not, the reality is the scope of Baltimore’s passing game has crumbled when he has had to step in for Lamar Jackson over the years. And there is every reason to believe Jackson is not throwing another pass this season , and maybe never again in Baltimore. And therefore any hopes they have of mustering even a pedestrian pass game rest with the ability to keep Brissett upright; and with this offensive line, that’s going to be no small task .
Having to drop into a new locker room to try to save a season with coaches and players you do not know and in a system that is fairly foreign is a lot to ask anyone. Let alone someone about to turn 34 without great mobility who was just demoted to third-string in Arizona. But that’s where Brissett and the Ravens find themselves.
Brissett will absolutely improve their ability to facilitate certain parts of this offseason, and give them a fighting chance to try to find out what youngsters like Ja’Kobi Lane  and Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas can do catching the football .
He’s a gamer, and he won’t go down without a fight.
“I've been super impressed by him,” rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle said, “just being able to work with him as he's picking up our offense very quickly, and also being able to provide a little bit of stability to the situation. But really excited about him being here and helping us."
Here’s where Brissett can help the Ravens the most:
Two of the core principles Doyle wanted to emphasize here have fallen totally by the wayside. The under-center running and passing game have washed away with Jackson not finishing a football game since Week 3 and the offensive line is once again one of the worst in the NFL. And with Huntley and then undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano thrust into duty, the play action pass game has faded away, too.
Brissett will lean into that heavily, and it should become more of a staple again.
Since Week 4, the Ravens have attempted just 38 play action passes, that’s 25th in the NFL. Those passes have averaged just 5.9 yards/attempt, that’s, frankly, pathetic and ranks 28th in the NFL since Week 4. And Ravens quarterbacks have completed just 55% of their play-action passes in that span, also 28th in the NFL.
All we heard all spring and summer long was that Doyle was a “genius” because his nascent playbook was loaded with “explosive” plays. This offense is desperate for them now, and getting Zay Flowers going again.
“He's been awesome,” Brissett said Doyle. “What he's thinking as far as the play structure and then obviously how we're attacking the defense, he's very vocal about it. I think that cleans up the communication. I know what he's thinking."
Brissett threw to tight ends more than any QB in the NFL during his two years in Arizona. More even than Jackson. He did it 33% of the time and helped dynamic TE Trey McBride take his game to historic levels . He doesn’t have that guy here, but it’s hard to think that Hibner, with the ability to win with some straight-line speed and a double move won’t become a favorite target if the Ravens do the right thing.
Getting Mark Andrews off the field and out of the way is the only thing to do with his mobility a detriment. They need to get these young TEs in the slot and get them running seam routes that Brissett loves to chuck downfield. Hibner was averaging 9.0 YAC/catch with Jackson in a very limited sample.
If Doyle wants to keep running 11 personnel and then wondering why he can’t run or throw the ball in the second half of games, then maybe he’s just over his head. Lane is even a Joker TE of sorts in the seam.
Brissett is going to throw it 20 yards or more downfield about 10 percent of the time and one of every three attempts with the Cardinals went at least 15 yards downfield – on par with league averages. He has a far bigger arm than Huntley. He isn’t afraid to throw it out of his own endzone.
He will force defenses to respect that and show it early in games to keep them honest in ways we just haven’t seen since Jackson hurt his ankle in early October. He also loves throwing crossers – Brissett had a 113.5 rating on those routes in Arizona – and that’s Flowers specialty coming across the face of the defense. Brissett also excels on outs – 79% completions and 103.9 rating with the Cardinals – and Flowers has been targeted on those routes more than any other.
"We all know he can throw the ball," Flowers said. "He can spin it. But he's just been connecting with us, telling us how he feels about a route, where we should be [and] talking to 'D-Hen' about certain things coming out of the backfield. So, he's just letting his experience show."
Flowers shouldn’t be getting shutout in the boxscore anymore.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Defense Hasn't Had a True Playmaker For Years. And It's Only Getting Worse
full_text:
The Ravens defense hasn’t ever really made a big play in the postseason through Lamar Jackson’s entire career.
Almost like that’s how they were built and hardwired. Because, well, they are .
You cannot go this long with reasonable questions being asked about which players will step up and get the sack or force the fumble or pick off the pass that cements a quality win over an elite opponent with any regularity and not have a fundamental problem. In fact, as much as folks in Owings Mills want to talk about their “culture” as if it’s some winning beacon as they constantly focus on their past and not their present, the reality of their “culture” is overpaid defensive players who don’t deliver , and are especially bad blowing leads and handling the fourth quarter and it spans over four coordinators, now, and two head coaches.
The modern game will come down to a handful of plays, over the course of three hours, in which your blue-chip guys have to be better than theirs. Especially on the defensive side of the ball with every rule change and point of emphasis implemented to incentivize scoring. And for all of Lamar Jackson’s unique brilliance, it still has not been enough to overcome a defense hardwired for failure, to the point that even much-hyper rookie head coach and veteran defensive coordinator Jesse Minter has been no match for it.
Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner, who has watched plenty of Ravens film over years, sees a lot of what I see – not enough go-to guys in the biggest moments who can impact the quarterback, or the football in flight, to put games away. And with $160M put into the defense alone this year, and with Minter’s arrival supposedly a panacea, and with him fully expected to take the defense’s most talented player, Kyle Hamilton, to another level ( it's been just the opposite) , there is reason for concern about the state of affairs.
“It really comes down to can you make the game-changing play?” Warner explained when sizing up this defense. “Can you force a fumble? Can you create, you know, a sack early on in the downs where somebody gets behind the sticks?  A sack, fumble, whatever those things are. That, to me is where the game really skews defensively, because it's hard to just play every down defense in this NFL … “And so that's really what this game comes down to so often on the defensive side is can we create negative plays?"
Instead of the above, the Ravens have the most lifeless and listless second-half defense in the NFL. Everybody shrinks, and no one makes the big play.
They do not have a second-half interception this season despite being throw as much as team in football. Their “closer” Trey Hendrickson (guaranteed a massive $60M for two seasons) hasn’t shown up in the fourth quarter all season and has five total passers in that quarter this season. (Most of general manager Eric DeCosta’s big moves have backfired, massively, and this one is unlikely to age well, either ). They rank 26th in pressure rate in the fourth quarter as a team.
Sadly, that’s become Ravens Football. On defense, that’s how you Play Like A Raven, and Minter has only made it worse.
Only four teams have produced fewer takeaways than the Ravens (who have just nine). No one on this teams has even four sacks – a year ago no one had over five for the season – and Tavius Robinson remains tied for the team lead with 3.5 and he went on season-ending IR weeks ago. Middle linebacker Roquan Smith is paid $20M a year and provides no big plays or momentum-changing hits anymore (he hasn’t for years), and their entire group of defensive backs have combined for zero interceptions all season (Hamilton got his playing linebacker.
Minter’s defense with the Chargers was top three in interceptions per passing attempts his two years there, but it remains the dregs in Baltimore. And there is no reason to expect that to change anytime soon, even if he gets Smith off the field in dime packages and benches $19M corner Marlon Humphrey like he should . Can Minter coach a team and call a defense at the same time, or should Anthony Weaver take over? They have major evaluation issues and roster-construction issues that go well beyond all the assistant coaches and coordinators who have been fired the past four years.
“It is kind of amazing that this has been an issue for the Ravens for years,” Warner said, “and you just say, ‘How does it continue to be an issue with either the same guys, or new guys and with new coaches.' It's hard to put your finger on.”
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Four Storylines For Ravens' Primetime Matchup vs. Chargers
full_text:
Coming off a much-needed mini-bye after having last played on Nov. 5, the Baltimore Ravens will be at home again and looking to snap a four-game losing streak in Week 10 for their fourth straight game against an AFC opponent when they take on the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday night at M&T Bank Stadium.
Going up against the only team in the league without a win and needing to bounce back from getting shellacked in primetime, the Ravens currently have the worst record in the AFC North at 4-5 but have a golden opportunity to get back to .500 with a win.
There are several intriguing storylines surrounding this matchup between these two teams that entered the season with Super Bowl aspirations. Here are the top four.
The 11-year veteran will be the Ravens' fourth different starting quarterback this season after being acquired via trade nearly 10 days ago. He's already beaten the Chargers once this year in the season opener, when he led the Arizona Cardinals to a 26-14 upset win in which he went  27-of-37 for 277 passing yards and a touchdown with no interceptions and a passer rating of 103.1. Brissett compared learning offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's scheme to a "crash course," but both he and the team are confident in his ability to comprehend and operate it at a high level .
"I would just say, [I'm] very, very impressed with how fast he's learned what we're doing," head coach Jesse Minter said. "I don't sit in every offensive meeting, but just the fact that the work that he put in over the weekend and the work that he put in kind of leading up to Wednesday [because] practice didn't operate at any sort of different level for having a guy that literally just got here."
As for how Brissett's presence under center will elevate the offense, he doesn't pose a threat with his legs like two-time MVP Lamar Jackson or even Pro Bowl backup Tyler Huntley. However, his passing ability is second only to Jackson's among Ravens quarterbacks this season, which will help get both the running and passing game back on track. He'll be able to get the ball in the hands of the playmakers through the air accurately in space, and the Chargers won't be able to load the box to slow down star running back Derrick Henry nearly as much as the Ravens' last four opponents did.
Coming out of what was essentially a mini-bye, Minter all but vowed that there would be some pivotal changes to both the personnel deployment and overall approach that the Ravens have had on the side of the ball that is supposed to be his expertise but has given up an average of nearly 35 points in their last three games. While he wouldn't get into specifics about which players could have their playing time reduced or increased, he reiterated that their top priority remains the same.
"I probably take as much pride of not giving up explosives as any defensive coach in the league, and obviously that's not showing up," Minter said. "It's all lip service right now. That's really, to me, major concern No. 1 from a defensive standpoint is limiting the explosive plays.
"If somebody goes on an 18-play drive and scores a touchdown on us, tip your hat and find different ways to get them off rhythm. But the one play, getting behind a coverage or whatever, those are the plays we have to eliminate."
When it comes to players who should have their roles on defense reduced or changed, four-time Pro Bowl cornerback Marlon Humphrey is at the top of that list. Having him predominantly play on the outside this season has made him a big-play magnet. Minter might consider playing him more in the slot, where he's had his best seasons, or continue rotating him with fellow veteran Chidobe Awuzie and third-year pro T.J. Tampa. Other players who've shown they're deserving more playing time on that side of the ball are veteran safety K'Von Wallace and undrafted rookie outside linebacker Ethan Burke.
The only roster, coaching staff and organization as a whole that the Ravens' first-year head coach is more familiar with than his own is the one he'll be going up against on Monday night. He spent the previous two seasons as the Chargers' defensive coordinator, where he went up against two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Justin Herbert every day in practice and masked the deficiencies of the defensive personnel by amplifying their strengths. His history with Los Angeles head coach Jim Harbaugh goes back even further, as the two won a national championship together at the University of Michigan in 2023.
To call this matchup one between familiar foes is an understatement to say the least but with extra prep time off a mini bye and desperately needing to snap this current losing skid, Minter was likely imparting as much of his knowledge of how to attack his former team on his assistants since their last game ended.
"You're going against somebody you care a lot about, which sometimes makes it even more competitive," Minter said. "I know how Jim feels about it, I'm sure. So, I'm excited about the challenge. I think after the game it's great to be able to catch up and say hey to a bunch of those guys. But obviously, [there's] major, major focus on our team, our players [and] getting our team ready to play at a high level. [I'm] excited to play in primetime in front of our fans and give them something to cheer about."
Staying on the topic of the Ravens Flock, it's been a season and a half since the team last won a nationally televised game at M&T Bank Stadium. They've not only lost their last four primetime games on their home turf, but each loss has been more embarrassing than the last, from getting steamrolled by the Detroit Lions for 224 yards in Week 3 last year to getting routed by the Cincinnati Bengals last Thanksgiving and allowing the eventual AFC champion New England Patriots to rally from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit in Week 16 last year.
Their first crack at redemption this season couldn't have gone any worse, as they were blown out by the Jacksonville Jaguars in their last game, but they were also being led by a hobbled, undrafted rookie free agent at quarterback , making his first career start. With a more experienced and capable starting quarterback in Brissett, going up against what has been the worst team in the league by virtue of their winless record and what they've shown on tape, there's no reason that the Ravens fans in attendance shouldn't go home with their heads held high after a victory for the first time since the 2024 Wildcard round. In that game, they ran the Pittsburgh Steelers out of two and held them to under 20 points for the second time that season.
Josh is a writer for Baltimore Ravens On SI focusing primarily on original content and reporting. He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: Don't Blame Mark Andrews For His Brutal 2026 Season; Blame Eric DeCosta
full_text:
Don’t blame Mark Andrews for the Baltimore Ravens having some of the worst tight-end production in the NFL. It’s really not his fault.
He’s been in decline for three years and obvious signs of athletic regression were there throughout the 2024 season – let alone last year when general manager Eric DeCosta made one of the more impetuous decisions in modern franchise history and gave Andrews money earmarked for 25-year-old Isaiah Likely when that youngster rightfully preferred to wait to hit the market at that point before opting whether to come back to Baltimore.
Don’t blame Andrews for merely continuing down a path the entire NFL knew he was on when DeCosta couldn’t get more than a very late-round draft pick for him after the 2024 season ended with Andrews dropping a critical two-point conversion in Buffalo that only hit him in both hands. Don’t blame him for taking the money when DeCosta offered it; if you were on the other side of someone playing favorites and giving you that kind of $35M handout, darn right you’d take it too.
Don’t blame him for taking the field when overmatched puppet coaches and coordinators continue to run him out on there way more than anyone should, because, well, when you are among the 10-highest paid at your position and the GM has all the power in the building , that’s how it goes. Don’t blame him when he’s back here in 2027, because the contract is virtually untradeable and he’s guaranteed another $5M next year regardless (multiple salary cap gurus have suggested he’ll be on this roster next year because of the terrible contract).
Please try to keep all of that in mind while you consider whether or not to boo one of the better pass catchers in franchise history when he continues to jump offsides a bunch (because he will and he’s doing it more than any non-offensive lineman in the NFL). And when he drops passes, because that’s been going on for years and his drop-rate leads all NFL tight ends (12%, most of any TE with 20 targets). And none of this has anything to do with the injuries to Lamar Jackson.
Those boos should be saved for the decision makers who have repeatedly built bloated and lopsided losing rosters with players who have now been DeCosta-ed (blowing a double-digit lead in the second half of games they lose) 17 times since he took over as GM in 2019, runaway leaders in the NFL.
He’s merely a symptom of the disease in Owings Mills. He’s not the cause. And all of this will get worse.
Andrews is the only veteran TE on the roster after impact blocker Dyrham Smythe was lost for the season on IR and Nick Vannett has toggled between the practice squad. And Baltimore’s tight end production has been abysmal.
The Ravens rank 18th in the NFL with 450 total yards from their tight ends. They have amassed three total touchdowns. They have been nonfactors in the redzone and especially in the second half of games, as the scope of this offseason shrinks once rookie coordinator Declan Doyle rips through his early-game script.
They rank 20th at 9.4 yards per catch and 27th in YAC at 4.2/reception. Much of that is due to the fact that Andrews cannot sprint to separate or high-point the ball anymore. His catch radius ain’t what it used to be, nor are his hands. He should have been benched a good month ago as we suggested, but there’s obviously politics involved in that.
Andrews averages an improbable 2.0 of YAC/catch for the second straight year, that is 37th (dead last among all qualified TEs) this season. He is 31st in Expected Pointed Added/Target among TEs (-0.10) and 50th in yards/route (4.56). None of that will improve in the second half as weather becomes an issue and his body absorbs more hits.
The Ravens best be prepared to run rookie Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas out there more than ever before, and hope they can deliver. With journeyman Jacoby Brissett taking over at quarterback, he loves pushing the ball downfield to tight ends on seam routes and no one attempted a higher percentage of passes to tight ends than Brissett the past two seasons . The fewer to Andrews, the better.
Oh, as for Likely, well, he's having an All-Pro season for the Giants despite shaky QB play and he’s making slightly less than what DeCosta bestowed on the aged tight end he preferred. But you can’t blame Andrews for that, either.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Won't Win Anything Until They Get Legit Outside Receivers
full_text:
The Ravens have been a failure at evaluating pass rushers and defensive backs under general manager Eric DeCosta, but don’t forget about wide receiver, as well.
Two-time MVP Lamar Jackson can do more with less, and he has throughout his entire career, but with no more guaranteed years on his contract and with the superstar holding complete and total leverage over this organization in 2027 and about to make over $70M/season no matter where he goes, now would be a good time for The Castle to get real about its deep receiver rot.
Zay Flowers is a great piece and he can do a lot of fun and exciting things. But he can't carry a modern passing game. And with tight end Mark Andrews beyond done, and Baltimore's rookie pass catchers doing nothing to this point (how about making Elijah Sarrat active Monday?), they could face a crisis in 2027.
But his lack of size is and always be a significant issue and he will never show up in the redzone and endzone like the very top receivers do, and trying to funnel a passing game to him on crossers and intermediate stuff is always going to come up empty when it really matters. Even with a football genius like Jackson at quarterback. Eventually, one would think the Ravens might recognize this, then again, stubborn and ego is their very scouting brand.
To this point DeCosta would rather keep playing his former draft busts like Rashod Bateman to pretend to be winning outside receivers and keep loading up on guys who really will only do damage in the slot (like all the pass catchers he drafted in 2026) than change his ways. Maybe he’s incapable of it. Whatever. But these kinds of rosters won’t be good enough - especially with running back Derrick Henry’s days as a 5.5 yards/carry guy long gone – and someone there better embrace that reality quickly.
Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner studies NFL offenses constantly as a game analyst and studio analyst on NFL telecasts, and is perpetually baffled by what the Ravens think they can get away with running Bateman and Devontez Walker out there on the outside and hoping Jackson can get by with those kinds of guys.
Warner seemed pretty frustrated for Jackson (dealing with yet another injury suffered in the pocket ) when I brough up the reality of Baltimore trying this “Zay And Pray” approach to the passing game on “The Daily Flock Show”, with one smaller receiver who warrants real attention and the boundary a wasteland.
“I think we all know what Zay Flowers is and he's really good at what he does,” Warner said, “in the slot, run after catch, you know, the quick throws, all of that stuff. And not that he can't break, big plays, because obviously he makes big plays all the time, but you need those complimentary pieces in your offense, even if they're not great, that, hey, when they want to stack inside, we can go outside and we can win the one-on-one battles.
“When they want to take Zay away in the middle of the field, we've got a guy that can stretch the field and give us some chunk plays to make life easier for us offensively. And, you know, that has been a question for a long time. They've really been built inside out. And they've never really found that outside piece that can be a difference-maker.”
Longtime Ravens defensive coordinator Wink Martindale brought up the same concept when we chatted about this roster “They don’t have any Werewolves,” he exclaimed when comparing Lamar’s weapons to other teams, and especially Joe Burrow with the Bengals. Flowers is a great piece, but as the main thing in a playoff winning offense that’s a big ask.
With Jackson holding all the leverage in negotiations, the Ravens need to recruit him to stay. And what they have to offer right now ain't much.
The state of this offensive roster is doing them no favors and they better have a pretty cogent plan to add a true outside receiver, because there isn’t one on this roster and Lane proving to be that guy is another reach and all DeCosta does is reach for receivers; finding the real thing (modern size/speed demon) has been impossible for him.
“There is something to having what I call an X receiver,” Warner said, “a big body, one-on-one receiver on the backside where we can put our three receivers to the right side and we can have this great concept. But if they go one-on-one on the backside, I know I can go there and win and make the game easier.
“I don't have to read through seven guys over here and get to the right read and make the throw. I can go back here and go, ‘Boom, take it!’ You know, throw it to him … Can be a jump ball, but I mean, even just winning on routes, you know, that was what Larry Fitzgerald was for me. You That was what, you know, Tory Holt was for me. If they want to push over here to Isaac (Bruce) and, you know, three receiver sets, I know that I have a great chance to win one-on-one on the backside and get a favorable matchup, and it just makes the game easier for all of us.
It's just go back and pitch and catch, you know, with that guy. And teams havie that guy as a difference-maker for their quarterbacks and especially if you don't have Lamar Jackson and you have a backup quarterback, man, it would be nice to be able to give them some easy completions here and there. And that's been something that, you know, they haven't seemed to have for as long as I can remember is a guy that can do that.”
Under DeCosta, perhaps they never will.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Top 4 Reasons The Chargers Could Upset The Ravens Monday Night
full_text:
Monday night is a must-win game for the Baltimore Ravens if they want any chance to pretend to be a playoff team.
A win over the winless Chargers isn’t going to provide some huge boost, mind you, and reaching the postseason will remain a stretch given the realities of this roster (it’s just not very good) and this coaching staff (overmatched thus far, by and large ). But a loss would be nothing short of damning, it would beg real questions about the present and future of this failing franchise and could perhaps further grease the path for two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson to decide to ply his trade elsewhere in 2027.
The Chargers have absolutely been the worst team in the NFL, they have earned that 0-8 record and they seem to have absolutely nothing going for them in any aspect of play, and particularly on offense. Traveling across the country on Monday night is probably not their preference right about now. But don’t think for one minute they can’t win this football game, and, believe it or not, they have several things working in their favor above and beyond the fact that Jacoby Brissett will become the fourth quarterback to start a game for the Ravens this season when he takes over in the huddle in Week 9.
Here are the top reasons why the Chargers could pull this off:
Minter looks horribly out of his depth so far, even messaging information about Jackson’s injuries has been a struggle and having his notes out on Monday to hint at lineup changes isn’t much of a bad cop routine. His veteran roster has walked all over him and his young assistants and he’s facing his mentor, in Jim Harbaugh, who knows his psyche and basically created him. The Chargers have nothing to lose and years of practicing against Minter’s defense in college and the NFL means Harbaugh knows a lot of buttons to push.
No one on Minter's staff exudes any real confidence – defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver has become exceptional at suggesting false confidence – they lack leaders and playmakers on both sides of the ball and expecting them to emerge now under extreme duress in a “can’t-lose game,” strikes me as problematic. Minter has been unable to inspire them to this point and they are incredibly weak, mentally, coming off four straight losses.
Minter was asked about trying to coach and call plays at the same time this week, as he should have been. But he seems shaken, and I don't fancy him against his mentor ( major coaching changes should be on the table now, as longtime Raiders exec Amy Trask suggested to us on "The Daily Flock").
This team is 3-9 in its last 12 at home and their choke gene is even more active at home than on the road. They are incredibly adept at getting DeCosta-ed – (blowing a 10-point lead in the second half to lose) at home, and no lead is safe … Oh and they also aren’t built to play from behind having to turn to yet another QB with a 30-year-old offensive coordinator, Declan Doyle, who has struggled to concoct anything that woks in the second half of games.
The front office is acting in a desperate and panicky mode and general manager Eric DeCosta really only builds choking rosters without many players who show up in the clutch. All of this bleeds into the locker room and the bloated payroll and it's an ugly concoction. And then instead of actual introspection, they throw around hollow words like "culture" and mythologize their past. Yuck.
It's like they are built to self-destruct by executives who really only know how to self -destruct from an Ozzie Newsome personnel family tree that has yet to product a single success as a GM.
Baltimore has lost four straight home prime time games, and the Ravens are going to be expected to discard with the worst team in football. Says here that won’t exactly bring out the best in them by a long shot. Collectively, they have a knack for coming up small, and all the weight is on them. Chargers season is already over.
Justin Herbert is not the worst QB in the NFL. He isn’t.
But that's how he's played this far.
Hall of Fame QB Kurt Warner laid out why he believes the star is struggling so mightily and much of it is how he is being asked to read the field with “pure progressions.” At some point Herbert is going to start ignoring his charlatan coordinator, Mike McDaniel, and do what he wants, how he wants. And Harbaugh is going to start getting on the headset and overruling things or taking over play calling himself.
Wouldn’t be surprised at all if that starts Monday night, whether it gets out publicly or not. Something has to change, sitting in Week 10 with 6 touchdown passes and 11 picks is probably rock bottom (QB rating of 75, and after that there is nowhere to go but up. Herbert knows Minter’s tendencies and defaults as well as anyone – certainly better than McDaniel – and I suspect he exhibits more autonomy against his old coach.
The Chargers got a look at Brissett in Week 1,  when the Cardinals pulled off an upset that no longer looks like an upset. Moving to a new team midseason is brutal – and doing it with a team fighting for its season at 4-5, is even tougher. The Chargers don’t miss Minter as much as they miss having a remotely competent offense that can run or pass the football.
Defensively, the Chargers are better than the Ravens.
They are far superior in the redzone (11th) and on third-down (8th) and have allowed a lower opposing passer rating for the season, too. The Chargers are also superior to the Ravens in points allowed per drive. Given just how pathetic both of these offensive lines are, there is the potential for big plays to be made on defense, but the relative lack of mobility from Brissett, in comparison to Herbert, could end up being a considerable factor in this game and we expect Herbert’s legs to be a big part of the game plan.
Sad as it is to say, given Minter’s pedigree and how highly the Ravens touted him, the Chargers have the edge on defense and a considerable edge at kicker and that might be enough to win a tight game. They are certainly overdue.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Bills' Week 11 Injury Outlook: Updates on Christian Benford, Dee Alford, Five Others
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills ' defensive backfield suffered its share of bumps and bruises during the November 15 road win over the New York Jets.
Both starting outside cornerback Christian Benford and slot cornerback Dee Alford did not finish the game due to in-game injuries. Starting inside linebacker Dorian Williams saw his day end early in the fourth quarter.
Starting safeties Cole Bishop and Amani Hooker, along with cornerback Maxwell Hairston, all briefly received medical attention during the Week 10 matinee, but all returned to action before the day was done. The same can be said for wide receiver Keon Coleman.
In a positive development, starting right tackle Spencer Brown was active despite being doubtful due to an ankle injury. Brown played the entire game up until the final three kneel-downs, and he appears ready to keep rolling.
The Bills have a normal Sunday-to-Sunday game week ahead with the Miami Dolphins set to visit on November 22. Only four days after that, however, they'll host the Kansas City Chiefs for a Thanksgiving night matchup .
"We're at the point in the season where the reality [is] Wednesday is going to be just a walkthrough. There's accumulation of reps and practices," said head coach Joe Brady on Monday afternoon.
Here are the injured players who warrant monitoring as the practice week progresses.
Alford initially left for a few plays late in the second quarter. He was evaluated for a head injury and cleared to return.
Back on the field for the Jets' opening drive of the second half, Alford went down to the ground hard in the end zone while covering wide receiver Garrett Wilson on a 1st-and-goal play. He left for another concussion check, and the Bills subsequently ruled him out for the remainder of the game.
Benford was questionable entering the game with a wrist injury from the November 9 primetime win, but he appeared unaffected in the early going.
Injuring his groin during the second half, Benford was ruled out and missed 18 of 71 reps. It doesn't sound as if he'll be ready to practice by Wednesday, but that doesn't mean he won't play Sunday.
"I've said all along, there's guys that might not practice, but have played a lot of football for us, and, if they have the opportunity to go play in the game, we're going to play them. Christian's really no different, and we'll kind of just progress it day by day," said Brady.
Late in the fourth quarter, Bishop appeared to get banged up while diving toward Jets' running back Braelon Allen on a screen play. He was shown be examined on the sideline, missing only three total snaps.
"A little sore, shoulder hurts a little bit, but we'll see how we're feeling tomorrow. [I'm] sure, we'll be alright, though," said Bishop postgame (h/t WGR's Sal Capaccio for the audio).
Early in the fourth quarter, Coleman absorbed a helmet-to-helmet hit from Jets' safety Minkah Fitzpatrick while making a catch along the Bills' sideline. After being evaluated for a head injury, the independent party cleared Coleman to return . He was back in action with 9:59 remaining in the game.
Injured on a first down with under 3:00 remaining in the game, Hairston exited briefly with what's presumed to be an ankle issue. He returned after an injury timeout.
Hooker was spotted entering the medical tent, but it didn't cause him to miss a single rep. He was the Bills' lone defender to play 100 percent of snaps .
Williams was ruled questionable to return due to a calf problem early in fourth quarter, but fourth-round rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr took over for him the rest of the way. His last play came with 2:07 remaining in the third quarter.

title: Former Bills Star Marcell Dareus Arrested After Allegedly Assaulting Officer
full_text:
Former Buffalo Bills defensive tackle Marcell Dareus made some unfortunate news this weekend as the two-time Pro Bowler was arrested following a traffic stop.
According to TMZ, Dareus was stopped in Hoover, Alabama for driving erratically. He was reportedly uncooperative and fled the scene after a physical altercation.
"The situation went down early Saturday morning after a police officer in Hoover, AL, pulled the 36-year-old d-lineman over for driving erratically. Things escalated quickly, according to Hoover PD, which says Dareus was uncooperative during the stop, assaulting an officer before driving off," TMZ wrote.
"Officers pursued the former Bills star to his house, where they say he resisted again ... though they finally got him in cuffs. When they searched Marcell, cops say they found marijuana. One of the cops was taken to the hospital, where he was treated for minor injuries."
According to the report, Dareus was booked on four different charges,second-degree aggravated assault on a police officer, attempting to elude a police officer, resisting arrest, and second-degree marijuana possession. He posted bond the same day.
Dareus is an Alabama native, who was born in Birmingham. He went on to play for Alabama, where he won a national title and was named the defensive MVP of the 2010 BCS National Championship Game.
Following his stellar career with the Crimson Tide, Dareus was selected third overall in the 2011 NFL draft by the Bills. He was a day one starter for the Bills and recorded 43 tackles and 5.5 sacks as a rookie.
His best season with Buffalo was in 2014 when he earned a spot on the All-Pro Team after recording 49 tackles and 10 sacks. He played six and a half seasons with the Bills, finishing with 300 tackles and 35 sacks in 91 games.
While he was great on the field, Dareus twice violated the NFL's substance-abuse policy. He was also arrested in 2014 while with Buffalo on charges for possession of a controlled substance. He also faced legal trouble for a car accident that same year.
Dareus was traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars during the 2017 season where he was reunited with former Buffalo head coach Doug Marone. His final season in the NFL was in 2019 when he had 13 tackles and a half-sack in six games. His tenure ended when he had core muscle surgery, and was released following the season.

title: Buffalo Bills' Highest And Lowest Graded Players from Week 10 Victory
full_text:
Another week resulted in another victory for the Buffalo Bills . They started slow, with the New York Jets cutting the lead to 10-9 early in the third quarter, but then took over from there.
Buffalo wound up winning easily , 31-12 and improved to 8-1 overall and 5-0 on the road this season. They're still sitting in first place in the AFC and fans are even more encouraged following the solid debut from newly acquired safety , Amani Hooker.
While Hooker played well, he actually finished outside of the top five for PFF grades this week. The veteran safety had a respectable 68.6, which left him sixth on defense for the Bills. That said, let's see which players stood out as the top five and bottom five performers during the win over the Jets.
Khalil Shakir continues to quietly do everything asked of him. He didn't get many passes thrown his way, finishing with 26 yards on two receptions, but he added 29 yards on three rushing attempts. A huge part of his 77.6 overall grade came from his blocking, which won't even show up on the stat sheet. Shakir earned an 80.3 in that respect , further proof of how well-rounded the veteran wideout is.
Fellow wide receiver DJ Moore and tight end Dalton Kincaid made the list as well, and each had a highlight-reel play. Kincaid hauled in a short pass and turned it into a 54-yard gain while Moore had a 45-yard touchdown. They were joined by offensive tackle Spencer Brown, who was a game-time decision , but showed no signs of being slowed down.
The lone defender in the top five was Damar Hamlin, who earned a 73.7 despite being relegated to just 17 snaps with the arrival of Hooker.
Michael Hoecht had the lowest score at 34.4 , although he did record his first full sack of the season. Bradley Chubb and T.J. Sanders each finished under 40 as well, as a frustrating season continues for both players.
Jordan Hancock also struggled as he spent a good bit of time playing the nickel. The only offensive player in the bottom five was Dawson Knox, who had one catch for seven yards on three targets. One issue for him was his run-blocking as Knox earned a mere 51.1 in that area on Sunday.

title: Poor Decision That Josh Allen Got Away With in Bills' Week 10 Win Simply Can't Happen
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills and quarterback Josh Allen cannot afford to let it become habitual.
While one can get away with such decision-making when facing a significantly inferior opponent such as the New York Jets, one's luck will eventually run out at the most inopportune of moments come January.
A formidable foe would've potentially used it as a starting point for a fourth-quarter comeback.
With the Bills looking to increase a 24-12 lead early in the fourth quarter, Allen ignored two wide open receivers not far past the line of scrimmage in order to throw a low-percentage deep ball that was intercepted.
"Turned the ball over, shouldn't be doing that," said Allen after the win.
It happened on a 3rd-and-12 play where running back Ty Johnson was open in the flat with green grass all around and wide receiver Khalil Shakir was seemingly uncovered on a shallow crossing route. Both potential receivers appeared in a position to get past the sticks after the catch.
Instead, Allen, targeting Greg Dortch, threw deep down the middle of the field into double coverage where Jets' cornerback Azareye'h Thomas picked off the pass.
No disrespect to Dortch, but he is no DJ Moore. While Allen completed a beautiful long touchdown to Moore in the game, it was to a receiver much bigger and more physical than the 5-foot-7 Dortch.
Azareye'h Thomas with an INT BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oSsC1E1ChR
The interception was the third of three consecutive Bills' miscues in the span of one snap.
Prior to Allen's poor post-snap decision, Buffalo made two pre-snap errors. On 3rd-and-7 from their own 43-yard line, the Bills were flagged for an illegal shift that pushed the line of scrimmage back five yards.
Then, the Bills failed to regroup quickly enough in the aftermath of the penalty call, and needed to burn a timeout facing 3rd-and-12.
"Honestly, I think offensively, we didn't play too well. I know you can look at the stat sheet and 31 points. Didn't feel like, first half, we executed the way we wanted to," said Allen.
The Bills made too many unforced errors, including four false starts, but at the end of the day, they left points on the field due to a poor decision by Allen .
Too many times has the incredibly talented Allen unnecessarily pushed the envelope as opposed to going for the higher percentage option. Against teams like the Jets, he can get away with it, but it can't happen in big spots.
Simply put, Allen needs to take what the defense is giving him more often, especially when the stakes are higher come January.
In a divisional round playoff game, it's an entirely different story with most likely a different final outcome. Allen has to clean it up before it comes back to bite him.

title: Bills' Stock Report: Two Traded Players Soar, But Offense Dips After Week 10 win
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills have yet to produce a complete performance, but even so they're 8-1 overall and atop the AFC standings .
As for their latest victory, 31-12 over the New York Jets in The Meadowlands, the Bills again left points on the field due to offensive miscues and questionable decisions.
Still, it's difficult to overly criticize an offense that scored 31 points on the road with multiple parties responsible for game-changing moments. Wide receiver DJ Moore and running back James Cook, who both exploded for long scoring plays, did plenty to boost their stock in the win.
On defense, safety Amani Hooker, who was making his Bills' debut following the November 10 trade, and rookie outside linebacker TJ Parker led a unit that kept the opponent out of the end zone for the second week in a row.
Notably, Hooker, Parker and Moore are all new to the Bills in 2026. Parker was the No. 35 overall selection in last April's draft while Moore came to Buffalo in an offseason trade with the Chicago Bears.
Without further adieu, here is the Bills On SI Week 10 stock report featuring four risers and one that must reverse course.
MOORE PLZ‼️ 📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/dWeufun8gS
Such performances are becoming commonplace for the NFL's reigning rushing champion. Accounting for his fifth 100-yard rushing performance in nine games, Cook carried 18 times for 157 yards and one touchdown.
Whether it's consistently grinding out three or four yards on early-down rushes or breaking off a 74-yarder like he did against the Jets, Cook has proven to be the ultimate bellcow running back for the league's highest scoring offense.
Arriving only five days ago, Hooker looked like he'd been in Jim Leonhard's defense as long as any other player on the field.
The Bills' trade deadline addition did not miss a single snap in the Week 10 win.  Hooker, the only Bills' defender to play 100 percent of snaps, totaled seven tackles and one pass break-up.
"So impressed with Amani Hooker," said Bills' rookie head coach Joe Brady. "The fact that he was able to play this whole game on a few days when we didn't practice. Kind of speaks to kind of who he is and how much he's going to help us."
It may seem crazy to criticize an offense that averages a NFL-best 31.9 points per game, but the Bills can be much better and so can their quarterback.
"Honestly, I think offensively, we didn't play too well. I know you can look at the stat sheet and 31 points. Didn't feel like first half, we executed the way we wanted to," said five-time NFL MVP finalist Josh Allen.
The Bills were only 2 of 10 converting on third down, and Allen passed up some potential chain-moving throws while trying to force chunk plays to happen. With both Khalil Shakir and Ty Johnson open in space close to the line of scrimmage, Allen threw deep to Greg Dortch into double coverage for his lone interception of the game.
Underscoring another failure by the Bills' offense, a presnap penalty directly preceded that Allen interception. Buffalo was flagged for an illegal shift, pushing the offense back five yards on a 3rd-and-7.
"I thought the penalties, there's too many pre-snap penalties today. We have to play cleaner football," said Brady.
Left tackle Dion Dawkins, left guard Alec Anderson, tight end Jackson Hawes and tight end Dawson Knox all committed false start penalties.
Furthermore, there was a squandered touchdown opportunity midway through the second quarter when the offense turned a 1st-and-10 at Jets' 16 into a 4th-and-13 field goal attempt.
It was an encouraging week on multiple levels for the Bills' top offseason addition. Finally off the injury report for the first time since Week 3, Moore played 58 percent of snaps and produced a team-high 90 receiving yards.
"When he's out on the field, he's a threat to score from anywhere. Thought he did a great job tonight," said Allen.
Moore made the play of the day for the Bills' passing game when he pulled in a 45-yard bomb with a Jets' defender draped on him at the goal line.
Parker seemed to start slow this season , but it was nothing out of the ordinary for a rookie. While he began percolating out of the bye week, the Week 10 win was a clear breakout performance.
Nearly matching Bradley Chubb and Greg Rousseau in snap volume, Parker consistently applied pressure during pass rush situations. He totaled five tackles and 2.0 sacks.
"His reps are going to continue to go up, because I think as much as we're keeping all those guys fresh, it's only going to help us. But he's playing confidently.  He's such a strong, powerful football player to be able to then transition that into sacks, it speaks to his development," said Brady.

title: Buffalo Bills' Recent Improvement on Defense Comes With Major Caveat
full_text:
After starting out the season with one of the worst defenses in the NFL, the Buffalo Bills have seen quite the turnaround in recent weeks.
Over their last three games, Buffalo has surrendered just 28 points in total, and the defense has not permitted a touchdown in 11 straight quarters.
That is certainly a welcomed site after the you-know-what show the defense was over the first six games, but there's a major caveat to those showings.
There is one common bond between the Bills' last three games: the lack of quality in the quarterback play.
In Week 8 versus the Baltimore Ravens, the Bills faced rookie Joe Fagnano after both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley exited early with injuries.
In Week 9, the Minnesota Vikings were forced to start Carson Wentz because of an injury to Kyler Murray.
We foolishly thought that might actually be worse for the Bills , but Wentz went on to throw up one of the worst quarterback performances we've ever seen.
It was so bad that the Vikings turned around and traded a third-round pick to the Las Vegas Raiders for Kirk Cousins, who was an immediate upgrade for Minnesota's offense in Week 10. Cousins was also the last quality quarterback the Bills faced for an entire game and he dropped a pair of touchdowns and 313 yards on Buffalo's defense en route to 30 points.
Then, on Sunday, the Bills knocked New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith out of the game twice , and he did not return the second time.
That led to rookie Cade Klubnik getting the football and the results were about what we expected, with Klubnik barely completing 50% of his passes for 137 yards and a pick.
Of course, the Bills can't control who they face at quarterback and it's certainly great to see the defense played well against signal-callers the unit should be able to stop, but we also know Buffalo is going to be playing a lot better competition when the games matter most, so the defense isn't out of the woods yet.
Buffalo will meet the lowly Miami Dolphins in Week 11 and they will not provide a test for the Bills' defense, either.
That's because starter Malik Willis is on injured reserve, which will likely lead to another start for Kyle McCord, who was not good in the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the also lowly Indianapolis Colts.
McCord completed just 53.1% of his passes for 209 yards and zero touchdowns to zero picks.
We will have to wait until Week 12 for the Bills' next true test. That game will see the Bills take on the Kansas City Chiefs and superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes.
Mahomes needs no introduction, especially for Bills fans who have seen plenty of him during the Josh Allen era.
Mahomes has dominated the Bills in the postseason to the tune of a 4-0 record, a 74% completion rate, 290.8 passing yards per game and nine touchdowns to zero picks.
The Chiefs quarterback has actually struggled against the Bills in the regular season during his career, with Mahomes sporting a 1-5 record in six contests while completing just 61.7% of his passes for an average of 258.7 yards per game and 10 touchdowns to eight interceptions.
That said, nobody should (or will) be taking Mahomes lightly when he walks into Highmark Stadium in Week 12. We'll know a lot more about Buffalo's defense after that game.

title: Josh Allen Surpasses Peyton Manning for NFL Record in Bills' Win vs. Jets
full_text:
Josh Allen, you've done it again.
It seems like every time the Buffalo Bills ' MVP signal-caller takes the field, he's setting another NFL record .
Well, this one may be his most impressive yet.
In Allen and the Bills' eighth win of the year against the AFC East rival New York Jets, he was able to notch three more touchdowns for the year. He passed for one through the air and rushed for two more on the ground, bringing his season total to 24 (13 passing, 11 rushing).
Those three scores now put him at 325 scored thus far in his career. It's a record-setting mark, passing Peyton Manning for the most in player's first 10 seasons. But what's even more impressive is thinking of how quickly Allen accomplished the feat.
Josh Allen is UNREAL 🤯 Allen is only in his 9th season, and Patrick Mahomes is currently in his 10th season 👀 pic.twitter.com/EKmqOZOIzM
What is craziest when thinking about this record is that Allen has a season and a half left to extend it for a player's first 10 seasons. It goes to show just how dominant of a player the 2024 NFL MVP has been since entering the league in 2018.
To think he's outpaced three current Hall of Famers (Manning, Dan Marino, and Brett Favre), as well as future HOF selections (Russell Wilson and Patrick Mahomes), showcases the caliber of player Allen has been in Buffalo.
It also goes to show that as strong as Allen has been with his arm, his legs have helped amplify his game to a legendary status.
The Wyoming product is now tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for the NFL's lead in rushing TDs. The win over the Jets marks the fourth time on the year that Allen has scored two or more TDs on the ground.
His rushing stats really are silly. The NFL's all-time rushing TD leader from the QB position is now tied for 14th in NFL history in rushing TDs at 90 with HOF running backs Eric Dickerson and Curtis Martin. This is for a player who already has 233 career TD passes.
He's also notched his fourth-consecutive season with 10 or more rushing TDs, pushing his total to 52 since 2023, tied for the most in the NFL in that span with Derrick Henry.
Allen has now rushed for 10+ touchdowns in 4 straight seasons, tying Jalen Hurts (2021-24) for the longest streak by a QB in NFL history. https://t.co/hyyiUkRwWj
But what might be scariest for NFL defenders? Despite these records and the Bills being the NFL's top offense in terms of points and yards per game, Allen and the offense aren't even playing their best ball yet .
"Didn't play too well in the first half," said Allen to NFL on CBS sideline reporter Melanie Collins after the game. "In the second half, we scored on a four-play, two-play, and a one-play drive. So, the explosiveness is there. We've gotta clean some stuff up. We're 8-1, gotta find a way to learn from this one, flush it, and move on to the next week."
Buffalo's offense really has a chance to tighten things up as the season progresses. And if it does, we should expect that much more TDs from Allen to extend this record.
"He just keeps on running. He's our workhorse." Josh Allen on what James Cook means to the Bills offense. 🎤: @Melanie_Collins pic.twitter.com/yEY5eLVd8w

title: How Amani Hooker Fared in Week 10 Debut With Buffalo Bills
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills saw the debut of their newest player in Week 10 when safety Amani Hooker, who was acquired via trade last week , took the field in the 31-12 win over the New York Jets on Sunday.
While we knew ahead of time that Hooker was going to play in the game just days after his was acquired, we weren't sure just how much the veteran safety would see the field.
Well, according to Pro Football Focus , Hooker played a whopping 70 snaps, which was more than any Bills defender in the contest, so the Bills did not ease him in. Hooker played 49 of those snaps at free safety, 12 in the box and eight in the slot for Buffalo, so defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard used him all over.
Hooker's ability to play that many snaps and line up in different spots in his debut is a testament to how quickly he picked up Buffalo's defense.
Hooker has seen better days in coverage, but he was still solid.
The former Tennessee Titan gave up receptions on four of six targets thrown his way (66.7%) for 47 yards and no scores. He permitted 21 yards after the catch and a long gain of 17.
PFF gave him a respectable 66.1 grade in coverage, the sixth-best mark on the team. Hooker notched one pass break-up and he nearly had two picks but couldn't come down with either one.
All in all, it was a pretty solid day on the back end for Hooker, especially when you consider it was his debut.
PFF gave Hooker another respectable grade in run defense, with the former fourth-round pick notching a 64.9 in that area.
That is below his season-long mark of 83.9, but it's still pretty solid.
Hooker totaled seven tackles, the third-most on the team, and his missed tackle percentage was just 10%.
We did see Hooker get shaken up during the contest, which led to him getting a trip to the blue medical tent.
However, the new Bills safety emerged rather quickly and got back into the game and finished without incident.
We'll be keeping an eye on the injury report for him this coming week, but Hooker should be good to go for Week 11.
After the game, Hooker talked about how much it meant to him that the Bills wanted to trade for him, and he loved the fact that Buffalo trusted him to play as much as he did so soon.
"Just for the opportunity for a team that's winning to want me, to put me out here Game 1 and trust me, my job during the week was to show them that they can trust me and everyone took me in and just showed love across the board," Hooker said per WIVB's Josh Reed .
"It was a challenge and I love challenges like that," he said of his limited preparation time for his debut. "It kind of felt like training camp, where I gotta be in the book constantly non-stop. I really just wanted my guys that were gonna be out here to trust me, to know I was gonna be in the right spot. That was big for me and I think we did a good job."
As you'd expect, head coach Joe Brady was impressed with what Hooker was able to do on Sunday.
"I'm so impressed with Amani Hooker. The fact that he was able to play this whole game on a few days when we didn't practice. Kind of speaks to who he is and how much he's gonna help us and, shoot, he almost made a couple of plays on the ball," said Brady.
Hooker was no doubt impressive on Sunday and even better days are ahead the more comfortable he gets with his new team.

title: Five Winners & One Loser From Bills Rout vs. Jets in Week 10
full_text:
It was a slow start for the Buffalo Bills, who had a 10-9 lead over the New York Jets in the third quarter. Then, the offense took off.
From that point on, the Bills outscored the Jets 21-3, leaving MetLife Stadium with a 31-12 victory . Buffalo was the more physical team and improved to 8-1 on the season. They're also 5-0 on the road this year, proving to be a tough opponent no matter where they play.
With this win in the books, let's see who stood out as both winners and losers for the Bills.
New York was set to punt the ball away for the second consecutive drive as they were facing a fourth-and-six. They decided to line up to attempt to draw the Bills offside, and it worked. A hard count got Ed Oliver to move, and that led to a five-yard penalty.
The Jets converted on the fourth-and-short following the flag, and that helped them pull off a 12-play drive, ending with a 41-yard field goal from Jason Sanders to make it a 7-3 game. Overall, Oliver didn't have a bad game, but this is a play he surely regrets.
Second-round pick TJ Parker entered this game with 1.5 sacks and more than doubled that number against the Jets. Parker had plenty of success rushing the New York quarterbacks, sacking backup Cade Klubnik twice in the game. He now has 3.5 sacks as he's beginning to show why Brandon Beane made him the team's top pick this year.
New York cut the lead to 10-9 following their first drive of the second half, but the Bills were able to respond thanks in large part to Dalton Kincaid . The star tight end caught a pass from Josh Allen and took off for a 54-yard gain. That helped them score their second touchdown of the game on a four-play, 62-yard drive.
BIG PLAY DALTON KINCAID BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LcQtgpdRSJ
Against the Minnesota Vikings, DJ Moore was rather quiet with just 25 yards on three receptions. He was much better against the Jets and even topped his yardage total from Week 9 with one reception in the third quarter.
Buffalo was up 17-12 and looking to put the Jets away when Allen fired a deep pass to Moore. The veteran wideout hauled it in and scored a touchdown on a 45-yard reception. Moore finished with 90 yards and a touchdown on four receptions, looking like the WR1 Buffalo knows he can be.
ALLEN TO DJ MOORE FOR 6 BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hfrUwKQlws
Other than an ugly second-half pick, this was another strong game from Josh Allen. The numbers weren't elite, as he had just 196 yards passing, but he made the plays when they were necessary. That includes three total touchdowns and a fourth-down conversion. Allen and the Buffalo offense are good enough that they can drop 31 points like this even when he's not throwing all over the field.
James Cook was special in this one. He continued to run tough throughout the game, and when he got in the open field, he was tough to bring down. His biggest gain was in the fourth quarter, when he broke free for a 74-yard touchdown to put the game away.

title: Former Bills Coach Sean McDermott Weighs in on Amani Hooker Addition
full_text:
Buffalo Bills general manager Brandon Beane made a bold move at the NFL trade deadline, bringing in safety Amani Hooker in a trade with the Tennessee Titans.
The move has been mostly met with positive praise as the Bills shored up one of their greatest weaknesses. Hooker gives them a true centerfield-type of safety, who enters Week 10 sharing the lead for the most interceptions with five.
One person who is a big fan of the move is former Buffalo head coach Sean McDermott. While appearing on The Rich Eisen Show , McDermott was asked for his take on the trade and said he was "all for it." He added that a team looking to contend for a Super Bowl has the responsibility to identify and correct any flaws, and he believes that's exactly what this trade did.
"Yeah, I'm all for it. You know, I've I've been all for it. You know, when you when your goal as a team, and this is true for any team, when your goal is to is to win a Super Bowl, ours was last year, certainly the Bills is this year, but any team that feels like they got a legitimate shot to win a Super Bowl, then you're tasked with the responsibility of identifying what could get in the way of you winning that Super Bowl," McDermott said.
"And then going out and finding those pieces, and so you saw Buffalo do that rather quickly in the start of this offseason, going to get the receiver (DJ Moore). And then, they did it again with some defensive pieces, and now going to get Hooker, I thought was a really good move. And if you're Joe Brady, or Jim Leonhard in this case, I'm sure you're extremely happy."
Shortly after being traded to Buffalo, Hooker made his intentions for this weekend clear. After being on a bye in Week 9 for the Titans, Hooker is ready to be back in action this weekend as the Bills take on the New York Jets.
“Oh I’m gonna play on Sunday. Yeah. I’ll be ready to go," Hooker said via the Bills official X page .
Hooker didn't see a full workload given the short time he had to learn the Buffalo defense, but he was certainly noticeable in the 31-12 road win over the Jets.

title: Saints Players, Coaches Complain About Penalty vs. Panthers, But They're Wrong
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers beat the New Orleans Saints on a walk-off field goal from Ryan Fitzgerald. The Panthers got into field-goal range thanks to a defensive pass interference call against Kool-Aid McKinstry. After that, they simply ran the ball to set up Fitzgerald to win it.
According to Mike Triplett, McKinstry was frustrated by what he called a "horrible, horrible" call. He also revealed that his teammates came up to him and just kept saying it was a "bad call" after the play.
Head coach Kellen Moore said, "Obviously, there’s disappointment when a call goes like that and now they’re in field goal range." He did admit that the Saints had plenty of calls go their way, but he was still upset about that one.
What is OPI https://t.co/u9V3deB1JD
Cam Jordan got online after the game, in which he recorded one tackle, and quote-tweeted the video with the caption "What is OPI," indicating that he believes this was a missed call.
Complaining about a consequential call is nothing new in the NFL. If ever there is a penalty that sets up a winning score, someone's going to comment about it. The coaches, players, and more usually do express their frustration.
But there seems to be some misunderstanding the Saints players and coaches have. For one thing, this is textbook defensive pass interference. Running into the receiver, preventing him from making a play on the pass, and not even looking at the football is pass interference.
Complain about the way the rule is written because it is a silly rule that often bails out underthrown passes, which this one from Bryce Young was. But it is the rule, and this was as clear-cut as it gets. McKinstry interfered with Jalen Coker.
But the bigger issue is that the Panthers were flagged for the same exact thing earlier, setting up New Orleans' go-ahead score. Corey Thornton did literally the exact same thing against Chris Olave near the goal-line.
He crashed into Olave before the ball got there and never remotely turned his head. It was rightly flagged (one of many valid penalties the Panthers committed ), and Moore wasn't outraged about the rule then. No one in New Orleans was.
The final ironic fact here is something Moore alluded to. The Saints got a ridiculous number of favorable calls from the replacement referees. For a full list, check out our coverage here . It's truly shocking.
Among many things, an incorrect horse-collar call set the Saints up to score (on the same drive as the Thornton DPI) and take the lead. A ridiculous, phantom facemask put the Saints basically in field-goal range to tie it with under a minute left.
The Panthers got hosed on numerous occasions, and the call against McKinstry was correct. Complaining about it only makes the Saints look bad, but it could provide more fuel for the rematch in Charlotte later this year.

Hubbard rushed for 92 yards on 27 attempts with two touchdowns and added 5 catches for 80 yards for a total of 172 yards from scrimmage. He was able to take a lot of pressure off of rookie quarterback Bryce Young as the Panthers relied on the ground game when the passing game was struggling.

title: Panthers Stock Up, Stock Down After Win Over Saints
full_text:
The Panthers picked up a big win Sunday as they defeated the Saints 20-17 in New Orleans. The win ended a three-game losing streak for Carolina and put the team in first place in the NFC South. It was a tough game for the Panthers, as they committed 17 penalties for 152 yards and struggled to pass the ball. Chuba Hubbard had a great game for Carolina, rushing for 92 yards and two touchdowns on 27 carries while also catching five passes for 80 yards. Ryan Fitzgerald made the game-winning field goal for the Panthers as time expired.
The bulk of Carolina's production came from running back Chuba Hubbard. He carried the ball 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught five passes for 80 yards. Hubbard totaled 172 yards from scrimmage on the day for Carolina.
Hubbard gave Carolina a boost when the offense needed it. His second touchdown put the Panthers ahead 17-14 in the fourth quarter after New Orleans had taken the lead.
Todd Wash was also very good, as New Orleans had only 49 rushing yards on the day. Carolina's defense had three sacks and one interception in the game. Even though New Orleans scored 17 points, Carolina's defense made several big stops to help the Panthers win.
Carolina's defense came up with some important stops against New Orleans. The unit also did a good job of limiting the Saints on the ground and putting pressure on their offense. Wash's defense was a major question entering the matchup.
Fitzgerald stepped up to make some crucial field goals in the game. He made a 55-yarder earlier in the game and then kicked the game-winning 54-yard field goal as time expired. Those two field goals accounted for six of the Panthers' 20 points on the day.
While Young did enough to get the win for the Panthers, it was not his best game. He went 17 of 30 for 200 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions. It is good that the Panthers did not have any turnovers, but Young is going to have to play better against the better teams Carolina will face in the coming weeks.
Young was also sacked three times. The Panthers' offense struggled to generate a passing game, and much of the production came from Hubbard. Carolina will need more from its quarterback as the season progresses. Young's performance against New Orleans showed both the positives and the areas that still need improvement.
Carolina had 17 penalties for 152 yards while New Orleans had only three for 46 yards. That kind of disparity in penalties gives the opposing team too many chances to win a game and makes it very hard to win close games.
The Panthers were able to overcome their mistakes in this game, but this is something the team needs to fix. Carolina cannot afford to give up so many yards on penalties in future games. This was a good win for the Panthers, but the penalty issues are still a concern.
The Panthers are in first place in the NFC South and will look to build on this win. Hubbard, Wash and Fitzgerald were the standouts, while Young and the rest of the team will look to improve their discipline on the field.

title: Panthers Surge in Power Rankings After Monumental Division Win Over Saints
full_text:
Try as they might, the Carolina Panthers did not lose their fourth straight game on Sunday. They committed several terrible and ill-timed penalties, and the referees aided that pursuit with some mind-boggling calls against the Panthers.
Despite that, they finally got off the schneid. They went into New Orleans, a house of horrors for them lately, and emerged with a clutch, walk-off victory that never remotely felt secure. It felt like a loss was coming, and they managed to snatch victory from the literal jaws of defeat.
With that, the Panthers broke their losing streak, remained in first place, and got moving back in the right direction in the NFL Power Rankings.
The NFL Power Rankings are totally meaningless, but they generally do reflect how the team is going. A big win usually means a big move up, so even if the placement feels wrong, the direction is the real takeaway.
Last week, the Panthers fell again after a soul-crushing defeat to the Denver Broncos . It was a trend; the Panthers had tumbled lower and lower for three straight weeks after, in the eyes of some, reaching top-10 status.
It's difficult to envision the Panthers ever getting back to that level, but a win is a win and moving in the right direction again, which they are, is key.
After last week , Sporting News' Vinnie Iyer ranked the Panthers 25th. After a big divisional win, they're soaring up to 20th. We can quibble about some teams ranked ahead (Dallas Cowboys, Las Vegas Raiders), but the important thing is they jumped five spots.
"The Panthers needed to beat the Saints in New Orleans to prove why they were expected to repeat in the weak NFC South. They found a new winning formula between much-improved defense under new coordinator Todd Wash and Chuba Hubbard producing 172 yards from scrimmage," Iyer wrote.
The Panthers could get on a roll next week. They host the Baltimore Ravens, who are without Lamar Jackson, next week, and that is a game they are actually favored in. They could get back to .500, remain in first place, and slide even higher.
The five-loss Panthers are probably better than their record or placement suggests. Injuries have ripped them to shreds more than almost any team in the NFL, and they've been jobbed by the referees on more than a few occasions .
But all that matters at the end of the day is that they're moving up and are in first place in the NFC South. For the first time in weeks, both statements are true.
