title: 6 Winners and 6 Losers from Panthers' Gutsy Victory Over Saints
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers were walk-off winners against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. It was a monumental win that felt truly in doubt late in the second half . They pulled it together, thanks to a few big performances and in spite of some others.
Devin Lloyd records his 3rd interception of the season. He becomes the first linebacker in the NFL since Wilber Marshall in 1988 to record 3+ interceptions in 3 of his first 5 seasons.
Devin Lloyd seems to often be where the ball is, and he was on Sunday. His early interception on a potential fourth-down conversion helped totally flip the momentum before the Saints looked like they were going to score. And shoutout to much-maligned Marco Wilson for deflecting it to Lloyd.
Ryan Fitzgerald is officially in a slump.
The magic Ryan Fitzgerald had last year has effectively run out. He's been bad on extra points, missed a few key field goals, and his kickoff woes keep coming up. It's not the strength it used to be, and it hurt the Panthers badly at times. Missing a field goal as well is simply inexcusable. But nailing two from beyond 50, including the stunning game-winner, was obviously clutch.
Jaelan Phillips with the fumble recovery. Was in the backfield, like he's been all game, and so was there for the scoop. Having a heck of a day: 1 TFL, 1 FR, 1 QBH. Feels like he'll get home for a sack at some point today.
It was immediately apparent how important Jaelan Phillips is to this defense. He made a TFL on the first play, and he had several pressures. His presence in the backfield led to a fumble recovery. He was maybe the most challenging Panthers defender for the Saints to handle on Sunday. And as Alex Zietlow predicted, Phillips did record a sack to end the first half and prompt boos from the crowd.
Good grief, Robert Hunt. Can't really bench him, given how much he's being paid, unfortunately.
So many times, the pocket was pushed back into Bryce Young's lap, and so many times, it was the fault of Robert Hunt. His rough season continued Sunday, as he struggled to hold up in pass protection versus the Saints' front.
How much more can we say about Chuba Hubbard ? The passing game took plenty of time to get anything going, but the Saints' defense had no answers for Hubbard all day. He was elite in the run game and very solid after the catch. He carried the Panthers to their game-winning drive literally by himself. If there were only two winners, it was Hubbard and Phillips on either side.
and now Darren Waller drops a perfect bucket touchdown
Two drops, including a would-be deep touchdown on a beautiful throw from Young, are bad. An offensive pass interference after a third-down conversion (admittedly a very weak call) is not good, either. Just an all-around struggle from Waller. The drop cost Young his touchdown streak, which had been the longest active in the NFL.
The Panthers looked like a different unit versus the run Sunday. They were filling gaps, making stops in the backfield, and getting push they haven't all year. It's the same players, though. Todd Wash has them better equipped to face the run, and they have responded incredibly well to the task.
Another week, another swathe of boneheaded penalties. They had eight in the first half, which is a step up from last week's outing. That has to change, and it comes down to coaching. Plus, Dave Canales' decision to challenge a spot call that was almost never going to be overturned on what ended up as a fourth-and-inches deep in his own territory was simply a waste, especially when he wanted to go for it on his own 27 anyway.
Kaye's Take: Chau Smith-Wade is having quite the day.
The coverage was pretty solid by everyone throughout, but Chau Smith-Wade had a number of consequential targets that amounted to nothing. He was very impressive against what had been a really solid passing attack for the Saints.
Brad Idzik's play-calling today has been horrific. I'm chalking it up to being relatively new to play-calling, but he has been a big reason why the #Panthers offense is not productive today. Very little quick game or RPO; still attempting 5- to 7-step dropbacks with…
Once again, the sequencing from Brad Idzik was not ideal. He couldn't get the offense into a rhythm and he also didn't rely on Chuba Hubbard as much as he should've. And it never felt like he was taking it to the defense, which had been a strength of his earlier this year.
What does Tracy Smith work on with his guys during practice? It's not kicking the ball in bounds. It's not how to line up on a kickoff. It's not how to return a punt without committing a bad penalty. All the fundamentals of special teams come back to bite the Panthers weekly, but especially on Sunday.

title: The Panthers Have a Serious Problem That Dave Canales Has to Fix or Else
full_text:
It wasn't without drama , but the Carolina Panthers finally got back in the win column. Carolina moves firmly into first place in the NFC South, improving to 4-5 on the season with a 20-17 win over the New Orleans Saints.
Carolina won the game on the backs of huge performances on both sides of the ball. The offense started and ended with Chuba Hubbard, as he had the best game of his career on Sunday. Against the Saints, Hubbard posted 172 scrimmage yards and scored both of Carolina's touchdowns.
On defense, Jaelan Phillips finally lived up to the  $120 million contract he signed with Carolina back in free agency. Returning from a hamstring injury, Phillips posted 5 tackles, 3 TFLs, 1 sack, and a fumble recovery.
While the Panthers didn't commit any turnovers, the game was sloppy, and the penalties piled up again on both sides of the ball, costing them big plays and making it much harder than it should have been.
Penalties have been an issue all season, with constant movement on the lines of scrimmage and the depleted secondary struggling to cover opposing receivers.
However, against the Saints, those issues were amplified. The Panthers set a franchise record, committing 17 accepted penalties for 152 yards,
If Carolina does that again, they have a 90% chance of losing that game. It's a miracle the Panthers walked out of the Superdome with a win despite such a lack of discipline.
Furthermore, the Panthers have committed 10+ turnovers in four games this season, and are 2-2 in those games. Carolina has been blown out twice this season; aside from the losses to the Bears and Buccaneers, they've hung around in other games, and timely penalties have proven to be costly.
This isn't to say Canales' job is currently on the line or anything, but severe amounts of penalties will only drag the Panthers trending down, even in a bad division like the NFC South.
Frankly, it's a miracle the Panthers are even 2-2 in games with 10+ penalties. Against the Saints, the penalties directly led to points; New Orleans' second touchdown drive featured four penalties for 42 yards.
The longer this continues, the more Carolina will lose, especially as the schedule that only gets tougher. In the next month, Carolina faces the Ravens, Buccaneers, Vikings, and Saints. Minnesota is the only juggernaut on that schedule, but all those games are just as loseable as they are winnable for Carolina.
Penalties against elite defenses like Tampa Bay's and Minnesota's will ensure not only a loss, but an embarrassing loss. If this doesn't get fixed and Carolina stays undisciplined, then uncomfortable conversations will start.

title: Panthers’ Massive Offseason Investment is Finally Arriving at the Right Time
full_text:
The drought is over ; the Carolina Panthers have finally won a game after what felt like an eternity. Carolina picks up a 20-17 division win over the New Orleans Saints on a walk-off field goal by Ryan Fitzgerald.
It was an ugly game, filled with penalties, questionable calls , and a lot of Chuba Hubbard. Hubbard posted a career-high in total yards, totaling 172 yards and scoring 2 touchdowns.
Hubbard is the MVP of the game, there's no denying that, but Carolina's defense played a complete game. The run  defense has been a weakness for Carolina this year; that wasn't the case against the Saints, allowing just 49 yards on the ground and 2.1 yards per carry.
Saints' QB Tyler Shough had a rough day, throwing for just 187 yards, 1 touchdown, 1 interception, and a lost fumble. Carolina also posted 3 sacks on Shough.
One player in particular was the highlight on defense, and did exactly what Carolina broght him on to do.
Jaelan Phillips returned to action today after not playing since Week 6 against the Philadelphia Eagles. In his return from a hamstring injury, he was the best player on defense, and was one of the two best players in this game.
Against the Saints, Phillips posted 5 total tackles, 3 TFLs, 1 sack, 2 QB hits, and a fumble recovery. According to SumerSports , Phillips also recorded 8 pressures, which is the most by a Carolina player since Patrick Jones II posted 8 in Week 5 of the 2025 season.
Not only was Phillips elite in affecting the QB, but he made multiple critical tackles against the run, not allowing New Orleans' offense to find a rhythm.
Phillips would've had a second sack, but it was called back for a horse-collar tackle. What stuck out on the screen was Phillips' first step, his bend around the edge, and just his pure strength, bull-rushing blockers towards Shough to close the pocket.
With a performance like his today, the investment Carolina made in Phillips looked more than worth it.
After the 2025 season, when the Panthers finished with the NFL's worst pass rush, it was clear that a premier pass rusher was the No. 1 hole to fill.
Carolina knew that, and filled that hole as soon as they could, making a splash signing on day one of free agency, signing Phillips.
Phillips was expected to re-sign with the Eagles, but Carolina swooped in with a four-year, $120 million deal that was impossible to turn down. With that said, a high price tag comes with high expectations, and on Sunday against the Saints, Phillips met those expectations.
Moving forward, the best-case scenario for Carolina is that Sunday's performance is a tone setter, and Phillips brings a major impact for the rest of the season.

title: Bryce Young Report Card: Panthers QB Does Enough to Secure Win Over Saints

Young had a few good moments, but he was also sacked three times and struggled to find consistency. Against a divisional opponent with first place in the NFC South on the line, protecting the football was important. However, the Panthers will need more production from their quarterback moving forward.

Chuba Hubbard helped take some of that pressure off Young. He ran 27 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns while adding 80 receiving yards on five catches. His production gave Carolina a reliable option on the ground and helped keep the offense moving despite its struggles in the passing game.

It was an important road win for Carolina, but Young's performance left some questions about the passing offense. His 200 yards and lack of touchdowns won't be enough against some of the better teams in the league. The Panthers will need more production from their quarterback as the schedule gets harder.

title: This Pet Ben Johnson Look for Bears Offense Keeps Coming Up Short
full_text:
While the Bears have struggled running the ball in the last five games during Kyle Monangai's absence, they've also experienced another loss.
This was the injury to veteran tight end Cole Kmet.
Kmet's experience and leadership are huge and another thing he did was quickly accept and adapt to his function within the offense. This took him from the featured tight end to a secondary figure as Colston Loveland became the tight end target du jour.
The Bears have had two games to try to adapt to having Sam Roush playing the Kmet role and Stephen Carlson playing the third tight end role formerly filled by Roush. They haven't done terrible in terms of run blocking if you accept Pro Football Focus grades as legitimate. The tight end run blocking has been graded slightly lower the last two games but they were facing two difficult rush defenses in Seattle and Tampa Bay.
Caleb to Colston. Big gain. 💪 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/5kQOveTpTI
They've probably done better as pass catchers than they have at blocking the run because Roush has two receptions for 23 yards in two games without Kmet and starter Colston Loveland has 11 for 119 yards. Between them, they've averaged 6.5 receptions and 71.5 yards in the two games.
This is good pass production for tight ends. In fact, in the first seven games with Kmet, they averaged 5.6 receptions for 52 yards from all of their tight ends including Roush. The main part of the increase has been Loveland kicking up his receiving to a higher level. He has come on strong through the current four-game winning streak.
Trey McBride, Year 2 (Age 24) - 8.3 fantasy points (8.3 expected) - 6.2 targets - 48.5 yards Colston Loveland, Year 2 (Age 22), in the 5 full Caleb Williams games: - 9.5 fantasy points (10.7 expected) - 7.2 targets - 50.6 yards
It would seem they're picking up the slack without Kmet, especially considering the two defenses were so strong.
"I wouldn't even say picking up," Loveland said. "I mean, it obviously still hurts and not having Cole out there is one thing, but I think we've done a great job and Sam and Steve have really done a great job in kind of mastering their role.
"And we all got a lot more to get better at for sure, but I think we've been doing pretty well."
Top 10 Tight Ends so far this season: 1. Brock Bowers 2. Trey McBride 3. George Kittle 4. Dalton Kincaid 5. Colston Loveland 6. Dalton Schultz 7. Brenton Strange 8. Isaiah Likely 9. Kyle Pitts 10. Darnell Washington HM: Jake Ferguson
Yet, it seems the Bears are not quite getting the type of overall production they need from a specific use of tight ends.
So much has been made of Johnson's belief in the EPA (expected points added) analytic as an indicator of offensive success, and one area the Bears offense hasn't achieved much success there involves their tight ends.
According to SumerSports Analysis, the Bears have not exactly smashed the record books with their production in 12-personnel and 13-personnel packages. That's two tight ends and three tight ends.
This shimmy by Colston Loveland at the top of his route helps him create this window for Williams to throw it to him, sick player pic.twitter.com/AwLDIvkvJx
When the Bears are in 13-personnel, the three-tight end grouping, they rank 30th overall in EPA and are 22nd in rushing EPA and 22nd in passing EPA. And they're in this 17.7% of the time, or the fourth most of any team.
Also, when they are in two-tight end or 12-personnel — which is the third-most in the NFL at 32.13% — they are only 24th in EPA, 13th in the passing game and a disappointing 29th running the ball.
Essentially, when they are in two- and three-tight end packages their running game has struggled. They're in those multiple tight end packages almost half the time (49.8%).
Bears trotting out 13 personnel, but split all 3 TEs out in a bunch formation to run a screen to Colston Loveland. pic.twitter.com/wpixlNwEjQ
However, when the Bears are in the basic three-receiver set with one running back and one tight end, they are second in the NFL in rushing EPA, 10th in passing EPA and seventh in overall EPA.
This isn't just an outgrowth of losing Kmet or losing Monangai as a runner for five weeks. The Bears were much better running in their one-tight end look throughout October, as well.
When Johnson did his self-scout over the break, hopefully it told him something they can do to be more effective when they go to multiple tight end packages. Before the break, he mentioned something about using extra offensive linemen at times. Maybe they'd better do it.
Considering how effective they've been when they don't use it and how ineffective they are when they do use it, maybe they just better stick with the three-receiver and four-receiver looks.
It can't make it any easier to operate in those looks when they don't have Kmet.
Ben Johnson loves using multiple tight ends, with the Bears running 12 or 13 personnel on an NFL-high 51.9% of plays, but Chicago has actually been more effective out of 11 personnel (3 WRs). 11 personnel: • 6.8 yards per dropback (7th-most) • 5.3 yards per carry (3rd-most) •… pic.twitter.com/4LULb8scaQ

title: Kyle Monangai Injury Update From Practice Signals Bears RB Will Play in Week 11
full_text:
The Chicago Bears were on the practice field on Monday for their first session since coming back from the bye week and running back Kyle Monangai was out there.
Of course, the Bears running back has missed the last five games with a turf toe injury, but he did show a sign of progress on the Friday before the Tampa Bay Buccaneers game when he participated in practice on a limited basis .
However, Monangai was ultimately ruled out , so there was still no guarantee he would return after the bye in Week 11.
On Monday, we got a very good indication Monangai will indeed make his long-awaited return against the New Orleans Saints.
The Bears were on the practice field on Monday because that's typical for teams coming out of a bye week. That said, the Bears don't have to put out their first official official injury report until Wednesday, so we don't have Monangai's exact level of participation.
But, according to video from CHGO Bears, not only was Monangai on the practice field, he appeared to be much more active than he was in his return to practice on Nov. 6.
KYLE MONANGAI IS BACK!!! 😤 pic.twitter.com/AKHmPJyvWT
Monangai looks to be moving very well, so that's a good indication that he's further along, which is to be expected after he had an additional week to get right thanks to the bye.
This isn't much of a surprise, though, as the belief was the limited he turned in before the bye was a clear sign Monangai had a good chance to return in Week 11.
Then, there was also the report from NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , who said on Nov. 8 that the expectation was Monangai would return after the Bears' week off.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) won't play today, but he's expected back in Week 11. Fresh legs for Chicago," he said.
According to Adam Hoge of CHGO Bears , Monangai spoke to reporters after practice and touched on his injury.
Monangai said he expects to return in Week 11 against the New Orleans Saints, but he also noted his injury is something he is going to have to continue to manage.
"We just talked with Kyle Monangai. Initially he didn’t even realize anything was wrong with his foot. Frustrated the turf toe kept him out this long. Will still be something he needs to manage, but he should return Sunday against the Saints," Hoge relayed.
We will obviously be monitoring the injury reports all week, but for now, based on the video out of practice and Monangai's own comments, we expect the Bears running back to play.

title: How Week 10 Injuries to Bears' Biggest Rivals Impact Their Playoff Hunt
full_text:
Week 10 was a mixed bag for the Chicago Bears during their bye. While the results in the NFC North moved Chicago down the standings to third place in the division, the Bears' main rivals were rocked by injuries to key stars for the season's stretch run.
The Detroit Lions had the most devastating injury, losing EDGE Aidan Hutchinson to a season-ending knee injury. Detroit's pass rush is completely transformed and will need herculean efforts from rookie Derrick Moore and offseason signing D.J. Wonnum to maintain a pass rush that was top-five in sacks and top-12 in win rate.
Meanwhile, newly acquired and reunited quarterback Kirk Cousins is down a weapon in the Minnesota Vikings' offense with Jordan Addison's recent thumb surgery . Addison suffered the injury in practice before missing the Vikings' 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. With Justin Jefferson and T.J. Hockenson typically reliable in the passing game this season, Kevin O'Connell and Co. may have enough ammunition to make it through. Still, Hockenson has been injury-prone himself and Jefferson doesn't have the cleanest bill of health this year.
With two games left against the Lions to end the season, and one more matchup with Minnesota, these are significant breaks for Chicago.
Injuries don't guarantee outcomes, of course, but it makes Ben Johnson and Dennis Allen's jobs easier over the next few weeks.
One look at the Bears' rest of the season schedule is enough to feel relieved about not facing one of the most fearsome edge rushers or outside receivers in the country. It's a tough slate besides the New Orleans Saints and Miami Dolphins.
The Packers are getting healthy again , though with the Matt LaFleur-is-the-head-coach caveat, of course, while the Buffalo Bills and Jacksonville Jaguars are legitimate threats from the AFC.
Chicago has already faced the weakest portion of the schedule, but a brutal division-heavy stretch is more palatable.
The Bears can't rely on outside help to make the road easier for them forever. For now, though, with fingers crossed that Chicago's own roster doesn't see as much bad luck as it had before the bye week, things will be a little easier as the temperature crashes down to freezing.
"Bear Weather" is more of a myth than an advantage, but the Bears' rivals' respective injury reports are tangible advantages down the stretch.

title: Luther Burden Back on Bears Practice Field Following Concussion
full_text:
Wide receiver Luther Burden III was on the field for warmups and individual work before Bears practice on Monday, although it's definitely not an indication he is fine to go for this weekend's game with New Orleans.
Burden's concussion status is entirely unclear even if he was on the field for the beginning of the practice. More is likely to be known Tuesday.
Coach Ben Johnson had indicated Burden suffered a concussion after the Nov. 2 game with Tampa Bay, but no confirmation through an injury report has been given about the second-year receiver even entering into the concussion protocol. There has been none saying he is out of concussion protocol, as a result.
The Bears didn't have injury reports last week because they had a bye and won't have an injury report until Wednesday. Johnson did not talk to reporters on Monday as the team returned for a light practice after being away for their bye week. They'll have a full practice on Tuesday and Johnson addresses the media then.
Luther Burden current stat projections: 93 Receptions 128 Targets 1216 Yards 8 TDS Can’t believe the league let Ben Johnson get this demon 😭😭✌️ pic.twitter.com/3fwtvHjqkQ
Still, the situation can't be interpreted as a negative after Burden was knocked out of the game with Tampa Bay on a hit near the sidelines.
With 49 catches and 644 yards so far, Burden has two more receptions and just 8 fewer yards than he had all last season. His four touchdowns are twice what he had last year.  The Bears need him as a key receiving threat for yards after the catch heading into the season's second half.
There is no WR better after the catch than Luther Burden. No one. No one is even close. Luther, then everybody else! pic.twitter.com/m48IYqKwUD
Running back Kyle Monangai also was on the field Monday, the second straight practice he has participated in after suffering toe and finger injuries in Week 4. Monangai practiced on a limited basis on the Friday before the Bears' 27-24 win over Tampa Bay.  Monangai has been out since Week 4, but two straight practices should be a good indicator of his status coming into Sunday's game with New Orleans.
Monangai gained 146 of his 324 rushing yards in his last game, against the Jets. He also scored two touchdowns in the game.
That first Kyle Monangai 8 yard run where he lowers his shoulder and runs a guy over is going to hit like crack next week
The window for defensive end Dayo Odeyingbo's return can open this week, after he suffered a quad injury and went on injured reserve Oct. 17. A return by Odeyingbo this week would result in someone being cut from the 53-man roster.
Generally, the Bears were expected to be back to 100% this week after the bye, and this first glimpse as they start preparations to host New Orleans on Sunday says it's still possible.

title: Bears' Strength of Schedule For Remaining Games Confirms Brutally Tough Path to Playoffs
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have looked like one of the best teams in the NFL this season and it feels like a foregone conclusion that the playoffs are in their future.
The Bears are sitting with a 7-2 record, which is only good enough for third place in the NFC North right now because of tie-breakers that aren't set in stone yet.
Chicago is also in the No. 6 seed in the playoff hunt and a full two games in the loss column ahead of the Green Bay Packers, who currently own the No. 7 seed at 6-4 going into Week 11.
But the Los Angeles Rams and Seattle Seahawks are right there at 6-4, also, so there isn't much room for error for any of the NFC North squads.
While the Bears' current positioning is all well and good, Chicago's road to the playoffs will not be an easy one.
According to Tankathon , the combined win percentage of the Bears' remaining opponents is .630. That is the highest in the league, which means the Bears have the toughest remaining schedule.
Taking it a step further, no other team in the NFL has a remaining strength of schedule above .600.
Here's the Bears' list of remaining opponents , along with their current records:
Week 11: vs. New Orleans Saints (3-6) Week 12: at Detroit Lions (7-2) Week 13: vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) Week 14: at Miami Dolphins (1-8) Week 15: at Buffalo Bills (8-1) Week 16: vs. Green Bay Packers (6-4) Week 17: vs. Detroit Lions (7-2) Week 18: at Minnesota Vikings (7-2)
The easiest out on that schedule is obviously the Miami Dolphins, who are one of the worst teams in the NFL. The next easiest out is the New Orleans Saints, who haven't had the breakout season many expected but are still dangerous.
Other than that, it's a brutal slate for the Bears, who will play a total of six teams with winning records, and all of those teams should make the playoffs.
Two of those teams, the Packers and Vikings, have already beaten the Bears this season, although there are caveats to those losses. The Vikings game was on a day in which there was inclement weather conditions and Chicago didn't have Caleb Williams available for the loss to the Packers.
But the Vikings are also an improved team since the last time they met the Bears after Minnesota traded for a much-needed upgrade at quarterback in Kirk Cousins.
The Bears are also better since they faced both the Packers and Vikings after the addition of Jeffery Simmons, though, so there's that.
If there's any team in the NFL that can successfully navigate this upcoming stretch of games, it's the Bears, who, again, have looked like an elite team this season thanks to top-notch play on both sides of the football.
We're going to find out a lot about what the Bears are really made of over these next eight weeks and if the the Super Bowl contender label is accurate.
One thing we can say for certain is that Chicago will be battle-tested.

title: Where the Chicago Bears Stand After Self-Scout as Second Half Begins
full_text:
The Bears begin preparations for the Saints following their bye week and time allowed for a self-scout. They know they stand on solid ground in most areas statistically but have slipped in some of their strengths while some of they've shored up some of their weaknesses, particularly on defense after the trade for Jeffery Simmons. Injuries played huge roles in where they stand statistically. For instance, Caleb Williams' TD pass total of eight is low but three missed games is a problem. The Bear started the year with a game for their ages, a 59-point effort in a 22-point win over Carolina. It had coach Ben Johnson saying he wanted to see his offense set records for scoring.
After eight more games, the usual NFL attrition and an unyielding NFC North, Johnson's team has to be more concerned with scoring and committing fewer turnovers than it does with setting records.
The best play call of Week 9 goes to @ChicagoBears HC Ben Johnson! @thefilmwatcher_ breaks down the All-22 ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/gKOSIw1Gg3
The Bears went from the NFL's best turnover differential at plus-22 to the fourth worst at minus-4. Yet they have a 7-2 record because they continue to be both explosive and efficient enough on offense to maintain the league's best time of possession at 34:31. They're a full 2:04 ahead of the second-place Giants and the combination of fifth most explosive plays with a TOP lead is difficult to beat. Now comes the Simmons factor. A defense struggling against the run has begun asserting itself with a new force against the run and pass. Combining this with Dennis Allen's defensive scheme can take them to even greater heights. Here's where the Bear stand as they come out of their one-week hibernation and tackle their remaining schedule.
Scenes when Kyle Monangai comes back and puts together the greatest RB season in NFL history pic.twitter.com/I6JQD9Jpth https://t.co/XXVmnKdGG2
The Bears are trending the wrong way at rushing, although the reason is obvious. They haven't had Kyle Monangai and D'Andre Swift is overworked. They've slipped from the top of the league in rushing to fourth 142.0 yards per game. The Bucs (163.9), Bills (152.7) and 49ers (144.0) all have climbed past them after they started the first quarter of the season rolling. Swift's 3.7-yard average shows how they're getting fewer explosive runs and the room to run supplied by their offensive line has closed. They're averaging only 2.5 yards before contact, 20th in the league. Last year they led the NFL at 3.1 yards before contact. Is the blocking difference a new center, stability issues at left tackle, or just teams knowing how to defend their use of the wide zone and gap schemes? Like with everything, it's probably a combination. Monangai's expected return this week could be a godsend but if the blocking is not there then he'll experience as much trouble as Swift. The number say Monangai will have a huge impact if healthy. He is third in the NFL in yards per carry at 5.4, trailing only Jaylen Warren (5.7) and Kenneth Walker III (5.5), but had only 60 carries in the first four games before his injury. The Bears were No. 1 in rushing when he went out.
This to me is the next step for Caleb. The Bears need more explosive plays. I’d love him to see the deeper part of the field better and take more shots pic.twitter.com/92pc6Mf5Tk
Despite the anomaly supplied by the last game, the Bears remain one of the league's most effective passing teams. Caleb Williams is still third in completion percentage (68.7%), eighth in yards per attempt (7.9). His passer rating took a hit with the four-interception game but he's still top half of the league in 14th at 95.4.  Williams' interception total is too high and his TD total too low, but missing three games with a hamstring injury holds down his totals. A 49.3% success rate on passes is eighth in the league and this says he's getting the job done. Per analytics, his EPA per dropback took a huge dip with the interceptions but he remains in the top half of the league among starters at 14th. Williams' eight TD passes and 10 by the team as a whole needs to be much higher. The number is 22nd in the NFL. The most important thing with Williams' play is they're unbeaten (5-0) in games he started and finished. Their receivers started the season rolling near the league lead in yards after catch and YAC/route run, and they're fifth in YAC but have slipped to 11th YAC/route run at 5.7. Ranking high in YAC was always a trademark of Johnson's offense in Detroit and last year the Bears improved at it but still need to be better. Bears receivers are not producing at the rate of last year in yards per route run, but they're slightly better at avoiding dropped passes. That was a major goal for Johnson with this group. They have 13 drops after they had 29 for all of 2025. It's still tied for the 10th most after they had the fifth most last year. Individually, Rome Odunze is ninth in the NFL in yards per reception at 16.5 and 20th in yards per target at 10.4. Luther Burden III has dipped somewhat in his yards per route run but is 16th in the NFL in receiving yards at a team-high 644. After only 13 receptions in the first five games, Colston Loveland has kicked into gear with six per game over the last four and 250 total yards. They have balance among receivers just like last year, as five players have at least 24 receptions. The Bears could use more explosive plays per game, according to Johnson. That's runs of 10 or more yards and completions of 20 or more. They still rank fifth at this at 6.8 big plays per game. The Bills, 49ers, Lions and Chiefs are better at this.
Offensive and defensive explosive play rates: Chicago's defense has been improving, but they're still giving up a lot of explosive plays pic.twitter.com/1UqI1R3hvA
A major weakness prior to and even early in the season, this has begun to shift. It helped having five straight games with 81 yards allowed on the ground or less. Early on, time of possession seemed to save their defense. Teams were effective running but eventually quit running on them because they couldn't keep up with a Bears offense that outscored opponents 76-17 in first quarters in the first nine games.
The NFC North & NFC West Playoff Race with 8 Weeks Remaining pic.twitter.com/xietx29RrW
Now the yards per rush have dropped from near 5.0 to 4.4. Overall they're seventh stopping the run even as their yards per rush needs to come down from 25th at 4.4. The key is they not only are No. 1 in rushing but opponents have the fewest rushing attempts against them. Devin Bush and a healthier T.J. Edwards are factors here and they've allowed 4.4 per rush since Simmons came to the team. Getting Dayo Odeyingbo back can't hurt, as one of his strengths is setting an edge.
They experienced what should have been expected with so much change in their secondary, and with the lack of a consistent interior pass rush without blizing before Simmons' arrival. The interception total fell off from last year, as many predicted, but the Bears defended passes better on third downs. Defenses struck for the big plays on occasion, but couldn't sustain drives against the best third-down defense in the NFL. Their conversion rate allowed of 22.83% is by far the league's best, with the Rams second at 30%.
"The Bears and the Vikings look like the two teams at the top of the division that are less vulnerable than the other two." @DavidHaugh weighs in on the NFC North race after Week 10. pic.twitter.com/9CI8F2SNun
This was already good before Simmons. Since he arrived they are allowing 13% conversions. With the rushing defense improving, it's easy to see teams even more desperate on third down and doing even worse against them. How were the Bears going to ever make up for an expected drop in takeaway rate? They simply take it back with three-and-outs by stopping third downs. This said, they still need to be better preventing big plays because they're 24th in net yards allowed per…

title: Will Luther Burden Play in Week 11? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears WR
full_text:
UPDATE: Great news from Bears practice on Monday, as Luther Burden was participating, according to video from CHGO Bears , which puts him on track to play on Sunday. The Bears don't have to put out an injury report until Wednesday, so we'll know more then.
The Chicago Bears have an injury concern with wide receiver Luther Burden ahead of their Week 11 game against the New Orleans Saints.
The Bears notched a razor-thin 27-24 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9 before the bye, but late in the game we saw Burden take a big hit to his head that resulted in a concussion and his early exit from the contest.
It looked to be a bad consussion, too, as Burden was clearly shaken-up before exiting the field.
Here's the latest on Burden and our expectations for him ahead of the Week 11 game versus New Orleans.
As previously noted, Burden is in the concussion protocol , head coach Ben Johnson announced after the win over Tampa Bay.
"Ben Johnson says Luther Burden had a concussion," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond wrote.
We've seen players return from a concussion the following week, but we've also seen players miss one or more games depending on the severity, so it's possible Burden could sit out in Week 11.
We would say Burden has a better chance to play than not. Let's say 75/25 in favor of him playing.
That's because Burden had an extra week to get right before the Bears' game this week thanks to the bye in Week 10.
It isn't clear if Burden made any progress through the concussion protocol in that time, but the week off at least gives him a better chance to not miss a game than he otherwise would have had if the Bears had played last week.
Entering the season, Rome Odunze was viewed as the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver, but he was anything but cemented in that role since Odunze had yet to fully prove himself.
Well, after nine games, Burden has clearly taken the mantle of the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver. Not only has he been more consistent, Burden is also leading the team in receiving yards with 644 to Odunze's 528. Burden also leads the team in receiving touchdowns with four.
Burden's impressive showing comes after an offseason in which both Johnson and general manager Ryan Poles raved about the second-year wideout .
There's no doubt the Bears' offense will take a hit if Burden does not play. If he does get ruled out, the Bears will need more from Odunze, tight end Colston Loveland and fellow wideouts Kalif Raymond, Jahdae Walker and Zavion Thomas.

title: Will Kyle Monangai Return in Week 11? Latest Injury Update on Chicago Bears RB
full_text:
UPDATE: According to video from CHGO Bears , Monangai was at practice and looked doing more than he did the week before the bye, which puts Monangai on track to return in Week 11, as we expected. The Bears' first injury report will drop Friday.
It has been five whole games since the last time Chicago Bears running back Kyle Monangai took the field.
That was in Week 4, when Monangai ran all over the New York Jets en route to 146 yards and a 23-12 Bears victory .
Unfortunately for Monangai and the Bears, he also came down with a turf toe injury that led to him missing a handful of games, which was surprising because he wasn't expected to miss more than three after the team didn't place him on injured reserve.
Now, as we turn the page to Week 11, here's what we know about Monangai's chances of returning to the field.
The last we heard of Monangai was on the Friday before the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 9.
That was a huge day for Monangai and the Bears, as the second-year back turned in a limited practice , which was his first practice participation since his injury.
Monangai even drew the questionable tag before being ruled out for his fifth straight game.
There are no guarantees with Monangai at this point, but the fact that he was able to practice on a limited basis right before the bye suggests he has a good chance to return in Week 11.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai (toe) practiced today for the first time since his injury during a 146-yard game vs. the Jets on Oct. 4," The Chicago Tribune's Brad Biggs said. "It's a positive sign for a potential return on the other side of the bye week."
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport even went as far as to say that the Bears running back is expected to be back this week.
"Bears RB Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) won't play today, but he's expected back in Week 11. Fresh legs for Chicago," Rapoport reported.
So, all signs are pointing to Monangai indeed making his return to the field for the game against the New Orleans Saints .
The Bears' rushing attack managed to maintain its elite status during Monangai's absence, as Chicago still ranks fourth in rushing yards per game.
However, it has still been tough sledding for D'Andre Swift, who is averaging just 3.7 yards per carry this season.
Adding to that, the Bears don't have the kind of runner Monangai is in either of the players who replaced him during his absence, Roschon Johnson and Salvon Ahmed.
Before his injury, Monangai was easily the Bears' best running back and the numbers show that.
He is averaging 5.4 yards per carry, the most among Chicago's running backs, and he only trails Swift by 252 yards despite playing in five fewer games.
The Bears' offense is already playing at a high level, but things should be even better once Monangai is back in the mix.

title: Bears Could Reunite With Former Draft Pick After Steelers Cut Ties
full_text:
Ahead of the NFL trade deadline, there were multiple reports about the Chicago Bears looking around for cornerback help .
It's not hard to see why that was the case, as Chicago could use more depth at the position amid struggles from Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson, and now the latter is dealing with a new injury he suffered in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Ultimately, the Bears didn't come away with a cornerback before the deadline, but that doesn't mean they won't continue to explore their options — and there just so happens to be a player available the team is quite familiar with.
Over the weekend, the Pittsburgh Steeleres decided to waive cornerback Terell Smith, the Bears' former fifth-round pick in 2023.
Smith appeared in one game for the Steelers but played only on special teams. According to Nick Farabaugh of Penn Live , the Steelers waived Smith after getting healthy in the secondary.
"When the Steelers signed Smith, they were dealing with injuries in the room and had just traded Joey Porter Jr.," he explained. "Now, the room remains healthy and the return of Doneiko Slaughter and Brandin Echols means those two players will take over the special teams role that initially belonged to Smith when he was signed to the Steelers’ roster."
Prior to his stint with the Steelers, Smith was on the Washington Commanders' practice squad but never got into a game for the NFC East squad.
The Bears cut Smith before cutdown day in August and the move came after the addition of Clark Phillips, who was acquired in the Gervon Dexter trade with the Atlanta Falcons.
Smith showed some promise as a depth cornerback over his first two years in the NFL, but a significant knee injury in 2025 forced him to miss the entire season and derailed him.
In his two seasons with Chicago, Smith posted completion rates allowed of 63% and 66.7%, and passer ratings of 93.9 and 72.7.
Certainly not great, but those numbers are actually better than those of both Johnson and Stevenson, and they are at least sufficient to be a quality backup.
Smith also offers some versatility after seeing snaps in the slot, on the boundary and even as a box safety over his 26 career games.
The Minnesota product offers special teams value, too, with 244 snaps in that area during his career.
A Smith signing remains a possibility regardless of what happens with Stevenson's injury, but if the veteran cornerback misses an extended period of time, it becomes more possible.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Why Chicago Bears Fans Must Become 49ers Fans Down the Stretch
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are now in third place in the NFC North , despite a 7-2 start through the bye week. Ben Johnson and Co. can't be upset at the season's first two and a half months of results, but the NFC playoff picture is already shaping up to be crowded.
The division itself is going to start eating its own, but the Bears, Detroit Lions, Minnesota Vikings, and Green Bay Packers could all make runs for the postseason .
That goal gets easier for all of them if the NFC West continues to see its leader rule the roost down the stretch.
In particular, Chicago and the rest of the NFC North need the San Francisco 49ers to continue nabbing big division wins in the final two months of the season.
For the Niners, it's about keeping up their torrid pace.
San Francisco has been rocked by injuries all year, but quarterback Brock Purdy has guided them through with an MVP-caliber season. Purdy has 2,369 yards and 20 passing touchdowns, on 8.97 yards per attempt, and a 115.2 passer rating through nine games in 2026. He was brilliant in a 46-40 win over the Dallas Cowboys in America's Game of the Week.
The Bears need more of that down the stretch given the schedule in front of Kyle Shanahan's squad.
San Francisco has the Vikings next weekend in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football, plus matchups with the six-win Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams. Both of those NFC West teams picked up big wins on Sunday, against the Las Vegas Raiders and Cardinals, respectively, to climb back into the postseason conversation.
What helps is that the Rams and Seahawks have both matchups against each other remaining. On some level, those two will hurt the other one's cause.
Still, this all gets easier if the Niners could rule the NFC West with an iron fist down the stretch. It's not a particularly difficult stretch otherwise with many postseason implications for San Francisco; the New York Giants look like a soft NFC East lock, the Los Angeles Chargers are winless and already irrelevant, the Kansas City Chiefs are in the AFC, and the Philadelphia Eagles and Arizona Cardinals are also practically out of the playoff race already.
There are only so many Wild Card spots if Chicago can't win the NFC North, so it's best that rising contenders in the NFC West are subdued.
The 49ers have the key to suppressing the Seahawks and Rams and making the Bears' lives easier down the stretch. A win next Sunday night against Kirk Cousins and Minnesota wouldn't hurt either.

title: Cris Collinsworth Compares Bengals’ Passing Attack to 2007 Patriots
full_text:
Cris Collinsworth is comparing the Cincinnati Bengals' recent passing surge to some of the most memorable offenses in NFL history.
The NBC analyst on the call during Cincinnati's 38-18 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday Night Football pointed to Tom Brady and Randy Moss' 2007 Patriots and the Rams' Greatest Show on Turf when discussing the Bengals' offense.
Cris' son, Jac Collinsworth, also praised Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins, citing Burrow's league-leading PFF grade and describing both receivers as playing at a top-five level across the league.
“One of the hottest passing months I've ever seen," Cris Collinsworth said. "Not just from a Bengals team. You start going back to what Tom Brady and Randy Moss did in '07, the Greatest Show on Turf. I mean, they really have been that dynamic here with some spectacular plays."
Cincinnati has won four straight games, scoring at least 31 points in each win. During that stretch, Buurrow has completed 77.0% of his passes for 1,215 yards and 16 touchdowns, with only three interceptions.
PFF's QB rankings confirm what Jac Collinsworth said about Burrow being the highest-graded player (95.2) at his position. Lamar Jackson (91.3) and Drew Lock (90.8) are the only two QBs with grades over 90, though neither has played in every game this season.
Jac also cited Burrow's 18 big-time throws before praising the receivers he throws to every game.
“Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase both playing like top-five receivers in the league,” Jac said.
Both receivers delivered in Cincinnati's Spain win, a 34-17 victory over the Atlanta Falcons in Madrid. Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown, including a memorable 47-yard score in the first half. Higgins added five catches for 32 yards and two touchdowns.
The Bengals and Steelers both entered Sunday night's matchup at 6-2, with first place in the AFC North on the line. Pittsburgh won the first meeting, 30-27 and took it on the chin under the White-Bengal lights
It marked the first time the Bengals played on Sunday night since Nov. 17, 2024.

title: 'Please Blitz Us' - Bengals Lured Steelers Into Trap and Game Was Over Before They Could Pivot
full_text:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin had a well-circulated quote last week where he said if you don’t get pressure on Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow with a four-man rush, it’s like trying to run on the beach.
As the Steelers found out Sunday night, if you don’t get pressure on Burrow when you’re blitzing, you’re running into a firing squad.
Pittsburgh blitzed Burrow on 12 dropbacks and repeatedly paid the price in the Bengals’ 38-18 triumph Sunday night.
Linebacker Patrick Queen recorded the team’s lone sack on one of the 12 blitzes.
Burrow was 11 of 11 for 181 yards, averaging a gaudy 16.5 yards per attempt.
“Every time they blitz us, it’s a big-play opportunity for us,” Bengals offensive coordinator Dan Pitcher said. “There is not an ounce of us that feels like, ‘Oh no, here comes the blitz.’ It's, ‘please blitz us.’”
“Because we have just supreme confidence in in our guys’ ability to protect it,” he added. “And then you guys can see what our skill guys and our quarterback can do.”
Last night against the Steelers, Burrow was a perfect 11 of 11 when blitzed for 181 yards and 16.5 yards per attempt. https://t.co/cWM8INg1fa pic.twitter.com/UgnL6JT5dF
Five of Burrow's 11 completions agaisnt the blitz went to Ja'Marr Chase for 126 yards. Chase had anothe rsix receptions for 105 yards when Pittsburgh didn't blitz.
In the last three games, Burrow is 30 of 33 for 391 yards with five touchdowns and one interception.
And the protection Pitcher referenced is a big part of that.
Burrow took just three hits Sunday night, a season low. The last time he got hit fewer than that was Week 4 of 2024 at Carolina, when the Panthers recorded just two.
In two games against the Steelers this season, Burrow has dropped back 81 times and has only been sacked twice with nine hits.
“I thought the protection was outstanding, and that certainly starts up front with five linemen,” Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said before also praising running backs Chase Brown and Samaje Perine as well as the tight ends.
“I thought Joe played really fast,” Taylor added. “And so there was times where he got the ball out of his hands quickly to maybe a quick outlet or an underneath throw instead of waiting on a big chuck, which is fine. That’s a frustrating way for a defense to play.”
Pittsburgh frustration and Cincinnati’s success led the Steelers to abandon the plan. Nine of their 12 blitzes came in the first half, and two more came on the Bengals’ opening drive of the season half.
After that, it felt pointless with the Bengals holding a 31-3 lead.
“Those guys make it hard to prepare because they do so many things (on) defense, and we handled it really well,” Burrow said.
The Pittsburgh defensive players and coaches are likely saying the same about Burrow and the Bengals after being forced to deviate from their original plan in a humbling loss.
“It's like anything you, you put together a game plan and you're gonna start the game with the things you think are gonna help you win,” Pitcher said. “We've been on the other side of that coin when it doesn't work out the way that you hoped early on.
“That's disconcerting, and then you have to evaluate and adjust and decide whether to just stay the course or whether to make some changes,” he added. “So yeah, I think the way we handled it early in the football game was a big part of our success.”
The book on Burrow always has been not to blitz him.
But with how well the Cincinnati offensive line is protecting, opposing defensive coordinators feel as though they have no choice because they’re left running on the beach trying to get home with just a four-man rush.
Burrow has been blitzed at a rate of 10.2 times per pass attempt this season, which is eight most in the league among qualifying quarterbacks.
Last year, Burrow faced blitzes on 6.5 pass attempts per game, the 31st lowest rate in the league.
In 2023, it was 7.6 attempts per game, which ranked 24th fewest.
Pitcher’s plea for teams to blitz the Bengals is coming true, and Burrow is composing an MVP-worthy season through nine games.
Next up are the Washington Commanders, whose defense has the fourth-highest blitz percentage in the league (38.0).
Despite the high blitz rate, the Commanders only have 18 sacks, which rank 22nd in the league.
“I think we completed every ball,” Pitcher said Monday while scanning each blitz in his mind. “I don’t know the yardage off the top of my head, but yeah, I think we handled it pretty well.”

title: 'Been Unbelievable' - Bengals Offensive Line Destroying Poor Play 'Narrative'  During 2026 Season
full_text:
The Bengals' hot streak may not be a hot streak if one key factor keeps up.
Cincinnati's offensive consistency is much firmer this year as they protect Joe Burrow better than ever.
Sunday's 38-18 win was the latest example as he lit up the league's best scoring defense since Week 5, while taking just three hits and one sack.
The Bengals' offensive tackles pitched virtual shutouts against a nasty TJ Watt & Co. Orlando posted 44 pass-blocking snaps without a pressure allowed (the most in a single NFL game this season), while Mims did not allow a single pressure on 23 pass blocks against Watt.
"Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said. "They take it very seriously and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. to understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out."
Mims has now held Watt without a pressure on 45 pass blocks this season. As a whole, the Bengals rank fifth in PFF pass-block grading and 13th in run blocking.
"They've been unbelievable, yeah," Burrow said before highlighting Chase Brown's lesser-discussed blocking impact (career-high 70.4 pass-blocking grade this season). "We know what we have in Chase. He's a big-time playmaker for us. When people devote too many resources to stopping the guys on the outside, Chase can beat you in a lot of different ways ... Yeah. He's been lights out in pass protection too. I know we like Samaje (Perine) to be in there, but Chase's ability to do that has really opened up some things for us on third down."
Zac Taylor can feel the "narrative" that Cincinnati can't block crumbling in real time.
"They've been showing that," the Bengals head coach said. "Maybe people didn't want to see it because they wanted to follow the narrative that's been going on for years now, but our offensive line has been playing really well now, dating back to last year. We know that, and hopefully everybody else is trying to see that as well."
Burrow is changing how he faces pressure as well, notching a career-best 14.8% pressure-to-sack ratio this season (13th-best in the NFL). PTS represents how often Burrow gets sacked when he faces pressure, and that number is roughly 5% lower than any other season in his career (next closest: 2024 at 19.4%).
The computer quarterback has added an upgrade, while the continuity everyone talked about across the offensive front is paying off in a huge way.
Amarius Mims pass protection cut up from last night. Truly special player with his combination of size, athleticism, and technical prowess. He's so comfortable pass setting. His dominance allows Cincy to turn all of the protection and chip help away from him. pic.twitter.com/yBzS0OyHRS

title: Zac Taylor Dials Into Dalton Risner's Week 11 Injury Status as Bengals Turn Page From Sunday Night Football
full_text:
Cincinnati is still pretty healthy as we enter the thick of November and cold football season moving forward, but one big name just got added to the injured group on Sunday night: Starting guard Dalton Risner.
He went down with a knee injury in the 38-18 win over the Steelers, and Zac Taylor updated his status on Monday after noting it wasn't "too serious" on Sunday. They are monitoring both of his knees throughout the week, along with an issue for Dylan Fairchild. Neither were ruled out for next Monday night against Washington.
Tee Higgins is fine after dealing with some pain during the game.
"Yeah, both his knees started to bother him," Taylor said about Risner. "He got sick the day before the game, as reported. So, proud of him for trying to fight through it, and then just got to the point where he came out."
Cincinnati may be able to get names like WR Andrei Iosivas, CB Jalen Davis, and guard Brian Parker back this week after they got cleared to practice in a ramp-up last week.
Backup safety Kyle Dugger is also a name to watch after he missed another game with the quad injury. He's played in just four games this season with the lingering issue.
Still, Cincinnati has avoided the major injury bug bites that can destroy a season and sits atop the AFC North at 7-2.
"We don't have to worry about what anybody else is doing. We just have to worry about our stuff," Taylor said about being atop the division. "And so, I'm really proud, especially after coming off an international game. I felt like the guys all week had a great energy about them. They were ready to go for this game. I'm proud. This obviously gave us a big lift. I'm just proud of how they handled the week."
Cincinnati's offensive line play has been a big driver of the team's strong health for Joe Burrow and the whole offense in general.
"Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said about the offensive line on Sunday. "They take it very seriously, and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out."
They hope to have Risner for a full slate of snaps this week. Jalen Rivers will likely fill in if not after playing palatably in Risner's place on Sunday (62.4 overall Pro Football Focus grade on 34 snaps).

title: Joe Burrow Posts Best 2026 Pro Football Focus Grade as Bengals Earn More Great Marks
full_text:
The Bengals dropped another hammer on Sunday night in the 38-18 win over Pittsburgh. It resulted in an 83 overall Pro Football Focus team grade (third-best of the season) and plenty of great marks from Cincinnati's stars.
The offense powered things, and we start there with Joe Burrow ripping a 94.1 PFF grade. It's his highest mark of the season after also posting a 96.1 ESPN QBR (that mark leads all quarterbacks in Week 10 entering Monday Night Football). He dropped 409 passing yards and four touchdowns on Pittsburgh.
Burrow is now the odds-on favorite to win MVP for good reason. He led all Bengals in grading and is passing better than any quarterback on the planet right now.
The rest of the top five on offense went in this order (min. 20 snaps): Ja'Marr Chase (90.3), Chase Brown (75.2), Amarius Mims (74.9), Samaje Perine (73.3). There weren't many sub-50 grades from an offensive buzzsaw like that.
Cincinnati's bottom-five offensive grades went in this order (min. 20 snaps): Dalton Risner (29.3), Mike Gesicki (50), Colbie Young (50.5), Drew Sample (55.6), Dohnte Meyers (59.6). It was a rare down day for Risner this season as we await Zac Taylor's update on his knee injury this week.
Shifting to the defensive side, it was another strong outing from that group, allowing less than 20 points for the third time in the last four games.
Boye Mafe (86.4) is turning into one of the greatest free-agent signings in team history after he replaced Trey Hendrickson (who holds that title right now). The mauling, versatile edge rusher led all defenders in grading and notched another seven pressures in the game.
He ranks seventh among qualified pass rushers with 43 pressures this season. Hounding offenses all game long.
The rest of the top defensive grades went in this order: Josh Newton (76.6), Jordan Battle (76.3), Barrett Carter (74.2), Bryan Cook (73). It was a banner day for the second and third level of the Bengals' defense, forcing Aaron Rodgers to miss on his first seven passes.
Jonathan Allen notched a sack, but still checked in with the lowest defensive grade among players to log 20-plus snaps (45.7). There weren't many other low grades: Myles Murphy (56.3), DJ Turner II (57.3), Demetrius Knight Jr. (58.5), TJ Slaton (60).
Cincinnati is playing really well as a team right now, and the PFF grades reflect their surge. Check out all of them here.

title: Bengals' Unique Decision Sunday Night Has Steelers, Rest of NFL Playing Catch Up
full_text:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow said he didn’t think the team was trying to send a message with the unorthodox, somewhat risky decision it made Sunday night prior to kickoff.
But perhaps head coach Zac Taylor was delivering one to his players.
The Bengals won the coin toss and took a left turn away from the norm, electing to receive the opening kickoff rather than deferring the choice to the second half, a decision that barely classifies as one any more with seemingly every team opting to start the second half, rather than the first, on offense.
But when your quarterback and the offense as a whole is on the sort of white-hot heater Burrow and the Bengals have enjoyed, it feels less like a gamble and more like wagering with inside information.
Burrow and the offense cashed in by receiving the opening kickoff and going 80 yards in 13 plays for a field goal that opened a portal to hell for a Steelers defense as the Bengals scored on five of their first six possessions on the way to a 31-3 lead and eventual 38-18 victory to take over the top of the AFC North Division.
“We just wanted to come out and be the aggressor, try to put points on the board early and get those guys behind so they didn’t feel great about running it, and (then) let our defensive line go to work,” Burrow said when asked if the team was sending a message with the rare decision to receive the opening kickoff.
Sunday marked the sixth time the Bengals have won the coin toss this season, and in each of the previous five they elected to defer the choice to the second half, which comes with the possibility of scoring on back-to-back possessions if they can add points late in the first half and then again to start the third quarter.
“I don’t know if (Taylor) told everybody, but I knew that we were going to set the tone and try to get out there and score points,” wide receiver Dohnte Meyers said. “We want to score points, and receiving the ball first, that’s the first opportunity to set the tone.”
Just last week, the Bengals won the toss in Madrid and deferred their choice to second half. They fell behind 7-0 but Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase lit up the Falcons, with Chase recording 142 receiving yards in the first half alone, a new career high for the opening 30 minutes.
Sunday night, he topped it with 146 to back up Taylor's decision to shrug off the consequences and try to strike first.
Taylor has been more willing than most coaches to buck the trend of deferring after winning the toss.
The Bengals 62-63 on coin toss during Taylor’s 125 regular season games.
Sunday was the 12th time he’s elected to receive the opening kickoff.
He only did it once during his first two seasons, and it didn’t go well. The Bengals lost 27-3 at Baltimore.
In 2022 after a string of poor opening drives, Taylor attempted to mix up the formula and opted to receive the opening kick in Week 3 against the Jets, and the Bengals scored on their first possession on the way to a 27-12.
Taylor also took the ball first in a 35-17 rout of Atlanta in Week 7 of 2022, and in a 27-24 victory at home against the Chiefs in Week 14.
He did it three times in 2023, with two coming in primetime – a Week 3, 19-16 Monday night win against the Rams and a Week 9, 24-18 win against the Bills. There also was the 27-3 loss at Tennessee in Week 4.
In 2024, Taylor did it again in primetime in a 17-7 win against the Giants in Week 6.
Last year there were three instances, all late in the season after Burrow’s return – a 39-34 loss at Buffalo in Week 14, a 37-14 win against Arizona in Week 17 and a 20-18 loss to Cleveland in Week 18.
With the way Burrow has been playing, don’t be surprised if the aggressive nature of scoring first and playing with the lead continues.
“He’s just on it,” Taylor said of Burrow. “I think Joe did an excellent job keeping his eyes down the field and finding guys for some big plays. Those guys made big plays and tremendous catches — all of those guys really. Everyone stepped up and made some plays for us. Obviously, he (Burrow) set the tone.
“This is just how he is,” Taylor added. “I feel like I’ve seen him in this rhythm quite a bit. He has a lot of confidence. Like I’ve said before, the offensive line is blocking so well, it allows us to play confident. At one point we had 24 passes and six runs. It is what it is. As long as these guys are doing that and we are making our way, that’s how it’s going to be.”
After falling behind early in three consecutive comeback wins against the Ravens, Titans and Falcons, the Bengals never trailed against the Steelers.
They led 17-0 before adding another TD on the final drive of the first half to go up 24-3. And it was 31-3 heading into the fourth quarter.
In Week 3 at Pittsburgh, the Bengals won the toss and deferred. The Steelers scored touchdowns on their opening two drives and got points on their first three, and Burrow and the offense were playing catch up.
Sunday night, they flipped things, both in terms of the game and the season, forcing the Steelers and the rest of the AFC North opponents to play catch up going into the second half of the season as they sit atop the division at 7-2.
“We don’t have to worry about what anybody else is doing,” Taylor said while answering a question about the division standings, but it could have just as well have been about the edge of taking the ball first and jumping on top.
“We just have to worry about our stuff,” he added. “This obviously gave us a big lift.”

title: Bengals Moderate Road Betting Favorites Against Commanders as Hot 2026 Season Rolls on
full_text:
The Bengals are rolling in the past month, and the betting odds for next Monday night's action against the Commanders reflect that. According to DraftKings Sportsbook, Cincinnati opened as a 4.5-point betting favorite, and the point total is set at 51.5.
Another 50-plus point total for the hottest offense in the NFL. Pittsburgh came into Sunday's 38-18 Bengals hammering with the NFL's top-scoring defense since Week 5, and Cincinnati plowed through them in the snow-white uniforms.
Cincinnati is now 7-2 overall as the AFC North leaders and 5-4 against the betting spread this season. They covered the 3.5-point betting line against the Steelers and now face a Commanders team fresh off a Thursday night win over New York. Washington is 3-5-1 overall and 5-4 ATS this season.
"It's one of the biggest wins we've had here in a while, but it's Week 10. We've got a lot of football here to be played. Learn from my mistakes, celebrate the win, but we'll come back and get better," Joe Burrow said after lighting up a fifth consecutive opponent for four-plus total touchdowns.
Burrow joined Peyton Manning in 2004 as the only QB in league history to score four-plus touchdowns in five consecutive games. Manning won the MVP that year, and Burrow is right at the head of the pack for that award in 2026.
“Yeah, feels great. We really haven't been in this spot since I've been in the league," Burrow noted. "Really, we were 5-2 in 2021, and then 7-6, and then trying to climb out of it. So it's nice to give ourselves some leeway, but we certainly aren't satisfied with where we're at and want to keep getting better.”
Burrow and Zac Taylor rallied the troops to respond well after a trip overseas and make major NFL history for the team. Cincinnati became the first team ever to win a game against a team off their bye after playing overseas (other teams 0-5 in prior outings).
Now, they get an extra day to rest before a road trip to face Washington.
That game kicks off at 8:15 p.m. ET next Monday.

title: 9 Winners and 2 Losers From the Bengals' Dominant Win Over the Steelers
full_text:
The Bengals dominated the Steelers through all four quarters on Sunday Night Football en route to a 38-18 victory in Paycor Stadium . The Bengals led 31-3 at the end of the third quarter, and Pittsburgh scored twice in garbage time to make the final score look more respectable. The Bengals are now 7-2 and are in first place in the AFC North.
Here are nine winners and two losers from Sunday night's victory:
Joe Burrow played at a level far above any other quarterback in the league on Sunday night in front of the world. He methodically marched the offense downfield on the team's first two drives and led the Bengals to a 10-0 score, completing 21 passes before Aaron Rodgers even completed one.
His dominant performance continued from that point on, and he finished with 35 completions, 409 yards, and 4 touchdowns for the fifth consecutive week. Burrow is playing the best football of his career and is the clear frontrunner for league MVP.
Risner was a late addition to the injury report with an illness; that said, he played through that issue and continued to play well before aggravating a knee injury he has battled all season. Should Risner miss significant time, Jalen Rivers should continue to fill his spot on the offensive line.
Hopefully, Risner recovers quickly and can return to the lineup at full strength. Obviously making him a "loser," simply means his injury was one of the only negatives in what was a dominant night for the home team.
Chase torched Asante Samuel Jr. and the Steelers' secondary regularly on Sunday. He caught 11 balls for 231 yards in the Bengals' big victory and proved once again that he is one of the best receivers the league has ever witnessed.
He sits at 64 receptions for 878 yards and seven touchdowns on the season and now has three consecutive weeks with at least 140 receiving yards.
Gesicki's only catch of the night happened on the game's opening drive when he caught a 9-yard pass from Burrow over the middle. Aside from that, he remained a non-existent piece of the game plan on a night where the offense dominated.
Brown is officially in mid-season form and showed up as arguably the most critical piece of the offense against Pittsburgh. He had multiple big plays in pass protection, and on top of that, he had 18 touches for 83 yards and two touchdowns.
It is evident how much this offense relies on Brown at times, and he is capable of delivering at a high level in those moments.
Taylor knew his team needed a fast start against the Steelers in a crucial AFC North contest, and he delivered massively. While his first challenge was unsuccessful, after the officials ruled Germie Bernard inbounds on a catch down the sideline, Taylor threw the challenge flag once more. This time he was successful, and officials reversed the call to an incomplete pass, forcing the Steelers to punt.
Taylor had this team ready to play its best football in the biggest moment of the season at this point and called a superb game offensively.
This is the game that everyone has waited for from the Bengals' young linebacker duo. Both Demetrius Knight Jr. and Barrett Carter played effectively enough to where everyone should have excitement for their growth. Knight finished as the team's leading tackler with eight total tackles, including six solo tackles. Carter, meanwhile, finished with six tackles on the night, including a solid run stop on Jaylen Warren on a 2nd & 2 in the fourth quarter.
The offensive line dominated the trenches against a stout Steelers defensive line. Throughout the night the Bengals offensive line allowed only six pressures, according to Sumer Sports. Amarius Mims held T.J. Watt in check all night, with Watt having zero pressures against Mims, while Orlando Brown Jr. allowed only one pressure from his side.
Jalen Rivers, meanwhile, held up well when he entered the game following Risner's injury, showing solid growth at right guard.
Golden's unit on defense played its best game of the season so far, holding the Steelers to just 3 points through three quarters. The defense held Jaylen Warren to just 41 yards on 12 touches, while both Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington had only three catches for 40 yards and a garbage time touchdown.
All of Boye Mafe, Myles Murphy, Jonathan Allen, and Dexter Lawrence notched sacks for a total of four on the night. The rest of the defense played with great discipline all game long, and young players showed solid growth in the middle of the field and secondary.
The most heartwarming moment of Sunday's victory happened at the end of the first half when Meyers caught his first touchdown of his NFL career on a 15-yard strike from Burrow. Meyers spent the first two years of his professional football career with the CFL Saskatchewan Roughriders before signing a futures deal with the Bengals last January. He is now a key piece of the best offense in the NFL and has become a fan favorite in Cincinnati.
Paycor Stadium hit new levels of loud for the Bengals ' white-out game on Sunday night, and the fans in Cincinnati consistently made communication for Rodgers and the Steelers' offense difficult. The Bengals fanbase showed up in the best way they possibly could.

title: Ja'Marr Chase Makes Big Statement About Bengals' Offense After Blowout Win Over Steelers
full_text:
After dominating the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, Ja'Marr Chase spoke with SportsCenter's Scott Van Pelt following the end of the game and said the Bengals offense is currently at its peak. Chase praised the offensive line and Joe Burrow for their performance.
"I think right now, we're at our peak with momentum," Chase said. "The O-line's been playing incredible right now and giving Joe enough time to get the ball out of his hands, and Joe is just trusting his playmakers to win in space."
Chase continued saying that confidence is high within the locker room and pointed to the team's victory in Madrid over the Falcons last week. He stated that he saw that game as the launching point for the offense to reach its peak.
"The confidence should be really high, especially after the Madrid game, we flew eight hours and had a great game in Madrid, after that game that's when we should see our momentum and be taking off," Chase said. "I said that last week in an interview after the game and that's what I wanna say we got it from."
Chase expanded further and emphasized how massive the additions to the defense have impacted this Bengals team. He explained that it is really what the team needed, saying that players such as Dexter Lawrence, Bryan Cook, and Boye Mafe have shown they were worth the investment.
"Those guys are such a big help, that's really what we needed this year, they're showing why they're worth it, showing why they got picked and why they've got that name on their back," Chase said.
Cook has provided an exceptional level of leadership to the Bengals' secondary, while both Lawrence and Mafe have combined for 11.5 sacks this year. Jonathan Allen has also shown up as a quality addition to the pass rush with four sacks this year from the interior of the defensive line.
Chase finished saying that the sky is the limit for this Bengals team, and that the team will continue to take each game one at a time.
"The sky is always the limit at the end of the day, but we've gotta take it one game at a time, control what we can control, and the only thing we're worried about is being number one in the division," Chase said.
