title: Joe Burrow Dominates as Bengals Take Down Steelers: Instant Takeaways
full_text:
The Bengals beat the Steelers 38-18 on Sunday night. It was a dominant performance by Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and a Cincinnati team that is a force to be wrecked with in the AFC.
The Bengals improve to 7-2 on the season. They've won 5-straight games and are in sole possession of first place in the AFC North.
Here are our instant takeaways to the victory:
The Bengals absolutely dominated the Steelers from the start. Cincinnati built a 31-3 lead late in the third quarter. They scored on five of their first six possessions and the only time they didn't score was due to a missed field goal. Four of those five scoring drives ended with touchdowns.
Meanwhile, the defense forced punts on 5-of-6 drives to start the game. They took away the Steelers' rushing attack and Aaron Rodgers couldn't find anyone open downfield for most of the game.
Pittsburgh scored two fourth quarter touchdowns to make the score look a bit more competitive, but this was utter domination.
This is exactly what a Super Bowl contending team should do to a team like Pittsburgh. The Steelers have talent, but they have some clear flaws. The Bengals protected Burrow, got after Rodgers and the rest was history.
Burrow completed 35-of-44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns. He finished with a 135.7 passer rating. Burrow joins Peyton Manning as the only other player to score 4+ total touchdowns in 5-straight games in NFL history. Manning did it in 2004 en route to an MVP. Burrow is well on his way to doing the same here in Cincinnati.
Burrow wasn't alone. Ja'Marr Chase led the way with 11 catches for 231 yards on 14 targets. He averaged 21 yards-per-catch. Tee Higgins finished with 66 yards on five catches. Chase Brown had eight catches for 39 yards and two receiving touchdowns.
This offense was so dominant that Joe Flacco and the Bengals' backups finished the game.
The Bengals sacked Aaron Rodgers three times. They also held the Steelers to just 62 rushing yards on 17 attempts (3.6 yards-per-carry).
Rodgers completed 15-of-29 attempts for 143 yards and two touchdowns. Most of his yards and both of his touchdowns came in the fourth quarter.
Rodgers entered the fourth quarter with just seven completions for 27 yards. Steelers star receiver DJ Metcalf didn't have a catch until the fourth quarter. Neither did starting tight end Pat Freiermuth. Both guys scored in the fourth quarter to pad their stats.
This was a dominant outing from Al Golden's unit and by far their best outing of the season.
The Bengals will try to extend their winning streak on Monday Night Football. They head to Washington to play the Commanders on Monday, Nov. 23 at 8:15 p.m. ET.
James Rapien is the publisher of Bengals On SI. He's also the host First Word With James Rapien, a daily morning show dedicated to Cincinnati sports and the co-founder of Cincinnati Bengals Talk on YouTube. The Cincinnati native also wrote a book about the history of the Cincinnati Bengals called Enter The Jungle.

title: Examining What Shedeur Sanders’ Future in Cleveland Looks Like
full_text:
The most popular player for the Cleveland Browns tends to be the backup quarterback. At this time in most Browns’ seasons, fans start clamoring for a change at the position to find any glimmer of hope for the next season.
But this year, the Browns are 6-4, and if the season ended today, they would be in the playoffs. Deshaun Watson is coming off three straight 300-yard games , and the offense was humming against a very good Houston Texans defense.
Todd Monken chose Watson to be the starting quarterback after a competition with Shedeur Sanders in the offseason. Monken cited that Watson gave the team the best chance to win. The decision was to the chagrin of everyone outside of the Browns’ locker room due to Watson’s preseason performance both on and off the field.
Sanders got his lone start in New Orleans when they came a two-point conversion short of another comeback win. His performance was similar to that of Watson’s, but the result was a loss.
Now the Browns are headed into their bye week with Watson cementing his grip on the starting position. The team chasing the Browns for the last playoff spot just lost their starting quarterback , and they have a challenging schedule to finish out the season.
#Browns Todd Monken said he hasn't talked to GM Andrew Berry about Deshaun Watson's future with the club. Said they have 7 games left and he's only worried about walk-through on Wednesday.
Watson’s contract expires at the end of the season, and the Browns have too many wins to draft a quarterback high in the draft. While Watson has won six games so far with the Browns, he has not played well enough overall to guarantee that the Browns have to extend him at the end of the year.
His contract will still count against the salary cap for the next two years, and they need a quarterback on a rookie contract.
Sanders will be on his rookie contract for the next two years while Watson’s cap hit is in effect. He will have a full year learning under Monken, so the playbook should come easier to him. Monken was hired for the head coaching job due in part to his confidence that he could squeeze out production from the quarterback room.
Watson has had his best season in a Browns uniform, and Monken has been correct every step of the way.
Monken had enough confidence in Sanders to start him in New Orleans after Watson cleared concussion protocol. The playcalling looked similar to a Watson-led offense, and when the offense needed Sanders the most, he came through. Monken will have a full offseason to create an offense around Sanders’ skill set.
If the season ended today, the Browns would be picking 18th (from the Los Angeles Rams) and 20th overall in the draft. The quarterback class does not look as deep as it did at the beginning of the season, and several teams need a quarterback draft pick before them.
The Browns already have three quarterbacks on rookie deals, and taking a flyer on a mid-round quarterback may be a waste of a roster spot.
The quarterbacks in free agency are no better, as Kyler Murray would be the best option. Murray would not cost much, but his tenure with the Minnesota Vikings was not as fruitful as they had hoped. Kirk Cousins is also a free agent, but he would not be a long-term answer at the position.
Sanders presents the Browns with their best option at quarterback for next season . Monken can tailor the offense towards him and he proved that he can make plays down the field with the rookie wide receivers. The Browns will have to start extending their young talent after next season, and his fifth-round rookie contract is team-friendly.
Although this season belongs to Watson, the future may very well belong to Sanders.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: ‘I Saw Someone Who Was Hurt’: Todd Monken Talks Deshaun Watson’s Growth From Preseason Boos to 6-4 Start
full_text:
Back on Aug. 22, Deshaun Watson was booed by Cleveland fans in a 31-7 preseason loss to the Buffalo Bills.
On Nov. 15, as Watson put together his sixth game-winning drive of the season to lead Cleveland to the comeback victory over the Houston Texans, only cheers could be heard from Huntington Bank Field.
Watson’s postgame comments from that preseason loss to Buffalo – where he called the boos “disrespectful” and “personal” – seemed to be a preview of yet another disappointing season for the Browns.
But now, as the team enters a bye week, it sits at a 6-4 record. It’s the first time Cleveland has started 4-0 at home since 1963.
So, what changed from Aug. 22 to now?
Todd Monken thinks his quarterback has been able to “let go” of the pain of the last four seasons.
https://x.com/camijustice/status/2122423150474371355
“I’ve said this many of times, when we met after that, it wasn’t really about his physical traits; it was really where you are mentally and emotionally. I’ve said it before, ‘Did you get this off your chest? Did you really let go? Have you really let go of the frustrations over the last few years that’s been on your heart?’” Monken said at Monday’s press conference. “If you have, you can say it, if you really let go of it. And if you haven’t, it doesn’t matter what we do. It doesn’t matter if you’re physically healthy; mentally, you’re not in a really good place.’ I felt like our conversation was on point. I felt like he had let it go; he had got it off his chest. I didn’t see someone who was broken; I saw someone who was hurt.”
Since signing a five-year deal with Cleveland in 2022, Watson has yet to play a full season due to a combination of injuries and a suspension for violating the NFL’s personal conduct policy. He played just 19 total games in his first four years with the Browns, missing the entirety of 2025 as he recovered from a torn Achilles.
While Watson’s been in the NFL for 10 seasons, he’s had limited opportunity to become fully accustomed to the Browns’ offense. And with this year’s change in coaching staff, Monken says he still considers his starting quarterback “under construction” in his system.
“I think the more we repeat concepts, I think the better we get in protection, I think the better our young guys get in terms of getting to spots and their details in terms of routes and concepts. I think the more confidence he’ll grow in terms of where to place the ball,” Monken said. “I think he’s under construction in terms of his drops, his consistency in his drops and his footwork, and where his eyes are, and exhausting all of his progressions.”
Even with the historic start to the season, it’s clear Monken isn’t fully satisfied with Watson’s production. Statistically, though, he’s putting together his best year since he arrived in Cleveland.
Through nine games – the most he’s ever played in a season with the Browns – Watson has passed for 2,118 yards with a completion rate of 65.1%. He also has seven passing touchdowns, matching his total from both 2022 and 2023.
His success so far brings attention to the fact that it’s a contract year for Watson. His original five-year deal expires after the 2026 season.
If he continues to impress, the Browns will have a decision to make regarding their quarterback. On Monday, though, Monken said there haven’t been any discussions of Watson’s looming contract.
As the Browns enter their bye week, Monken will have some extra time to evaluate Watson’s future with the organization.
But for now, with a 6-4 record, it looks like the quarterback is back in Cleveland’s good graces.
A Northeast Ohio native, Rachel grew up following all things Cleveland sports. She has experience in broadcast and digital media and graduated from West Virginia University with a degree in sports media.

title: Can the Browns Make the Playoffs? The Path May Not Be as Hard as You Think
full_text:
After 10 weeks of the NFL season, it is no longer a question if the Cleveland Browns can make the playoffs.
Time after time, this team has proven they can win tough games .
Now, let's take a look at the remainder of the season and see how hard it will be to get to the postseason. Spoiler alert: it is not nearly as hard as you think.
Browns are 4-0 at home for the first time since 1963.
After playing six of their first nine games on the road to start the season, the schedule makers gifted the Browns with five straight weeks at home. Following the win over the Texans, Cleveland now heads into their bye week.
Following the time off, here's the Browns next three opponents all in Cleveland:
Realistically, the Browns only need to win two out of these three games.
For the Raiders, they just traded Kirk Cousins and will be led by their first overall pick, Fernando Mendoza. While a win against the Bengals is tough, it will be a great test to see how the Browns stack up against a true contender.
Following that game, the Browns' former coach from last season, Kevin Stefanski, comes back to the Dawg Pound, where you would hope the players would give it their all to prove they are better off without him.
If the Browns can win two of three in the home stand, they will have a record of 8-5 heading into the final four games of the regular season. This already gives the Browns a 62.5% chance to make the postseason.
Going further, the stats show that teams that win 10 games in a season have a 91% chance of making the playoffs.
This would mean the Browns would need two wins with out of these matchups:
While the Giants and Bengals matchups may be rough, the Browns get two easier opponents in the Colts and Ravens. The Colts already began to wave the white flag at the trade deadline after dealing multiple starters for future draft capital.
For Baltimore, the only reason they could be an easier matchup is the current state of their injured quarterback room. Now, if Lamar Jackson is healthy by then, that matchup changes completely.
Since joining the AFC North in 2002, the Browns have never won a division title. For that honor, you'd have to travel all the way back to 1989 when they won the AFC Central.
So far this season, the Browns have played half of their divisional games, and sit with a 2-1 record.
If Cleveland can split the season series with Cincinnati and beat the Ravens on the road, that would set them up with only two divisional losses this season.
While it seems like more of a reach than the playoffs with the Bengals being red hot, clearly the Browns have proved that anything is possible in 2026.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: Deshaun Watson Steals the Spotlight, But This Browns Player Deserves More Credit
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns took down the Houston Texans at home in week 10.
For Cleveland, Deshaun Watson stepped up and had a huge game once again. However, there is another player who is constantly making an impact that isn't getting the credit he deserves.
Harold Fannin Jr. finished Sunday's game with 7 catches for 91 yards.
So far in this season, Harold Fannin Jr. has 37 receptions for 453 yards and four touchdowns.
This stat line comes after a slow start to the season, and multiple weeks with one catch for less than 10 yards.
Despite this, Fannin is second on the team in receiving yards, only behind rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston.
If he continues at his current rate, along with the unknown injury status of Boston, Fannin could definitely turn into the first option out of all the pass catches and potentially finish the year with over 1,000 yards.
But in the past few weeks, his production has ramped up significantly, and some of the plays he's made have changed the game.
Harold Fannin Jr. down to the 5! HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GQL0DtQAaV
Looking at the last three games, Fannin has really increased his production with the Browns.
It all starts with his career day against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In that contest, Fannin recorded his most catches in a single game with 10, and also his most receiving yards with 154.
Last week against New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders struggled to get him the ball. However, we all remember what happened when he finally did see an opportunity in overtime, taking a five-yard pass to the house and earning the "Angry Run" title.
Then, once again on Sunday, Fannin proved to be a big part of this Browns offense. Not only did he post another great stat line, but he also made another big play late in the game to set the Browns up for victory.
While some say Fannin needs to learn how to block and further develop his game, others are already calling him one of the best tight ends in the entire NFL.
Let's be honest, if Fannin keeps up his production and starts having these great games more consistently, who's to say he can't achieve that top title and be looked at as the next Travis Kelce or George Kittle?
Clearly, the skill set, playmaking ability, and stardom are already there. It really is up to the Browns and Todd Monken to utilize him more in passing plays.
Regardless, the future is bright for the young tight end.
No matter what happens, he deserves more credit for the Browns success in 2026.

title: Could Deshaun Watson be the CPOTY? Making His Case Following Browns' 6-4 Start
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have put together an impressive first half of the season and head into their bye week with a 6-4 record.
Not only are the Browns 6-4 and still heavily in the mix for the playoffs, but they’re also undefeated at Huntington Bank Field for the first time since 1963.
This is undoubtedly an overall team effort, but much of their success is thanks to quarterback Deshaun Watson. After a troublesome first few years in Cleveland, Watson is finally playing like the quarterback they had originally invested their future into.
After a massive 27-24 victory over Watson’s former team , the Houston Texans, the fans and the media are giving him his much-deserved credit for getting the team to this point. Now, Watson’s name is cemented in the running for this season's Comeback Player of the Year.
Here’s why Watson is being considered for the CPOTY award this season:
It’s safe to say that leading up to this season, most Browns fans were expecting another down year especially if Watson was the starting quarterback of this team. That’s a fair assumption considering how poorly he had played in recent years.
Fast forward to this week, Watson has played like his Houston-self and rewrote all of the narratives that had been published for years now. Multiple season-ending injuries and lackluster play contributed to that, but it doesn’t seem to be affecting him now.
Watson now has six fourth quarter comebacks this season to help his Browns secure much needed wins. His stats on the year through ten weeks include 1,800 passing yards with seven touchdowns to three interceptions.
He’s already played more games this season than he has in each of his previous three seasons, as he averaged six games played each year to this point. His stats are the best he’s seen since arriving in Cleveland, and the team is reaping the rewards of his consistency.
Watson also hasn’t topped seven passing touchdowns since joining the Browns and already has that number matched through ten games. He is the unanimous starting quarterback in Cleveland and is certainly making his case to sign an extension this offseason.
Between Cleveland’s young core of star players , both first year and second- or third-year players combined with their respectable veterans, this Browns team is looking to make noise down the stretch of a very manageable second half of their schedule.
Watson is still creating chemistry with his offensive weapons, and some weeks are better than others. However, if he continues playing at this level and orchestrating late game comebacks, there’s no doubt he should be in serious contention for the CPOTY award in February.
Dominic Pagura is from Medina, Ohio and a graduate from Kent State University.

title: Wild Stat Shows How Clutch The Browns Have Been This Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns pulled off a very inspiring victory on Sunday over the Houston Texans, winning 27-24 after Houston scored on their first three drives of the game. Cleveland then went on to score the next 20 points of the game, leading 20-17 after three quarters.
After a long missed field goal from Andre Szmyt, Houston capitalized on a long pass interference called on Myles Harden and punched it in to lead by four with nine minutes to go. Deshaun Watson then got picked off on a pass that went off Blake Whiteheart’s hands; two more three-and-outs were forced by the Browns defense.
Then it was time for Watson to do what he has done better than any quarterback in the league: go win the game. The Browns did just that, as Watson completed a strike to Harold Fannin Jr., who rumbled his way to the Houston five-yard line, and then Judkins punched it in for the eventual game-winning score.
The Browns are the first team in NFL history whose first six wins of a season all come by 4 points or fewer, according to ESPN Research.
That stat says a lot about this group and who is in the lead of the Browns: head coach Todd Monken . While some fans might not think this way of winning is sustainable, you will take any win you can get in this league.
Over the last two years under Kevin Stefanski, the Browns went 6-10 in one-score games; this season under Monken, Cleveland is 6-2 in the same criteria.
Another stat that shows how great Cleveland has been this season in terms of comeback victories, from Daniel Oyefusi, is that Cleveland now has four double-digit comeback wins this year, which is tied for the most by a team through the first 10 games in NFL history.
Watson has now led his sixth game-winning drive of the season, proving his coach right in putting him right back into the lineup after he had to miss a game with a concussion.
The Browns are keeping pace with the top of the AFC North, as the Bengals and Steelers match up on Sunday Night Football, and the winner will take the lead of the division. Cleveland will finally get their bye week next week, before staying home for the next three weeks.
Those home games range from facing up against rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in Week 12, then the divisional foe, Cincinnati Bengals, led by MVP candidate Joe Burrow; former coach Kevin Stefanski brings his Atlanta Falcons into Cleveland for an emotional matchup to cap off the homestand.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: 3 Takeaways From Browns' Nail-Biting Win Over Texans for Sixth Victory of 2026
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns love to get the nerves going.
And on Sunday, Nov. 15, they did exactly that again.
Trailing 17-0 early to the Houston Texans, the Browns rallied to take a 20-17 lead in the second half of play. They then proceeded to fall behind 24-20 before starting quarterback Deshaun Watson led the team to a game-winning drive, his sixth of the season, to secure a 27-24 victory.
On the final drive of the game, Watson, after drawing a 15-yard unnecessary roughness call, completed a 30-yard pass to tight end Harold Fannin Jr., getting the Browns into position to score. He would hand off the ball to Quinshon Judkins, who punched in the eventual winner.
"The game is never over," Watson said postgame. "As long as we have time on the clock and we have an opportunity, we are going to believe we can finish it off."
“The game is never over. As long as we have time on the clock and we have opportunity, we're going to believe we can finish it off.” Deshaun Watson speaks with @MeganOlivi after the Browns’ 17-point comeback win over the Texans. pic.twitter.com/fOBKC362A5
Here are the three biggest takeaways from Sunday's victory that improved the Browns to 6-4 on the season:
The Browns always seem to turn it on a bit late, but Watson is always there to deliver.
Deshaun Watson has a game-winning drive in all 6 wins this season. Brown are 4-0 at home for first time since 1963. pic.twitter.com/V5ROnWUxBr
In all six of the Browns' wins this season, Watson has been credited with being the catalyst for the game-winning drives.
He finished Sunday's victory with 25 completions on 40 attempts, going for 312 yards on an average of 7.8 yards per reception. He did not find the end zone through the air, but added one score on the ground, along with 49 yards on eight carries.
Looking to continue making the offense more versatile, the Browns have been pushing Watson outside of the pocket more and more, hoping to see him extend drives with his legs.
He is now up over 2,100 yards passing this season , all while recording back-to-back-to-back 300-yard games.
If he can keep this up, the Browns are going to be in good hands as they search for a spot in the playoffs over the coming weeks.
Running back Quinshon Judkins couldn't be in a more confusing system.
Each week, the offensive scheme has him diving headfirst up the middle, whereas his speed and athleticism certainly have him much more suited for outside runs. However, he still made advantage of his limited opportunities on Sunday.
Scoring the game-winning touchdown on the Browns' final offensive drive, Judkins capped off his day with 10 carries for 38 yards and one score.
He is now up to over 400 rushing yards and four scores this season, but still sits below 3.5 yards per carry.
In order to get the most out of the rushing attack, Judkins either needs 10 more carries a game or more versatility in where he is expected to run. Gaining one or two yards up the gut as he crashes into a wall of bodies is just simply not getting the most out of the 23-year-old.
After falling down 17-0 through the first two quarters, not only did Cleveland's offense finally turn things up a notch, but so did the defense.
They would go on to give up just seven points for the rest of the contest, limiting Texans quarterback CJ Stroud's ability to get the offense going. They also forced him to throw an interception.
A wild juggling INT from Tyson Campbell 😳 HOUvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o05D4nQ0We
Stroud's final score of the game came on the Texans' second-to-last drive, but the Browns' defense had held the offense to a punt or an interception on the previous six straight drives.
After allowing him to score early in the fourth quarter, the defense forced him and the offense off the field on every subsequent drive without allowing them to do any further damage:
~  3 Plays, -1 Yard (Punt) ~ 3 Plays, 0 Yards (Punt) ~ 6 Plays, 3 Yards (Turnover on Downs)
That type of production with the game on the line is so important, and also proves that this team has what it takes to compete when the stakes are the highest.
Now, they have to just turn Sunday's result into an all-game constant, rather than a late-game surge.

title: Browns Rookie Earns High Praise From Head Coach Amid Growing Pains
full_text:
There have been plenty of storylines following the Cleveland Browns all season long.
However, one that has lost some of its spotlight since the opening few weeks is the development of the team's rookie offensive linemen.
Following several struggles along the offensive line in recent weeks, most notably from veteran Tytus Howard, rookies Austin Barber and Spencer Fano have been overshadowed.
And honestly, it isn't hard to understand why.
Even with both Barber and Fano playing well, quarterbacks Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders have been sacked a total of 38 times across nine games , averaging out to over four sacks a game. If Cleveland wants to legitimately contend by the time the playoffs roll around, the line is going to have to be better.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke about Fano in particular, saying that the issues the line has gone through have allowed the ninth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft an opportunity to learn and grow.
"It’s so cool for him because of the way he’s wired, how he works at it — highly intelligent, very prideful, but it’s not easy being indoctrinated into playing left tackle as a rookie," he said. "And every week it feels like there is no off week, right? There isn’t an off week of these guys that are paid to get to the quarterback.
"And it really stresses your mental stamina, play after play, right? There is no ‘oh, I get a little bit of a smoke break here’. Oh, no, right. You don’t get that."
Fano currently ranks 17th out of 71 in the league in overall Pro Football Focus grade , placing him among some of football's best offensive tackles. In pass rush, there is still work to be done, with him ranking 39th out of 71, but his rushing ranking of 22nd pushes him back up towards the top of the ladder.
As Monken mentioned, even with him being moved from right tackle, which he was accustomed to in college, to left tackle, the 22-year-old has made incredible strides quickly.
He went on to say that the difference in competition is something that Fano has had to learn to be ready for, especially with edge rushers being so dynamic at the NFL level. One play he could be going up against a veteran before a shifty, young rusher comes flying his way the next.
Browns HC Todd Monken talked about the growing pains Spencer Fano is going through as a young tackle in the NFL and said there's "no smoke break" to catch your breath "It’s so cool for him because the way he’s wired, how he works at it, highly intelligent, very prideful, but… pic.twitter.com/qE0e7PTtyt
"You know, and then they roll (Jadeveon) Clowney in there, and they roll other guys that are young and trying to get the quarterback," Monken continued. "Like, that’s what’s the coolest thing about being a part of professional sports and being in professional football. Everybody’s got really good players, and it really challenges you.
"And I like his mental makeup. I like the way he’s wired. He’s only going to continue to get better."
Fano's next chance to return to the field and try to lead the Browns' offensive line comes on Sunday, Nov. 15.
The Browns play host to the Houston Texans from Huntington Bank Field at 1:00 p.m. EST.

title: Texans Rule Out Two Key Players Ahead of Browns Matchup on Sunday
full_text:
On Friday, the Cleveland Browns, just two days ahead of their matchup against the Houston Texans at home, announced that they would be without safety Ronnie Hickman and fullback Mike Burton.
Rookie Browns wideout Denzel Boston was also ruled questionable , putting the team in an even more difficult spot on Sunday against the Texans.
But the Browns aren't the only team banged up.
Following the Browns' injury report, a few hours passed, and the Texans issued their injury report ahead of Sunday's game, ruling out newly acquired wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. and defensive end Danielle Hunter.
Most importantly, the Texans may be without defensive end Will Anderson Jr., too, as the 6-foot-4, 243-pound defensive end is reportedly dealing with an ankle injury.
The #Browns won't face DE Danielle Hunter or WR Marvin Harrison Jr. on Sunday—and DE Will Anderson Jr. is in question with an ankle injury. https://t.co/wM1hRzoezb
For the Texans, not having Anderson Jr. on Sunday is something that could be a big impact, as the two-time pro bowler has put together a great season with 9.5 sacks in only eight games . Anderson Jr. has surpassed his 2023 rookie sack total (7.0 sacks) and will look to surpass the career high he set last season with 12.0 sacks.
Offensively, the Texans are looking to get Harrison Jr. involved more following their trade with the Arizona Cardinals, as Harrison Jr. became a part of the franchise on October 12 and has only been targeted 11 times in the three games played.
On the season, with both the Cardinals and the Texans, he has only been targeted 24 times with 11 receptions, averaging around 13.2 yards per reception. That is good enough for just 145 receiving yards and two touchdowns.
He hasn't had a big impact on the game this season, but missing Sunday keeps him behind the curve as he tries to adjust to the new system in Houston.
With Harrison Jr. out, the Texans will have to work in other guys on the offensive side of the ball.
While Anderson Jr. ruled questionable, the Texans know they will be without at least one defensive end in Hunter, as he is dealing with a hamstring injury.
Hunter has played in all eight games ahead of the matchup against the Browns and has played in all games since 2022, dating back to his days with the Minnesota Vikings. Hunter has been with Houston since 2024 and will miss his first game as a Texan on Sunday.
With the Texans' injury report being out and a good chunk of important pieces being on the list, Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson could have bought himself another week to succeed as the starter.
Defensively, the Browns will have a much easier time at locking down the passing game with Harrison Jr. inactive.
The two sides will clash at 1:00 p.m. EST from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 15.

title: Colin Cowherd Claims Cowboys Players Don't Respect Brian Schottenheimer
full_text:
In predictable fashion , the Dallas Cowboys were bullied on Sunday by the San Francisco 49ers. The road team came into AT&T Stadium with plenty of confidence, which was aided by the fact that the crowd was full of 49ers fans .
San Francisco had 584 yards of offense during their 46-40 win as the defense continued to operate like a turnstile. There is a much larger problem beyond their defensive ineptitude, however, as this is clearly a roster full of individual players rather than a cohesive team.
The primary reason for this, according to Colin Cowherd, is a complete lack of respect for head coach Brian Schottenheimer. Cowherd said the penalties over the past two weeks from DeMarvion Overshown and George Pickens are examples of players doing whatever they want while knowing Schottenheimer won't drop the hammer.
"They always say, you should fear a really good boss. Maybe not a lot, but know that he'll drop the hammer. She'll drop the hammer, if you screw up. I mean, DeMarvion Overshown, running on the field, lack of discipline a week ago. Yesterday, George Pickens, the taunting penalty. Tom Brady's like, the Niners don't do stuff like that because they respect Kyle Shanahan and they fear him. Like, Shanahan will move off you. He will not care about you if you get in the way of his process or his offense or his structure," Cowherd said.
"Cowboy players don't respect Brian Schottenheimer. They don't care." 😬 @colincowherd on another embarrassing Cowboys loss pic.twitter.com/95b7Y3TsZR
"Cowboy players don't respect Brian Schottenheimer. They don't care. I mean, you can see it from the penalties. You can see it from the taunting, running on the field. And, I mean, I'm just watching. They're on pace for their third straight losing season, and it's got very much a Dave Campo feel to it, where they don't do anything particularly well. Last in total defense, last in rush defense, last in third-down defense, next to last in scoring defense."
Hearing Cowherd compare the Schottenheimer era to the Dave Campo tenure is sure to bring up some bad memories for Dallas fans. That said, it could be a good thing if the Cowboys do hit rock bottom.
As Cowherd pointed out, Jerry Jones is wildly stubborn, especially when it comes to coaches. Ever since Jimmy Johnson got more credit than Jones for their success in the 1990s, Jones has refused to hire a big-name coach. The only exception came when Campo went 5-11 for three consecutive seasons from 2000-2002.
That led to the shocking decision from Jones to hire Bill Parcells. While that hire didn't lead to a Super Bowl run, it helped Dallas rebuild their roster and they were competitive for several seasons, even after Parcells retired.
Perhaps seeing the team hit rock bottom under Schottenheimer will be enough for Jones to actually look for a coach who can make a difference. Then again with Jones, it's also just as likely he keeps selling the fan base on the idea that Schotty is trending in the right direction while ignoring the results on the field.

title: Christian Parker's Job in Danger After Brian Schottenheimer Refuses To Give Vote of Confidence?
full_text:
It seems like everyone has run out of patience when it comes to the Dallas Cowboys' defense, because there has been zero improvement despite making an effort to invest in the unit during the offseason.
From hiring Christian Parker as defensive coordinator to trading for players like Joey Porter Jr. and Dee Winters, along with Quinnen Williams last year, there is just something missing: competent coaching and overall talent. Williams and Porter have done a great job, but the rest of the unit has been miserable throughout the year.
After Sunday evening's collapse against the San Francisco 49ers , chatter about the future of Parker in Dallas was reignited, with many talking heads calling for his job. Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer also ripped the team's defensive performance after the game, while star quarterback Dak Prescott called for changes .
On Monday, with a day to digest the loss, Schottenheimer was asked about the defensive performance, and " refused to give Christian Parker a vote of confidence nor guarantee he would remain as DC," according to Cowboys insider Clarence Hill.
Schotty was asked today about his confidence in Christian Parker remaining as DC after the Cowboys defense allowed a franchise record 584 total yards at home. His answer: #dallascowboys pic.twitter.com/Wp4xbMnOZ9
"At the end of the day, the tackling and some of the covered stuff really led to the [explosive plays]," Schottenheimer said. " I'm taking a deep dive and looking at everything . "
Dallas' defense allowed the most yards in a single game at home in franchise history , while giving up a 70+ yard passing touchdown and a 70+ yard rushing touchdown for the first time. It was a brutal performance all around.
It's clear that something needs to chang in Dallas, so we'll have to see whether the team gives Parker an opportunity to change that or whether he will have to fall on the sword.
Total Defense: The Dallas Cowboys are officially the worst defense in the league, ranking No. 32 overall. The team allows 393.8 yards per game and has given up 33 total touchdowns, behind only the Las Vegas Raiders (36) and Arizona Cardinals (35).
Pass Defense: The Cowboys surprisingly don't have the worst pass defense in the league, ranking No. 26 after allowing 239.7 yards per game and 19 touchdowns.
Run Defense : Dallas is back at the bottom of the barrel when it comes to the team's ability to stop the run, allowing 154.1 yards per game and a league-high 14 rushing touchdowns.

title: Stephen Jones Addresses Job Security of Dallas Cowboys Coaching Staff
full_text:
Another loss has the Dallas Cowboys sitting at 4-6 . As has been the case in every loss, as well as some of their victories, the Dallas coaching staff was completely outclassed .
Offensively, Dallas had to scratch and claw for every yard , putting up the ugliest 40-point performance you will ever see. Defensively, they had no answers for the San Francisco 49ers as Kyle Shanahan proved what a true elite play-caller looks like. Throughout the game, he was thinking two steps ahead of Christian Parker, leading to an epic rant from Michael Irvin .
In addition to criticism from former players, the latest loss again has head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker in the hot seat. Questions are flying about their job security once again, and Stephen Jones was asked about the calls for their job on Monday. Jones, who was a guest on 105.3 The Fan, said he understands the frustration, while calling their recent performance unacceptable.
“I certainly understand their frustration because there’s no doubt that we’re frustrated. We feel like the way we’re playing ball right now is unacceptable. Our fans certainly deserve better," Jones said.
Cowboys EVP Stephen Jones when asked on @1053thefan about fans calling for Brian Schottenheimer’s and Christian Parker’s jobs: “I certainly understand their frustration because there’s no doubt that we’re frustrated. We feel like the way we’re playing ball right now is…
Jones elabortated more, and pointed the finger at Parker, saying the Cowboys are going in the wrong direction on defense.
"At the end of the day we’re not doing what it takes to win these football games. At times you feel like things are going in a good direction and then you have a second half, especially on the defensive side of the ball where you feel like you take one step forward, three steps back," Jones said on 105.3 The Fan . This is obviously very frustrating. As this season goes, we’re making things very difficult on us to stay in the hunt.”
It's beyond frustrating to see the way the defense plays, and it seems everyone is turning on Parker. That said, the head coach oversees everything and it's time to put the blame where it belongs, on Schottenheimer, who oversaw a terrible defense in 2025 but was absolved of guilt.
Following this latest defensive letdown, Jones tried to sound upset by using the term "unacceptable," but those words fall flat without action. While he might think he's sending a strong message, the only way to truly prove that failure is unacceptable is to move on from it.
After 10 weeks into his second season as the head coach, it's painfully clear that Schottenheimer has failed as a head coach. We can continue to point the finger at Parker, but even more blame should fall on Schottenheimer.
Not only was Parker his guy, but the defense was just as bad the prior year with Matt Eberflus calling plays. And if we're being honest, the offense isn't that good. Sure, they put up a lot of points, but Schottenheimer's play-calling is predictable and lacks creativity.
Nearly every yard comes from the players winning one-on-one matchups, which is why every play seems to be so difficult for them. If this offense wasn't full of All-Pro talent, they would struggle to score 14 points per game under Coach Schotty.
Despite these glaring coaching flaws, Jones' words still ring hollow. He claims this type of play is unacceptable. However, the Cowboys keep rolling out a coaching staff that is being embarrassed week after week, sending the message that this poor performance is perfectly acceptable.

title: Dallas Cowboys Highest & Lowest Graded Players from Week 10 Defeat
full_text:
Somehow, the Dallas Cowboys found themselves within striking distance of the San Francisco 49ers near the end of the fourth quarter, but fell short . The 46-40 loss was frustrating, and if we're being honest, it never should have been that close.
The 49ers dominated every phase in this one and their coaching staff was light years ahead of the Cowboys'. Still, some individual performances, especially on offense, made it exciting at the end.
Despite the best efforts of Dak Prescott and company, the defensive shortcomings were too much to overcome. For proof of that, we just need to check out the highest and lowest-rated players from Week 10, which is full of underperforming defenders.
Right now, Quinnen Williams is on a tear and he came close to making a potential game-winning play when he forced a fumble on the final drive for the 49ers. It was recovered by San Francisco, but Williams continues to shine. Imagining this defense without him is absolutely frightening.
He was joined in the top five by rookie defensive lineman LT Overton, who had three tackles and a sack. Overton has been a pleasant surprise this season and could be carving out a long-term role.
On offense, CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens were both excellent. Pickens led the way with 145 yards and three touchdowns while Lamb had 72 yards and a touchdown. The best offensive player, according to PFF, was Tyler Guyton. The third-year left tackle was dominant with an 83.8 and had an 89.7 in run blocking .
This looks bad at first glance to see the five lowest-graded players all on defense, but don't worry, it was actually much worse. In fact, the two worst were actually DeMarvion Overshown with a 27.5 and DaRon Bland with a 28.1, but since they both had fewer than 10 snaps, they were left off the list. There were also 11 total defenders who had scores lower than the worst-rated offensive player, which was Luke Schoonmaker (49.0).
That said, you don't need to look further than this to see why the Cowboys lost. While the interior of their defensive line got plenty of push and generated pressure, their most experienced pass-rusher was a no-show. Even worse, the defenders who covered the middle of the field were all awful, including slot cornerback Caleb Downs, who had an abysmal 30.1 overall .

title: Cowboys Superfan Post Malone Delivers Expletive-Laden Rant After Loss to 49ers
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys fans are extremely frustrated with the current state of their team and a rant from music superstar Post Malone perfectly encapsulates that frustration.
The latest source of anger for Cowboys fans came from the Week 10 game with the San Francisco 49ers, when Dallas' defense was at its worst all season after allowing a season-high 46 points.
We fully expected the Cowboys to lose that game against an elite team, and they didn't disappoint.
It was yet another reminder that this Cowboys team isn't anywhere near the upper-echelon of teams in the league
Following that depressing effort, Malone took to social media to vent his frustration with how things are going this season.
"I'm absolutely f****** furious right now," Malone stated. "There's no reason... no f****** reason why we have the best team in the f****** league and we don't win f****** football games. I don't understand."
"600 f****** yards," Malone added. "(Dak Prescott) threw five f****** touchdown passes today and we don't win f****** football games. We're better than the rest of the f****** league."
The Cowboys didn't give up exactly 600 yards, but they did give up a ridiculous 584, which amounts to the most Dallas has given up in a home game in team history.
While we would firmly disagree with Malone that the Cowboys are the best team in the league, we do agree with his statement that there needs to be change in Dallas.
"Something's gotta change over in Dallas and I don't know what it is. I love my boys more than f****** life itself, but holy f****** s***, something needs to change."
The needed change is obvious. The Cowboys must fire both head coach Brian Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker, both of whom have shown no indication they are the right coaches to right the ship in Dallas.
The silver lining for Malone? The awful division the Cowboys are in, which still gives them hope for at least a playoff berth through that avenue.
"But, at least our division f****** sucks," he added. "I love you boys, don't give up, but something has to f****** change."
The division is really the only hope the Cowboys have to snap their two-year playoff drought with so many good teams ahead of them in the playoff race, but they have a lot of work to do.
Dallas trails the New York Giants by three in the loss column, and what made Sunday's loss even worse was that it squandered an opportunity for the Cowboys to gain ground on the Giants, who lost to the Washington Commanders on Thursday.
The good news is, the Giants have the fourth-toughest strength of schedule in the NFL the rest of the way while the Cowboys have the eighth-easiest, according to Tankathon .
But, as we've seen in losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Arizona Cardinals, and the razor-thin win over the Indianapolis Colts, there is no such thing as an easy win for the Cowboys.
And, even if they manage to overcome that deficit and win the NFC East, there is just no way Dallas is going to make it past the first round, so a playoff berth is only delaying the inevitable.

title: Dallas Cowboys Legend Blasts Christian Parker After Brutal Coaching Mismatch
full_text:
Stop me if you’ve heard this one before. The Dallas Cowboys were absolutely embarrassed on the defensive side of the ball this weekend.
Offensively, they did everything they could as they dropped 40 points on the San Francisco 49ers while Dak Prescott threw five touchdown passes . It wasn’t enough, however, as the defense gave up 46 points including two touchdowns of at least 70 yards and one from 66 yards out.
It was clear throughout the day that San Francisco was the better coached team as they continued to find ways to make the plays when needed. They racked up 584 yards of offense and killed Dallas with the run and pass. The 49ers had 370 yards passing and 214 rushing. It was a thorough enough beating that Cowboys legend Michael Irvin put defensive coordinator Christian Parker on blast.
According to Irvin, it was a complete beating for Parker, as Kyle Shanahan knew exactly what to dial up on every play.
"It was just, it was BAT. I'm talking about Kyle Shanahan putting on Christian Parker. It was BTA. Straight belt to ass in what he did to that defensive coordinator,” Irvin said.
"I'm talking about Kyle Shanahan putting on Christian Parker. It was BTA. Straight belt to ass in what he did to that defensive coordinator" – Michael Irvin on the Dallas Cowboys pic.twitter.com/y50HpOHsdM
Irvin then went on to discuss how Shanahan used misdirection to completely fool the defense on multiple occasions. Shanahan also set up his team for success by selling the power run game with Kaelon Black, only to hit a home run when the defense overcommitted by running a wide receiver reverse.
What made the beatdown feel worse is the fact that 49ers fans took over AT&T Stadium , with this one sounding like a San Francisco home game.
Irvin isn’t alone in his frustration with the defense. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer went off following the loss, saying their performance was “unacceptable.”
"I thought the second half was unacceptable. Tackling was atrocious. And we got to do a deep dive on the film and see why," Schottenheimer said to reporters following the loss. "You can't give up three explosive plays of over 65 yards for touchdowns and expect to win in this league.
"So do a deep dive on the film, see the problems. But yeah, totally unacceptable defense in the second half... At the end of the day, we tackled like sh*t .”
Now at 4-6, the Cowboys are running out of chances to turn things around. They should be favored in Week 11 as they host the 1-8 Tennessee Titans, but even that struggling offense has to be licking its chops while watching the Cowboys’ defensive tape.

title: Cowboys Week 10 Report Card: Dallas' Historically Bad Defense Fails Miserably vs. 49ers
full_text:
Things went about as we expected them to go in the Dallas Cowboys' Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers .
The Cowboys did manage to drop 40 points, but that simply wasn't enough because of a Cowboys defense that might be the worst in team history at this point.
Dallas gave up 584 yards of total offense to the Niners, which is the most the team has given up in a home game in franchise history.
It's even hard to get excited about the offense because Dallas' unit didn't wake up in the second half until it was down three scores.
As you'd imagine, the grades aren't pretty for this one, but that's what Cowboys fans have come to expect this season.
Dak Prescott threw for 343 yards and five touchdowns to one pick and George Pickens had his best game of the season with 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns.
But, lest we forget, the Cowboys' two scores in the first half were both off of big plays and the unit disappeared in the third quarter and only reappeared in the fourth during what was essentially garbage time when Dallas was down three scores.
That's the exact kind of inconsistency we've seen this offense have all season long.
It really was a boom-or-bust day for a Cowboys offense that could not find much consistency or put together methodical drives. The Niners had 11 explosive plays and three scores of 60-plus-yards, yet they still won time of possession by over three minutes.
The Cowboys actually rushed for four yards per carry, something the team hasn't done a lot of this season, so kudos for that, especially against a top-10 run defense.
But Javonte Williams himself did not hit four yards per with 16 carries for 63 yards and the Cowboys running back was really a non-factor in a game in which Dallas needed long, methodical drives to keep the Niners' offense off the field.
The result was a 46-point explosion for San Francisco and another loss for Dallas.
The Cowboys got good pressure on Purdy, especially in the first half, and the pass-rush even notched five sacks, although only a half of those sacks came from an edge rusher (James Houston).
But there were also several instances where the Cowboys didn't get home and Brock Purdy would escape to extend the play and find an open receiver for a big gain, which is not surprising since Dallas can't cover for a short period of time, let alone for an extended period of time.
San Francisco also busted off a handful of explosive plays, two of which went for touchdowns. When it was all said and done, Purdy finished 22-of-28 for 389 yards and three touchdowns.
The Niners enjoyed another handful of explosive plays on the ground and finished with a whopping 214 yards and three touchdowns on 29 carries (7.3 yards per carry).
The duo of Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black were every bit of the challenge we figured it would be , and even Deebo Samuel got in on the fun with his 70-yard touchdown run on a reverse displaying Dallas' complete lack of discipline.
We also saw an embarrassing display of tackling, especially on Black's touchdown run that saw him bulldoze Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.
As a result of their putrid showing, the Cowboys are now back in the cellar as the worst run defense in the NFL.
Brandon Aubrey didn't miss either of his 50-yard field goals, which was good to see because Aubrey had missed five going into the game. However, he did miss an extra point.
KaVontae Turpin was a zero in the punt return game in his first game back with four yards per, and Camden Brown and Israel Abanikanda were decent on kick returns with 23.3 yards per.
In terms of defending kick returns, the Cowboys did a pretty good job in that area with 20.2 yards per return allowed.
There's nothing more that needs to be said about Christian Parker. We've known for weeks now that this hiring has been a failure and the abysmal showing from Dallas' defense on Sunday just reinforced that.
Offensively, that might have been the ugliest 40 points we've ever seen. Week in and week out it just seems like the Cowboys have to scratch and claw for every point they get and head coach Brian Schottenheimer's lack of creativity is abundantly clear.
We also have to call Schottenheimer out for his decision to punt on a fourth-and-2 from near midfield late in the second quarter when it was obvious the Cowboys needed to be much more aggressive in what was going to be a high-scoring game.
Long story short: Dallas might have the worst combination of offensive and defensive play-callers in the NFL and change is desperately needed.

title: Tyler Booker Injury Update After Week 10 Loss is Tough Blow For Cowboys' Offense
full_text:
The hits just keep on coming for the Dallas Cowboys, who are set to be without a key offensive player for what could be as long as a month or more.
During the Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , the Cowboys saw guard Tyler Booker exit early after 33 snaps due to an ankle injury .
And it isn't just a minor injury, either. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Booker has been diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which can be a four to six week injury.
However, Rapoport notes that the hope is Booker will be back within four weeks.
"Cowboys G Tyler Booker suffered a high-ankle sprain in his team's loss to the 49ers, sources say," Rapoport reported on Monday.
"While it's generally a 4-6 week injury, the hope is that Booker can be back within that 4 week window," Rapoport added. "Last year, a similar injury kept him out three games."
The good thing for the Cowboys is that there will be a bye week in Week 14 after the next three games, so Booker will have an extra week to get right without missing another game.
The big reason why it's important Booker avoids IR has to do with the fact that they can only bring back so many players off the list in a single season.
The Cowboys have three more return designations left, as Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reported, and they have guys like running back Tyler Goodson, edge rusher Malachi Lawrence and safety Jalen Thompson still on the list.
So, if Booker misses more than three games and you're wondering why they didn't just place him on IR, there's your answer.
Booker has been phenomenal once again this season and it will be no small task to replace him.
According to Pro Football Focus , Booker has the best run-block grade in the NFL among guards with a 90.4, and his pass-block grade is a respectable 65.6 and he has not given up any sacks while allowing just 12 pressures.
As we saw on Sunday, the Cowboys will replace Booker with T.J. Bass, who was the replacement for Tyler Smith when he was injured at the start of the season .
Bass has proven to be a very reliable backup once again this season, with the veteran posting the 16th-best run-blocking grade (72.0), per PFF, and the 39th-best pass-blocking grade (60.7). Bass has not given up a sack and has allowed only 12 pressures.
As always, Bass leaves the Cowboys in a better position than most other teams would be in the same situation.

title: Did Dak Prescott Take Shot At Dallas Cowboys Coaching Staff After Week 10 Collapse?
full_text:
All eyes were on the Dallas Cowboys' defense after a miserable performance against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10, including an epic collapse in the second half.
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer ripped Christian Parker's unit during his post-game press conference, and star quarterback Dak Prescott was also clearly frustrated with the way things played out on Sunday evening.
After the game, Prescott sat in front of the media to answer several questions about the team's letdown at AT&T Stadium, making it clear that the status quo just isn't cutting it .
While Prescott does believe that the Cowboys have some pieces in place to have a successful team, there are clear changes that he believes need to happen in Dallas. The question is: what changes are Prescott looking for?
Safe to say Dak feels things need to look different in Dallas. pic.twitter.com/h6aPVoAmCA
While Prescott didn't say it outright, it sure seems like he would be open to changes to the coaching staff. That's the impression several members of Cowboys Nation received as well.
“Things gotta get better. Simple as that," Prescott said. "I truly believe we have the people, but something’s gotta change. We've got to find a way to change. Whatever it takes, individually. Whatever it takes is an organization . We gotta find a way to be better."
The Cowboys aren't a team that is keen on making midseason coaching changes, but if the team is unable to turn things around before the bye week, there are serious conversations that will need to be had.
Dallas has two very winnable games at home to finish off November, a Week 11 showdown against the ailing Tennessee Titans and a Thanksgiving Day clash against the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles, so it's the perfect opportunity for the team to show some improvements.
Jerry Jones' patience seems to be wearing thin, so if the Cowboys miss out on the postseason for a third straight year, we could see either Brian Schottenheimer or Christian Parker sent packing.
It's a crucial time for the team and coaching staff, so we'll have to see over the next few weeks whether they are ready to answer the call.

title: Super Bowl Champion DC Destroys 'Garbage' Christian Parker & Cowboys Defensive Staff
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered a brutal reality in the team's Week 10 loss to the San Francisco 49ers . It may be time to admit that defensive coordinator Christian Parker is in over his head .
Dallas had no answers for the 49ers offense in the second half, and gave up a whopping 29 points. The team allowed 584 total yards of offense throughout the game, which is the most allowed at home in franchise history .
People are taking notice, especially after the embarrassing effort on a 70+ yard Deebo Samuel touchdown on a reverse.
DEEBO LEFT THEM IN THE DUST 💨 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/jWJ7pgBTUb
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer ripped the unacceptable performance during his postgame press conference, while star quarterback Dak Prescott called for changes to be made.
On Monday morning, the criticism of Parker and his defense continued, with ESPN's Rex Ryan, who won a Super Bowl leading the Baltimore Ravens defense, sounded off on the entire defensive staff in Dallas with an epic rant.
“This is the worst coached defense I think I’ve ever seen.” 😳 Rex Ryan with some words on the Cowboys after yesterday’s loss to the 49ers. pic.twitter.com/j7ehsnmJVk
When it came time to share his thoughts on the Cowboys' defensive struggles, Ryan did not hold back.
"Christian Parker? Really? Like, to me, that's the worst coached defense I think I've ever seen . Period. And I'm trying to be nice, whatever. What did I say? Sunday Countdown , I said, if you do too much, if you're multiple in this game, this is not the team to do that against," Ryan said. "They were just like, let's try this defense. Let's try this defense. Let's try this, like, whatever defense we can try... No. 1, the guy has no feel for the game. He doesn't know when to call things, when not to call things.
"Forget this. And I'm so sick and tired of it. These players, they act like, well, the players aren't good. Well, they were pretty good when you got them. Yeah. Why the hell aren't they good now? ... So to me, absolute garbage. You know, you can't fire them all yet, but you're damn sure better. And to me, it's the whole defensive staff. It's just not Christian Parker, okay? It's not. It's every one of those coaches on defense."
These are the kinds of harsh criticisms the Cowboys (and Jerry Jones) need to hear, because sugarcoating the reality of the situation in Dallas has done nothing to help the team over the past few years.
Christian Parker came to the Cowboys with a lot of hype, but he has failed to deliver. He hasn't even shown the ability to adjust his game plan to the flow of the game, which Ryan highlighted. After Sunday night's brutal collapse, Parker will certainly be under the microscope, and if things don't get better, we may see the Cowboys with a new defensive coordinator for the fourth consecutive year.

title: Broncos Could Dodge a Major Bullet This Week Against Raiders
full_text:
The Denver Broncos' struggles to cover opposing tight ends dates back years. In fairness, though, as NFL tight ends have become more athletic and explosive, they've become an increasingly featured aerial component, so covering the position is a challenge for all defenses.
It just so happens that Denver has been one of the worst defenses at covering tight ends, and that includes this season. The Broncos have given up the second-most receiving yards to tight ends entering Week 10, and with the Las Vegas Raiders coming to town this week, the issue may again take center stage, especially in the wake of the failed Daiyan Henley trade .
Kirk Cousins is now calling the signals in Minnesota, pushing rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza into the starting lineup this week. Raiders tight ends Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer accounted for more than 1,000 of Cousins's passing yards this season before he was dealt to the Vikings.
Mendoza targeted his tight ends just six times in his first career start against the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, but a big reason for that was Bowers suffering an early ankle injury that kept him out of the second half, finishing with just two receptions for 18 yards.
The Broncos may not have to worry about Bowers this week, as head coach Klint Kubiak revealed on Monday that his star tight end's injury is "significant," even if it isn't as bad as the Raiders feared.
"It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak told The Athletic 's Sam Warren on Monday .
Bowers is "day to day," per Kubiak, so Denver has to plan for the Pro Bowl tight end, just in case. It will be interesting to see how the practice reports for Week 11 take shape, beginning on Wednesday.
Mendoza will be making just his second NFL start this week against the Broncos. That's a tough row to hoe for any quarterback — regardless of whether he's the No. 1 overall pick in the draft — having to face the Seattle and Denver defenses back-to-back to begin his career as a starter. I don't envy the former Heisman Trophy winner.
If Mendoza must face the Broncos without his security blanket, Bowers, he's likely to still look his tight ends' way early and often. Kubiak knows how his bread gets buttered and will likely test the Broncos' leaky tight end coverage when the Raiders are in their base offense, attacking linebackers Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad.
Singleton is having one of the best years of his career, but he's struggled mightily in coverage. Teams have identified that and schemed to isolate Singleton in coverage . Strnad is better in coverage, but in relative terms.
Neither is an ideal candidate to run with Bowers, Mayer, or Ian Thomas, so Broncos defensive coordinator Vance Joseph will need alternative plans of attack if the Raiders start attacking with tight ends.
Mendoza will trust Mayer and Thomas if Bowers is unable to go, as he told Hondo Carpenter of Las Vegas Raiders On SI .
"So the next guy up, I have as much confidence in, and so I just need to get the ball to the right players on time, efficiently and accurately," Mendoza told Carpenter.
The Broncos need a better coverage plan moving forward because they're giving up way too many yards, and not just to tight ends. No NFL team have up more receiving yards to running backs entering Week 10 than Denver, and guess who Mendoza's stop target was against Seattle?
You guessed it: running back Ashton Jeanty. Mendoza connected with Jeanty on all four of his targets for 46 yards against Seattle, and once with rookie running back Mike Washington.
Joseph has, at times, deployed cornerback Jahdae Barron as a tight-end eraser, with varying degrees of success. Most of Barron's one-on-one wins against tight ends came last year as a rookie; nobody in Denver has done a good job of blanketing tight ends this season.
Whether Bowers plays or not, you can expect Kubiak and Mendoza to target the middle of Denver's defense with running backs and tight ends. The Broncos were well aware of this vulnerability, which is why they tried to trade for Henley — an experienced linebacker who excels in coverage — but the deal with the Los Angeles Chargers fell through when he failed his physical .
With the NFL trade deadline in the books, the Broncos' linebacker personnel is what it is. To improve against tight ends in coverage, it's going to require some Xs and Os adjustments by Joseph, and maybe some additional help from the secondary players.
If the Broncos can limit the tight ends and backs in the passing game and stop Jeanty and Washington as runners, it could be a long day for Mendoza, making his second career start. We'll keep a close eye on Bowers's status on the practice reports as the week progresses, so keep it locked with Denver Broncos On SI .

title: Sean Payton Pinpoints What's Holding Broncos Back Ahead of Stretch Run
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 7-2, but head coach Sean Payton knows some things need to change coming out of the bye.
The Broncos were back in the building on Monday, and in the first team meeting since Week 9's road win over the Carolina Panthers, Payton laid out to the players "certain areas" that need to improve moving forward.
“Specifically, I mentioned this last week, we need to block better on offense and we need to be in the right place," Payton said on Monday morning. "I thought we did an average job against Carolina, and I think that’s an area of focus relative to more consistency in our run game."
The Broncos' run game has failed to launch this season, and the only thing keeping it out of the NFL doldrums has been the emergence of rookie running back Jonah Coleman, since he returned from injured reserve in Week 7. J.K. Dobbins has struggled as a ball-carrier, but the Broncos' biggest issue has been their run blocking, whether it's the offensive line or the tight ends.
Payton sounds much more forgiving of the Broncos' blocking foibles in Carolina now than he did a couple of days after the game. On Wednesday of last week, Payton appeared on The Herd with Colin Cowherd, pointing to the Broncos' run-blocking woes vs. Carolina, and hinting that personnel changes could be in store as he and the coaches drilled down on the subject over the bye.
In Monday's Zoom presser , though, Payton was a bit dismissive of the potential for personnel changes on the offensive line, doing his level best to walk back his comments to Cowherd.
“I don’t think there’s any tie to the interview last week with Colin. I just want to make sure we’re clear," Payton said. "I think in that interview, I made sure to make a point about evaluating all assets of what we’re doing in our front in the offense. So I want to make sure one story doesn’t lead to another. We’ll spend an inordinate amount of time looking at mid-season cutups where we’re at relative to scheme and personnel.”
I'll say it again, just as I wrote last week, the Broncos were always extremely unlikely to bench one of their O-line starters. This team is proud of the fact that it returned the same starting five for the third straight season, and it has a lot of money invested up front; the problem is that Denver has been completely unable to capitalize on such a football blessing.
The Broncos rank 26th in rushing, averaging 91.4 yards per game on the ground through nine weeks. Again, Coleman has moved the needle, and while that's been encouraging, the rookie can't be expected to elevate the Broncos' entire rushing offense on his own. He needs help, and that's, ostensibly, what Payton and run game coordinator Zach Strief spent a lot of time on over the bye.
The Broncos' pass protection early in the season wasn't on par with the previous couple of years, with Bo Nix taking pressure at a career-high rate, but they turned that ship around starting in Week 5 when Payton took back the play-calling responsibilities from first-year offensive coordinator Davis Webb. Since then, the Broncos have done well in protecting Nix; he remains one of the NFL's toughest quarterbacks to sack.
Speaking of Nix, he's taken some big leaps forward since Payton took back the play sheet, but he really began to build momentum in Week 7. Nix's 62-yard touchdown run against the Arizona Cardinals seemed to unlock something in his return from offseason ankle surgery, and his confidence came flooding back.
Nix has thrown for over 200 passing yards in each of the past three games, which, on the surface, isn't exactly an illustration of a quarterback blowing the doors down, but compared to the four sub-200-yard passing days he had between Weeks 1 and 6. If the Broncos can get the ground game truly rolling, it'll open up all kinds of passing opportunities for Nix, especially in the play-action game.
"The run game hasn't been great. It's something we need as an offense, [that] Bo needs as a quarterback, we need some play-action. It just ties everything in," tight end Adam Trautman said on Monday via 9NEWS ' Mike Klis . "That's our biggest emphasis on offense and we're working to get it fixed."
Payton and the coaches dove deep into the run-game subject over the bye, we can assume with confidence. With the players back in the building to prepare for Sunday's home game against the Las Vegas Raiders, now it's time for the coaches to begin implementing the points of emphasis they discovered over the bye.
Payton is looking for improvements on defense, too. Vance Joseph's unit has been great at rushing the passer and has established itself as one of the NFL's best clutch-time defenses, but Payton demands better execution on third and fourth down.
"Then there were some third-down, fourth-down-and-longs defensively that was an Achilles heel for us a year ago, and the other day became one," Payton said. "Those are just a few things.”
The Broncos rank 21st in third-down efficiency, allowing conversions on 41.2% of opponents' attempts. That's actually an improved mark, compared to where the Broncos ranked for much of the season on third down, so there's reason to believe the improvements have already begun.
On fourth down, the Broncos' defense ranks 20th, allowing conversions 58.8% of the time. Teams are going for it on fourth down more frequently in the modern NFL, and the Broncos will need to improve this area of defense for their stretch run into the playoffs.
The Broncos are 7-2 for a reason. This defense keeps most games close, buying Nix and the still fledgling offense the time to come together and finish strong in the fourth quarter.
Payton would still prefer not to be in so many one-score games, his team's success in them notwithstanding. Denver's early-season gauntlet of a schedule played a big role in some if the inefficiencies Payton addressed in his Zoom presser.
With the schedule opening up now, it's time for the Broncos to prove they can make use of the callus they built up from going against the NFL's toughest first-half-of-the-season schedule. Next up, it's Fernando Mendoza — the No. 1 overall pick in the draft — and the 4-6 Raiders.

title: Sean Payton Pushes Back on Chargers' Accusations: 'There's No Loophole'
full_text:
The botched Daiyan Henley trade has garnered no small amount of scrutiny and criticism around the NFL, intensified by Los Angeles Rams head coach Jim Harbaugh's complaint that a " loophole " in the rulebook allowed the Denver Broncos to ask for a lesser compensation package after the linebacker failed his physical.
Some have all but accused Denver of operating in bad faith, or at the very least, trying to exploit a post-deadline opportunity, while L.A. had no other options, given that the deadline had passed.
In his regular Monday morning Zoom press conference, Broncos head coach Sean Payton declined to go into detail about the trade that never was, but he did dismiss Harbaugh's "loophole" critique.
“I saw it all. There’s no loophole," Payton said. "It just is part of the trade process every step of the way.”
Payton's morning presser began with a question about what had changed with the in-principle trade agreement Denver had with L.A. for Henley.
“Nothing changed. It was already stated," Payton said on Monday. "Everything was pretty clearly spelled out. I’m not going to get into the specifics. He’s a prospect we thought—and still do [think]—very highly of. It just didn’t work out and it’s not uncommon with trades. That’s kind of where it went, and I’ll leave it at that.”
Payton wasn't interested in stirring the pot, but he came prepared on Monday, knowing that it was the media's first chance to get a Broncos shot-caller on the record regarding the Henley trade. But Payton's a savvy guy who'd been around the NFL block, so he offered nothing really, besides "there's no loophole."
It's important to remember that both the Broncos and the Chargers spoke with the NFL front office after Henley failed his physical in Denver. The Broncos sought clarity on what their rights were and whether they could ask to amend their offer to L.A. for Henley, while the Chargers needed to hear from the NFL that Denver had the right to do so.
It didn't go anywhere, and the trade was canceled. That was that. It disappointed Broncos fans, though, that's for sure.
Henley returned to L.A. and promptly practiced in full on Thursday and Friday, with no restrictions or limitations on his puportedly arthritic knee that so scared the Broncos. That only enflamed fans who were trying to understand how bad Henley's knee must have been to cause Denver to back out of the trade.
Daiyan Henley was a full participant in the Chargers' two final practices of the week after his brief sojourn to the Mile High City. Playing on that arthritic knee, no problem, it would seem. *Sigh* pic.twitter.com/FBirY7OTAu
Cynics said, "Well, of course Henley practiced in full. The Chargers would have listed him as a full regardless just to score points in the PR arena." I'm not so sure.
One thing we know is that Denver really likes Henley. Payton's comments further reinforced that, so if the Chargers are unable to get him re-signed between now and the new league year in March, expect the Broncos to pursue him in free agency.
The Broncos saw Henley as more than a short-term rental, which is why they were willing to give up a fourth- and fifth-round pick to acquire him, and were still willing to offer up the fourth-rounder and an additional pick after he failed his physical, just not a fifth-rounder, from what I've gleaned.
It's all water under the bridge now. What hasn't changed since the botched Henley trade is Denver's need for a coverage linebacker . Going into Week 10, the Broncos had allowed the most receiving yards to running backs in the NFL, and the second-most yardage to tight ends.
This team will now have to figure out how to solve that problem with the horses it has. The Las Vegas Raiders are up next, as the Broncos emerge from their bye week.
Whether it's been Kirk Cousins or Fernando Mendoza, the Raiders like targeting their tight ends and running backs in the passing game, so let's hope Vance Joseph has a good plan in place when the Broncos host their long-time division rival on Sunday at Mile High.
