title: 5 Unsung Broncos Who've Made Their Case to Stay in 2027
full_text:
The Denver Broncos currently have 25 players set to hit free agency after the 2026 season ends. Some of Denver's free agents will be unrestricted, while others will be of the restricted and exclusive-rights variety.
The Broncos have several key players who could be extended before the 2026 season ends , though with the bye week ending without such a deal, the likelihood has diminished. However, looking past this season, the Broncos have several players who should be retained in 2027 for low-cost deals, even if some of them are better suited as depth or special teams.
These players don't need to be extended before the end of the season, but they should be up for either restricted free-agent tenders or short-term deals as free agency is about to get underway in the spring.
With half the season in the books, let's examine five such players who shouldn't be overlooked when the Broncos start making decisions in 2027.
Key is set to become a restricted free agent in 2027. The Broncos could go in one of two directions: tender him at the second-round level or sign him to a short-term deal.
The second-round tender is estimated at $6.26 million, which is a bit high for a depth and special -teams player, even though Key has been decorated as a third-phase All-Pro. However, if Denver tendered him at the original-round level, another team could sign him to an offer sheet.
The best move for the Broncos is to sign Key to a two-year deal. The original-round tender is $3.82 million, but the Broncos could come in between the two tender levels and give Key, say, a two-year, $9.5 million deal as a reward for his contributions over the past two seasons.
Adkins was a restricted free agent in 2026 whom the Broncos signed to a one-year deal at the veteran minimum. He made the 53-man roster and has proven to be a good blocking tight end and a solid pass-catcher.
The Broncos would be wise to retain Adkins, who might get more than the veteran minimum this time around. A possibility could be a two-year, $7.5 million deal, similar to what Adam Trautman got in 2024.
Speaking of Trautman, it will be difficult to move on from him in 2027 because of his guaranteed money, but the Broncos could cut him in 2028 without much trouble. Keeping Adkins in the fold would give the Broncos an option to eventually take over Trautman's role in the offense.
Tillman is set to become a restricted free agent in 2027. He has proven to be valuable depth on defense, particularly when Jonathon Cooper missed time on the commissioner's exempt list to start the season.
In Tillman's case, the second-round tender would be fine, as $6.26 million is a reasonable salary to pay for what he brings to the defense. But the Broncos could opt for a two-year deal here as well.
A two-year deal for $10 million might be possible and a way to recognize Tillman for his contributions and continued role. It would also allow the Broncos to keep the edge rusher around for more than one season.
It might seem odd to list Badie here, but let's look at the facts. J.K. Dobbins might not be with the Broncos in 2027 , and though Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey would form a good pairing, the team still needs reliable depth.
Badie would give the Broncos an experienced back who could be the No. 3 or No. 4 option in the backfield, particularly with his pass-blocking ability, and would be a much cheaper alternative to Dobbins, who is due $8 million in 2027. Badie has also been good on special teams.
Badie will be a restricted free agent and isn't worth the second-round tender, but the Broncos should be able to keep him for the veteran minimum.
Skinner has had a few highlights on defense , but his play hasn't been good enough to warrant a starting role. However, he's been valuable on special teams.
While the Broncos do have seventh-round pick Miles Scott on the practice squad, they should keep Skinner around because of his experience. That would put less pressure on Scott to fill an immediate hole in 2027.
Skinner will be an unrestricted free agent, and like Badie, is a player the Broncos should be able to retain at the veteran minimum.

title: 5 Broncos Veterans Whose 2027 Futures Are Suddenly in Doubt
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have a handful of veterans whose future may be in question after this season, even though they're under contract next year, and in some cases, beyond.
The Broncos aren’t in a bad salary-cap situation, with $29.5 million in cap space projected in 2027. However, that 2027 figure accounts for just 38 players under contract, so some of that cap space will be taken up by players signed to futures contracts after this season ends.
The Broncos also have some players with expiring contracts they might want to extend, as well as restricted free agents to decide on, so they will need to find ways to clear cap space for 2027.
With that imperative in mind, there are five Broncos whose 2027 contract status is currently in question, three of whom might be asked to convert base salary into incentives. One is trending toward being released, while another's future is dependent on a criminal case against him that is still pending.
Let's break each one down.
McGlinchey's run blocking has always been reliable, but pass protection is his weakness. He was good overall in 2025, but his play has slipped this season .
The Broncos have already shown they will renegotiate with an offensive lineman in the final year of his contract, as they did with left guard Ben Powers . But Powers missed much of 2025 with a biceps injury, while McGlinchey has played all but four games since joining the Broncos in 2023.
Also, the Broncos aren't in a great position regarding potential McGlinchey replacements already on the roster. Alex Palczewski has some experience at right tackle, but now seems to be viewed as a guard, while Frank Crum — who's been on injured reserve all season — may be better suited to the left side of the line.
Still, there's a chance the Broncos will approach McGlinchey about reducing his $16.99 million base salary and converting some of it into incentives. Even if they don't, the Broncos need to draft an offensive tackle who can eventually compete for the right tackle job.
Jones has been a solid player for most of his time with the Broncos, but it's fair to ask whether he's worth the $12.235 million base salary he's due in 2027.
I've previously suggested that Jones is a candidate to have his base salary converted into incentives next season. His play this season hasn't been bad, but the Broncos have more depth on the defensive line, with Malcolm Roach and Tyler Onyedim — both younger players — being good against the run.
As evidenced by his four sacks this season, Roach is also a good pass rusher, while Onyedim has potential there.
It might make sense to approach Jones about renegotiating his base salary to convert it into incentives, but his play hasn't reached the point where the Broncos would have to cut him if he doesn't renegotiate.
Sutton is due a $19.325 million base salary for 2027, $10 million of which will become fully guaranteed if he's on the roster on March 10, 2027. The Broncos already chose not to exercise his option bonus for 2026 , with that money being paid out as base salary instead.
The option-bonus decision might indicate the Broncos are prepared to move on from Sutton in 2027 if it comes down to that. It doesn't help that at the midway point, he's on pace for a career-low season, with just 25 receptions on 46 targets for 266 yards (10.6 avg) and two touchdowns.
A straight cut would free $10.225 million in cap space, with a $15.85 million dead-money charge, while a post-June 1 designation would free up $20 million (but not until after June 1), with $6.075 million dead. A trade can't be ruled out, but a trade would take immediate effect on the salary cap.
In Sutton's case, it would make sense to ask him to convert some of his base salary into incentives in exchange for more than $10 million becoming fully guaranteed. That would free up some space and still allow the Broncos to easily move on from him in 2028.
Dobbins signed a two-year extension during the offseason, but he hasn't played well. Between his play and the Broncos' other running back injuries, the team explored trading for a running back before last week's deadline.
As things stand, this will be the easiest decision the Broncos will make in 2027. Cutting Dobbins would free $8 million in cap space with just a $2 million dead-money charge.
An offseason trade can't be ruled out, but if it doesn't happen, all signs point to Dobbins being released.
Cooper missed six games on the commissioner's exempt list due to a criminal case he was charged with this past summer, but he's still awaiting trial. His trial was postponed, and he was activated ahead of Week 7.
Cooper's outlook depends on what happens in the jury trial. If he's found guilty, the Broncos may opt to release him, likely with a post-June 1 designation, to save $13.5 million in cap space with a $4.055 million dead-money charge.
If Cooper is exonerated, the Broncos will likely keep him. If that's how it shakes out, Denver is unlikely to ask him to renegotiate his salary.

title: Jensen's Judgment: Broncos Fans Wanted a RB Trade, But George Paton Knew Better
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were heavily linked to Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of last Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Instead of a backfield weapon, the Broncos ended up agreeing to a trade for Los Angeles Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley, though the deal fell through after he failed his physical.
It makes you wonder how interested the Broncos really were in running backs, and how much of it was a smokescreen to throw teams off ahead of the deadline. All the Taylor rumors led to speculation in the blogosphere and on social media about several other running backs and whether the Broncos might also be interested in them.
Tony Pollard was one of those running backs. Before the deadline, there wasn't solid reporting on the Broncos being interested in Pollard, but that was then.
Now, a few days after the deadline, we know the Broncos were actually interested in Pollard. According to ESPN 's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport , the Broncos "checked in" on Pollard, but the Tennessee Titans' asking price of a third-round pick scared them off.
It's curious that the Titans wouldn't part with Pollard for anything less than a third-rounder. He's in the final season of the three-year, $21.75 million contract Tennessee gave him, which means that, if he departs in free agency in the offseason, the Titans can expect to get a compensatory draft pick back from the league.
But a third-rounder? Not likely for a running back who will be turning 30 shortly after the 2027 free-agency window opens. He's playing at a high level this season, but at his age, he's unlikely to be offered a contract next year that'll put him in the top-35% salary threshold at his position.
It's possible if Pollard stays healthy and continues to produce at high level for Tennessee's guttering offense. But whether he'd return a comp pick to Tennessee at all — let alone a third-rounder (the highest possible) — will also be dependent on how the Titans spend in free agency.
When it comes to Taylor, the Broncos reportedly backed away when the Colts began asking for first-round value. Barring that, Indy was looking for Christian McCaffrey-type compensation.
The San Francisco 49ers gave the Carolina Panthers a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick for McCaffrey back in 2022, but he was younger then than Taylor is now and nowhere near as close to the 2,000-carry milestone.
If the Colts had been more reasonable with their asking price, the Broncos likely would have been more serious about Taylor. Alas, for Colts fans, the team's decision robbed them of the chance to add to their rebuild war chest. Taylor will turn 30 after next season.
The Broncos made the right call in not paying through the nose to acquire a running back. Giving up a third-round draft pick for a soon-to-be 30-year-old running back in a contract year, when the Broncos have two young players on the rise — Jonah Coleman and RJ Harvey — would have been questionable.
Pollard would have certainly helped the Broncos' offense in what remains of this season, but he would have been a short-term rental. The third-round draft pick is more valuable to the Broncos in the grand scheme of things.
Don't get me wrong; Pollard is having a big season, with 595 rushing yards and six touchdowns. He's on pace to post his fourth straight 1,000-yard rushing season, with a legitimate chance at resetting his career high (1,082 yards).
But at the end of the day, the Broncos believe they have the horses in the running back stable (pardon the pun) to turn the rushing ship around down the stretch, and that includes J.K. Dobbins. Denver knows that fixing the blocking up front is likely to be the catalyst to maximizing the investments it has already made in the backfield.
Harvey was a second-round pick. Coleman was a fourth-rounder. The Broncos are paying Dobbins $8 million this year. And they made these investments for a reason, believing they had the foundation in the trenches to make some hay with these backs.
Sean Payton's remarks to Colin Cowherd earlier this week, the day after the trade deadline, hinted at how the Broncos view their lack of rushing success as a team this season. It's more of a blocking deficiency than a talent shortage at running back.
Sure, given the Broncos' blocking issues up front, it would have been nice to add another running back like Coleman who could create for himself, but with the deadline coming during the team's bye week, Payton must have been confident that he and run game coordinator Zach Strief would have the breathing room to get to the bottom of the O-line problems.
Payton issued a veiled threat to his blockers in his conversation with Cowherd, pointing to the Broncos' O-line depth and hinting that personnel changes aren't outside the bounds of the possible during the bye.
I'll be surprised if Denver benches any of its starting five, but if there are technical or schematic explanations for the troubling regression of center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey, it's now or never for Payton and Strief to identify it.
I would have liked to see the Broncos add one more running back ahead of the trade deadline, mainly because Harvey is on injured reserve for two more games. Taylor may have been worth a third-rounder and then some because of his unique talent and ability to create, and the fact that he's under contract beyond 2026.
A third-rounder for Pollard, though? No way.
That's a deal that only a desperate team makes, not the Broncos. And it turns out the Titans couldn't find any suckers willing to take that deal, so they bypassed the opportunity to stockpile some draft picks in yet another lost season.
First-round value or a McCaffrey package for a nearly 29-year-old Taylor? No. And certainly not when the Broncos have two young backs just scratching the surface of their NFL potential.
With the schedule opening up coming out of the bye — only one plus-.500 opponent until Christmas — the Broncos will have plenty of opportunity to get their fledgling ground attack rolling in time for the true stretch run.

title: Broncos' 3 Toughest Remaining Opponents—and One Sneaky Trap Game
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are enjoying the fruits of a well-timed and well-earned bye .
The 7-2 Broncos are in control of the AFC West and are the favorites to repeat as division champions after defeating the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 8. The Broncos had to take care of another opponent that was in the playoffs last year — the Carolina Panthers — before hitting their bye, but they took care of business on the road .
After successfully navigating a grueling early gauntlet that was the toughest slate of opponents in the NFL, the Broncos now face one of the league's easiest remaining schedules. However, three of Denver's eight remaining games are against a plus-.500 opponent.
Today, we're breaking down the Broncos' three toughest opponents coming out of the bye, plus another that's flying under the radar. If the Broncos sleep on this opponent, they could get caught in a dreaded trap game.
This is a weird game, as it's one of the NFL's new forays into Black Friday. It's strange to imagine a Broncos football game being played on a Friday, but it's what the NFL wants.
The Steelers have exceeded expectations under first-year head coach Mike McCarthy. His reunion with Aaron Rodgers, while far from the explosive heights the two reached at the height of their Green Bay Packers tenure, has borne fruit for the Steelers.
Pittsburgh leads a competitive AFC North division, and aside from a veteran quarterback, it has a top-ranked defense to hang its hat on, led by TJ Watt. The Steelers' defense ranks fourth in points and yardage. They're also tied with the Broncos with the fourth-most sacks this season.
The Broncos are different offense when they're on the road, especially against quality defenses. This is a game that looked far more forgiving before any football was played. As it inches closer, it's looking tougher.
But as a conference opponent, the Broncos will have to bring their A-game against the Steelers. That's one thing fans shouldn't doubt about Sean Payton's team: the Broncos can be relied upon to elevate their game against quality opponents, though they're not perfect, especially on the road.
Both of Denver's losses this season were stinkers on the road against opponents that are above .500 currently. The takeaway? Don't overlook this matchup.
If the season ended today, the Broncos would be the No. 2 playoff seed in the AFC. The Bills would be the No. 1 seed.
It feels like these two teams are on a collision course to decide AFC playoff-seeding supremacy this season. And after last year's divisional round matchup between these two clubs ended with a Broncos overtime win at Mile High that cost them Bo Nix , you can bet Buffalo will have its dander up for this one. But so will the Broncos.
Now, the next two weeks should be a breeze for the Bills, but that's the calm before the storm. They'll face the Kansas City Chiefs, New England Patriots (road), Green Bay Packers (road), and Chicago Bears before traveling to Mile High for their rendevouz with the Broncos.
There's a good chance the Broncos will be in control of the No. 1 seed by the time they host the Bills on Christmas Day. But it's still sure to be a doozy of a matchup with big-time AFC playoff implications.
Josh Allen is still playing at the top of his game with Joe Brady as his first-year head coach — the same guy who's been calling the Bills' offensive plays for a few years now. The Bills can gash you in an number of ways on offense, whether it's through the air or on the ground with Allen and James Cook.
Defensively, though, the Bills are vulnerable. Jim Leonhard's first year as an NFL defensive coordinator hasn't gone swimmingly thus far, with some calls for the Bills to fire him. Brady has stuck with Leonhard, who served as the Broncos' secondary coach and defensive pass game coordinator for the preceding two years.
The Bills are a juggernaut offensively, though, and that's allowed them to overcome their defensive foibles. Thankfully, this one is Denver, but it's going to be a dogfight.
The Patriots are above .500 currently, but they've got several tough opponents between now and their Week 17 home game vs. Denver. The Patriots are home against the Detroit Lions this week, followed by their bye.
The Patriots get a small Week 12 reprieve in the form of a road game against the Los Angeles Chargers, then it's back-to-back home games against the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings, before going back on the road to face the Chiefs. Who knows what New England's record will be come Week 17, but the fact that it's a road game against another 2025 playoff opponent means all bets are off for the Broncos.
Nix would love nothing more than the opportunity to show how differently the AFC championship game would have played out if he hadn't gotten hurt. And you know Nik Bonitto, Zach Allen, and the Broncos' pass rush would love to balance the scales against Drake Maye.
Again, though, the Broncos can be a different team on the road. As it stands, the time and broadcast channel for Broncos-Patriots is currently to be decided, but if New England is still alive in the playoff hunt come Week 17, this game could get flexed to primetime, especially with the Nix vs. Maye storyline to bring in the eyeballs.
Roll your eyes, but there are three reasons to be wary of this game. One, Nix has faced the Jets twice before, and both games were ugly, requiring fourth-quarter heroics, though he came out on top.
Two, it's an East Coast game scheduled for the NFL's early slate, and the Broncos haven't been great in those areas traditionally. However, under Payton, Denver has improved dramatically in early-start East Coast games, but it's a factor.
Three, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn knows Payton and his schemes and philosophies. Glenn played for Payton in New Orleans back in 2008 and he coached under him for five years as the Saints' defensive backs coach.
Glenn's familiarity with Payton was a big reason why the Broncos struggled against the Jets in England last year, escaping with a narrow 13-11 victory . Glenn's team is only 2-7 this season, and his future as the head coach is cloudy, but he'll have the Jets' dander up for the Broncos.
Geno Smith isn't blowing the doors down in his return to the Big Apple, but he's played an efficient brand of ball, with 2,078 yards and 12 touchdowns thus far. He's only been picked off three times.  Statistically, Smith has had a better season than Nix (1,730 YD/11 TD/3 INT), though the Jets' schedule has been a complete softball compared to what the Broncos have faced.
After last year's experience across the pond vs. Glenn's Jets, I doubt Payton's Broncos will be overlooking them, especially on the road. But this game has some of the 'trappings' of an upset.

title: How Close Broncos Came to Acquiring RB Tony Pollard Before Deadline
full_text:
Jonathan Taylor wasn't the only running back who interested the Denver Broncos prior to Tuesday's NFL trade deadline.
ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport reported Saturday that Denver "checked in on" Titans RB Tony Pollard but were rebuffed by Tennessee's apparent price tag of "anything less" than a third-round draft pick.
"The Packers and Broncos checked in on Titans running back Tony Pollard, whom Tennessee would not have traded for anything less than a third-round pick," the report stated.
This tracks with what league insider Jordan Schultz previously reported -- that the Broncos (and New York Giants) were among the teams in the short-lived Pollard sweepstakes.
"But Tennessee was adamant for weeks that they were unlikely to move him, as he’s been vital to the locker room and the continued development of Cam Ward," Schultz wrote on X on Nov. 10.
A prototypical dual-threat back, Pollard has accounted for 665 yards from scrimmage (595 rushing yards, 4.5 yards per carry) and six total touchdowns (all on the ground) across eight appearances this season.
Pollard was among several NFL RBs who were viewed as potential trade candidates prior to the deadline, along with Taylor , the Jets' Breece Hall, the Eagles' Saquon Barkley, and the Ravens' Derrick Henry. In the end, none of these players were moved by their original clubs.
It's clear that Denver was seeking an upgrade to pair with ascending rookie Jonah Coleman and pass-catching extraordinaire RJ Harvey. What's more, had they acquired Taylor or Pollard, the Broncos likely would've made veteran J.K. Dobbins available for trade .
Obviously, none of that transpired, and the club now heads into the second half of its 2026 campaign with the status quo at the position: Coleman and Dobbins on early downs, with Harvey seeing extensive third-down opportunities once he returns from injured reserve.
The Broncos will hope the trio can find their collective groove following a less-than-impressive statistical start prior to the bye. Entering Week 10, the rushing offense ranks 29th in yards per carry per game and 27th in total yards per game.
"Those runners are going to be important," head coach Sean Payton said after last Sunday's victory over the Panthers. "I'm not going to answer running-back depth questions, and certainly our running backs are not going to sit in front of a 15-minute interview about their playing time. Man, those guys are really important. [Running backs] J.K. [Dobbins] played, Jonah [Coleman] played, RJ [Harvey] will be back here shortly, and I'm glad we got both of them. I didn't feel like we ran it particularly well with either of them, and it wasn't back driven. It was ‘Oh, that was a Buffalo front.’ Like, it took us a minute. And now, we threw it better for chunk plays than we ran it, but we got the runs when we needed it later."

title: Broncos Midseason Awards: MVP, Breakout Star, and Biggest Disappointment
full_text:
The NFL put the Denver Broncos' bye week at an ideal spot, about as close to halfway through the season as is possible in a 17-game campaign.
The Broncos are 7-2 entering Week 10's bye, leading the AFC West. They're favored to win the division , though one or two slip-ups down the stretch could change that, and the AFC's No. 1 playoff seed is still very much on the table.
The bye has offered us a chance to breathe and take a deep dive into the Broncos, from cumulative player grades to rookie report cards and five warning signs . Today is a day for superlatives, though; we're handing out midseason awards to the deserving Broncos, and there's been plenty of sample size to feel confident about each one.
Let's start with the most important award.
I know, I know. Nix has had a weird campaign, returning from the broken ankle that ended his 2025 season and torpedoed the Broncos' championship ambitions on the doorstep of the Super Bowl. He doesn't rank highly in any of the common quarterback stats, and most of the advanced analytics aren't kind to him.
However, Nix remains the Broncos' most valuable player. Even amid a step-back of a third season, without him, this team's outlook would immediately fall into the gutter, just as we saw in the AFC championship game last year.
Nix was bad at times against the Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams, and Seattle Seahawks, but as a thought exercise, imagine how those games would have shaken out if Jarrett Stidham had been the quarterback. Yeah. That's right. Denver loses all three of those games without Nix.
Even amid his early-season struggles, the one thing that no one could take away from Nix is his clutch-time excellence. There isn't a better NFL quarterback when the chips are down, and that clutch-time will to win is a big reason why the Broncos were able to weather their early-season gauntlet of a schedule.
CHUNK PLAY MARVIN MIMS JR. DENvsAZ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/o13qfZGfzC
Since Week 7, Nix has been improving by leaps and bounds. His confidence is back, and he's no longer so painfully hesitant in his decision-making. In fact, he's hunting with the football again .
There's every reason to believe that Nix's upward momentum will continue coming out of the bye. He wanted to be peaking at the right time, and the stars are aligning for the Broncos to get the best possible version of their young franchise quarterback down the stretch and into the playoffs.
Waddle hasn't exactly been an off-the-charts producer, but he's been the Broncos' most important non-quarterback player on offense. Amid Nix's early slump, Waddle bided his time, finding ways to make an impact in Denver's low-percentage passing attack.
But even when the ball doesn't go his way, or isn't intended to go his way, Waddle's presence on the field has changed the math for opposing defenses. It has opened things up for other players, and will continue to do so as the Broncos' schedule opens up down the stretch.
Jaylen Waddle gets his first big play as a Bronco! 🐧 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/FAioYbx0Fs
Waddle has dealt with some minor injuries and he suffered a concussion in Week 9, but he's appeared in all nine games, leading the team with 30 receptions on 52 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns. He's also made some big plays on two-point conversions, without which, the Broncos don't come back in two of their one-score victories this season.
The Broncos don't have any buyer's remorse after giving up a first- and third-round pick to acquire Waddle. He's just getting started.
Allen is in the middle of perhaps his best season as a pro, which is saying something, given that he's been an All-Pro in each of the past two seasons, and was a first-team selection last year.
Allen is near the top of the NFL in pass-rushing metrics, including quarterback pressures, and his 4.5 sacks are tied with Nik Bonitto for the team lead. Allen affects the quarterback on every snap, commanding double teams, which frees up other guys to make plays. He even blocked a field-goal attempt in Week 4.
IT'S BLOCKED! 📺: @CBSSports / @paramountplus pic.twitter.com/8wHodVFVIN
He makes his own fair share of plays, even against double teams because Allen is just that good. Against the run, he's one of the NFL's best interior defenders, too. He's just an all-around elite player at the point of attack. Without him, this defense wouldn't be nearly as formidable.
Only two of Denver's 2026 draft picks have actually seen the field this season, but Coleman has easily been the club's top rookie. That's saying something, given that he missed four games on injured reserve with an ankle sprain.
In four of the five games he's dressed for, Coleman has touched the ball and has been a key contributor. In fact, the Broncos haven't lost a game yet in which Coleman has touched the ball, so Sean Payton may want to remember that.
Coleman has 47 times for 191 yards and three touchdowns, averaging a team-high 4.1 yards per attempt. He's also caught 13 passes for 128 yards and six first downs.
JONAH COLEMAN DOWN TO THE 4 KCvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/nRd1e0xIhC
As the Broncos' new RB1, the sky is the limit for Coleman, especially if Payton is able to get to the bottom of the offensive line's blocking issues, as promised to do during the bye. It's a pretty distant thought, but with eight games left to go, the rookie still has the chance to rush for 1,000 yards, though it will take the O-line stepping its game up significantly.
Wide receiver Pat Bryant may have been my choice here, were it not for his missing four games with an ankle injury. He's been a tremendous player for this offense and has taken some big steps forward since his rookie year.
What Bryant and Robinson have in common is they're both in Year 2. Robinson has appeared in every game thus far — another illustration of his improvement, given that he was a healthy scratch in 11 games as a rookie — and without him, I'm not sure Denver would have been able to weather Jonathon Cooper's absence so successfully.
Robinson has 28 tackles (12 solo), three tackles for a loss, one fumble recovery, and a tipped pass. He's tied for third on the team with 25 pressures, despite not being a starter.
Zach Allen leads the pass rush 😤 JAXvsDEN on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/awIGMbyXcq
The Broncos love Cooper, but given his off-field drama and cost, if the team was of a mind to move on in 2027, Robinson's emergence would likely be a big reason why. The 2025 fourth-round pick out of Alabama has been an absolute stud in Year 2.
This is a bit of a cheat because it's not an individual player, but the Broncos' offensive line was billed as the NFL's best unit entering the 2026 season. Alas, this O-line has been far from it.
Nix faced the most pressure of his career through the first six weeks of the season, and the Broncos still haven't been able to generate at reliable run game, Coleman's emergence notwithstanding. The presence of All-Pro tandem Garett Bolles and Quinn Meinerz hasn't been enough to elevate the unit, not with center Luke Wattenberg and right tackle Mike McGlinchey playing so poorly.
The Broncos have a lot of money tied up in Wattenberg and McGlinchey, which is why fans shouldn't expect any personnel changes over the bye, even though Payton threatened it earlier this week . Left guard Ben Powers has gotten a lot of grief from fans this season, but he hasn't been the biggest culprit in the O-line's blocking inefficiencies, and has taken on more responsibility to cover for Wattenberg's foibles.
The continuity Denver has maintained up front is rare, fielding the same starting five for the third straight year, but the O-line, as a unit, hasn't been able to capitalize on it. There's time yet, though. Let's hope the Broncos are able to get to the bottom of the problem during the bye.

title: Broncos' Season Has Exposed a New 2027 First-Round Draft Priority
full_text:
At 7-2, the Denver Broncos are enjoying a well-earned bye week .
The Broncos remain one of the NFL's deepest and most talented rosters, but halfway through the 2026 season, some of the holes have become obvious. This team could use reinforcements and upgrades at tight end, inside linebacker, safety, and running back.
But offensive tackle may be rising to the top of the Broncos' list of needs, especially as it pertains to the first round of next year's draft. NFL Draft On SI 's Justin Melo seems to be evolving on this subject, going from projecting Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson in several of his most recent mock drafts to offensive tackle.
Projecting the Broncos to be picking at No. 29 overall (as it currently stands), Melo mocked Texas offensive tackle Trevor Goosby to the Mile High City.
"Texas left tackle Trevor Goosby now faces a complicated pre-draft process after suffering a season-ending knee injury. The Denver Broncos can afford to be patient, but need an eventual successor for the aging Garret Bolles. With Mike McGlinchey underperforming, the Broncos could address both offensive tackle spots," Melo wrote .
Listed at 6-foot-7 and 325 pounds, Goosby would step in as the biggest and likely the longest tackle on the Broncos' roster. For his size, he's extremely athletic, and balances that with a fair amount of power.
Goosby was named first-team All-SEC last year, which is no mean feat in that Conference, and has been Arch Manning's blind-side protector at Texas. Goosby has played in some big games and has excelled against quality opponents.
As a red-shirt senior, this will be Goosby's last collegiate season. It will be interesting to see how he tests at the 2027 NFL Combine. He could go earlier in the draft than No. 29 overall.
Both Bolles and McGlinchey are well on the wrong side of 30. At 34, Bolles is still performing at an All-Pro level , and while he's getting up there, he's actually young for his age, given his late foray into football after serving a two-year LDS mission.
Meanwhile, McGlinchey will turn 32 in January. He's never been an All-Pro-caliber talent, but up until this season, he's been a competent and reliable right tackle.
That has changed rather dramatically this season. McGlinchey's run blocking has devolved and as a pass protector, he's become a liability for Bo Nix.
Bolles isn't showing any signs of slowing down. With McGlinchey, though, alarm bells have to be ringing at Broncos HQ — so much so that it wouldn't completely shock me if the coaches were to make a change at right tackle during the bye and give Alex Palczewski a crack at the job.
It's unlikely to happen, given McGlinchey's $23.775 million cap hit — the highest on the team this year — and his leadership. Teams often fall prey to the sunk-cost fallacy, where the highest-paid players simply have to play, and the Broncos aren't immune to this flawed line of thinking.
He may not be a team captain, but McGlinchey is very much a leader that guys look to on offense, and that will always factor into any conversation about potentially benching him.
The Broncos started thinking ahead by drafting Kage Casey in the fourth round earlier this year, anticipating the coming departure of left guard Ben Powers. Denver's center situation isn't great, with Luke Wattenberg playing poorly on a second contract and backup Alex Forsyth hitting free agency after this year, so it wouldn't be a shock to see the team prioritize interior offensive line in the draft.
If you're going to invest a first-round pick, though, it should be offensive tackle; a position that Denver hasn't drafted since Bolles in 2017. Casey was a career tackle at Boise State, but the Broncos drafted him to play guard.
As we inch closer to draft season, fans will likely be pounding the table for a tight end, running back, or linebacker, but don't be surprised if the Broncos finally go back to the offensive tackle well in Round 1.

title: Playoff Picture, Week 10: Detroit Lions Climb to Top of NFC North
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are in first-place in the NFC North.
With a 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany, the Lions improved to 7-2 with their fifth-straight win and put themselves in a first-place tie with both the Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings.
Detroit has the head-to-head tiebreaker over the Vikings, and a better divisional record than the Bears. Both of Chicago's losses this year have been in the division, which gives the Detroit the advantage and the top spot in the NFC North with eight games to play.
In the three-way tie, the tiebreaker is decided by winning percentage in head-to-head meetings between the three teams. The Lions have beat the Vikings, and the Vikings beat the Bears. Because the Lions have the head-to-head over Minnesota, they're currently in first.
Detroit was unable to gain any headway on the San Francisco 49ers, who defeated the Dallas Cowboys to move to 8-1 on the season.
Chicago was on its bye week this week, and returns to action next week against the New Orleans Saints. If they defeat New Orleans and the Lions handle business Sunday against Tampa Bay, the Thanksgiving meeting at Ford Field will carry massive divisional stakes.
A lot can still happen, but at this point Detroit controls its own destiny in it's pursuit of a third NFC North title in four years. Half of their final eight games will be against divisional opponents, including that Thanksgiving matchup with the Bears looming in less than two weeks.
The Lions will have to run the gauntlet of the division without two of their top defenders, as Aidan Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a knee injury, while Jack Campbell is on injured reserve after a scary injury against the Minnesota Vikings in Week 8.
The NFC North remains the best division in football with all teams at least two games over .500, but the Minnesota Vikings knocked the Green Bay Packers out of the playoff picture for the time being with their 30-10 victory Sunday at Lambeau Field.
Green Bay dropped to 6-4 on the year with the loss, but are currently on the outside looking in as the Los Angeles Rams claimed the seventh seed for now thanks to having a better record than the Packers against NFC opponents.
The Packers and Rams have a big matchup looming, as both teams will be on their bye weeks this upcoming week before squaring off on Wednesday, Nov. 25 at SoFi Stadium. That game will be a big factor in the postseason picture, as the winning team will gain the valuable head-to-head tiebreaker in addition to going a game up in the standings.
Meanwhile, the Vikings have the opportunity to impact the standings in a big way next week with a matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City on Sunday Night Football.
1.) Detroit Lions (7-2) 2.) Minnesota Vikings (7-2) 3.) Chicago Bears (7-2) 4.) Green Bay Packers (6-4)

Sports journalist who has covered the Detroit Lions the past three NFL seasons. Christian brings expert analysis, insights and an ability to fairly assess how the team is performing in a tough NFC North division.

title: Lions Claim Former Cowboys DE, Waive DB
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have made an addition to their defensive line room in the wake of the injury to Aidan Hutchinson.
On Monday, the Lions added depth by claiming defensive end Tyrus Wheat off of waivers from the Dallas Cowboys. Wheat is a familiar face for Lions fans, as he spent last season with Detroit. He appeared in 15 games last year for Detroit, notching 1.5 sacks.
In 2026, Wheat had played in five games for Dallas and totaled three combined tackles. He is in his fourth NFL season and has appeared in 40 career games, logging 35 tackles and two sacks.
In a corresponding move for the waiver claim, the Lions waived cornerback Nick Whiteside. Detroit signed Whiteside to the active roster prior to their game against the Miami Dolphins.
The addition comes on the heels of the team's 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Munich on Sunday. In the win, though, they had to overcome the injury of one of their top defensive players in Aidan Hutchinson.
Hutchinson went down in the first quarter after leaping in the air to celebrate a sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. He landed awkwardly on his right leg, with his knee appearing to buckle, and he exited the game and did not return.
In the hours following the game, reports indicated that he had torn his ACL and may have suffered additional damage to his knee. It is the second season-ending injury suffered by the standout over the past three seasons.
The Michigan product is second on the team in sacks with six, and has 49 in his career through four seasons. He is coming off a 2025 campaign in which he earned Second Team All-Pro honors after a career-high 14.5 sacks.
However, Hutchinson suffered a season-ending leg injury in Week 6 of the 2024 season, and will now miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a knee injury.
This is also the latest major injury to Detroit's defense over the past three weeks, as they lost linebacker Jack Campbell against the Minnesota Vikings when he suffered a neck injury making a tackle in the fourth quarter, as well as rookie linebacker Jimmy Rolder missing the rest of the season to a hamstring injury.
With these injuries, the Lions have had to make some additions to their defense. They signed K.J. Britt to the active roster off the Patriots' practice squad, and added Owen Pappoe to their practice squad.

title: Detroit Lions Snap Counts Reveal Likely Aidan Hutchinson Succession Plan
full_text:
The Detroit Lions earned a dominant win over the New England Patriots Sunday, but the tone wasn't all upbeat in the following hours.
Even though the team ended Sunday in first-place in the NFC North, emotions were somewhat somber as news broke that defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL and potentially more damage to his knee.
Hutchinson suffered the injury after celebrating a sack that ended the Patriots' first drive and forced them into a field goal attempt. He played just nine snaps in Sunday's win.
With Hutchinson out, Lions fans got a first look at what the defensive line rotation could look like in his absence.
The standout pass-rusher will not be easy to replace, but the Lions appear to have more depth than in years past in this area. Veteran DJ Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore have both played well as of late, and Detroit can also utilize players such as Levi Onwuzurike and Tyler Lacy as big ends to provide depth.
Detroit has also gotten good pass-rush efforts from the interior, particularly from Alim McNeill and rookie Skyler Gill-Howard.
Elsewhere, the Lions' cornerback rotation appeared to be less of a complete effort on Sunday, with Roger McCreary playing every snap and Rock Ya-Sin playing all but four. Khalil Dorsey got 21 snaps, but Nick Whiteside and Ennis Rakestraw were limited to seven and five snaps, respectively.
With the Lions up comfortably in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game, they were able to get their backups on offense an extended look. Joshua Dobbs got 10 snaps, as did offensive linemen Larry Borom, Miles Frazier and Seth McLaughlin.

title: Grades: Lions Dominate Battered Patriots Behind Jahmyr Gibbs' Big Day
full_text:
The Detroit Lions made the most of an international trip.
Detroit played a game on foreign soil for the first time since 2015 Sunday and handled business against the New England Patriots. They routed the Patriots 35-10, but did have to endure what could be a devastating injury to one of their stars.
Here are grades for each position group based on performance in Sunday's game.
Goff's performance on Sunday was something of a mixed bag. He got things going early with a touchdown pass to Amon-Ra St. Brown, and delievered a perfect ball to Isaac TeSlaa for his second scoring pass of the afternoon.
However, he was also indecisive at times and took an early sack after pump faking multiple times. He also had two interceptions, one to Christian Gonzalez and another in the end zone to Kevin Byard III where he never saw the safety at the end of the first half.
Gibbs added a third touchdown pass in the second half, and finished with 303 passing yards on a 20-for-31 performance.
Jahmyr Gibbs once again staked his claim to being one of the best all-around players in the sport. He had 171 yards from scrimmage by halftime, headlined by a 50-yard reception and a 5-yard rushing touchdown.
Gibbs would add another rushing touchdown in the second half and finished with 252 all-purpose yards, including 153 on the ground and 99 receiving yards on seven receptions. He's now gone over 150 rushing yards in three of the last five games, and is making a legitimate case for Offensive Player of the Year.
Sione Vaki continues to provide a solid compliment for Gibbs, as he provided quality pass-protection reps as well as a 17-yard reception and six carries for 28 yards.
Amon-Ra St. Brown was determined to make a statement playing in a country that is so close to home for him, and he did just that. On the Lions' first drive, St. Brown hauled in a short pass and made multiple Patriot defenders miss en route to a 56-yard touchdown.
St. Brown would add a second touchdown later in the game, and finished with 98 yards on four catches. Isaac TeSlaa had two catches for 19 yards and a touchdown, his first of the season on an acrobatic diving grab to secure a ball thrown to his back shoulder.
Jameson Williams chipped in four catches for 50 yards on seven targets.
Sam LaPorta notched just one catch for 16 yards, and nearly had a touchdown on a throw that was knocked out of his hands by Kevin Byard III. Brock Wright also got in the mix, chipping in two catches for 11 yards.
Over the past four games, LaPorta has been quiet as he has just nine total catches in that span. It will be intriguing to monitor the role that he has moving forward within Detroit's passing game.
Penei Sewell had one of the best blocks of the year on Gibbs' second touchdown run, coming all the way across the formation and serving as the lead blocker on the corner positioned on the opposite side of the field.
Tate Ratledge was whistled for holding in the first half, while the Lions allowed two sacks in the first two quarters. One of those sacks appeared to be on Goff, who held the ball after multiple pump fakes.
The Patriots quickly drove into the red-zone on their opening drive, but Aidan Hutchinson thwarted the momentum with a third-down sack of Drake Maye. Unfortunately, Hutchinson suffered an injury while leaping to celebrate the big play and did not return to the game.
Derrick Moore and Alim McNeill both picked up the slack, as each recorded a sack in the first half. Moore added a second sack in the second half against Tommy DeVito, while DJ Wonnum also got to the quarterback.
In total, the Lions' defensive line was responsible for six of their nine tackles for loss. Rookie defensive end Eric O'Neill also got in on the action with a pass defensed.
The Lions continued to make the most of their short-handed group at this position without Jack Campbell and Jimmy Rolder. Derrick Barnes led the group with seven tackles, including one for loss.
Malcolm Rodriguez added six tackles, while former Patriot K.J. Britt had five combined tackles including four solos. It was Britt's first opportunity for extended defensive action in a Lions uniform after being signed off New England's practice squad last week.
Rodriguez was in part responsible for New England's only touchdown, as he was on the wrong end of a pick from a Patriots offensive player in man coverage which resulted in DeVito hitting running back Lan Larison for a touchdown.
After a difficult first drive that ended in a Patriots field goal, the secondary settled in and had a good day against DeVito. Roger McCreary recorded his first interception of the season amidst his two passes defensed.
Brian Branch had another good day, logging a tackle for loss amidst a five-tackle performance. In D.J. Reed's absence, Rock Ya-Sin got more opportunities and notched a tackle for loss and a pass defensed.
The Lions were better in the red zone than in weeks prior, so they did not need to utilize Jake Bates on any field goal attempts on Sunday. Jack Fox punted four times, averaging just under 45 yards per and pinning two inside the 20-yard line.
DeAndre Carter totaled six yards on his two punt returns, and returned a kickoff 25 yards. Jacob Saylors returned to action and had a 26-yard kickoff return as well.
It can be a difficult task to get up for an international game given all the travel and logsitics of it, but Dan Campbell had his team ready to play on Sunday. They scored touchdowns on their first two drives, and played extremely well defensively en route to their fifth-straight win.
Drew Petzing had some creativity for the Patriots' defense, but the bread and butter of the run game stole the show. Meanwhile, the Lions' defense handled business against a team playing with a backup quarterback for the majority of the game.
Now, the Lions need to continue playing at a high level ahead of a big two-game stretch. They take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers next week, then have a short turnaround for their Thanksgiving matchup with the Chicago Bears.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Is To Blame For Freak Injury, Must Tone Down Celebrations
full_text:
The Detroit Lions continued their winning ways Sunday morning in Munich, Germany, easily defeating the New England Patriots, 35-10, for their fifth straight win.
It was a dominant effort from start to finish for Dan Campbell's team , which accumulated nearly 500 total yards (494) and allowed just 151 yards to Mike Vrabel's squad.
Yet, the Week 10 victory was overshadowed by the likely season-ending knee injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions’ star pass-rusher.
Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack of Patriots signal-caller Drake Maye; he leaped in the air and upon coming down, landed awkwardly on his right leg. The fifth-year defender never played another snap Sunday.
If that was not a clear-cut sign to cut the acrobatics out of his celebration repertoire, I don't know what would be. Nonetheless, he needs to – no ifs, ands, or buts about it.
The University of Michigan product will receive further testing upon returning home to the states. However, his 2026 campaign is believed to be over, cutting short what had been an All-Pro-caliber season.
His sack of Maye was his seventh on the season, and he also logged another two pressures in the international affair, bringing his season total to 52 (the second-highest total in the NFL).
He easily was one of the league's most productive pass-rushers in 2026, earning a league-leading Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade of 91.1 and an overall mark of 91.9 through nine games (the best overall grade among 111 qualified EDGEs).
Plain and simple, Detroit does not possess another EDGE defender in the same stratosphere as the 2022 No. 2 overall pick. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum have each had their moments of looking like competent pass-rushers. However, neither of them is going to be confused for Hutchinson anytime soon.
The Michigan native has become an irreplaceable talent; consequently, losing him for the year is undoubtedly a detrimental blow to Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit. Without the premier quarterback disruptor , it certainly is harder to envision Detroit capturing the NFC North crown and making a Super Bowl run.
It begs the question: Should Lions head man Dan Campbell mandate that his players are no longer allowed to leave their feet to celebrate big plays? If I were Campbell, I would do just that.
And no, I'm not trying to take the fun out of the game. I'm fully aware that players like Hutchinson are also entertainers and that they have a genuine passion and love for playing the game. So, I would never want to take away their ability to enjoy themselves while they put their bodies on the line 17 weeks a year. That would be a bad look for Campbell, too, and likely cause him to lose the respect of his players.
It's why the celebrations can and should remain. However, they need to be toned down. And specifically, I'm talking about eliminating the acrobatics, and in the process, reducing the likelihood of another Lions player suffering a season-ending ailment while celebrating a major play.
And Campbell can't sugarcoat the importance of this being the new celebration policy, either. He needs to be steadfast with it and emphasize there is no wiggle room for a Hutchinson 2.0. The NFC North is too good and deep, with the Bears continuing to rack up wins and Kirk Cousins now under center for the Vikings, for the Lions to endure another celebration gone wrong.
Unquestionably, Detroit can ill-afford to lose another core member of its roster – e.g. Alim McNeill or Jahmyr Gibbs – to a serious injury. And if it were to, the team's Super Bowl chances would cease to exist.

title: Evaluating Lions Internal, External Options to Replace Aidan Hutchinson
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are preparing for the worst regarding the future of defensive end Aidan Hutchinson.
On Sunday, the star defender went down with a non-contact knee injury after leaping in the air to celebrate a sack on New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. He didn't return to the game, and reports across the league are indicating that the team is preparing to be without him for the remainder of the season.
Hutchinson leaves big shoes to fill in Detroit's defense. Through nine games Hutchinson ranked second on the Lions in sacks with six and is among the NFL leaders in pressures with 52 pressures.
The trade deadline was Tuesday, meaning any additions the Lions want to make to account for this loss will have to come via their own practice squad, an opposing practice squad or the external free agent market.
Here are 10 possible options for the Lions to replace Hutchinson following his injury.
Moore appears to be the most likely next option as a starter in Detroit's defense. He began the year playing a small role, but injuries to Hutchinson and last week DJ Wonnum have given him extended opportunities that he's made the most of.
All four of Moore's sacks this season have come in the last two weeks. With Hutchinson out now, Moore will likely get more chances to prove he belongs in the mix as opposed to playing a rotational pass-rushing role.
Through nine games, fans have yet to see the 2025 sixth-round pick. Hassanein didn't appear in a game last year, and has been a healthy scratch for each of Detroit's games up to this point.
There was a belief that Hassanein could've gotten an opportunity last week when Wonnum was out, but the Lions elected to go with Anthony Lucas as a call-up instead. Perhaps he's better suited for an opportunity with Hutchinson out now.
As mentioned, Lucas got his first opportunity as a practice squad elevation against the Dolphins in Week 9. He played just 12 snaps, but the Lions' desire to use him instead of Hassanein seems to indicate that they have some confidence in his overall ability.
It's worth noting that Lucas wasn't as flashy in terms of production as a pass-rusher in college, and could be better suited for a role as a big end as opposed to playing the rush-end position.
A Michigan native who has carved out a nice career after playing collegiately at Division II Grand Valley State, Judon has been tied to the Lions at times throughout the last several seasons. Now a free agent, perhaps the Lions finally make the homecoming official for the veteran.
Judon has played in one game this season , that being for the San Francisco 49ers in early October against the Denver Broncos. A four-time Pro Bowl selection who is in his 11th season, Judon has plenty of experience and could provide a burst of energy for the Lions for their stretch run.
However, he's also an aging veteran who started just three games last year and didn't record a sack. After notching 15.5 sacks in 2022, Judon has notched just 9.5 total in over the last four years.
Throughout his career, Reddick has been at his best as a pass-rush specialist. While his production has been declining in recent years, he does have the ability to spark a defense with his athleticism off the edge.
Reddick has remained unsigned throughout the year after appearing in 13 games for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers a season ago. He notched 2.5 sacks last year, and had just one in 10 games for the New York Jets during the previous year.
The Temple product does have some versatility, though, as he can also play the SAM linebacker position. With the injuries Detroit has dealt with at linebacker, Reddick's versatility could be helpful.
Floyd has carved out a nice career over the past decade, with 70 career sacks across stints with five different teams. Floyd has experience in the NFC North having played his first four seasons with the Chicago Bears, and won a Super Bowl with the Los Angeles Rams in the 2021 season.
The veteran doesn't have flashy totals or accolades, as he's never been an All-Pro and has had just two seasons with 10 or more sacks. However, he's been consistent throughout his career, and could be a stabilizing force for Detroit's line.
Injuries have derailed what was a promising career for Bosa, particularly over the past four seasons. A highly touted prospect out of Ohio State, Bosa was the third overall pick by the Chargers in the 2016 Draft and wound up being the Defensive Rookie of the Year.
Bosa made five Pro Bowl appearances throughout his career, but in recent seasons he's struggled with injuries. He was limited to five games in 2022 and four games in 2023, but has played 14 and 15 over the past two years, respectively.
The Ohio State product proved to still have some upside last year with five sacks for the Buffalo Bills, but has gone unsigned. If he's healthy, perhaps he's worthy of an opportunity to see what he still has left in the tank.
BJ Ojulari (Jacksonville Jaguars)
A former second-round pick of the Arizona Cardinals in 2023, Ojulari has showed some promise in his career but injuries have ultimately been too much for him to overcome. He recorded four sacks as a rookie in 2023, but then missed the entire 2024 season and appeared in just eight games last year.
Now with the Jaguars, Ojulari has yet to make his season debut. Perhaps the Lions would be intrigued by some of the flashes of upside he's shown in his career.
Andre Carter II (Los Angeles Chargers)
Carter had a very short stint on the Lions' practice squad last season, as he signed with the team in August before being poached by the Miami Dolphins in November. He hasn't appeared in an NFL game since 2024, but has bounced around the league as a coveted depth option.
The Army product has very limited experience, but could be a solid depth option assuming he'd be familiar with the scheme in Detroit under second-year coordinator Kelvin Sheppard.
Michael Heldman (Kansas City Chiefs)
A Michigan native who went undrafted out of Central Michigan this year, Heldman had a big preseason debut for the New Orleans Saints but would be waived with an injury designation in early September.
He's landed in Kansas City, where he's yet to make his debut. He does have some intriguing athletic tools and was one of the top pass-rushers in college football last year across all levels.
When the Lions were in need of safety depth, Brad Holmes targeted an undrafted safety in Bishop Fitzgerald to add to the active roster. While Heldman wouldn't be the flashiest addition, he would be one that fits the mold of how Holmes has approached these situations in the past.

title: Everything Dan Campbell Said After Detroit Lions Beat Patriots

Especially with his first big play. Our defense takes field; we end up holding the field goal, but then Saint's big catch, man, makes somebody miss. He runs it in. Our guys are running down to help him in the end zone, and you could just hear the crowd erupt. So this has been an unbelievable experience. Been very special because we did feel like this was a home game. We felt like this was our home, and that was important. Everybody's taking unbelievable care of us all week. I mean, just the hospitality has been unbelievable here. So this is icing on the cake."
"Yeah, I got mine two nights ago. I went in and got my victory beer, because I don't know if I'm gonna be able to get it tonight. We've got to get right back on the plane and get ready for next week's game. I'm with you. We're going to enjoy this victory, this meant a lot to us. When you're able to win and be in this environment that we were able to be in, it's one of those things you'll never forget."

You run off the football and you get guys on blocks. You put a hat on a hat, Gibbs will do the rest. He'll do the rest. But you could feel it, man. The O-line really showed up today. You can feel the sense of pride here. And number two, a song that I know very well in the third quarter, John Denver, Country Roads. I'm like 'Whoa.' I wasn't expecting that, and everybody in the stadium knows it. It blew me away. I'm like 'Wow, okay, that's a that's a little piece of home,' and you know that was — it was cool. "Yeah. Nothing new. We'll know more when we get back in the states, but anytime you lose a player of his caliber, type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours. That doesn't make things easy. It's what I just mentioned. This is the second time this has happened and our guys have responded in a tough situation and didn't bat an eye. We just went back to work and that's not an easy thing to do, but no, certainly you don't want to know that a player like that is down."
"Well, we like them. It's why we acquired them where we did, and I know this, Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets, he gets better. It was good to get Wonnum back today. title: 6 Winners, 1 Loser From Lions Win Over Patriots
full_text:
On Sunday, the Detroit Lions were the first team playing, squaring off at 9:30 a.m. EST with the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. After both teams scored on their opening drives, there was an air of anticipation for a high-scoring game.
Instead, both teams lost star players on the same play, with Drake Maye and Aidan Hutchinson each suffering lower body injuries. With the Lions squaring off against a backup quarterback, they quickly ran out to a 21-3 lead at half and did not look back, winning 35-10.
Here is who won the day and gave Lions fans a stress-free Sunday.
As is the case with Gibbs, any time he sets a mark that is “first since Barry Sanders,” it is a good day. This time, it was Gibbs’s 93 rushing yards at half being the most since Barry Sanders in a 1994 game.
Gibbs’s footprints were all over the game, with 171 total yards at half, with a touchdown that he set up with a long reception among his multiple plays. On his first touch of the second half, Gibbs crossed 175 yards from scrimmage.
Gibbs added another touchdown in the fourth quarter, rushing in from 26 yards out. He showcased excellence patience, weaving into the end zone and following his blockers for the final ten yards. It pushed the back over 150 yards rushing on the day and 250 yards from scrimmage.
With seven minutes to play, his day, alongside the starters, was over with the Lions up by 25 points. Gibbs did all of his damage in 3 1/2 quarters of action.
Amon-Ra St. Brown had a very happy homecoming, with the wide receiver recording his first touchdown since September on the opening drive of the game. The All-Pro had an uncharacteristic 56-yard catch and run touchdown as opposed to his normal redzone damage.
The good day continued, with St. Brown recording a second touchdown on the game in the third quarter with a strong catch-and-run for 28 yards, powering through a pile for the last five yards. St. Brown finished at 98 yards in his return home.
McCreary had a tough matchup with AJ Brown on Sunday, and performed admirably. The star receiver was held to two catches for 27 yards through three quarters before leaving with injury, with his best catch coming against Khalil Dorsey.
Meanwhile, McCreary recorded his first interception as a Lion and his first since Week 1 in 2025. It set up the Lions for what should have been a scoring drive to end the first half before a turnover on the goal line.
McNeill continued his strong season, jumping up to 6.5 sacks as the midpoint of the season nears. The NC State product is putting up numbers not seen since Ndamukong Suh in 2011, as pointed out on the broadcast.
McNeill nearly had three other sacks on the day as well, getting close on a flea flicker and then flushing Tommy DeVito into DJ Wonnum’s arms for a sack, before flushing DeVito from the pocket on the second play of the fourth quarter.
Upon Aidan Hutchinson’s injury, the fellow Michigan product Moore was the next man up. Moore responded with his third and fourth career sack in two weeks. On the first, Moore benefitted, taking down DeVito after DJ Wonnum pressured the quarterback towards Moore.
Moore got close to another sack on New England’s sole touchdown for the game, and then got home for his second sack, outright speeding by his lineman to take down DeVito hard.
It is not a stretch to say that this has been a tumultuous week for the Boston College product. The left guard was held out of the Miami game for disciplinary reasons, with head coach Dan Campbell saying that it is on the lineman to respond.
The former Lions’ sixth-round pick responded with a strong game, as he and Penei Sewell had a massive push the entire game, leading to Gibbs’s massive 153 yards on the ground. On Gibbs’s first touchdown, Mahogany had moved the defensive tackle five yards left of his starting spot on the dive.
Mahogany earned the nod over Sewell in the winners category after the franchise tackle was whistled for a hold in the second half.
Hutchinson had a short day in Germany , with the star player getting injured following a sack of Drake Maye. The Michigan product’s sack celebration has faced some concerns in the past regarding how dangerous stress towards his knees is in his jump and landing.
That caught up to the EDGE on Sunday, with his landing instantly buckling his right knee and forcing him out of the game in subpar field conditions. It has been a point of criticism from fans in the past, and it was proven right, with the Lions suffering a humiliating injury in a celebration similar to what happened to Stephen Tulloch in 2014.
Postgame reports indicate that Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season with a significant knee injury.

title: Report: Lions to Lose Aidan Hutchinson for Season
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are celebrating a big win over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. But the emotions have been altered by an injury to one of their stars.
On Sunday, defensive end Aidan Hutchinson went down with a knee injury after jumping into the air celebrating a first quarter sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Hutchinson did not return to the game, and fans immediately feared the worst.
While Lions head coach Dan Campbell did not immediately have an update during his postgame press conference, reports from NFL insiders indicate that Hutchinson is believed to have suffered a serious injury that will keep him out for the remainder of the season.
"Lions star DE Aidan Hutchinson suffered a significant knee injury," reported The Ringer's Tom Pelissero. "Imaging in Munich confirmed the injury to Hutchinson, whose right knee buckled as he celebrated a sack against the Patriots. He's out for the season."
NFL Network's Ian Rapoport added, "There does not appear to be hope that Hutchinson returns this season."
The injury to Hutchinson is a devastating blow for the Lions, who will be without one of the NFL's best pass-rushers. Even as they currently sit in first-place in the NFC North as winners of five straight with a 7-2 record, it makes the future somewhat gloomy given how impactful he is to the defense.
In Hutchinson's absence, the Lions will likely rely more on 2026 second-round pick Derrick Moore . After playing a small role earlier in the year, Moore has had two sacks apiece in each of the last two games including Sunday's win over the Patriots.
D.J. Wonnum is the other starter opposite of Hutchinson, while Tyler Lacy, Eric O'Neill and Ahmed Hassanein are other options on the EDGE. When Wonnum missed last week's game, Detroit also utilized undrafted rookie Anthony Lucas as a practice squad elevation.
With this news, Hutchinson has now suffered a season-ending injury for the second time in three seasons. In 2024, he was playing at an elite level before suffering a significant leg injury in the team's fifth game of the year.
Hutchinson has six sacks this season and 49 for his career through his first four seasons. Drafted second overall in the 2022 NFL Draft, the Michigan product has quickly asserted himself among the game's best at his position.
Last year, Hutchinson bounced back from the previous year's injury to have a career-best year. He logged 14.5 sacks, which earned him Second Team All-Pro honors. He also inked a four-year contract extension worth $180 million in October of last year.

title: Dan Campbell Addresses Aidan Hutchinson Injury: ‘Hurts a Little Bit’
full_text:
The Detroit Lions (and their fans) took over Germany's Allianz Arena on Sunday morning. They controlled the international clash from start to finish, easily dispatching the reigning AFC champion New England Patriots, 35-10.
Yet, Detroit couldn't fully celebrate the Week 10 victory, a fifth straight win for Dan Campbell's squad. The reason why: Aidan Hutchinson, the team's star EDGE rusher , suffered an apparent knee injury on the first series of the game.
It came following a third-and-goal sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye by Hutchinson. The sack forced New England to settle for a field goal on the drive and led to Maye missing the rest of the game.
While the play shifted the momentum in favor of the Lions, it also cost them Hutchinson for the remainder of the contest. The University of Michigan product proceeded to hurt himself while celebrating the sack; he jumped in the air and upon coming down, landed awkwardly on his right leg.
In the immediate aftermath of the injury, Hutchinson was ruled questionable to return. Yet, he never played another down Sunday and was eventually downgraded to out.
After the game, Campbell didn't have an update regarding the injury. But, he did express it “hurts a little bit” to lose the pass-rusher.
“We’ll know more when we get back in the states,” Campbell said of Hutchinson. “But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy. But, I thought guys stepped up in his wake, and showed up for us today and helped us out.”
Entering the Week 10 affair, Hutchinson was the highest-graded EDGE defender in the NFL, with a Pro Football Focus overall grade of 91.7. Plus, he had generated 50 total pressures, the second-most among 110 qualified EDGE defenders.
Additionally, his sack Sunday was his seventh of the 2026 campaign and the 53rd of his five-year NFL career.
Consequently, if the Lions have to play without him for any significant period of time, it'd be a brutal blow to defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit .
Hutchinson last missed a significant portion of a season in 2024, when he suffered a broken left tibia and fibula in a Week 6 contest against the Dallas Cowboys. The ailment cost him the remainder of the aforementioned season.
He bounced back from that major setback, though, and recorded a 16-sack, 100-pressure campaign in 2025. It earned him a 91.7 overall mark from PFF.

title: Latest NFC Standings Show Packers Might Have Dug Playoff Grave Against Vikings
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Had the Green Bay Packers beaten the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, they would have taken a big step out of the seventh-seed pit they’ve been stuck in the last three years.
Now, it might be seventh seed or bust.
Here’s a look at the NFC playoff standings at the end of Week 10.
1. San Francisco 49ers, 8-1.
3. New York Giants, 5-3-1.
4. Carolina Panthers, 4-5.
The Three Wild-Card Front-Runners
5. Minnesota Vikings, 7-2.
7. Green Bay Packers, 6-4.
In the Hunt Because of Lousy Divisions
11. Washington Commanders, 3-5-1.
12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 3-6.
13. New Orleans Saints, 3-6.
15. Arizona Cardinals, 3-7.
16. Philadelphia Eagles, 2-7.
Had the Packers beaten the Vikings, they would have been in the No. 6 spot in the NFC and just a half-game behind the Lions, who they’ll host in Week 18, and the Bears, who they beat earlier this season. That would have placed the NFC North championship and a move up to the No. 2 seed – meaning a home game in the wild-card round with the potential of another in the divisional round – within their grasp.
Instead, the Packers are clinging to the No. 7 spot because of a flimsy tiebreaker. Seattle is No. 8 and Los Angeles is No. 9 because Seattle has the better NFC West record. Thus, the Seahawks rank ahead of the Rams, but the Packers are ahead of the Seahawks because of a better record in conference games.
With eight weeks left in the season, the tiebreakers are subject to change.
In this case, the tiebreakers are irrelevant.
After this week’s phony-baloney bye, the Packers will visit the Rams on Thanksgiving Eve. The winner, obviously, will be 7-4 and own the head-to-head tiebreaker. The loser, obviously, will be 6-5, so one game behind officially but really two games behind because of the tiebreaker.
So, it won’t be a must-win game for the Packers but it’s not too far off.
“Oh, for sure,” quarterback Jordan Love said after the game about being behind the 8-ball in the playoff race. “We’ve talked about [how] these are the games you’ve got to win – NFC North games, and we’re 1-3 in the North. So, yeah, we’ve got to obviously just keep rolling, take it one week at a time, like we’ve talked about.
“But we’ve dropped the ball in three of these games, obviously – two against the Vikings, one against the Lions – that you’ve got to win these games to have a chance in this division. Obviously, we talk about, ‘Everybody’s good, everybody’s winning.’ So, it starts with the division games. You’ve got to handle business, and we didn’t do that today.”
The No. 7 seed is a bad spot to be in because it means a wild-card game at the No. 2 seed and a potential divisional-round game at the No. 1 seed. But, at this point, the No. 7 speed would be better than nothing.
According to Tankathon , the Bears have the toughest remaining strength of schedule, with their eight opponents having a combined .630 winning percentage. The Rams are next at .597, with the Packers fifth at .547, the Seahawks seventh at .538, the Lions eighth at .534 and the Vikings 10th at .527.
So, once again, the Packers blew a huge opportunity against the Vikings. They would have been hot on the heels of the NFC North front-runners, all of whom have difficult closing schedules.
Remaining Strength of Schedule pic.twitter.com/gpSDHvHqyH
In the seventh-or-bust race, the Packers’ remaining schedule includes games against the Rams, Bills, Lions and Bears. The Rams have two games left against the Seahawks along with the Packers, 49ers and Chiefs. The Seahawks have the two games against the Rams along with the 49ers and Giants.
The Packers and Rams will have the equivalent of a mini-bye to get ready for their Thanksgiving Eve showdown.
“Certainly, we’re all disappointed by the product we put out there yesterday,” coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday. “When you’re playing a good football team, you can’t lose the turnover battle like that. We knew that was a critical element going into the game. They were 6-0 when they won the ball; now, they’re 7-0.
“It’ll give our guys a chance to reset, gives us a chance as a coaching staff to try to put together the best plan possible, because we know we got a really good football team in the Rams. I know they’re beat up in some spots, but I think there’s no disputing they’re one of the best teams in the National Football League.”
Here’s what the computers say about the Packers’ playoff chances.
According to The Athletic’s Playoff Predictor before last week’s games, the Packers had a 64 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs, with a 13 percent chance of winning the division. At the time, a win would have moved the Packers’ playoff chances to 76 percent and loss would have sent them down to 46 percent.
Instead, the Packers have a 35 percent chance.
If the Packers can beat the Rams, that would rebound to 58 percent. With a loss, it would fall even further to 23 percent.
At ESPN , the Packers had a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. With a win, that would have improved to 75 percent; with a loss, that would have fallen to 45 percent. Instead, it plunged to 33 percent.
At NFL.com , the Packers had a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. Instead of 74 percent with a win and 45 percent with a loss, their playoff probability is down to 34 percent.
At Playoff Status , the Packers had a 66 percent chance of reaching the playoffs. Instead of 87 percent with a win and 56 percent with a loss, their playoff chances fell to 47 percent.
Using Stick to the Model ’s Playoff Machine, the Packers had a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs, with a swing of 72 percent with a win over Minnesota but 40 percent with a loss. Instead, their playoff probability tumbled to 35 percent.
“I think you’ve got to take it one week at a time,” Love said. “We’re 6-4, so it’s not like we have a losing record. We got to obviously just overcome, take it one week at a time, and win games. But it’s a disappointing loss, and like I said, you just got to get back to work.”
The LaFleur-Love teams have been good during their three-plus years together. They’ve never been great. The Packers' loss to the Vikings was the latest example, writes @JacobWestendorf . ⬇️ https://t.co/uBFicTGOLQ
