title: Chargers Veteran Leader Forcefully Benched After Comments Attacking Front Office
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers have been one of, if not the worst, teams in the entire NFL. With this continuous streak of losses, it will obviously bleed into the general vibe of the team's locker room, with the Bolts' locker room finally seeing some cracks begin to form.
These cracks go beyond the failed Daiyan Henley trade , a trade that facilitated one of the team's most beloved and well-respected defenders on the roster to the division rival, the Denver Broncos. It was coupled with one veteran speaking out.
On Nov. 13, 2026, The Athletic's Chargers beat reporter, Noah Furtado, shared a very good read into the team's view of the roster, with several quotes from general manager Joe Hortiz and players on the team. One of those quotes came from beloved locker room presence, 12-year veteran Bud Dupree .
Unprompted to the article itself, Dupree saw a group of media members standing by the locker room and said: "Don’t ask hard questions to us; ask hard questions to them.. Ask the hard questions. Everybody pull they cameras out and go upstairs and ask questions to them. Everybody. Walk upstairs and ask them.”
Quite a damning quote on its own, but even more so coming from someone who has been around the league for a long time. Dupree has been on multiple teams, many of which had playoff success, giving his opinion to 'press' the front office even more validity.
On Nov. 16, 2026, the Chargers played their next game following the Dupree comments. Dupree, only listed on the injury report for one day of veteran rest, was not active for the Bolts game against the Baltimore Ravens. A game on Monday Night Football, a primetime matchup.
With a large audience watching, it seemed that Dupree was forced to sit out the game , likely due to a disciplinary reason stemming from his comments. This team has been notably obsessed with the media's opinion of them, and with Dupree giving the media ammunition to negatively change the wanted narrative around them, it gave the reason to sit the veteran in favor of young EDGE rushers Caleb Murphy and practice squad elevated player Myles Adams.
The Chargers are Dupree could be in for an ugly divorce if the team continues to lose football games, especially if the offense continues to be the main issue for such losses.

title: Is Ladd McConkey Playing Today? Chargers vs. Ravens Updates for Week 10
full_text:
The winless Los Angeles Chargers have Ladd McConkey injury concerns chasing them into the Monday night primetime game against the Baltimore Ravens.
There are other concerns, of course. The Chargers’ botched trade at the deadline has the front office spiraling while trying to do PR damage control . That’s a thing that is, in a word, difficult, considering the team is 0-8 and now star quarterback Justin Herbert will gut through an injury in a hopeless situation on the road Monday night.
But back to McConkey. Here’s a live-updating look at the latest on McConkey before the Chargers play the Ravens.
Ladd McConkey injury impact, Chargers fantasy football outlook
We recently wrote that it’s time for the Chargers to have uncomfortable Ladd McConkey conversations .
After the breakout rookie season, McConkey just hasn’t been able to stay healthy. This year alone, he’s had knee, calf rib, foot and now back issues, in addition to a concussion.
This obviously makes him a no-fly zone when it comes to fantasy football. But it’s worth wondering if he can keep making the "foundational building block” list when talking about the Chargers long-term, too.
As for fantasy football otherwise, the Chargers are a wasteland. McConkey has hardly played, yet still leads the team in receiving with 17 catches for 286 yards and one score. None of the other wideout options are a threat and the tight ends like Oronde Gadsden have no impact. David Njoku just got activated but doesn't figure to be a huge part of the game plan, either.
Even running back is a mess. Mike McDaniel oddly ignored former first-rounder Omarion Hampton early in the year. The former first-rounder averages just 3.6 yards per carry.
None of this is what anyone expected for a Herbert-McDaniel combo, but it’s become one of the most obvious must-avoids in fantasy football.

title: Neither Chargers Nor Ravens are Ready for Prime Time
full_text:
It’s certainly not what anyone expected a little more than halfway into the 2026 NFL season. Tonight at M&T Bank Stadium, the Baltimore Ravens host the Los Angeles Chargers in a mini-reunion of sorts. The latter team’s new head coach this season is former Chargers’ defensive whiz Jesse Minter.
70 seconds of horrific Justin Herbert interceptions pic.twitter.com/JxamkAbtZv
The Bolts are 0-8, the franchise’s worst start since losing their first 11 games in 2000. They are the first team in the league to drop their first eight games since the 2021 Detroit Lions.
After getting off to a 4-1 start, the Ravens are in the midst of a four-game slide. A year ago, Baltimore got off to a 1-5 start, rebounded to win five straight but eventually missed the playoffs with an 8-9 record.
For the Chargers, the team is in the midst of a nightmarish campaign. Jim Harbaugh’s club hasn’t actually won a game since Week 16 of 2025. That’s a total of 11 consecutive losses, which includes that ugly 16-3 setback to the New England Patriots in the wild card round.
There’s plenty of blame to go around when it comes to the last-place Bolts, a playoff team during each of Harbaugh’s first two seasons at the controls. But the main focus of the finger pointing has been at the offensive side of the football—in particular coordinator Mike McDaniel and seven-year quarterback Justin Herbert.
The Chargers are averaging just 291.6 total yards per game, 26th in the league. The club’s offensive unit has reached the end zone just 11 times in eight outings. That’s two touchdowns less this season than San Francisco’s Christian McCaffrey (13) and Detroit’s Jahmyr Gibbs (13), and as many times as Buffalo’s Josh Allen (11) and Kansas City’s Kenneth Walker III (11).
As of Monday morning, only the Arizona Cardinals (minus-105) had a worst scoring differential than Harbaugh’s team (minus-98). The Chargers have been outscored a combined 116-54 in the first half of their eight contests.
Of course, Minter’s team is having its own issues. The Ravens have been outscored a combined 117-43 during their current four-game losing streak, scoring 13 points or less in each contest.
Talk about irony? Now the Chargers look to get well against a Ravens’ team that will be starting its fourth different quarterback tonight in Jacoby Brissett. Yes, the same Brissett who was at the helm of an Arizona team that marched into SoFi Stadium in Week 1 and handed the Bolts a surprising 26-14 loss —putting them on their current path to no wins.

title: Chargers' NFL Draft Order Update Before MNF vs. Ravens
full_text:
There are questions around the futures of both Justin Herbert and Jim Harbaugh for the Los Angeles Chargers going into the Week 10 finale on the road against the Baltimore Ravens.
Those Chargers are a mess with a focus on messaging amid an 0-8 start.
But there is only one big message hitting home that will capture the attention of the fans right now: The Chargers are 0-8 and, though it stings a bit, running away with the No. 1 overall draft pick in next year’s 2027 NFL draft.
Before the Chargers even took the field against the Baltimore Ravens and old friend Jesse Minter on Monday night, they gained serious headway in the draft order thanks to other results around the NFL.
The Chargers had two serious competitors for the No. 1 pick entering the week: The Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins.
Both of those teams lost on Sunday, with the Titans going down at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars, 40-23, and the Dolphins losing to the Indianapolis Colts, 24-22.
Those outcomes have the NFL draft order shaping up like this at the top:
The Chargers beating the Ravens on Monday night would throw a wrench in things a bit. But there are still tiebreakers and plenty of other things to consider over the next two months or before season’s end.
One of those is a possible “tank bowl” between the Chargers and Dolphins in Week 16 just a few days after Christmas. Given how in games the Titans have been over the last month, too, it’s easy to project them winning a couple more games the rest of the way too.
The bigger story might be the fact it’s hard to see a win on the Chargers’ schedule at all. That, and if they do back into the No. 1 pick, what they might actually even do with such a resource, given the dire state of the roster and the unknown status of Jim Harbaugh’s coaching staff after the season, anyway.
Normally, thinking about someone like Jeremiah Smith catching passes from Justin Herbert would be fun, but things have been anything but normal for the Chargers lately.

title: Fantasy Football Start or Sit: Quentin Johnston to be Strong Flex Option on Monday Night Football
full_text:
Monday night’s matchup against Baltimore brings some important fantasy decisions for managers with players from the Chargers .
Not every option is worth putting into your lineup , so knowing who could make the most of their opportunities is important .
Here are the decisions you should make ahead of the Monday night football matchup.
Johnston is one receiver I’d give serious consideration to this week. The main reason is the absence of Ladd McConkey.
He has the ability to create separation and make something happen when the ball comes his way. With an opportunity to contribute in the passing game, he could be a useful flex option for fantasy managers.
The Ravens won’t make things easy obviously, but Johnston has enough playmaking ability to make him worth taking a chance on.
Gadsden is another name worth keeping in mind for this matchup. He’s shown that he can be a reliable option when called upon, and his receiving ability gives him a chance to contribute in the red zone.
This year has been weird for everyone on this team, but I think it's only a matter of time until he has another big game. Tight end production can be unpredictable, but Gadsden has the potential to put together a solid night. If you’re looking for an option with upside at the position, he’s worth considering.
Herbert is a difficult fantasy decision heading into Monday night.
He’s dealing with a finger injury, and his recent performances haven’t made him an automatic choice for fantasy lineups.
Hebert has been a risky option all year to be honest. Unless you don’t have another dependable quarterback available, I’d consider looking elsewhere this week.
Mitchell is someone I’d be careful about putting into a starting lineup. Although he brings plenty of speed and explosiveness, his workload remains a concern with multiple running backs competing for opportunities. It’s difficult to count on consistent fantasy production when the touches aren’t guaranteed.
Vidal is another player I’d leave on the bench for this contest. The competition in the backfield makes his weekly workload difficult to predict, which isn’t ideal when fantasy managers need dependable production.
The truth is that he could be a great dependable back. He can contribute when given opportunities, but there are too many questions surrounding his involvement to make him a comfortable start.

title: Chargers Confidence Meter: The Ravens Present Another Big Challenge For LA
full_text:
Well, the Los Angeles Chargers are under the bright lights in a matchup against the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. Former Jim Harbaugh protege Jesse Minter will be looking for a passing of the torch moment.
The Bolts face another uphill battle , which is nothing new this year. Justin Herbert and the offense are still searching for their identity. When things get bad, they get real bad for this franchise and we could possibly see another beatdown come game time.
The biggest question will be, if the Chargers can stop this new and improved offense backed behind quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
The Baltimore Ravens enter this matchup with a major change, acquiring Jacoby Brissett via trade.
Now Brissett has an opportunity to provide some stability to an offense that desperately needs direction. For the Chargers, preparing for Brissett creates an interesting challenge. He is not a quarterback who needs to rely on spectacular plays to make an impact. His experience gives him the ability to recognize defensive looks, make adjustments, and take what the opposition gives him.
A huge factor or game changer you could say is the defensive line. If Mack, Mesidor, Tuipulotu, and others can put pressure on that offensive front, more mistakes are bound to happen for a new guy trying to learn a different scheme.
The Bolts will need to be disciplined in coverage and avoid giving him easy opportunities to keep Baltimore’s drives alive. Allowing him to settle into a comfortable rhythm could make the evening much more difficult. Overlooking them because of its quarterback situation would be a mistake. The Ravens still have experienced playmakers who can make life difficult for a defense. He did beat them the first game of the season, so there's that.
However, there is an adjustment period that the Chargers should look to take advantage of. Brissett is joining a new locker room, learning a different offensive system, and developing chemistry with receivers he has not spent an entire season playing alongside. Communication and timing will be especially important. If the Bolts can create pressure and force Baltimore into uncomfortable situations early, it could disrupt the Ravens offensive plans.
The defense has done an incredible job this year and with a hot start they might just be on their way to a win. Anything opposite of that, you might as well kiss the win goodbye.

title: Chargers' Future, Justin Herbert Status Speculated by Ian Rapoport
full_text:
Though they have kept the messaging consistent about staying the course , it feels inevitable that the Los Angeles Chargers will look at major changes this upcoming offseason.
It’s a point that’s hard to argue given the 0-8 start and the lack of any games left on the schedule to feel very comfortable about right now.
Big changes could mean anything too, really. While the organization is worried about sending the right messages around the trade deadline disaster, one would think that Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz could be in danger next offseason.
Jim Harbaugh and his Chargers coaching staff, with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel topping the list, will likely face severe hot seats and the front office blowing up the whole thing and starting over wouldn’t be that shocking.
Granted, these are just presumptions based on what outsiders can see. But even major reporters are saying the same thing.
Is this a case of smoke pointing to an obvious fire?
During an appearance on ESPN, Ian Rapoport called the Chargers the “most stunning thing of this entire season,” and suggested that the team could be looking at massive changes soon.
“I would expect a pretty wholesale look at everything after the season,” Rapoport said. “This is a place that really should win games…the acclimation process should be over. Everything that could go wrong has gone wrong.”
A big disclaimer, though: Everything doesn't include moving on from Justin Herbert. Rapoport added this on Herbert: “I’ve gotten zero sense that they would move on from him at all.”
Zooming out, the Chargers struggling this season isn’t that big of a surprise. The front office sat on loads of free cap space and tried to find bargains, leveraging the now for a “future” the current regime might not even see. McDaniel was a splash hiring, but the personnel department never matched his speedy needs and he’s made some odd decisions, like steering away from first-rounder Omarion Hampton.
If one had to guess, Harbaugh and his staff will be gone after the season no matter what ownership has to pay. Starting over yet again around Herbert and continuing one of those problematic themes of his career stinks, but indeed, even the worst of projections would’ve never been bold enough to suggest the Chargers would end up like this.

title: NFL Trade Rumors Feel Like More Damage Control from a Lost Chargers Organization
full_text:
The Los Angeles Chargers are completely lost and it impressively doesn't have anything to do with the 0-8 record.
By now, everybody knows about the Chargers’ botched NFL trade deadline deal with the Denver Broncos.
What they might not know is the Chargers’ ridiculous damage control messaging aimed at good PR around the move. They might also not know about how this debacle has started to officially help lose the locker room completely .
And somehow, keeps getting worse. More and more reporting keeps coming out about the deadline disaster, and more and more of it keeps feeling like PR efforts put out by a team that can’t win off the field, either.
The first set of buzz pushed to the spin cycle presumably by the Chargers suggested that they never actually wanted to trade Daiyan Henley anyway. But the addition of a 2028 fifth-round pick alongside a fourth-round pick was basically a “godfather” offer they couldn’t refuse.
Now, new reporting from The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones goes as far as suggesting this might’ve been some sort of master plan by the Chargers to get a few draft picks and then re-sign Henley next offseason.
“After considerable back-and-forth, the Broncos added a 2028 fifth-round pick to get it over the finish line,” Jones wrote. “The Chargers dealt their young, well-liked team captain to Denver with a hope that they could actually re-sign him come March. Being able to get two mid-round picks for Henley only to lose him for half of a lost season would be a coup for the team.”
It sounds more WWE than NFL. The Chargers were going to throw a key core piece of the roster to a division rival to help them compete in the playoffs, then attempt to re-sign him in free agency.
And the Broncos, after coughing up two draft assets for Henley, were going to be happy if he played well enough to help them and…get a single compensatory draft pick back for his departure after half a season.
Look, the Broncos trying to change this deal after the deadline is indeed a loophole the NFL should close. But that’s really missing the point here.
The grander point is the Chargers said they wouldn’t trade key pieces, wound up changing their minds over a fifth-round pick and have since masked the erratic behavior by floating the idea this was all some master chess play to get extra draft picks and possibly Henley back, too.
And the longer this foolishness keeps popping up around the Chargers, the easier it is to understand why they play the way they do on the field…and the more concerning it is when thinking about the long-term future of the club.

title: Why Did Chargers Leave Out 1 Critical Name When Talking Untradeable Players?
full_text:
While trying to control the messaging around a lost season and a botched NFL trade deadline, the Los Angeles Chargers made some pretty interesting comments that might shine a light on where things go from here.
Granted, comments from players and reporting suggests the Chargers have lost the locker room. Pounding the table for the core group of players, then trading one of them in a panic to a rival at a deadline, only to botch the trade and get that player back, tends to do that to a team.
But while addressing these happenings over the last week or so, Chargers general manager Joe Hortiz made a noteworthy comment, where what he didn’t say seemed to be pretty notable.
Endless reporting and common sense said the Chargers were never going to trade players like quarterback Justin Herbert and wide receiver Ladd McConkey.
But other recognizable names were quite a bit more debatable. This week,Hortiz made sure to address the “core” group of players who entered the trade deadline as untouchable.
An excerpt from The Athletic’s Noah Furtado hits on this point: “He offered his list of hard noes by name. Quarterback Justin Herbert. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey. Tackle Joe Alt. Safety Derwin James. Cornerback Tarheeb Still. He stopped there, but perhaps he could have continued.”
Really astute onlookers will notice a missing name: Tuli Tuipulotu.
We’re not going to outright claim this is a sign of things to come for the Chargers. But Hortiz rattling off core players and omitting a 24-year-old pass-rusher with 29 sacks in 58 games due a major contract extension feels like it could be a big deal.
And hey, maybe not. Lots of factors went into the list of names and not everyone was going to get included. But there’s a smudge of deja vu here. Hortiz, after all, traded for Odafe Oweh, watched him break out at the age of 26 and refused to pay him market rate last offseason and then compensated by using a first-round pick on an “older” prospect like Akheem Mesidor to attempt to immediately fill the production gap.
In other words, misguided bargain hunting that burned unnecessary draft capital. Who is to say the same doesn’t happen again? There have already been rumblings that the Chargers and Tuipulotu talked extension and it didn’t work out.
There are other future factors at play, like franchise tags. But scanning the Chargers’ roster, Tuipulotu is 100 percent a building block who should be a hard-no as a trade candidate, or at least mentioned as such.
Not this time with Hortiz though, it seems.

title: Rams Week 10 Snap Counts Reveal Interesting Changes at Key Positions
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams were forced to make several adjustments in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Injuries forced head coach Sean McVay to make some changes. With Puka Nacua and Davante Adams sidelined, the wide receiver rotation looked significantly different. Meanwhile, the running back rotation saw a surprising shift as well. Let's take a closer look at the snap counts from Week 10.
The Rams were without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams on Sunday against the Cardinals, relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels, and Xavier Smith. While most of those players were in the WR3 rotation prior to Nacua’s injury, someone was going to get the most snaps and targets.
That player ended up being Konata Mumpfield . Mumpfield led the Rams with four targets, but also saw 63 percent of the offensive snaps. That was three times as many as Tutu Atwell’s 21 percent and more than Xavier Smith’s nine percent.
However, it’s worth noting that rookie CJ Daniels was second in the rotation. Daniels only had one catch on two targets for 22 yards.Still, he played 61 percent of the offensive snaps and filled some of the Puka Nacua role because of his size.
The Rams may get Adams back for Week 12 against the Packers, but it will be interesting to see how the rotation continues as Nacua is out until Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys.
For much of the season, Kyren Williams has gotten around 65 percent of the offensive snaps while Blake Corum has gotten 35 percent. That has generally been the split over the last four games as well.
Against the Cardinals, Corum and Williams each played 51 percent of the offensive snaps. Additionally, Corum led the Rams with 17 carries. It’s certainly a shift from what we’ve seen this season. Some of that had to do with the Rams running 20 personnel and both Corum and Williams being on the field together.
With that said, Corum was also the more effective back as he averaged 5.9 yards per carry and had his second career 100-yard game. Due to Ronnie Rivers closing out the final drive, he actually ended up with more carries than Williams as well. The running back rotation will be something to monitor, but the Rams still trust Williams.
Last week, Myles Garrett dominated with three sacks in his first game back. However, Garrett didn’t have much of an impact on Sunday against the Cardinals. He was only credited with one pressure via PFF. He also only played 43 percent of the defensive snaps, which was down from last week’s 59.7 percent.
Some of that was likely due to the score. Still,Garrett's ineffectiveness while on the field, combined with his admission last week that he's not 100 percent yet, leaves some room for concern.
This is likely going to be a week-to-week thing and the Rams having 10 days of rest should help. While Garrett is back on the field, his knee issue is something to monitor, especially with him showing up on the injury report last week.

title: Rams Position Grades: Running Game Shines in Blowout Win Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams beat the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 behind several dominant performances. Matthew Stafford played efficiently at quarterback while Blake Corum rushed for 100 yards. The Rams also got good production out of their wide receiver depth. Let’s jump into this week’s position grades.
This was arguably Matthew Stafford’s most efficient game of the season . While he still needs to clean up the turnovers, Stafford threw to nine different receivers, and his 0.63 EPA per pass was second only to Brock Purdy. The Rams don’t need Matthew Stafford to be special every week. If the Rams can get Stafford to be efficient while playing good defense, they will win games.
According to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop, The Rams have outrushed their opponents by 478 yards over the last four games. That’s their largest rushing yardage differential over a four-game span since 1984, which is also the year Eric Dickerson ran for 2,105 yards. Blake Corum, Kyren Williams, and Ronnie Rivers combined for 44 carries for 204 yards.It won’t look like that every week, but the Rams have a very strong rushing attack.
For the most part, the Rams’ wide receiver depth exceeded expectations . Konata Mumpfield led the group with three receptions for 81 yards as Xavier Smith scored a touchdown. All four players had at least one reception of more than 20 yards. This group will be challenged in the next two games, but they stepped up in a big way on Sunday.
While there has been a lot of conversation around the Rams and their usage of 20 personnel in this game, they still relied heavily on 13 personnel. The tight ends delivered as Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen found the end zone in the passing game.
The offensive line deserves a lot of praise for how it played on Sunday. They are a big reason why the Rams were able to run as successfully as they did. The Rams also did it with their third-string left guard and third-string center. They will hope to get healthy after the bye, but this group played well.
Wesley Bailey has been a star for the Rams as an undrafted free agent. Against the Cardinals, he became the NFL's first undrafted rookie to record an interception, multiple sacks and multiple forced fumbles in a season since at least 2000. Aaron Donald also recorded his first sack of the season .
It’s unlikely that the Rams would play Shaun Dolac over Nate Landman. It’s a limited sample size, but when he has been on the field, Dolac has played like one of the best linebackers in the NFL. Dolac also had a forced fumble that resulted in a turnover on downs while leading the defense in tackles.
This wasn’t as strong of a performance from Josh Wallace and Quentin Lake as we’ve seen from them this season. Lake got beat on the second drive of the game for a big gain in man coverage. However, McDuffie remains a lockdown cornerback when he’s healthy, and Kam Kinchens had a key interception at the end of the first half.
The Rams had two kickoffs land outside the landing zone or field of play. They need to get more consistency with the dirty kickoff because it is something that works. Special teams didn’t have too many mistakes outside of that, which makes it a positive week.

title: 10 Takeaways From Rams’ Dominant Win: Sean McVay's Masterclass, Blake Corum's Emergence, and More
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Arizona Cardinals, 34-6,  to win their fourth straight game. Despite managing injuries throughout the roster, it was arguably the Rams’ most complete win of the season as they now enter the bye week at 6-4. Let’s get into this week’s 10 takeaways.
For as much criticism as Sean McVay can get in losses, he deserves credit for these kinds of wins. The Rams were seen as the better team heading into Sunday, but there was a chance that it could be ugly without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. McVay installed a new personnel grouping, utilizing two running backs on the field at the same time. That wasn’t something that he had done prior. When the Rams were down to their third center and third left guard, they used six offensive linemen on a handful of plays. What McVay did on Sunday against the Cardinals was a testament to his coaching and ability to adjust the offense to its personnel.
There were a lot of questions about how the Rams would replace Nacua and Adams. It’s fair to say that it was only the Cardinals. The next two games will test that depth further. With that said, Xavier Smith’s touchdown was a turning point. Konata Mumpfield led the Rams with three receptions for 81 yards. The Rams’ four wide receivers combined for seven catches for 174 yards and a touchdown.
Stafford threw an interception for the fourth straight game, and it seemed to be when attempting a no-look pass over the middle. However, he bounced back after that and had a QBR of 81.9. His 0.63 EPA per pass ranked second behind only Brock Purdy. Without Adams and Nacua, Stafford threw to nine different receivers and no player had more than three catches. That’s a drastic change to even a week ago when Nacua had 19 targets and no other receiver had more than five.
This isn’t to say that Kyren Williams doesn’t still have value in the Rams’ offense. However, Corum has outperformed Williams over the past month , and that was the case again on Sunday. Corum led the Rams with 17 carries for 100 yards. During the Rams' four-game win streak, Corum is fifth in the NFL in rushing yards, leads the NFL in rushing success rate and EPA per rush, and ranks ninth in yards after contact per attempt. Williams has a role, but it may not be a bad idea for the Rams to ride the hot hand.
The Rams were able to rush for over 200 yards and they did it without Steve Avila at left guard and Coleman Shelton at center. For much of the game, the Rams were down to their third left guard in Bill Murray and third center in Beaux Limmer. The Rams don’t rush for over 200 yards without the offensive line doing its job and creating rushing lanes.
Over the last two weeks, the Rams have allowed 16 points on the opening two drives of the game. After that, they’ve allowed three. In the first eight games of the season, the Rams allowed 21 points per game. They haven’t allowed more than 13 points in the last three weeks. Sunday was the fourth time this season that they haven’t allowed a single touchdown and it was the third time in the last five weeks. If the Rams can count on the defense to play like that, they’ll be tough to beat once the offense gets healthy.
It’s easy to see how Aaron Donald is enjoying himself now that he’s able to play alongside Myles Garrett. This isn’t to say that he wasn’t having a good time previously, but playing alongside Garrett was a big reason Donald returned in the first place. Donald got his first sack of the season on Sunday. With the monkey off his back, there will likely be many more to come over the rest of the season.
Sunday’s game against the Cardinals would have been a perfect time to give Simpson some live game reps. During Jordan Love’s first two seasons, the Green Bay Packers played him during blowouts. The Rams led the Cardinals 34-6 in the fourth quarter. Instead, Simpson remained inactive, and Stafford played until the final whistle in a 28-point win.
While the Rams had their usual slow start, this was arguably their most complete win from start to finish. The offense punted one time and had one interception. Outside of that, they scored four touchdowns while the defense held the Cardinals to six points and forced two turnovers. There have been a lot of games this season where the Rams disappear for long stretches. They were in control of this one from the jump.
Nobody would have been surprised if the Rams just got by the Cardinals with an ugly win . Instead, the Rams won 34-6 without their top two wide receivers and injuries along the interior of the offensive line. However, this is a Rams team that just keeps battling through every pitch thrown their way. We’re going to learn a lot about this team after the bye week, but at 6-4, they are right in the hunt.

title: Monday Morning Rambling: The Rams Have Become a Team That Refuses to Break
full_text:
Five weeks ago, the Los Angeles Rams were arguably at rock bottom when they lost at home to the Arizona Cardinals. They were 2-4, there were calls for head coach Sean McVay to give up play-calling, and given the injuries, there were predictions of how this was just going to be another 2022.
If this 2026 team had existed in 2022, it’s possible the coaching staff and players would have spiraled and things would have begun to snowball. However, that wasn't this Rams team, and it never was. After avenging their loss to the Cardinals , the Rams have now won four straight games and sit at 6-4 heading into their bye week.
This is a Rams team that, over the last four years, has become resilient. In 2023, they came back from 3-6 to make the playoffs. They recovered from 1-4 in 2024 to make the postseason as well. Heartbreak after heartbreak in 2025 and early on this season, the Rams continued to bounce back.
Resilience. That’s exactly what this Rams team is.
All season, they’ve managed heartbreak losses to the Denver Broncos and Buffalo Bills. They haven’t allowed injuries to define them. It wasn’t until last week that the Rams finally got Myles Garrett back in the lineup. They’ve missed key players such as Kobie Turner, Poona Ford, Jaylen Watson, Terrance Ferguson, and others.
Against the Cardinals, the Rams were without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Instead of waving the white flag, Konata Mumpfield led the Rams with 81 yards receiving. Xavier Smith, who was cut after Week 3, scored his first career touchdown at the end of the first half that completely changed the game.
Last season, when the Rams were without Nacua, McVay installed 13 personnel that week of practice before they beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 35-7. On Sunday against the Cardinals, the Rams ran 17 plays out of 20 personnel. They had only ever operated out of 20 personnel six times under McVay, and all six plays were in victory formation.
The Rams have gone through their share of hardships this season, but McVay has found a way to get them to the other side. There have been claims that McVay has lost his touch or should give up play-calling.
Sunday was another example of McVay’s mastery. To be able to install a new personnel grouping during the season isn’t easy. McVay has done it two years in a row when his team has been forced into that corner.
Without Nacua and Adams, there was a serious argument that Blake Corum and Kyren Williams were two of the best players on offense. When the Rams operated with three wide receivers against the Cardinals, instead of also using a tight end and lining up in their typical 11 personnel, they used another running back.
Beating the Jaguars in Week 7 was arguably the Rams’ most complete win up to that point. However, despite being without Nacua and Adams, an argument can be made that Sunday's performance against the Cardinals was even better.
Offensively, the Rams rushed for 200 yards and scored more than 30 points. The defense had two turnovers and didn’t allow a touchdown. It may have been a slow start, but the Rams effectively dominated from start to finish.
A win against the Cardinals is just that. Getting that first division win is nice, but beating the Cardinals 34-6 is what should happen. It’s important for the Rams not to put too much stock in that win, but after everything they’ve gone though, that is a win they can still feel good about going into their bye week. They've climbed out of rock bottom and are ready
The Rams using two-running-back sets on offense and pony personnel is something that I’ve been wanting them to do for years. They finally did it and had success. Now, it’ll be interesting to see if they use it more or if it was a one-week adjustment and the Rams go back to what they’ve done as they get healthy. Either way, it was cool to see the adjustment pay off.
This isn’t to say Kyren Williams doesn’t have value in the offense. The Rams have found a two-back system that works and should stick with that. However, Corum rushed for 100 yards, showing off his impressive jump cut and explosiveness through the hole. During the Rams’ four-game win streak, Corum ranks fifth in the NFL in rushing and leads the league in EPA per rush.
Following Week 3, the Rams cut Xavier Smith and that wasn’t necessarily the wrong decision at the time. However, the Rams brought Smith back this week with some of the injuries at wide receiver, and he scored his first career touchdown on a play that ended up changing the game. You could see how much it meant to Smith, and those moments are what sports are about. He shouldn’t see time as the team’s punt returner, but as a receiver, he’s shown some value.
It might be a cop-out to give Sean McVay the game ball as they don’t normally go to coaches. However, McVay deserves a lot of credit for that win and the changes made to the offense.For as much criticism as he gets when the Rams lose, he deserves credit when they win, especially after a coaching display like Sunday's.
That’s how many designed runs the Rams had on Sunday against the Cardinals. It’s worth noting that 15 of those runs came on the final drive. With that said, if the Rams are going to be successful without Adams and Nacua, they are going to have to run the ball and play good defense. Against the Cardinals, the Rams ran the ball 44 times and didn’t allow a single offensive touchdown for the fourth time this season.
We’ll get into playoff scenarios and things like that during the Rams’ bye week. However, as it stands, the Rams sit at 6-4. After the bye, things get much more difficult as the Rams have one of the toughest schedules in the NFL. In 10 days, they’ll play the Packers on Thanksgiving Eve at SoFi Stadium. If they want to make the playoffs, that one feels like a must-win.

title: Rams Winners and Losers: Sean McVay's Masterclass, Blake Corum Shines in Blowout Win
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams defeated the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday to get their first division win of the season. It was a dominant performance as the Rams won 34-6 . The defense allowed just six points and forced two turnovers while the Rams rushed for 202 yards. Let’s jump into this week’s winners and losers.
Without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams in the lineup, Sean McVay adjusted the offense. It’s sometimes taken for granted how difficult it can be to install a new personnel grouping in a week.Last season, the Rams did it against the Jacksonville Jaguars when they installed 13 personnel. Against the Cardinals, the Rams installed 20 personnel after only using it on six plays under McVay. The Rams also used six offensive linemen at times once Beaux Limmer took over at center. Sunday was a McVay masterclass.
It felt like it was only going to be a matter of time before Aaron Donald finally got his first sack since his return. For the first time since New Year’s Eve of 2023, Donald got a sack. He finished with 1.5 sacks, and with the monkey off his back, it wouldn’t be surprising to see the production continue. Donald has played well the last two weeks with Myles Garrett in the lineup and it’s easy to see him enjoying himself more.
This isn’t to say that Daniels didn’t play well. It’s possible we’re talking differently about his performance if Matthew Stafford hit him in the end zone. However, he finished with just one catch for 22 yards. He also had two pre-snap penalties, one of which took away a touchdown from Kyren Williams. There’s a lot to like about Daniels, but it was also easy to see why he hasn’t been on the field as often as some may have expected.
It might be time to have a conversation about whether Blake Corum should be the lead ball carrier in the offense going forward. Over the last two weeks, it has been Corum who has provided a spark to the offense. Corum finished with 100 yards on 17 carries and scored a touchdown for a sixth straight game. It was also the sixth straight game that he’s had 50 scrimmage yards and a touchdown.
When the Rams cut Xavier Smith after Week 3, it was for the right reasons. Smith shouldn't be playing on special teams, but he does provide some value as a wide receiver. However, he does provide some value as a wide receiver and the advanced metrics support that. Smith caught a screen pass in his return and took it 20 yards to score his first career touchdown. It was easy to see how much the moment meant for him.
The Rams ran the ball 44 times. Blake Corum ran 17 times for 100 yards and Ronnie Rivers had 15 carries for 81 yards. Both Corum and Rivers averaged more than five yards per carry. Williams had 12 carries for 23 yards. When the Rams needed to close the game, they went to Rivers, who had 15 straight runs on the final drive. Williams is still important to the Rams’ offense, but he was the lone running back who didn’t have success on Sunday.
A good day running the ball always points to the offensive line. It wasn’t easy against the Cardinals as the Rams lost Coleman Shelton and his backup Dylan McMahon. The Rams had Beaux Limmer at center and Bill Murray at left guard. For the most part, they also kept Matthew Stafford upright in the second half.
It was once again in limited snaps, but it’s hard not to like what we’ve seen from Shaun Dolac this season. Dolac led the Rams with six tackles and had half a sack.Additionally, he forced a fumble by Carson Beck on fourth down, resulting in a turnover on downs. He’s currently behind Nate Landman and Omar Speights. However, when he’s been on the field, Dolac has done well.

title: Rams Show They Can Win Without Puka Nacua in Dominant Victory Over Cardinals
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams entered Week 10 shorthanded and needing a division win . After putting Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the Rams were without their top two wide receivers. However, the offense had no problem. Behind 31 unanswered points, the Rams earned their fourth straight victory, winning 34-6 to improve to 6-4.
When the Rams managed injuries at the wide receiver position last year, they implemented 13 personnel for the first time. Prior to that game, Sean McVay had used 13 personnel on just 6 snaps since 2021.
On Sunday against the Cardinals, the Rams used two running backs with three wide receivers (20 personnel) on six snaps that were all in victory formation. The Rams used two running backs on the field on nearly 30 percent of their offensive snaps against the Cardinals.  They ran 17 plays out of 20 personnel, totaling 197 yards and a touchdown.
The Rams still used plenty of 13 personnel. They used 13 personnel at a 63.5 percent rate, which was the second-highest mark in the McVay era. Still the twist to have both running backs on the field was a welcomed twist.
The Rams started slow as the two teams traded field goals. Matthew Stafford struggled initially with the pressure from the Cardinals  defense, throwing an interception in a fourth consecutive game. The offense had just 10 yards rushing with a little over five minutes to go in the first half, trailing 6-3.
However, much like last week against the Washington Commanders, it was running back Blake Corum who sparked the offense. Corum rushed six times for 44 yards as Matthew Stafford capped off the touchdown drive with a pass to Tyler Higbee in the end zone to give the Rams the lead. From there, the Rams didn’t look back.
Kam Kinchens intercepted Carson Beck and returned the ball into field goal range. With 13 seconds left in the half, Stafford hit wide receiver Xavier Smith on a screen, who took the pass 20 yards for the score. After being cut following the Week 3 loss to the Denver Broncos, Smith scored his first career touchdown in his return to the Rams and put them ahead 17-6.
Without Nacua and Adams, the Rams’ wide receiver depth stepped up. Konata Mumpfield led the way with three catches for 81 yards. All four wide receivers had at least one reception longer than 20 yards.
Following Joshua Karty’s kick that fell short of the landing zone, it looked like the Rams may go into the half with a one-point lead. Instead, they led by two scores and carried that momentum into the second half.
Late in the first half, Coleman Shelton went down with an injury and backup center Dylan McMahon left the game as well. Down to their third center, McVay used six offensive linemen to start the second half to combat the Cardinals’ defensive pressure.
On the opening drive of the second half, Stafford hit Mumpfield for 44 yards on 3rd-and-7 before Corum found the end zone from a yard out for the sixth straight game to put the Rams up 24-6. Corum had his second career 100-yard game and his first since the Rams’ win in Arizona last season. The Rams running back finished with 17 carries for 100 yards to go with three receptions.
With the offense short-handed, the defense consistently stepped up on Sunday. TThey didn’t allow a touchdown for a second straight game against the Cardinals.Aaron Donald got his first sack of the season as the Rams got to Carson Beck five times in the game. Following two short fields due to kickoffs out of bounds, the defense got a turnover both times. The second one was an interception by Wesley Bailey that resulted in a touchdown from Stafford to Davis Allen.
This was a win that the Rams needed following the injury to Nacua. While the schedule certainly gets more difficult after the bye week, this should give them some confidence that the offense can still operate without their top playmaker.
For as much criticism as McVay gets during losses, he deserves a lot of credit for the Rams’ win against the Cardinals.It’s not easy to implement a new personnel grouping in a week, and he’s done it in two straight years.
The Rams enter the bye week at 6-4 and remain tied with the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks for the final playoff spot in the NFC. They will have some time to hopefully get healthy before entering a grueling part of their schedule as they try to make a push for the postseason.

title: Rams Sunday Morning Notebook: Davante Adams Return Timeline, Puka Nacua Update, and the WR They Should Have Drafted
full_text:
As the Los Angeles Rams head into Week 10, they are still looking for their first division win of the season. They should have a good chance on Sunday as they play the Arizona Cardinals with Carson Beck set to make his first career start. There’s a lot to discuss this week as the Rams continue to manage injuries. Let’s get into this week’s Sunday Morning Notebook.
The Rams entered the trade deadline needing a wide receiver, and while they made calls, nothing ever got serious. A big reason for that was because the Rams are expecting Davante Adams and Puka Nacua back this season.
Earlier this week, head coach Sean McVay was asked when he expected Adams to be back. McVay seemed to think Week 13 after the Packers game was realistic.
“I would think after Green Bay is a realistic timeline for him, but he looks great,” McVay said on Wednesday. “I talked to him the other day and he's feeling good and excited whenever that time is to get him back.”
However, despite McVay saying that Adams could be back after Green Bay, NFL Media’s Ian Rapoport seems to believe the target date is the Packers game.
“They believe the Thanksgiving Eve game, that’s Wednesday against the Packers, would be the target date. So sooner rather than later,” said Rapoport.
From @NFLGameDay : A look at when the #Rams may be getting WR help... pic.twitter.com/jcRcxqFFix
Rapoport’s report seems to contradict what McVay said earlier in the week, but either way, the expectation is for Adams to be back shortly after the bye.
After Nacua got injured last week against the Washington Commanders, there was some thought that the Rams might not put him on injured reserve. Nacua’s injury is expected to keep him out for around four weeks. With the Rams projected to have already used six of their eight return designations from injured reserve, they considered saving one by not putting Nacua on IR.
However, the Rams ended up deciding to put Nacua on injured reserve . McVay explained what changed on Friday.
“We needed the roster spot. We didn't need it initially, semantics, mechanics of it. There was never going to be a time that he was going to be able to return prior to it anyways,” said McVay. “It really was not putting him on because of roster mechanics. Some things changed where we needed that spot because of all the moving pieces…That was what went into the thought process there, but he's in good spirits.”
The Rams will be without Nacua for four games, not four weeks. That would put Nacua’s return in Week 15 against the Dallas Cowboys on December 20.
With every passing week that the Rams deal with another injury at wide receiver, the victory laps from those who believed they should have drafted a wide receiver in the first round only continue to grow. However, while Simpson is just the emergency third-string quarterback every week, that is all part of his development plan. Simpson looked good at the end of training camp and the preseason.
If Simpson works out, it will have been the right call. Additionally, Makai Lemon has been one of the least-efficient rookie wide receivers in 2026, struggling to make an impact for the Eagles. He hasn’t looked good for the Eagles so far. Maybe that would be different with the Rams, but the overall production would likely look similar. Lemon is averaging 0.97 yards per route, which ranks 88th out of 111 wide receivers. He also ranks 82nd in EPA per target.
The argument that the Rams should have taken Lemon with the 13th overall pick is growing tired.  However, the correct takeaway is that the Rams probably should have taken Antonio Williams over Max Klare.
Williams scored a touchdown for the Commanders in their win on Thursday Night Football against the New York Giants. While we can call it hindsight, Williams is the player that I took for the Rams in my shadow draft .
ANTONIO WILLIAMS TO THE PYLON. COMMANDERS RESPOND. WASvsNYG on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6dLcWP6Mos
His 0.32 EPA per target ranks 45th, putting him between players like George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb.. Williams is also averaging 1.38 yards per route run. At the end of the day, he’s also contributing.
Had the Rams drafted Williams, he may be in the same spot Klare is with limited snaps. However, Klare’s upside this year was always TE5. Even when the Rams have been hurt at tight end, they’ve barely used him. At worst, Williams would have come in as the WR4.

title: Joshua Karty's 'Dirty Kickoff' Is Making a Big Difference for Rams Special Teams
full_text:
Special teams has been a consistent theme for the Los Angeles Rams this season. For much of the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams were by far the worst special teams unit in the NFL.
Through eight weeks, the Rams had a -12.9 special teams DVOA. While the Rams still have the worst special teams unit, they’ve improved to a -9.5 special teams DVOA over the last two weeks.
A big reason for that improvement has been the addition of Joshua Karty and the “dirty” kickoff. It’s certainly been unconventional for the Rams to roster two kickers, but it has worked out for their special teams. Karty had inconsistencies last year on the field goal unit, but he excelled on kickoffs. Instead of a high, soaring kick with hangtime, Karty’s dirty kickoff is a low, wobbling kickoff designed to mimic a ground ball in baseball, making it difficult for returners to handle.
As seen in Karty’s return against the Los Angeles Chargers, there is some risk with the dirty kickoff. Given the low trajectory, there is a possibility of it landing before the landing zone, resulting in a flag that puts the offense at the 40-yard line.
However, for the most part, the Rams have reaped the rewards and it’s helped the kickoff coverage unit. Through the first eight weeks of the season, the Rams were allowing an average of 28.7 yards per kickoff return and teams were starting at the 34.7-yard line on average.
With Karty’s dirty kickoff, that has improved dramatically. It’s still a small sample size and teams may adjust as they see it more. With that said, over the last two weeks, the Rams have allowed just 18.8 yards per return and teams have started at the 29-yard line on average. That’s almost a 10-yard improvement per return and a better field position of 5.7 yards.
What makes that even more impressive is that Karty has done that despite two kicks landing short of the landing zone. However, Karty helped offset those mistakes with two touchbacks last week. Given that the ball hits the ground before the end zone on the dirty kickoff, touchbacks go to the 20 rather than the 35.
Karty's two "dirty kickoffs" that resulted in touchbacks. Returners may get more comfortable as they see it more, but there's also a reason these guys are playing football and not shortstop. pic.twitter.com/7lbXx8zJoR
There is still a lot of room for improvement with the Rams’ special teams, but the in-season implementation of the dirty kickoff is evidence of the coaching staff doing what it can to improve the operation. With limited roster spots, it’s also worth considering how long the Rams can afford to roster two kickers.
Outside of kickoffs, the Rams have also improved on the punt team in recent weeks. Over the last two games, Ethan Evans’ 44.6 net yards per punt is ninth in the NFL and he is PFF’s second-highest graded punter. Brandon McManus has yet to be tested on the field goal unit, but is perfect on extra points and his three field goal attempts.
For much of the season, the Rams' special teams were actively hurting their chances of winning games. Signing Karty and implementing the dirty kickoff shows the coaching staff continuously working to improve that facet. With the dirty kickoff, the Rams have found something that works, but they still need to prove they can be consistent. Given how costly special teams mistakes have been this season, that's at least a step in the right direction.

title: Rams Desperately Need Wide Receiver Help, But Is Hollywood Brown the Answer?
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are in a desperate spot at wide receiver following the injury to Puka Nacua. With Davante Adams set to be out at least the next two games, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, and CJ Daniels at wide receiver .
After the Rams struck out at the trade deadline, they will likely wait for players to become available as free agents when veteran players begin asking for their release. The Rams benefitted from this in 2021 with Odell Beckham Jr. and in 2022 with Baker Mayfield.
That process has already started. Late this week, wide receiver Marquise “Hollywood” Brown requested his release from the Philadelphia Eagles. According to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk , that request is set to be granted.
Following the trade deadline, the Rams restructured the contracts of Kyren Williams and Kam Curl to open up around $3 million in cap space for situations like this and to help get them through the season.
As a cheap option, Brown makes a lot of sense. Due to the release happening after the trade deadline, Brown will be subject to waivers. His minimum base salary makes him an intriguing option for teams in need of a wide receiver.
The waiver order is updated weekly and is based on a reverse standings order. Heading into Week 10, the Rams would be 18th in the waiver order. However, given that Brown is asking for his release from the Eagles, it’s likely that he wants to play for a competitive team and his agent will make that known. According to NFL Insider Jordan Schultz, Brown is expected to sign with a playoff contender.
He wants to be here, bring him in Les pic.twitter.com/DGAsNw04st
Brown had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns last season with the Kansas City Chiefs. However, this season with the Eagles, Brown has just five catches for 63 yards and hasn’t been a fit in that offense.
There’s no doubt that Brown would give the Rams a more experienced third option at wide receiver, which is what they are lacking. At the same time, he is very similar to the types of players the Rams already have an abundance of at the position.
Heading into Week 10, the Rams’ depth chart at wide receiver will include Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and Brennan Presley. All of those players are listed under 5’10”, and Smith is the heaviest at 180 pounds. Brown is 5’9, 170 pounds.
If a player like Stefon Diggs, Brandon Aiyuk, or someone similar became available , it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Rams explore those options. Given the Rams’ current wide receiver room, it’s hard to see them signing another undersized wide receiver unless they were to move on from someone like Atwell or Smith. However, that seems unlikely given how the Rams seem to prioritize players with familiarity in their system.
The Rams should absolutely explore every available option at wide receiver, especially with some of their injuries at the position. Brown may be one of the more recognizable names to become available, but that doesn't necessarily make him the right fit.

title: Without Puka Nacua, It's Time for the Rams to See What They Have in Rookie Wide Receiver CJ Daniels
full_text:
It’s been no secret that the Los Angeles Rams haven’t gotten a lot of production out of their rookie class. With their first pick, they took Ty Simpson, who has been the emergency third-string quarterback most weeks. With their next two picks, the Rams selected depth players in Max Klare and Keagen Trost. The most productive rookie for the Rams has been undrafted free agent edge rusher Wesley Bailey.
Through nine weeks, the Rams rank 31st in snap rate for their rookie class at 1.7 percent. The only team worse than them is the Denver Broncos at 1.3 percent. For the most part, unless the Rams have been forced to play their rookies, they haven’t seen the field.
Rookie snaps for every NFL team What do you notice? pic.twitter.com/VVzHr2LAgZ
With the Rams down to just three tight ends against the Los Angeles Chargers, they reverted to 11 personnel to start the game, a personnel grouping they weren’t built for. The Rams’ offense struggled, and they were forced to play Klare in the second half. That adjustment and going back to 13 personnel was a turning point in that game .
Despite Klare playing well against the Chargers, he was back to playing 0 snaps on offense last week against the Washington Commanders.
As the Rams head into Week 10 against the Arizona Cardinals, they are in a similar predicament at the wide receiver position. Without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, the Rams will be relying on Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith, and CJ Daniels at wide receiver.
The x-factor in all that is Daniels. Throughout training camp and the start of the season, head coach Sean McVay has consistently described Daniels as a mature rookie. All accounts are that Daniels impressed in training camp and, from a production standpoint, he performed well in the preseason.
“He’s just had a mature presence, kind of no nonsense but it's not too big for him. He's so secure to be able to handle coaching or corrections,” said McVay on Friday. “He plays big at the catch point. He has a physicality. A lot of the things that you're looking for from our receivers, he's checking those boxes and he's very curious. That's what you really want from these guys is the humility and the passion for the game.”
There’s certainly a difference in the level of play and complexion of the offense being run in the preseason compared to the regular season. Throughout the McVay era, the Rams have typically brought rookies along slowly, especially those at the skill positions outside of a few exceptions. The Rams have shown that when rookies demonstrate they are ready and can handle the intricacies of the offense, they will get an opportunity.
Still, given everything that Daniels showed in the offseason, it seems odd that he has yet to get that opportunity despite some of the injuries to the wide receiver position. Based on body type alone, it would seem that Daniels would be the most logical replacement for Adams. McVay hinted at a larger role for Daniels last week, but he played just one snap.
“He's had a lot of great moments behind the scenes,” said offensive coordinator Nate Scheelhaase this week. “We've been really encouraged about his development and his progression as the year has gone on. He's been as fun of a player to watch on our practice field for the last few weeks. I'm obviously excited for him to continue to get opportunities, but they're opportunities that he's earned through a lot of hard work, through a lot of consistency in how he's approached.”
The Rams are at a point in the season given their injury situation that they have nothing to lose by playing rookies. While the Rams needed the wide receiver depth, it was almost concerning when they brought Xavier Smith back this week after striking out at the trade deadline. The worst thing the Rams can do is give an ‘edge-of-the-roster’ type player snaps over someone with upside like Daniels.
That’s not even to say that Smith isn’t a good wide receiver. He showed some value last season when he ranked second in the NFL in EPA per target, was fourth in targeted success rate, and was top 20 in yards per route run. However, he should be getting snaps over a player like Tutu Atwell, not Daniels.
It’s time for the Rams to see what they have with some of their rookie class, and specifically Daniels. During the preseason, Daniels earned the most targets per route among wide receivers. His 1.91 yards per route run ranked sixth.
“C.J. has done a hell of a job,” said quarterback Matthew Stafford. “You look at the crossover tape when  Stetson and Ty are working against our defense, he's showing up in a big way a lot of different times. I'm excited to get some chances to throw with him, get it out there on Sunday, and just get his feet wet.”
Without Adams, Daniels is arguably the only wide receiver with the size to play outside the numbers. From a size standpoint, he’s a 99 percent match to Nacua via Mockdraftable. He’s 6’2, 202 pounds. Heading into Sunday, the average size of the Rams’ wide receiver depth chart is 5’9.8, 182.4 pounds.
With the Rams missing their top two options at wide receiver, it’s time to see what they have in Daniels. Given the depth of the roster early in the season, it made sense to be patient with the rookie. If Daniels is as ready as the coaching staff has suggested, it's time to put him on the field and let him prove it.
