title: From Beck to Brady: Trying to Predict Where Dolphins QB Kyle McCord's Debut Will Fall
full_text:
Not sure if you've heard, but first-year quarterback Kyle McCord will make his NFL debut for the Miami Dolphins against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.
Of course you knew that, it's been the topic of conversation since the Dolphins placed starter Malik Willis on injured reserve Tuesday with what now is being described as a core muscle injury.
The Dolphins offense struggled for most of the first eight games of the season because of a wide variety of issues and the question is whether McCord can bring some life to it.
This is an exciting time for some fans quick with an evaluation that Willis simply isn't the long-term answer at quarterback for the Dolphins based mostly on the results and what they've seen as Willis' hesitation in the pocket and too-slow decision-making.
It's been a saying for a long time that the backup quarterback often is the most popular player on the team if you don't have a star at the position because the unknown brings hope of something better.
But, of course, the grass isn't always greener ... and if the backup was better than the starter, then maybe he wouldn't be the backup.
That brings us to McCord, who is an unknown as a quarterback can be because he's never played a down in the NFL. Yes, he looked good in Green Bay's preseason finale against Arizona this summer, but that was the preseason and that's nothing like a regular season game because defensive coaches keep things very simple for those games and pull out all the stops for games that count.
McCord is a different type of quarterback than Willis, and maybe he'll be quicker with his decisions and let it rip more freely, and maybe that produces more completions but maybe that also produces more throws into traffic with a bad outcome and maybe an interception or two more.
Head coach Jeff Hafley said he would encourage McCord to be aggressive, but any rookie making his first start is bound to have some hesitation. That's just natural.
The bigger issue for McCord is that the Dolphins supporting cast, which everyone can acknowledge is sub-par, didn't get any better over the past week. On the contrary, McCord now will have to play without starting center Aaron Brewer and rookie wide receiver Chris Bell.
So what do the Dolphins have in Kyle McCord? And what might it first NFL look like?
For some fans, the idea is that maybe he becomes for the Dolphins what Brock Purdy became for the San Francisco 49ers after taking over for the injured Jimmy Garoppolo late in his rookie season — against the Dolphins no less.
We also saw — pretty sure we saw — a reference to another former sixth-round pick taking over for an injured starter in his second season and never let go of the job. You know, Tom Brady?
The other end, of course, is McCord turning into former Dolphins second-round pick John Beck, who flamed out after getting his first NFL start in October 2007.
Beck was a poor 9-for-22 for 106 yards in his first NFL start in a 17-7 loss against the Eagles.
Even Brady's first start was pretty mundane in terms of stat, as he went 13-for-23 for 168 yards with no touchdowns or picks, though it did come in a 44-13 Patriots win against Peyton Manning and the Colts when the defense dominated.
We certainly have no reason to expect that kind of dominance from the Dolphins against the Colts today, even if Peyton Manning isn't playing anymore.
We would suspect, however, that McCord's stat line will look more like that of Brady than that of Beck.
It's a guess as to what McCord actually will look like again because judging his work at Ohio State and Syracuse and in the preseason — his stats were uninspiring last year with Philadelphia and this year with Green Bay before that finale — though he does look the part.
A best guess from here in terms of what his stats will look like would be something like 15-for-27 for 189 yards with one touchdown and one pick.

title: Dolphins Sunday Mailbag: Grant, Uche, Jonah, and More
full_text:
Part 2 of the pre-Colts game Miami Dolphins On SI mailbag:
Hi Alain, with Uche getting huge backing being named a captain, what sort of deal do you expect? This is Grant's chance; should we have high expectations of him finally living up to his draft status? A loss is a win on Sunday considering the Jets have their pick … thoughts? Thanks
Hey Colin, let’s begin with the idea that Josh Uche absolutely deserves a contract extension after the way his season has started, and how he finishes will determine what kind of contract he might get. I don’t know it will be big money regardless, but maybe a second year gets tacked on. As for Grant, yes, this absolutely is a big moment for him because he’s going to get additional snaps and he’s further removed from the foot injury that cost him the start of the season. He needs to show something, period. As far as the game and the draft, the Colts don’t have that extra incentive — if any team were so inclined — to lose because their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the Jets.
From Damian from Pittsburgh:
Hi Mr. P! Greetings from Pittsburgh. Hope all is well, and your holiday plans are coming into focus. Thinking about the OLine, specifically the disappointing right side. Jackson is a lost cause; even setting aside the injuries, he's a below-average RT. Not quite a bust, but way overdrafted. I'm more interested in Jonah, and if he's salvageable. Is he gonna come around? And what if MIA swapped him to LG? Put him between two strong OLineman, and pop Proctor over to the right side (guard or tackle). Thoughts?
Hey Damian, Jackson has been a solid starter for most of his career, though, yes, absolutely overdrafted. With Jonah, no, I would not advocate switching him back to the left side. At some point, he’s got to make it work on his own. The good news with him is he’s definitely better than he was as a rookie, though there still are some holes in his game, particularly in pass protection.
Hi Alain, good to see the Dolphins defense contain Goff and the Lions last week. It made me wonder about your thoughts on Hafley’s defensive philosophy and his tree. My understanding is that he runs a scheme similar to Fangio’s but from what I can tell, he never worked with Vic. Do you have any insights on his defensive influence, and how you feel about his coaching overall at the halfway mark of the season?
Hey Daniel, I’d say overall I’ve been very impressed by Hafley in terms of getting his players ready to play and I like his defensive scheme and how it’s progressed throughout this season. The inspiration for his defense come from the Pete Carroll scheme with the Seattle Seahawks and also from working with Robert Saleh when the two were assistants with the San Francisco 49ers. My only complaint with Hafley is I’d like to see him be a more aggressive in fourth-down decisions, but that’s being picky because I do think he’s off to a very good start.
Hi Alain. Great work as always. Any idea how much a GM considers a draftees age as part of the evaluation process prior to drafting? As a for instance and considering two recently drafted Dolphins players, Chop has played 39 NFL games vs. Jacob’s 8 with Chop being 4 months younger. I appreciate that a longer college career could mean a more developed player coming out and possibly maturity issues but considering wear and tear long term, I would assume if the potential is seen to be there a younger prospect is seen as a big bonus. Thanks again for the fantastic, objective  reporting.
Thanks Lee, appreciate the kind of words. As you indicated, an older prospect logically gives you a more mature, more polished draft pick, while the younger prospect might have a longer shelf life. But the reality is a GM won’t be thinking 8-9 years down the road, so the longevity issue takes a back seat to getting somebody more ready to contribute quickly. So if everything else is equal, particularly in terms of ceiling, a GM likely will go with the older prospect who’s going a better chance to help out right away.
Greetings Alain ! After the Colts started their own rebuild, I thought Miami had a good chance to win. But now the Dolphins have a QB who has never thrown a pass in a real NFL game & in a hostile environment. While they may have traded best their best D-lineman, they still have Sauce Garder & Charvarius Ward vs rookie WRs plus Lou Anarumo, who can confuse a young QB. They still have Jonathan Taylor vs a Miami DL without Zach Sieler. Not to mention a terrible Special Teams unit. As the late, great Dick Enberg used to say, "Oh my!" Do we see a heavy dose of Ollie Gordon ? A lot of check-down passes ? As always, I look forward to both All Dolphins (appreciate the shout-out, doing much better) & Dolphins Collective podcasts plus all the best out there written content on Miami DolphinsonSI.Com.
Thanks Dave, it’s a pretty good assessment of the game you had right there, and a heavy dose of Ollie Gordon II and check-downs absolutely is a logical thing to expect, simply to make Kyle McCord’s NFL debut as simple as possible.
If McCord goes 2-2 and plays well, does Willis return as starter?
Jeff Hafley already has said that Willis will be the starter once he returns, and it’s exactly what Hafley should have said but with the understanding that if McCord lights it up, then he’ll have every right to reconsider that stance. And it’s not going to be about whether the Dolphins win or lose, but rather how McCord performs. But it would have to be a really impressie performance to just shelve Willis like that.
Not a game question, but I read things about Miami’s team needs, I see lots of positions of need but it’s almost as if WR is being considered not a need. This is one of the worst rooms in football, even if Douglas is somewhat OK. Do you think they still need upgrades there, Alain?
Oh, without question. What the Dolphins have at wide receiver is a lot of potential with Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman Jr., but only Douglas should be locked in for a big role in 2027, along with Malik Washington. So, yeah, that group still could use some help,  which is why so many fans like the idea of taking Jeremiah Smith if the Dolphins have the chance.

title: Jordan Addison Injury News Will Likely Impact This Vikings Trio the Most
full_text:
The 2026 Vikings offense may have finally taken its first stride toward success in a promising performance against the Packers on Sunday, but Monday brought news that could delay our chance to see the unit at its full potential.
Jordan Addison was questionable heading into Sunday’s game with a thumb injury and was ultimately sidelined after testing the injury pregame. On Monday, head coach Kevin O’Connell shared that Addison will miss time after having the thumb surgically repaired .
Jordan Addison is likely a short-term IR candidate after aggravating a thumb injury Kevin O'Connell: “Just on Jordan Addison, tried to see if we could get him all the way to game day and see if we could possibly have him yesterday. But he did sustain a thumb injury, actually a… pic.twitter.com/emDjOFc7dn
While the news is certainly less than ideal with a matchup against the top-seeded 49ers approaching this week, three Vikings in particular will have a chance to prove themselves through the adversity.
Justin Jefferson is fresh off a season-high nine receptions without his main sidekick against the Packers, proving he can still take over games on his own when needed. Now, with Addison out for the next few weeks, Jefferson’s situation gets a bit complicated.
The Kirk Cousins to Justin Jefferson connection is so back MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/VKdh3yVImv
It's safe to assume Jefferson will continue to get looks, especially now that his old friend Kirk Cousins is back under center, but Addison’s absence will allow defenses to focus more on number eighteen. I expect to see more double and even triple coverage against one of the best wideouts in the NFL.
The good news? We’ve seen Jefferson make plenty of spectacular catches in tight coverage before. He’ll certainly get more chances in the coming weeks.
One thought kept running through my mind after Sunday’s game in Green Bay: “Imagine what Cousins will be able to do once Addison is back!” Well, looks like we’ll have to wait a while longer to see what that looks like. The good news is Cousins seemed ready to rock in his return to the Vikings, even without one of his best weapons.
8️⃣ ball pic.twitter.com/2MVUeWF0zl
Cousins was decisive, finding eight different pass catchers during his first game back in purple on Sunday. Most impressively, Jefferson was the only one Cousins had played with before this week. After only a couple of practices, Cousins proved he’s willing to get the ball to his new teammates, which may be good news for one young receiver in particular.
Was Sunday the breakout performance for Myles Price ?
The second-year undrafted free agent has already proven his value as a kick and punt returner, but his performance this past weekend on offense was certainly eye-opening. With both Addison and Jauan Jennings sidelined, Price saw a career high in receptions (four), receiving yards (49), and his first NFL receiving TD.
Kirk Cousins with a dot to Myles Price for the TD! pic.twitter.com/LDWKjEjR9V
While these stats aren’t exactly jaw-dropping, it's clear Price’s speed and versatility could benefit the Vikings' offense. While Jennings will likely take the WR2 spot upon his return, I’d expect Price to get more looks with Addison recovering. If he continues to impress, he may prove to be another useful offensive weapon even after Addison's return.

title: What the Sudden Jordan Addison Injury News Means for the Vikings Moving Forward
full_text:
After popping up on the Vikings' injury report with a thumb injury late in the week, Jordan Addison missed Sunday's Packers game, and the news following the win isn't promising.
Kevin O'Connell told reporters on Monday that Addison's thumb injury will require surgery (h/t Alec Lewis of The Athletic ), knocking the star receiver out for at least a few weeks. The expectation is that Addison could land on short-term injured reserve, meaning he'll miss a minimum of four games.
The sudden news deserves one star and two enthusiastic thumbs down, as Kirk Cousins and the Vikings will now be forced to navigate life without their No. 2 weapon.
Against Green Bay, Cousins showed he can work with very little when Addison, Jauan Jennings, and T.J. Hockenson all sat, but losing Addison for the foreseeable future will be a tough hurdle for the offense to overcome as Cousins continues to settle into the system. Luckily, O'Connell also mentioned on Monday that he expects both Jennings and Hockenson to return this week against San Francisco.
And in the least surprising take of the century, the Vikings will now lean heavily on Justin Jefferson and hope Jennings becomes the receiver they hoped he would be when signing him this spring. Jefferson saw season-highs in both targets and receptions in his first game with Cousins, and that duo will need to be even more in sync now. But while Jefferson's outlook looks its brightest in years, Addison's injury makes one big decision even more difficult.
Addison's production has dropped in each year since his standout rookie season, and now, with the missed time coming up, the Vikings' offseason decision to extend him (or not) won't be so clear.
Inside the Vikings building, Addison is well liked, and his potential as one of the best No. 2 receivers in football is still very much in play. But now, with a recent thumb injury, Addison will see his catches, yards, and possibly touchdowns drop in three straight seasons.
Obviously, the injury isn't his fault. But without the next three or four games on tape, Nolan Teasley and company will be forced to base their decision on previous versions of their receiver unless they opt to let Addison play out his fifth-year option without a deal.
Jefferson has a cap hit of nearly $50 million dollars on 2027, and while Addison has seen his production fall, he's still a candidate for a $100 million deal himself based on his potential alone. He'll be just 25 next season, and the Vikings will likely be very tempted to pay two receivers top dollar despite the laundry list of other free agents.
Blake Cashman, Andrew Van Ginkel, Jalen Redmond, and more will be looking to get paid as well, so somebody will end up heading elsewhere. Could it be Addison? His slow start and unfortunate injury haven't helped his case, but neither Tai Felton nor Myles Price look to be ready for a WR2 role either.
Ideally, Addison can return quickly and show the Vikings why he deserves to be paid next year.

title: Harmon’s Vikings Longship Week 10: 4 Pressing Thoughts After Season-Saving Win vs. Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, W.I. — Vikings fans have certainly been on an emotional roller coaster through the first ten weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
From being the NFL’s last undefeated team after a 6-0 start, to watching two great defensive efforts be wasted by terrible quarterback play, then reacquiring Kirk Cousins , the last two months have been a ride. Sunday marked a fork in the road, a chance for Minnesota to reestablish its identity against its most bitter rival.
With a unique mix of uncertainty and optimism, the Vikings set sail for what would become a season-defining 30-10 victory over the Packers.
It’s fair to say there were more questions than ever heading into Sunday’s Border Battle, as the Vikings were missing one of their best defenders, linebacker Blake Cashman, and two offensive weapons, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson. Cousins’s job would be hard enough after only a couple of days of practice, but the injury report certainly didn’t help.
One thing was clear: this would be a perfect “prove it” moment for Cousins and the Vikings.
While Cousins’s stat line was less flashy than many past performances Vikings fans are used to, this may rank as the most impressive day of his career. Cousins finished with a hard-fought 207 passing yards and two TDs. Impressively, both came to pass catchers he had never thrown to before this week: Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew.
To come in and take control of the offense in less than a week is an incredible feat after spending the last two and a half seasons away from head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense.
What a difference a week can make. pic.twitter.com/GfiRVSc4d0
As great as Cousins was, this was another day decided by defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit. The pass rush racked up an incredible eight sacks, the highest total by any team in the 2026 season. Their 37 sacks for the year now lead the entire NFL, while star outside linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel’s 8.5 sacks for the season are the second-most in the league.
The Packers were certainly feeling confident after their 45-point showing last week, but they left Sunday’s game with only 10 points on the board.
Safe to say Flores can ruin your mood in a hurry.
This likely won’t come as a shock, but it seems that simply adding a steady, competent QB may have been exactly what the Vikings needed to prove what they can do. Sunday’s showing previewed what could be possible once Cousins gets more comfortable in the offense.
Oh, and did I mention he was missing two of his top three pass-catchers? I feel like that’s important…
With a defense that continues to prove why it was worthy of general manager Nolan Teasley’s trade-deadline urgency, the sky truly is the limit once things start to click. Sunday represented an imperfect but hope-inspiring look into what Vikings fans everywhere hope to see in January.
An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq
I feel confident saying that the eventual NFC champion will have a distinct advantage in the Super Bowl. That is, if they aren’t too bloody and bruised from the path to get there. The conference is a beast, and the NFC North is a particularly terrifying gauntlet.
With the Bears on their bye week, the Lions kicked off Sunday’s festivities with a 35-10 win against the Patriots in Munich, but suffered greatly from the loss of star defender Aidan Hutchinson. Initial reports indicate that he may have torn his ACL while celebrating a sack.
From @GMFB : #Patriots QB Drake Maye could be lost for the season with a lower leg injury, while #Lions edge Aidan Hutchinson suffered a season-ending knee injury, likely a torn ACL. pic.twitter.com/yBvpbU5g30
The Lions now leap into the top spot in the NFC North while the Vikings leapfrog the dormant Bears for second place. If the season ended today, the fifth-seed Vikings would travel to Charlotte to face the fourth-seed Panthers in the playoffs.
Luckily, there is still a lot of football left to earn back the NFC North title and a home playoff game at U.S. Bank Stadium, starting with a trip across the border.
The Vikings will head south next weekend for a primetime international matchup in Mexico City. Their opponent is their toughest conference challenge: the top-seeded 49ers.
The 49ers and Cowboys battled in an absolute shootout on Sunday, as San Francisco left Dallas with a 46-40 victory. The 49ers have been the clear favorite in the NFC this season, overcoming injuries to put together one of the most consistent and disciplined squads.
BROCK TO CMC OH MY SFvsDAL on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/JoKDvzWC3K
If the Vikings want to prove they now have all the tools needed to contend with the best, Sunday’s Mexico matchup is their best opportunity.

title: Expanding Myles Price’s Role Will Be in Vikings' Best Interest Moving Forward
full_text:
Week 10 sent the Vikings to Green Bay to face off against the Packers in an important NFC North showdown. It was also an opportunity for the Purple and Gold to rebound after a humbling defeat to the Bills on Monday Night Football.
Several factors weren't working in Minnesota's favor. The Vikings' starting quarterback, Kirk Cousins, arrived through a trade earlier in the week and had less than a week to prepare for the game. Not only that, but two wide receivers—Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings—missed the game due to injury.
With Addison and Jennings sidelined, second-year WR Myles Price stepped up to help the Vikings achieve a 30-10 victory over their rival . Price caught all four targets for 49 yards and a touchdown while adding one rushing attempt for 12 yards, giving him 61 of Minnesota's 312 offensive yards.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
Considering how the Vikings' WR depth behind Justin Jefferson has left much to be desired this season, it's in head coach Kevin O'Connell & Co.'s best interest to keep feeding Price the ball moving forward.
Heading into Sunday's game against the Packers, Price had been mostly used on special teams as a return specialist. He had only played 90 offensive snaps in the team's first eight games, and 29 of those came against the Bills last week, finishing with a six-yard catch on four targets.
Price played a season-high 33 offensive snaps on Sunday (four more than in Week 9) and got five touches on those opportunities. It was obvious that Jefferson would lead the wide receivers in snaps, but it was surprising that Tai Felton saw more offensive reps than Price.
Felton played all but 10 offensive snaps for Minnesota, participating in 59 plays. He was targeted more than Price, catching three of five passes for 33 yards. Considering Addison and Jennings were out, it was nice to see Felton step up, even if he was outplayed by Price.
O'Connell may need to re-evaluate his wide receiver room if Cousins develops a rapport with Price. Having him as the fifth wide receiver on the depth chart seems unreasonable if he can be more productive than the players above him. For reference, Addison has finished with 27 or fewer yards in five of his seven appearances, while Jennings has 54 receiving yards on the season.
That doesn't mean Price shouldn't continue as the team's return specialist, but it does mean that he could be ready to do more for Minnesota. The Vikings are used to rostering specialists who can contribute offensively, such as Cordarrelle Patterson and Percy Harvin.
Price may not have the pedigree of Harvin or Patterson, but he seems to rise to the occasion when given opportunities. Against the Packers, he played less than half of the team's offensive snaps, finished second in receiving yards, and found the end zone.
If given more chances, what else could the 24-year-old accomplish with the Vikings? We'll find out on Sunday Night Football in Week 11 against the 49ers, who allowed 343 receiving yards and five TDs on 30 catches in their 46-40 win against the Cowboys over the weekend.

title: 3 Vikings Studs & 2 Duds in Sunday's Dominant Win vs. Packers: Minnesota's Offense is Waking Up
full_text:
The Vikings desperately needed to regroup after an embarrassing loss to the Bills on Monday Night Football. This week would be another challenge for the Purple and Gold: a road trip to play the Packers.
Week 10 felt different. The Vikings looked competent offensively, and the defense did its best to contain the explosive Packers offense. Minnesota looked like the team many fans hoped they would be this season, earning a 30-10 win over their division rival .
Some players were studs in this game, doing a lot to help win the contest. Others struggled to contribute in a positive way, earning a "dud" title for the game against the Packers.
Let's take a look at five notable Minnesota players from Week 10's win against Green Bay.
Welcome back to Minnesota , Kirk Cousins. The veteran quarterback didn't have crazy numbers for the Vikings on Sunday, but he completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception.
In their first game with Kirk Cousins, the #Vikings already have their second-highest point total of the season. pic.twitter.com/KLNGNrD5wo
The offense converted half of their third downs after not converting a single one last week against Buffalo. Minnesota's 11 passing first downs helped to win the time of possession and control the pace of the game.
The Vikings have been playing fullback Max Bredeson a lot less since the start of the season, instead looking to tight end Ben Yurosek as an active blocker. Bredeson was once again used lightly in Week 10, even with Minnesota running the ball on half of their 62 offensive plays.
Bredeson was targeted with one pass, but was unable to haul it in. Minnesota might be struggling to find a role for the rookie blocker if he continues to struggle to be effective when given opportunities to make an impact.
Patience has paid off handsomely for rookie safety Jakobe Thomas. After being inactive all season , the third-round pick finally got an opportunity to take the field against Green Bay and made an impact in his small role.
Thomas was credited with two tackles against the Packers, but the most celebrated contribution was a forced fumble on a kick return from J. Michael Sturdivant early in the fourth quarter that was recovered by fellow rookie Jake Golday.
Even the @Vikings ' special teams is forcing turnovers! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F8HXXTeFb4
It's great seeing the young guys making plays.
The Vikings' offensive line has struggled this season, and not even starting left tackle Christian Darrisaw is immune to mistakes. Heading into this game, he has been credited with allowing nine quarterback pressures and six sacks while being flagged for three penalties.
Honestly, almost any Minnesota offensive lineman could have been included here due to some protection issues that led to Cousins being sacked three times for a loss of 24 yards. Thankfully, those plays didn't hurt the Vikings too much, but the status quo won't be good enough if the Vikings want to win a Super Bowl.
Wide receivers Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings were out for this game. Justin Jefferson played well, leading all pass catchers by grabbing nine of 13 targets for 74 yards. However, the team still needed someone to step up.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
Myles Price made the most of his opportunity, catching all four passes thrown his way for 49 yards and a touchdown. With Cousins at the helm, it will be interesting to see if chemistry continues to develop with Price as the season goes on.

title: Vikings Report Card Week 10: Grading Every Position After Beating the Packers in Kirk Cousins's Return
full_text:
It appears the Vikings just have the Packers' number, finishing their season series at 2-0 while averaging 34.5 points per game.
Kirk Cousins made his return to Lambeau, the place where his first tenure with the Vikings ended, and simply played quarterback the way Minnesota needed QB to be played.
The defense was suffocating; the offense was watchable ; the Vikings are now 7-2 with two wins over the Pack. Here's how Cousins and the rest of the team graded out in the win.
The gaudy video game numbers weren't there, but the third-and-23 and third-and-15 conversions during the first half showed exactly why the Vikings brought in Kirk Cousins. The Minnesota offense finally looked respectable after weeks of misery, and it's in large part due to the steady play of Cousins. A midweek trade and just days to assimilate weren't enough to stop "Kirko" on Sunday.
Yeah, the Vikings probably should have made a trade for a back at the deadline . Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason were once again decent enough with 106 combined yards, but it's clear Kevin O'Connell doesn't trust his backs with the constant screens and bubbles on third-and-short. Cousins elevates the passing attack, but the run game still isn't scaring any defenses.
Funny how the offense moves when Justin Jefferson gets his touches. Cousins looked his way a season-high 13 times, and Jefferson looks very much back on track. Myles Price notched his first receiving touchdown, and the Vikings survived without their No. 2 and No. 3 receivers. Things are only looking up once the corps gets healthy.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
With no T.J. Hockenson, Gavin Bartholomew reeled in his first career touchdown on a 20-yard strike from Cousins. No other pass-catchers besides Jefferson had played with Cousins before today, so seeing the young guys get involved was certainly encouraging. Rookie TE Ben Yurosek added a reception as well.
The offensive line continued to be just good enough once again, but hasn't been a strong piece of this offense by any stretch of the imagination. Cousins was dropped three times, and even the strengths of the line—tackles Christian Darrisaw and Brian O'Neill—were each beaten badly off the edge on plays that resulted in sacks.
The Packers were utilizing six offensive linemen at one point during the game, trying anything and everything to slow down the Vikings' pass rushers. The defense notched eight sacks on Jordan Love while allowing just 56 yards on the ground, and the defensive front was at the forefront of the effort.
Caleb Banks was quiet in his first start with just two tackles, and his outlook remains undecided for now .
The Vikings were without Blake Cashman, and Ivan Pace Jr. wasn't especially productive with just a pair of tackles, but Eric Wilson and the edges stepped up in a big way. Wilson led the team in tackles, adding a sack as well, and Andrew Van Ginkel's strip in the first quarter set the tone for the entire game.
Andrew Van Ginkel just took it right from him! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/qROgreyURh
Harrison Smith notched his 41st interception, and the secondary as a whole held strong against the league's leading passer. Love was held to under 230 yards for just the third time this season, and even a fluky, pinball reception to Savion Williams wasn't enough to ignite the Packers' lethal passing attack.
Will Reichard was steady as usual, but the star on special teams today was the rookie Jakobe Thomas, formerly the No. 8. Wearing his new number after gifting away the eight to Cousins, Thomas popped out the ball on a late kickoff return, setting up the Vikings' drive to ice the game.
Even the @Vikings ' special teams is forcing turnovers! MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/F8HXXTeFb4
Not bad for a season debut.

title: 3 Most Important Vikings Takeaways After Week 10's Statement Victory vs. Packers
full_text:
GREEN BAY, W.I. — Less than a week ago, the Vikings took the field on primetime TV and put up one of the most embarrassing offensive performances imaginable. The resulting loss sparked a whirlwind 24 hours that eventually led the team to reacquire their long-time quarterback , Kirk Cousins, in a trade with the Raiders.
On Sunday, Cousins retook the offensive reins after only a few days back in Purple and Gold. With Blake Cashman, Jordan Addison and T.J. Hockenson all ruled out , “Kirko” and crew would certainly have their work cut out for them.
Would the move immediately pay off? Would Cousins’s rust in head coach Kevin O’Connell’s offense define the day? Would the Vikings' defense put up another stellar showing against a talented offense?
Let’s break down the most important takeaways from the Vikings 2026 Border Battle-sweeping 30-10 win on Sunday.
If you were wondering how long it would take Cousins to get comfortable, the answer was not long at all.
After a few unspectacular plays early on, Cousins found Myles Price with a precision toss for a 38-yard touchdown late in the first quarter.
COUSINS TO MYLES PRICE FOR A TD ON 3RD AND 23 MINvsGB on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/jSQvCluTla
With no Addison or Hockenson and a lack of familiarity with many of his new teammates, Cousins was able to work wonders given how stacked the odds were against him. He would throw for 207 passing yards and two touchdowns (with one interception) in his first game back in Purple and Gold.
Justin Jefferson had another relatively quiet day, a fact not helped by Addison’s absence. He did manage to bring in a few key catches on a drive that ended with a Gavin Bartholomew score. Jefferson finished the day with nine catches for 74 receiving yards—better than your average WR, but not enough for what Vikings fans want from the star playmaker.
Defensive coordinator Brian Flores and his unit came out swinging early.
Dallas Turner bullied Packers left tackle Jordan Morgan by throwing him into Jordan Love for an early sack; then Harrison Smith snagged his 41st career interception on the first play of the second quarter. Levi Drake Rodriguez and Eric Wilson also brought Love down on back-to-back plays early in the second.
Jalen Redmond with a sack. The Vikings have brought down Jordan Love SEVEN times. There are 8 minutes left in the third. pic.twitter.com/N1OSx9gbjk
The sack attack continued early in the third, even as Green Bay finally got on the board with a 32-yard passing TD. The Vikings’ eight sacks on the afternoon are the most by any team in the NFL this season, as they held the Packers to 10 points one week after they scored 45.
The circumstances were less than ideal for the Vikings, yet they put together their most complete team performance of the season to end a two-game losing streak. With a difficult battle against the 49ers in Mexico City on the horizon, this week will be a crucial opportunity to get healthy and continue to get the offense in sync.
If Sunday was any indication, this revamped Vikings squad can hang with anyone.

title: Vikings Can’t Ignore the Looming Jalen Redmond Decision They Should Make ASAP
full_text:
The Vikings will face many difficult decisions to make after the conclusion of the 2026 NFL season, but the decision of what to do with defensive lineman Jalen Redmond shouldn't be complicated .
Redmond is scheduled to become a restricted free agent after this year, and the Vikings shouldn't wait until the last minute to get an extension done with the third-year defender since he has made himself such a valuable part of defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit.
Heading into Week 10's showdown vs. the Packers, Redmond has an 81.5 Pro Football Focus grade , which ranks him as the third-best interior defensive lineman in the NFL. Additionally, his 90.1 run defense grade makes bringing him back to Minnesota essential.
The only reason the Vikings should even consider waiting to re-sign Redmond is if Minnesota feels comfortable with the other pieces on the defensive line. At the moment, there are still enough questions about rookies Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange to make them want to extend Redmond, who's up to 25 solo tackles, 20 pressures and 15 run stops across 416 snaps, according to PFF .
Jalen Redmond was incredible against the Bills. 5 pressures, half a sack, and his usual great run defense. He's playing at an All-Pro level this season. pic.twitter.com/7bEsuRnyDV
For Redmond, staying in a defense where he thrives would be smart, but only if he feels he is being compensated fairly. For 2026, the Purple and Gold are getting an absolute bargain , employing the 27-year-old for $1.075 million on a one-year deal.
A significant pay raise is in order, and the longer Minnesota waits to make him an offer, the more the price tag will increase. NFL salaries are skyrocketing at an alarming rate, and allowing Redmond the opportunity to hear offers from other teams that the Vikings would then have to match is a scary situation.
According to Spotrac, the Vikings are projected to have $28.4 million in cap space next offseason , along with a list of unrestricted free agents that includes:
If Redmond is allowed to test the market as a restricted free agent, a team that needs a run-stuffing defensive lineman will likely throw a lot of money his way to get his services, even if it means potentially losing a draft pick in the process.
One of the only ways Minnesota could safeguard itself from Redmond leaving is to give him a first-round tender. That would cost the Vikings $4.149 million for 2027, but teams would likely not want to part with a first-round pick to take him from Minnesota.
Redmond is young, productive and important enough to offer an extension before he becomes a restricted free agent. That would show the young defender that the Vikings appreciate what he does for the team, but it would also reward him for his play and give him stability for one more year in Purple and Gold.

title: Potential Hollywood Brown Flyer Leaves Vikings With Nothing to Lose (And Everything to Gain)
full_text:
Kirk Cousins's return will elevate the Vikings' passing game, but there's only so much the veteran quarterback can do. With Jordan Addison banged up, Jauan Jennings ruled out for Week 10 and Justin Jefferson needing more help, adding wide receiver depth when possible isn't a bad idea.
Interestingly, an opportunity to add reinforcements may have fallen in the Vikings' lap.
On Friday, the Eagles released veteran wide receiver Marquise "Hollywood" Brown . He played only four games for the NFC East team before being let go.
We have waived WR Marquise Brown and T Fred Johnson. pic.twitter.com/S4ieutMSfU
Brown wasn't used much in Philly. He played a total of 120 offensive snaps in four games for the Eagles, catching five of eight targets for 63 yards and running the ball twice for 12 yards. Considering that he had over 1,000 receiving yards in 2021 with the Ravens, it is surprising to see his contributions to a team fall so far.
Now that he is a free agent, he is free to sign with any team. While Minnesota doesn't make a lot of sense at first for the 29-year-old receiver, he might be exactly what the Vikings need to spark their passing offense.
There is little debate that the Vikings have one of the most anemic offenses in the NFL. As of Sunday morning, they are currently 31st in yards per game (266.8), 31st in passing yards per game (160.8), 27th in points per game (18.3), and 26th in yards per target (6.4).
Brown has been known for his ability to stretch the field and open up plays for underneath players. Now that Minnesota traded for Cousins , this could be an opportunity to add a deep threat to take pressure off Jefferson and Addison.
Brown would also have a friendly face upon joining the Vikings' locker room: now-backup QB Kyler Murray. The duo was on the 2022-23 Cardinals together, connecting for 62 receptions, 699 receiving yards and three touchdowns across the 13 games they shared the field during that stretch.
Since entering the league in 2019, Brown has averaged 11.7 yards per reception and 7.0 yards per target. Even while underused in Philadelphia, he turned all five receptions into first downs for the Eagles.
That is significant because the Vikings are dead last in the NFL with 14.8 first downs per game. That number is even worse over the last three games, when Minnesota averaged just 13.7 first downs per game.
Jennings has struggled to make an impact for the Vikings after signing as a free agent this offseason, catching six passes for 54 yards this season. Odell Beckham Jr. has played only two offensive snaps since coming to the team and has not been targeted once.
Unless one of those players steps up to become a contributor soon, the Vikings would be silly not to take a hard look at Brown to see if he would be a good fit for Minnesota. If he ends up being a valuable offensive piece, that would be a huge help to a 6-2 team in the most competitive division in the NFL.

title: The Vikings' Best, Worst and Most Likely Outcomes vs. the Packers in Week 10
full_text:
The Vikings won't need any extra motivation this weekend when they take on the rival Packers, but their playoff chances will take a huge swing with either outcome . A win puts the Vikings at a 92% chance to make the postseason, while a loss drags that number all the way down to 68%.
Kirk Cousins was brought in at the deadline to ensure that those odds only go up, but he'll face an ascending Packers team that just steamrolled the Patriots in Week 9.
Still, it's always interesting with Green Bay regardless of the stakes, so here are the best, worst and most likely scenarios for the game.
Cousins is essentially coming into Week 10 having to play the hero already. The Vikings offense has been listless the last few weeks, and now Cousins will be asked to play at a high level despite just a few days of practice and a speed run through the playbook. And yet, most Vikings fans fully believe he's going to pull it off. But is that hopeful ignorance, or just sheer desperation?
Maybe that answer doesn't matter, but if Cousins actually does come in on a short week and looks like 2023 Cousins, there's nothing the 2026 Vikings can't accomplish. Besides the short timeline, Cousins will also be without T.J. Hockenson, Jauan Jennings and possibly even Jordan Addison. That's really not ideal, and it may pour some cold water on the Vikings' dreams of reigniting things right off the bat.
Still, even a marginal improvement in Week 10 is something to build on, and 7-2 with two wins over the Packers is a feeling that can't be beat.
On paper, the Vikings now possess a top-2 defense and a top-15 offense with the addition of Cousins. That's a winning formula, but the games also need to be played. Cousins is playing some great football, but relying on him to completely salvage the season comes with its challenges.
If the Vikings—and specifically Cousins—come out flat against Green Bay, it's hard to see the banged-up defense saving them in this one. Minnesota will be without Blake Cashman and Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins, and already allowed 387 yards to Jordan Love back in Week 1
. If the injuries continue to stack up and the Vikings enter a date with San Francisco at 6-3, the season could start to spiral before the calendar turns to December.
The bar for Cousins to clear is remarkably low, so even an average game from him on Sunday will be encouraging—at least for the long term. But the Packers, much like the Lions and the Bills, will eventually find ways to score, and the Vikings' defense has begun to show some fatigue after carrying the team for nine straight weeks.
This game just feels like an ugly one, with turnovers both ways, penalties, and two teams who are already feeling desperate in a crowded NFC North. Cousins likely shows more juice than Murray or Wentz offered, but there will be growing pains. Hopefully, the defense can find ways to slow down a Green Bay offense that has averaged 36 ppg over its last two wins.

title: Why Patriots Should, Shouldn't Sign QB Jimmy Garoppolo
full_text:
Could the New England Patriots reunite with a Super Bowl champion quarterback in the wake of Drake Maye's ankle injury ? It's not impossible.
NFL insider Jordan Schultz mentioned that Jimmy Garoppolo , a 2014 draft pick by the Patriots who was part of two Super Bowl teams as a backup, could be an option for the Patriots under center as they start to re-evaluate their quarterback options. Currently, Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton are the two on the roster, and for now, no external decisions have been made.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Mike Vrabel said. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see."
But should the Patriots replace the current No. 10 with a former No. 10? Let's weigh the options.
When you think of a typical Josh McDaniels quarterback, Garoppolo is one of those guys who can operate it very well. Spending the first three-plus seasons with the Patriots offensive coordinator in New England, and then for a short time in Las Vegas in 2023, Garoppolo is well-versed in the Patriots' offensive terminology.
Sure, what you might get out of Garoppolo isn't the same you'd get out of the explosive 24-year-old Maye, but it's not like you're getting a quarterback who's in over his head in the playbook. Both DeVito and Morton know what the system is, but Garoppolo has proven to operate it well in the past.
Garoppolo is 35 and has already contemplated retirement. He hasn't started a game since 2024 and hasn't made more than one start in a season since the year prior. He isn't getting any younger and for a Patriots team that still has postseason expectations, throwing a dart at this dartboard might not be the ideal scenario.
In his final year as a full-time starter (2023 with the Raiders, before injuries and McDaniels' firing sent him to the bench), Garoppolo went 110-for-169 with 1,205 passing yards, seven touchdowns and nine interceptions in seven games. Since then, you have no real productive snaps out of him.
At first, it felt like Garoppolo would be the future behind Tom Brady. Then Brady kept winning and Garoppolo was sent off to San Francisco in 2017. How funny would it be for the Patriots to somehow reverse course and bring back their former quarterback-in-waiting nearly 10 years after trading him away?
Patriots fans have proven to enjoy Garoppolo's play, at least before injuries in 2016 soured how people viewed him. It would be pretty poetic for the Patriots, seemingly dead in the water , to be saved by the player fans once assumed would be the heir apparent.
The Patriots likely woudn't sign Garoppolo to a contract to stick him on the bench. If they make this move, that feels like it would mean he's the starter over both DeVito and Morton. The Patriots agreed to a two-year extension with DeVito in the offseason to make him the QB2, so it might not be worth bringing in a quarterback who'd want to start on a deal that might not make sense.
If the team is looking for more depth and/or experience, there's certainly a lot more names that could be added for much cheaper (Will Levis, a fomrer Vrabel draft pick in Tennessee, is currently on the New York Jets' practice squad).
At this point, the Patriots are 5-5 and currently possess a roster that is capable — on paper — to make a playoff run . Injuries have hurt them beyond belief, but the hopes and expectations are still there for this group to succeed in the stretch.
If Garoppolo, who's played in a Super Bowl as a starter before, is the best chance to get this Patriots team there, then why not pull the trigger. Based on how DeVito looked against the Detroit Lions post-Maye injury, it can't get much worse. The Patriots have a chance to become a surprising second-half team, and maybe all it takes is Jimmy G to make those surprises happen.

title: Patriots QB Drake Maye is Injured, So Now What Happens?
full_text:
The New England Patriots' fortunes have gone from bad to worse . According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Patriots are concerned that quarterback Drake Maye suffered a fractured ankle in their Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions. Maye remained in Germany for further evaluation to determine the extent of the injury and whether surgery will be necessary. Regardless of the results, he is expected to miss an indefinite amount of time, with the possibility that his season is over. "Once he gets back here and our people are able to visit with him again and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters Monday. "I wouldn't imagine him being available when we come out of the bye." The prospect of losing Maye for any amount of time, let alone the remainder of the season, is a devastating blow to the Patriots and their hopes of making a playoff run. Regardless, New England has to pick up the pieces. Maye's potential absence will have a ripple effect across the roster, forcing the coaching staff to reevaluate their approach heading into the second half of the season. So, what's next?
Will the Patriots bring in a veteran quarterback to help weather the storm, or will they roll with backups Tommy DeVito and Behren Morton? For now, the former seems more likely. New England handed DeVito a two-year, $7.4 million extension during the offseason and selected Morton in April's draft. Despite a difficult outing in relief of Maye, DeVito appears to have the coaching staff's confidence moving forward. "I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
However, NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that New England is expected to explore the quarterback free-agent market during the bye week. Vrabel pushed back on those reports when asked about the possibility of bringing in another quarterback. “I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said. "But we'll have conversations, and we'll discuss it, and we'll look and see." Still, several QB options remain available if New England wants to go down that route. Notably, former Patriot Jimmy Garoppolo, who was named in the aforementioned Schultz report.
New England and DeVito struggled to find much success through the air after Maye's departure, completing just 50% of his pass attempts for 81 yards, one touchdown, and an interception. That came against a Lions defense that entered Week 10 ranked dead last in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (260.9) and was without their top pass rusher, Aidan Hutchinson, for most of the contest. While the Patriots have mainly moved the ball through the air with Maye under center, they'll need to establish a more consistent rushing attack moving forward to take pressure off DeVito. New England currently ranks 17th in the NFL in rushing yards per game, averaging 114 yards. That's a middle-of-the-pack unit that will likely need to shoulder a larger share of the offensive workload with Maye likely out of the picture. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker will be eligible to return from injured reserve following the bye week, potentially giving the offensive line a significant boost ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers. Paired with the return of fullback Reggie Gilliam, New England could have some reinforcements to help get its ground game back on track.
Losing Maye is obviously a major blow to the on-field aspirations, but it also presents a significant challenge for Mike Vrabel and the coaching staff inside the locker room. New England is entering one of the toughest stretches of its schedule, with matchups against the 7-2 Minnesota Vikings, 8-1 Buffalo Bills, 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs, and 7-2 Denver Broncos looming. The Patriots have already dealt with considerable adversity this season. Now, they'll have to prove they can respond to another major setback without allowing it to derail the foundation they've spent the last year and a half building. "We'll have to look at all things that we possibly can and find ways to improve, find ways to be on the same page, find ways to believe that we're all in this together, which is the first thing I told them," Vrabel said. "That it starts with me, and we're all in this together, and that the coaches will be connected, and they'll find ways to help each other and be part of the solution." Ultimately, this stretch will test more than just New England's depth at quarterback. It'll test the culture, leadership and resilience Vrabel has been working to establish since arriving in New England.

title: Mike Vrabel Expresses Confidence in Both Patriots Backup QBs
full_text:
The New England Patriots, a few years removed from all the Mac Jones/Bailey Zappe hoopla, are back under the quarterback spotlight. Drake Maye's ankle injury is reportedly serious enough to potentially knock him out for the remainder of the season and now the job under center may fall on two of the team's backups.
Tommy DeVito, who earned a two-year extension in the offseason, came in to replace Maye after his first quarter injury and didn't look all that promising. Behind him is seventh-round rookie Behren Morton, who's been working as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback in each of the team's 10 games this year.
While Mike Vrabel won't comment on Maye's status any more than saying he likely won't be available in Week 12, it's clear that the Patriots will have to roll with someone not wearing No. 10 for a bit.
"He stayed with a few of our people and they're en route back here," the head coach said Monday. "Once he gets back here and our people are able to visit with him again, and talk with him again, I think we'll have more to offer."
Currently, the Patriots have just DeVito and Morton in the building — and Vrabel is confident in both of them.
DeVito, who has experience as a starter in the NFL , came in to Sunday's game against the Detroit Lions and really struggled. The Patriots offense could not move the ball and he completed just 50% of his passes and threw under 100 yards. It wasn't a promising outing.
"I mean, the assessment was pretty much like the team. I don't think it was good enough," Vrabel said of DeVito's play. "I think there was some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp. And really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye.
"I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand — whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket or, you know, get us int he right play or get the ball out quicker, or look at protections or tations, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."
DeVito has won games before as a starting quarterback, including one against these Patriots back in 2023. But with a tough slate of games and postseason expectations looming, this will be a tougher challenge for him.
"I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."
Right behind DeVito on the depth chart is Morton, who the Patriots drafted with the 234th overall pick this year out of Texas Tec h . He's yet to step onto the field this year in a regular season game, but did have some positive plays in the preseason — including a game-winning touchdown pass to Nick DeGennaro in the closing seconds of their second game.
It's expected that the Patriots will have Morton jump into the QB2 spot, but maybe an external addition enters the picture as well. For now, Vrabel feels like his rookie is getting better.
"Tommy and Behren have been in our system, have been working," Vrabel said. "Behren's been improving. He's been working each week and I know that if he has to play for us, that he'll be ready to go. And I'm excited for his challenge and I hope that everybody else is because that's really what we're at. We're 5 and 5 in the middle of the season, just past the middle of the season."
NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported that the Patriots could potentially explore the market for a new quarterback , but Vrabel pushed back on that notion.
"I don't see that being the case right now," Vrabel said, just mere moments before Schultz's report came out. "We'll, you know, I mean, we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see."

title: Exploring 4 QB Replacements For Patriots After Drake Maye's Injury
full_text:
The New England Patriots are faced with the daunting task of finishing the 2026 season on a positive note, while sitting at 5-5 and looking to find a solution to the biggest problem the organization has been faced with in years.
Star quarterback Drake Maye is expected to have an ankle fracture that will sideline him for an extended period of time, according to NFL insider Ian Rapaport.
With this news entering the NFL spotlight, the Patriots will need to rework the entire makeup of their team. On Sunday, the offense struggled to find any production under backup quarterback Tommy DeVito.
Sources: #Patriots QB Drake Maye is believed to have suffered a significant lower leg injury that will keep him out an extended period of time. It’s even possible that Maye will miss the rest of the season. Maye came back from Germany and will seek more medical information. pic.twitter.com/jaOFw9qLGu
"I don't think it was good enough, I think there were things that he missed," Mike Vrabel said on DeVito's performance.
He also shared: "I wouldn't imagine [Maye] being available when we come out of the bye."
Vrabel alluded to DeVito being the starter in their Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers in two weeks.
While the game plan certainly changes with Maye on the sidelines, there's potential that the personnel changes too. In the coming weeks, New England may look at the practice squads of other teams or free agents for a solution at quarterback.
On Monday, Vrabel was asked about looking outside of the organization for quarterbacks and said that it's not "the case right now," but added that "we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it, and look and see."
If Vrabel and the front office look elsewhere for quarterbacks, here are some available players that the Patriots could sign in light of Maye's injury:
(Note: The Patriots cannot trade for any players signed to another team's 53-man roster, as the trade deadline passed on Nov. 10).
Bailey Zappe (Current Status - Free Agent)
Bailey Zappe started his NFL career in New England as Mac Jones' backup quarterback . He played in 14 games for the Patriots and was the team's transition player between the Jones and Maye era under center.
While Zappe never played under Josh McDaniels, his ties to New England and his experience as a depth player in offenses like Kansas City's and New York's would make his transition back to the Pats a fairly easy one.
Sam Hartman (Current Status - Washington Commanders Practice Squad)
The third-year quarterback could hit headlines for a second week in a row — this time, however, in an unrelated way to his participation in a reality dating show.
Hartman is a long-time friend of Drake Maye, having both grown up in North Carolina and played on the same youth football teams. While Hartman's notoriety isn't a product of his on-field performance, the Patriots could explore the potential of bringing in a second Carolina-born quarterback.
Jimmy Garoppolo (Current Status - Free Agent)
Ten years ago, if someone said that Jimmy Garoppolo would be the Patriots starting quarterback, it would have made a lot of sense. As crazy as it sounds now, Garoppolo realistically could compete for the Patriots starting job.
At 35-years-old, Garoppolo is well-seasoned, playing behind Tom Brady, of course, but also leading the 2019 San Francisco 49ers to the Super Bowl. Garappolo was hand-picked by McDaniels in the second round of the 2014 draft, and could reunite with his old offensive coordinator for a second time (after McDaniels signed Garoppolo to the Raiders in 2023).
Chris Oladokun filled in for an injured Patrick Mahomes in the back-half of the Chiefs 2025 season, where he threw for 235 yards and one touchdown in three games.
Oladokun was released by the Chiefs prior to the start of the 2026 season, but was given an injury settlement. Oladokun's health would obviously impact his ability to play with the Patriots, but his recent NFL experience and two-way ability as a runner and a passer would allow him to fit in the Patriots offensive scheme built around Maye.

title: Tommy DeVito Preparing as Patriots Starting QB After Drake Maye's Injury
full_text:
With Drake Maye down for the count (and the forseeable future) , the New England Patriots are going to have to figure out their quarterback decision after their bye week. The leader in the clubhouse is Tommy DeVito, who came in to replace Maye after his injury in Week 10.
DeVito and the Patriots offense struggled all game, scoring just once against the Detroit Lions in a 35-10 drubbing.
"Not good enough are the words I would say. Offensively, just never really got going," DeVito said. "Never really was able to get into a rhythm, really get drives going. Too many three and outs and just hurting ourselves. Even the one drive that we had that resulted in a touchdown took 16 plays and there were still errors on that that happened. We just need to be better at that and just sustaining drives."
DeVito didn't end up inspiring much hope in Maye's place, going 12-for-24 with 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception. They weren't able to to move the ball consistently and it took until the fourth quarter for them to find the end zone.
Now Maye, who's reportedly going to be out a long time with what the Patriots fear to be a fractured ankle , DeVito is going to be tasked with carrying this team through a tough stretch of games. The 28-year-old says he's prepared to do so.
"I'm going to continue the process I have been doing up to this point," he said. "Something that as a two, as cliche as it sounds, you have to be prepared to be a starter. So just keep doing what I'm doing, keep my head down, and then if something like that were to happen, you would have the reps and practice and the walkthroughs and everything going forward, so just keep on preparing and on to the next."
The Patriots have dealt with a ton of injuries on offense , putting that unit behind the 8-ball for most of this season. A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs, TreVeyon Henderson, Alijah Vera-Tucker, Mike Onwenu, the list goes on and on. With Maye out, it's DeVito's team — and he'll have to pull them out of this mess going into a Week 12 game against the Los Angeles Chargers.
"It starts with the quarterback, so it starts with me," DeVito said. "I just have to play better and sustain drives and get the thing going and stop feeling so lax."
This season in a reserve role, DeVito is 16-for-32 with 132 yards, that one touchdown to Lan Larison and an interception. The Patriots signed him to a two-year, $7.4 million extension in the offseason to be the top backup, so it's safe to assume he'll be under center through the next few weeks. Seventh-string rookie Behren Morton backs him up.
Sitting at .500, the hopes aren't that high for the Patriots . But DeVito isn't putting his head down, and that's all he can do at this point.
"I think we just focus on the next week," he said. "We have a bye week here, a lot of time to reflect and process the games that have happened and the games that are coming. All you can focus on are the games coming ahead."

title: Patriots Get Horrible Update on Drake Maye's Ankle Injury
full_text:
As if the 35-10 result on the Munich scoreboard wasn't bad enough, the New England Patriots might have just seen their season slip away on the field as well.
According to NFL Network, quarterback Drake Maye — who left the game in the first quarter with an ankle injury — is believed to have suffered a significant lower leg injury that could "keep him out for an extended period of time." It's possible that the injury knocks Maye out for the remainder of the season.
ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Patriots fear that Maye fractured his ankle and that he's going to be out indefinitely.
Maye got sacked by Detroit Lions edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson with just under 10 minutes to go in the opening quarter. Hutchinson got hurt celebrating the play, while Maye headed to the New England sideline and talked with head coach Mike Vrabel. After a brief discussion, he walked to the Patriots locker room with several trainers.
"Obviously wasn't able to finish the game, so we'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has," Vrabel said postgame.
After Maye went down, the Patriots offense looked like a shell of itself . Backup Tommy DeVito came in and didn't play well enough to push the ball downfield. He did lead a touchdown drive in the fourth quarter, but it was well into garbage time.
"Yeah, it was pretty quick," DeVito said about how fast everything happened with Maye's injury. "It was kind of just, looked at me, it was good, and said I was rolling, so that was kind of that."
Now the Patriots , currently sitting at 5-5, don't have a pretty outlook on the horizon. After their Week 11 bye, they'll have some really tough games on the schedule (Minnesota Vikings, Buffalo Bills, Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos).
With a backup quarterback and no expectations for Maye to come back into the lineup, the postseason might not be in New Englnad's future this season.
On Monday morning, Vrabel spoke on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show and gave a travel update on Maye.
"The update that I have is just out of caution, Drake stayed back. He'll be traveling back here shortly," Vrabel said. "But just wanted to make sure that everything was good for him to travel back and safely. The things that go around injuries and just wanted to make sure everything was in line for him to travel, and it seems like he is. He'll be returning here, I think, shortly."
Maye's injury is the worst possible news for a team that's been banged up beyond belief this year. Now, they'll have to rely on DeVito and rookie Behren Morton under center.
"My concern level anybody gets hurt is the same," running back Rhamondre Stevenson said about Maye. "I want everybody to be available, so, yeah, tough one there. Hopefully he gets healthy soon."

title: 5 Losers, 0 Winners in Patriots' International Embarrassment vs. Lions
full_text:
Even in another continent, the New England Patriots could not escape another poor performance. The team had arguably its worst performance of the season in a 35-10 loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.
New England fell back down to a .500 record and made a few substantial additions to its grocery list of injured players.
Here are the five biggest losers, and no winners, from the Patriots' rock-bottom performance against the Lions.
A 2028 first-round pick and a 2027 fifth-rounder. That is what the Patriots had to give up to acquire Brown from the Eagles to be their top pass catcher. Since then, the 29-year-old has appeared in four games, and has played from start-to-finish just twice.
On his 26 targets this year, he has tallied just 11 receptions for 128 yards and no touchdowns. On Sunday, he totaled 27 yards on his pair of catches. However, as has been a recurring theme for Brown, he also had a drop what should have been a routine grab.
AJ Brown drop in his Week 10 return pic.twitter.com/UEZ7z4N9vO
Plus, the receiver did not finish the game due to a hamstring injury.
"Wasn't able to finish," Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said when asked about Brown. "We'll see what the severity of that is once we get back and kind of go from there."
After starting quarterback Drake Maye went down at the end of New England's first drive of the day, DeVito came in and played the remainder of the game. In that span, the Patriots put just seven points on the board.
The 28-year-old finished Sunday with just 81 yards on 24 attempts. That total marks the few yards by a Patriots single-game passing leader since former New England quarterback Mac Jones' three attempt, 19 yard performance in the snow against the Buffalo Bills on Dec. 6, 2021. Not to mention, the signal caller also had a brutal interception with a clean pocket and multiple open receivers.
Nobody at Fox noticed the Patriots WR running down the left side of the field WIDE OPEN on the DeVito interception that he threw into 3 guys. pic.twitter.com/nI6o15UDch
"Not good enough are the words I would say," DeVito said. "Offensively, just never really got going; never really was able to get into a rhythm, really get drives going. Too many three and outs and just hurting ourselves. Even the one drive that we had that resulted in a touchdown took 16 plays and there were still errors on that that happened."
At this point, "LOSER: Injuries" can be pre-penciled into this article on a weekly basis. On Sunday, the depleted Patriots squad lost Maye, Brown, edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones (cramps), linebacker Robert Spillane (illness) and cornerback Charles Woods (undisclosed).
Fortunately, New England has an extra week to get healthy . However, for the Patriots to lose their top QB, WR, LB and one of their best EDGEs, is a disastrous development for a squad which has already dealt with countless injuries.
"We'll have to get some more tests run and we'll see when we come back what it ends up being and the severity of whatever injury he has," Vrabel said when asked about Maye.
New England's run game was borderline non-existent against Detroit. Kiner was the team's leading rusher ...with 25 yards on his 10 attempts. Yet, somehow, his abysmal 2.5 yards per carry looks elite in comparison to Stevenson's final tally. The 28-year-old had four yards on six rushes, good for .7.
Plus, neither player helped much through the air. Kiner had no receptions, while Stevenson had just one catch which he picked up a single yard on.
"We got beat," Stevensons said. "We didn't play well enough as a unit. Really that's offense, defense, and special teams. We didn't play good enough. We have to go back and watch the film and see what we can pick."
Sunday's performance for Gonzalez can be chalked up to a less-steep stock down than the rest of the names on this list. However, after a career-worst performance last week, another poor showing from the 24-year-old is far from encouraging.
On the bright side, Gonzalez hauled in his first interception on the season. Even still, his most memorable play of the day was allowing a 56-yard catch-and-run touchdown to Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, who made the Patriots defender look like he was on a Slip 'N Slide.
AMON-RA ST. BROWN 56-YARD TOUCHDOWN IN GERMANY NEvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/47fPY2mHzx
"Again, he slipped and the guy made a play," Vrabel said. "Nobody else helped him get the guy on the ground, so they're going to catch passes on everybody. It's good to see him come back and respond and challenge guys and get an interception and try to get a turnover."

title: The Good, Bad, and Ugly from Patriots' Brutal Loss to Lions
full_text:
The New England Patriots' trip to Germany didn't quite go as they had hoped, falling to the Detroit Lions, 35-10. New England drops to 5-5 heading into its Week 11 bye, with plenty to reflect on after a disappointing performance on both sides of the ball.
After orchestrating a promising opening drive, completing 3-of-4 pass attempts for 48 yards and picking up a first down with his legs, Maye was sacked by Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson in the red area following a pair of New England penalties. While New England trotted out its field goal unit, Maye was seen limping toward the sideline before heading to the locker room. He was quickly ruled out for the remainder of the game with an ankle injury.
This was Drake Maye's final play before leaving the game questionable with an ankle injury. pic.twitter.com/Yi1rQYpMeW
Injuries have headlined a frustrating season for the Patriots, but losing Maye proved too much to overcome. Their offense failed to consistently replicate the success of their opening drive and will await a status update on their young signal-caller heading into their bye week. "That he couldn't function," head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters when asked about the decision to rule Maye out without knowing the severity of the injury. "Couldn't play, couldn't run, couldn't do whatever he needed to do to play quarterback, to protect himself, to execute or function at that level."
Coming off their worst defensive performance of the season against the Packers, a game in which they surrendered 478 yards and 45 points, the Patriots hoped to bounce back in Munich. That didn't happen. Defending an offense as talented as Detroit's was always going to be a challenge, but it wasn't even close. New England was thoroughly outmatched, allowing the Lions to move the ball at will. Detroit finished with 494 total yards of offense . Running back Jahmyr Gibbs looked unstoppable, rushing 22 times for 153 yards and two touchdowns, adding another 99 through the air. He led Detroit in rushing and receiving.
Another Gibbs TD, this time from 28 yard out 🔥 NEvsDET on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/r3d1sVUKu5
And for wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, a dual citizen of the United States and Germany, he couldn't have asked for a better showing. Four catches for 98 yards and two touchdowns. Combined, Gibbs and St. Brown accounted for 350 yards of offense, more than double the Patriots' entire offensive output of 151 yards. Over the last two weeks, New England has surrendered 80 points and 974 yards of offense. "There's a lot that we have to fix," Vrabel said. "You play good teams in this league, and you don't play well, you have no chance. And again, we know that."
AJ Brown is headed to the locker room. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/W6U11AHev3
It's been a difficult season for Brown in 2026, having appeared in just four games through 10 weeks while dealing with ankle and knee injuries. Through his first five targets, Brown had managed just one catch for 6 yards while also being flagged for a false start. His fortunes appeared to be turning when a slant route turned into a 21-yard catch-and-run, something he had consistently done so well throughout his career. However, Brown was slow to get up after the play. He made his way to the sideline, shaking his head as the Patriots medical staff prepared the blue medical tent. Brown eventually headed to the locker room with a hamstring injury and did not return for the remainder of the game. "Wasn't able to finish," Vrabel said. "We'll see what the severity of that is when we get back and kind of go from there."
Despite the poor defensive showing, the Patriots forced two turnovers, something they've struggled to do all season. After allowing a catch to St. Brown, Gonzalez was left on the wrong end of a nasty juke from the Lions wideout as he scampered for a 56-yard score. It looked like another rough outing for Gonzalez after his poor showing against Green Bay. But later in the second quarter, Gonzalez undercut an in-breaking pass from Jared Goff intended for St. Brown, recording his first interception of the season. "(St. Brown) made a play, I came back and made a play," Gonzalez said. "Obviously, we want to win; it's not about me getting an interception or someone scoring or something like that. We went out there two weeks in a row and played bad. So I mean, we just gotta get to the drawing board and be ready for two weeks." Kevin Byard added another pick with 0:12 remaining in the first half when Goff threw a pass over the middle, right into the safety's waiting hands. Goff hadn't had a multiple-interception game this season before today.
Without Maye, Tommy DeVito and the Patriots offense just couldn't get it going. DeVito struggled to manage the offense. He threw an ugly interception over the middle on a pass intended for Mack Hollins, while Kyle Williams was wide open along the left sideline. "Not good enough," DeVito said. "Offensively, just never really got going, not really was able to get into a rhythm or get drives going. Too many three-and-outs and kind of just hurting ourselves." The offense managed only 151 yards and reached the end zone all but once on a 10-yard Lan Larison reception.
