title: Jets Week 10 Report Card: Grading Every Position After Injury-Riddled Loss to Bills
full_text:
For the second consecutive week, the Jets failed to score a touchdown as their losing streak reached five games in a 31-12 loss to the Bills , dropping head coach Aaron Glenn's record against divisional opponents to 0-9.
Sure, this was not a game the Jets were expected to contend in against the highest-scoring offense in the league. At the same time, the same struggles were prevalent for Gang Green after going 3-of-13 on third down, 0-of-2 in the red zone and committing costly penalties (seven for 53 yards) throughout the game.
Despite the injury concerns that have plagued the Jets this season, it was an encouraging injury report heading into Week 10 as the full collective starting offense was cleared to play together for the first time since Week 1, while Harrison Phillips and Joseph Ossai returned to the defensive line.
That said, it did not take long for things to unravel for the Jets as the Bills outscored them 21-6 in a second-half runaway at MetLife Stadium.
Before the attention turns to an upcoming two-game road trip that begins with a Week 11 clash against the Chargers, let's hand out some grades for each unit after another disappointing result on Sunday.
Although the Jets teased a much-needed offensive shift to account for Buffalo's explosiveness and take advantage of the league's fourth-worst passing defense (238.8 ypg), it was a mixed bag of results as Geno Smith completed 13 of his 21 passes for 148 yards, zero TDs and zero interceptions. However, that was also with a pair of injuries that reared their head on the veteran, the first of which put him in concussion protocol after getting "sandwiched" by two Bills defenders in the third quarter (h/t RealJoshBrownie).
Geno smith sandwiched .. should be just wind knocked out pic.twitter.com/ElqPUjH46C
The injury news only got worse for Smith when he suffered an ankle injury that sidelined him for the rest of the game.
While that put rookie Cade Klubnik into the game, and he did a commendable job by going 11-of-20 for 137 yards, along with three rushes for 26 yards, he also took three sacks and threw an interception late in the third quarter as the offense failed to sustain any drives and keep pace with their AFC East rivals.
It was the type of game you would expect from WR1 Garrett Wilson, who returned to action after missing the Week 9 loss to the Chiefs due to a concussion. He finished the game with seven catches (on 14 targets) for 106 yards and a season-high 15.1 yards per catch. However, there were some missed opportunities along the way and a crucial lost fumble with five minutes remaining in the game as the Jets were driving near the red zone, trailing 24-12.
While that specifically proved costly as the Bills officially put the game out of reach with a TD on their next offensive play, there was not much help behind Wilson as Adonai Mitchell had just three catches (on eight targets) for 59 yards and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. re-injured the same ankle that placed him on injured reserve earlier this season when he was rolled up on in the opening quarter (h/t Banged Up Bills).
WR Omar Cooper Jr. (Right Ankle) Cooper gets rolled up on again, this is the same high-ankle that he injured in Week 1, sent him to IR, returned, and injured again last week. pic.twitter.com/N9BtGAUFog
It was a similar story for the TE group once again, as the receiving impact was minimal for another week. Mason Taylor was the best of the bunch with four catches for 20 yards, but a long reception of nine yards speaks to how much the Bills limited him when the ball was in his hands.
Aside from Taylor, rookie Kenyon Sadiq was held to one catch (on two targets) for three yards, which wasn't exactly the best recipe for success for someone viewed as the Jets' X-Factor in their bid to upset a vulnerable Buffalo defense. They provided solid complementary work to the wideouts, but their quiet impact in the passing game is something that still needs to be cleaned up.
Although the ground game was not dominant, the tandem of Breece Hall and Braelon Allen provided a nice balance and helped control the tempo when needed. Hall went for 41 yards on 11 carries and added four catches for 67 yards in the passing game, while Allen had eight carries for 40 yards with a solid five yards per carry.
The RB duo did not create any explosive runs to help get them back in the game, but they were not the reason the Jets lost to the Bills.
Perhaps an uptick in snaps for Allen would be beneficial due to how impressive he has been in relief of Hall this season. That said, Hall has moved into fifth on the all-time receiving yards list among RBs in franchise history (h/t Jets) and continues to provide the star power they need even when the supporting cast is not doing its part.
Breece Hall now ranks No. 5 in receiving yards among running backs in franchise history pic.twitter.com/eghbq1rRGf
Coming off a disappointing effort against the Chiefs, the hope was that the OL would bounce back and provide something encouraging going forward. That was far from the case on Sunday, with four sacks allowed and an inability to consistently open up lanes for the offense as the Jets struggled to convert their red-zone opportunities once again.
Overall, the protection was better as the Jets put up a fight through the first half, but failed to finish out drives and create enough movement to punch it in the end zone. Combine that with some inopportune penalties and it was another forgettable performance from the unit up front as the Jets struggled to keep pace for the duration of the game.
Going up against NFL MVP candidate Josh Allen, who has made it a routine of extending plays and making opponents miss with his elusiveness in the pocket, one of the key matchups coming into the game centered on the DL's ability to contain him. While the Jets have frequently blitzed this season and Allen has tended to struggle when faced with pressure in the pocket, the Jets only got to him one time thanks to Will McDonald IV.
Additionally, Allen and the Bills' run game completely took over coming out of the locker room. The Jets have particularly been susceptible against the run this season, and that became an issue again after allowing Buffalo RB James Cook to go off for 157 yards and this 74-yard TD (h/t NFL) that put the game out of reach
74-YARD TD FOR JAMES COOK BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DFRLVP17FL
The unit up front did nothing to ease the challenge the LBs faced trying to contain the explosive Bills offense, but the issues still remain. Jamien Sherwood finished with nine tackles (four solo), and Demario Davis was close behind with six tackles (three solo), but he continues to get beat in coverage. It was an uneven performance for a group that could not limit the Bills' run game.
Although Allen was held to just five carries for five yards, he still scored two TDs to go along with his 196 yards and one TD through the air. Cook, meanwhile, set season-high marks in rush yards (157) and yards per carry (8.7), which ultimately proved costly and wore the LBs down in a game that slowly got away from them.
Coverage issues have plagued this group for most of the season, and Sunday was no different, as WR DJ Moore and TE Dalton Kincaid broke free for explosive plays. However, there was a bright spot as cornerback Azareye'h Thomas came down with the team's second interception of the season (h/t NFL) with this grab early in the fourth quarter.
Azareye'h Thomas with an INT BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oSsC1E1ChR
While Thomas was banged up after the play, it was an encouraging sign of what the former third-round pick can do when given an opportunity. This unit helped keep the game close for most of the game, but there were still too many explosive plays allowed that proved detrimental in the end, especially with the lack of support from the offense.
The offense hasn't scored a TD in the last nine quarters, but that hasn't…

title: Dissecting the Jets' Most Important Quotes After Bills Loss Sends Gang Green to 2-8
full_text:
Jets fans have had it. They were already tired of the same answers and style of play throughout the team's five-game losing streak, but Sunday's loss to the Bills was just the next stage of their frustration.
Gang Green competed hard against their AFC East rivals, but still lost by three scores in a 31-12 romp to the Bills. Many of the same problems fans have watched this season reared their heads at the worst possible time.
As head coach Aaron Glenn and the rest of the roster continue to try and find a solution to their struggles, the reality is the Jets have simply run out of answers.
Here are some of the biggest quotes from Sunday's loss.
Arguably, the biggest problem for the Jets right now is that their philosophy as a team does not match the talent that they have.
Glenn wants his team to be able to run the football and play excellent defense. There's just one problem with that: their defense isn't good enough to be the key cog of things. New York needs to be able to put up points in order to give their defense a buffer, but they make mistakes and play calls that are at odds with what they need.
For example, the Jets had four scoring drives in Sunday's loss that were deep inside Buffalo territory. Instead of going for it on fourth down, they opted to kick field goals. The Bills then traded those field goals for touchdowns.
And after the game, Glenn has to explain why his offense is unable to score where and when it matters.
New York was just the second team this century to have four scoring drives but still get blown out by three scores in back-to-back games. That's a sign of a team that wants to play conservatively on offense, but aggressively on defense.
It simply doesn't match what the team is. Even if players continue to defend the current staff.
"It comes back again on that execution," Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson said. "The plays are there to be made, and at the end of the day, it does tighten up in the red zone. So, knowing that, we have to be that much more on our stuff, and we haven't been up to this point."
Sunday was supposed to be the first time since Week 1 that the team had their entire starting offense together on the field.
That lasted for a single play. Rookie wideout Omar Cooper Jr. and veteran guard Dylan Parham left the game in the first quarter, and even quarterback Geno Smith went into concussion protocol before leaving the game entirely due to another injury .
#OmarCooper @nyjets Rolled up on from behind while engaged in block Worry for mild high ankle injury Off IR for ankle earlier this season Came in with ankle on injury report pic.twitter.com/e52gJUbs3d
After the game, Glenn gave a clear injury update.
" Coop had an ankle , (Dylan) Parham had a knee, same knee, and Geno (Smith) had an ankle. Those are the injuries they had in the game," Glenn said. "I’ll end up getting that information sometime next week."
No news is good news in this case, but we'll know more as the week progresses.
We've already talked about how the Jets were without GenSmith in the game. That meant fourth-round rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik saw his first NFL action.
The Clemson product was pretty solid throughout, completing 11-of-20 passes for 137 yards. He was tagged for an interception late in the game, but he did use his legs in solid action (three rushes for 26 yards).
Cade Klubnik's first NFL pass is a completion to Garrett Wilson! BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Cyxg8tuqzq
Based on the context as a mid-round rookie and getting his first action, Klubnik impressed his coaches.
"I thought he did a pretty good job," Glenn said. "That first drive that he did was pretty impressive. Some of the throws that he had were pretty impressive. His ability to maneuver around the pocket and evade some of these guys, and make plays with his feet were impressive."
The jury is still out on what kind of quarterback he can be. Klubnik's mobility is a superpower of his, and he certainly has the arm talent to make every throw. But his anticipation and decision-making are still very raw for an NFL signal-caller.
He is as close to a project as you will find for a rookie. Which is why getting him some playing time in a lost year is perfectly fine.
"It was fun to be out there, but the fun’s in the winning," Klubnik said. "I wish we would’ve come out with a win, and it felt like we were really close the whole time, until the very end. I thought we did some good things. We definitely have to clean up a lot of stuff."
We've talked about how the Jets failed to put up points on Sunday, but their current drought remains one of the worst we've seen.
New York has gone through nine straight quarters since its last touchdown. The last TD score was a Braelon Allen run with eight minutes to go in the third quarter in their loss to the Raiders. It's left players frustrated over their lack of success.
The Jets' struggles in the red zone are twofold. New York's coaching staff appears unable and unwilling to figure out ways to get the football to all of their talent. The players who do get chances, though, aren't able to make the most of those opportunities either.
It's an ugly rotating list of struggles that the team simply hasn't been able to figure out through 10 games.
"I'm frustrated because I know our offense is better than the amount of points that we've been scoring, and it shows in the stats because we're able to move the ball up and down the field how we want, so that's frustrating," Jets running back Breece Hall said. "You get down there, players have to make plays; it's not super special play calls that you make."
There is too much offensive talent for the Jets to not score a touchdown in one game, let alone for nine quarters. It needs to change immediately.
After their eighth loss in nine games and fifth in a row, some of the Jets' leaders tried to put their struggles into perspective: by thanking them for their loyalty and showing up to watch them play despite all the travel problems over the weekend with the FAA shutdown.
"I know it was a lot of traveling issues that are out there, so before we get to the game, I really want to make sure I acknowledge fans that had to persevere and the people who are out there having issues with traveling," Jets linebacker and captain Demario Davis said. "Just knowing that you guys are in our thoughts and prayers."
Davis is right to appreciate the fans. New York fans deserve more than what they have seen over their last 16 years of futility.
But they also deserve a stadium that is going to be full of their own fans. Sunday was overwhelmed by Bills fans who made the game feel more like a road game for some of New York's players. That isn't the fault of Jets fans either. Their players need to actually win to bring fans back.
But for those who traveled not only to see their Jets, only to be rewarded with a blowout loss and their stadium overrun by the opposition, they deserve so much more than what they have been given.

title: 4 Jets Duds & 4 Studs in Sunday's Blowout Loss to Bills: Glenn Sinks Lower Despite Bailey's Standout Effort
full_text:
The numbers keep getting worse. At this point, there's very little left to save the Jets or their head coach.
New York fought hard for three and a half quarters against their AFC East rivals, but made similar mistakes as in the last few weeks and ultimately were blown out by the Bills 31-12. They have gone two games without scoring an offensive touchdown and haven't won an AFC East game in three years.
The numbers are what they are.
As always we have plenty of studs and duds to break down from Sunday's loss. Let's go through it now.
New York got what they needed from their stars on offense . Breece Hall recorded 100 yards from scrimmage, including 67 yards receiving. He finished second on the team in that category behind Garrett Wilson, who added seven receptions for 106 yards. Throw in another five yards per carry average from Braelon Allen, and the Jets offense remains solid when it comes to the talent on offense.
Breece Hall now ranks No. 5 in receiving yards among running backs in franchise history pic.twitter.com/eghbq1rRGf
The Jets have a collection of talented pieces on offense that will make finding a quality quarterback next season easy for them. They appreciate the 1-2 punch at running back they have with Allen and Hall. They also like the fact that their receiving room is deep.
New York's stars showed up on Sunday. The frustrating part is that few others did, especially their coaching staff.
If you feel that the Jets have played the same football game in each of the last two months, you aren't wrong. New York has battled hard through the first half of each game they have played this season, only to be outschemed and outcoached in the second half.
On Sunday, the Jets were down 10-6 at the half. They had kept the Bills' offense in check for most of the afternoon. Then in the second half, they were outscored 21-6. New York was comfortable trading field goals for touchdowns and was burned throughout.
The loss moves Jets head coach Aaron Glenn to 5-22 in his career and 0-9 in the AFC East. By the time his tenure is over at the end of the year, he will go down as one of the worst winning percentages not just in team history, but in NFL history as well.
The biggest example of that came in the fourth quarter. The Jets were down 12 late, but the offense was moving well inside Bills territory. The Jets opted for a hook-and-ladder play that Wilson missed the lateral player by two yards. Buffalo picked up the fumble and, on the next offensive play, scored ona  74-yard touchdown run.
Glenn's time with the Jets is ending soon . And that two play sequence tells the whole story as to why.
The Jets didn't get much pressure on Josh Allen throughout the game. Bailey's performance today should be listed as "average" and nothing more.
However, he continues to find ways to make high-impact plays. In Sunday's loss, Bailey recorded two pass deflections early in the contest, highlighting his ability to read what the quarterback wants to do outside of the pocket. On one of the deflections, he seemed in play to even pick the pass off but ended up dropping the pass (h/t Glenn Naughton).
David Bailey juuuuust misses a pick six.  DROY candidate keeps making plays.  The @nyjets force a punt and have the ball for the first time today. pic.twitter.com/p6rHVQzehc
No edge rusher is working on ball drills in practice. But there's still a lot to like about what the second overall pick is putting out on the field.
Going into the game, the Jets were throwing out their full collection of offensive talent for the first time since Week 1.
By the end of the first quarter, though, they had lost Omar Cooper Jr. and Dylan Parham. By halftime, Geno Smith had entered concussion protocol . New York lost several starters across both sides of the ball in Sunday's loss, but it's uncanny that in the first game, all their starters are set to play together, they get nothing more than a single play or drive.
It's another microcosm of the team's poor season.
New York's defense is devoid of many star performers. They also lack just pure starters at this point.
Some of that conversation, though, changes with the play of second-year cornerback AZ Thomas. The Florida State cornerback has been solid through his first full year as a starter. His best play came in Sunday's loss when he leaped over a Bills receiver on a deep throw to pick off a Josh Allen pass.
Azareye'h Thomas with an INT BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/oSsC1E1ChR
Thomas got banged up after the play, but it was the kind of athletic showing that provides New York hope that their former third-round pick can be another starter for the team.
And that the outlook for the defense's future is far better than anyone may admit.
Today highlighted the inconsistencies of officiating when it comes to the Jets. This isn't to say that the refs cost the Jets a game, but one can be critical of the officiating and still understand they had no impact on the game itself.
The biggest play in question came before the first half when Buffalo injured Smith, when a defender launched himself into Smith up high while another defender went low. "High-low" penalties don't exist on tackles, but targeting and unnecessary roughness penalties do exist, and that should have been called.
Here's the play in question:
Geno Smith is down on the field after taking this hit. pic.twitter.com/yLMaYc5ZGN
And here is Glenn's response, clearly highlighting that the call would have been different if Allen were the player who got hit.
“Here’s my problem with that, if that was Josh Allen every flag on the field would be thrown” Aaron Glenn is right. #Jets pic.twitter.com/pk8fYHaB3F
Glenn is absolutely right. There's a double standard in how referees call penalties against them and other teams.
New York has gone nine straight quarters without scoring an offensive touchdown. You'd think that would be impossible with how much talent the collective unit has. Alas, that is the current situation.
Thank god for Jason Sanders.
The Jets' kicker was 4-for-4 again on kicks today and has moved to 21-for-24 on the season. He's been one of the few bright spots this season for New York's special teams and remains a player the team should consider keeping around beyond 2026.
Stop me if you've heard this before, but the Jets' run defense remains one of the worst in the league. Buffalo recorded 201 yards on the ground and over six yards per carry. James Cook ran for over 150 yards and a touchdown during the game as well.
There are many reasons for this, of course. New York's linebackers are a major hindrance to the team's success at this point. Demario Davis and Jamien Sherwood collectively have been poor over the last several weeks and were washed out on several runs on Sunday.
Making matters worse, the team also didn't get much production at all from their defensive tackles. This defense simply isn't good enough, and everyone knows they can be beaten by running the ball.

title: Geno Smith Injury News Could Force Jets to Look at Free-Agent QB Trio After Week 10
full_text:
It's safe to say that the Jets' Week 10 clash with the Bills isn't going as planned. Not only was rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. ruled out after leaving with an ankle injury in the first quarter , but veteran quarterback Geno Smith was also forced to leave the game with a concussion, thrusting his outlook into uncertainty.
Smith left the game and was evaluated for a concussion in the third quarter after being hit by two Bills defenders . The unfortunate exit led to rookie QB Cade Klubnik making his sooner-than-anticipated NFL debut, in which he completed three of his first seven passes for 48 passing yards and an interception.
Geno smith sandwiched .. should be just wind knocked out pic.twitter.com/ElqPUjH46C
Smith eventually cleared concussion protocol and returned to the game... only to exit again as he "limped" out of the game and entered the blue medical tent , according to SNY TV 's Connor Hughes. The 36-year-old signal-caller eventually headed to the locker room before a commercial break, further fueling speculation about his immediate future and down the line.
At 3:46 p.m. ET, the Jets officially ruled Smith out of the game with an ankle injury.
Geno Smith (ankle) has been downgraded to OUT
Given that Klubnik was expected to be a project prospect, while the in-game emergency QB was wideout Isaiah Williams, it's safe to say the Jets might want to add another quarterback. Sure, Will Levis is on the practice squad , but too many arms is never a bad idea.
Aaron Glenn says that Geno Smith and Omar Cooper both have ankle injuries. They are both ankle injuries. He doesn’t know yet if high or low. pic.twitter.com/QxPoJo0mF9
Here are three free-agent QBs that New York can target as Smith's outlook remains a question mark.
When it comes to available QB options, few have as much experience as Jimmy Garoppolo. The former 2014 second-round pick has started in 64 of his 85 regular-season appearances while also making six postseason starts (4-2 record), and that's without mentioning the two Super Bowl-winning teams he got to be a part of in New England.
Injuries and circumstances have led to Garoppolo being more of a supporting cast member in recent years, but that doesn't mean he can't help the Jets in a time of need. He completed 65.2% of passes for 1,539 yards, nine touchdowns and 10 interceptions in seven starts over three seasons with the Rams, and having him around would help New York avoid throwing Klubnik into a situation he isn't ready for.
Although imperfect, the Jets could do a lot worse.
Continuing the unintended theme of former Patriots quarterbacks, Bailey Zappe is one potential option whom the Jets know well. New York signed the Western Kentucky product to a future contract back in January to compete for the QB2 job. He was re-signed after being part of the last wave of roster cuts , only to be released again to make room for Levis.
Even though he was dumped twice, the Jets might feel like going with the familiar face makes the most sense at this point in the season. Zappe appeared in two preseason games for Gang Green this summer, going 14-of-23 (60.9%) for 135 passing yards with two INTs. Far from an impressive performance, but the chance to right those wrongs may motivate Zappe to put in a stronger effort.
How about someone whom the Jets previously showed interest in but didn't sign? After all, it was back in April when Hughes reported that New York was interested in Cooper Rush's services ; however, a deal never materialized and Rush eventually signed a one-year contract with the Falcons.
Rush's time in Atlanta was short-lived, though, and he found himself back in the unemployment line in October after a pair of forgettable starts. The Falcons lost both of his appearances as Rush went 22-of-39 (56.4) for 229 passing yards, one TD, four INTs and a 42.5 passer rating. Obviously, those stats don't illustrate a great picture, but the Jets don't exactly need an MVP-caliber performance.
The last two seasons haven't been kind to him, but Rush's time with the Cowboys proved that he can be one of the NFL's better backup quarterbacks. If he can even get back to being a semblance of that guy, he'll still be better than what Jets fans were used to before Smith came to town.

title: Omar Cooper Jr. Injury Tracker: Every Update After Rookie Jets WR's Early Exit vs. Bills
full_text:
It didn't take long for things to go poor for the Jets in Sunday's Week 10 clash against the rival Bills.
Just as the offense was slowly becoming healthier, rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. left the early matchup with an ankle injury in the first quarter. The injury occurred when multiple players fell on Cooper's ankle (h/t Banged Up Bills ) while he was blocking for fellow rookie Kenyon Sadiq on a catch-and-run play.
WR Omar Cooper Jr. (Right Ankle) Cooper gets rolled up on again, this is the same high-ankle that he injured in Week 1, sent him to IR, returned, and injured again last week. pic.twitter.com/N9BtGAUFog
Cooper was seen sitting on the sidelines, looking dejected after being forced to step out of the game. Unfortunately, the situation took a turn for the worse a few moments later, leaving Jets fans worried that the promising first-year WR's campaign would be derailed yet again.
Update #2 (Nov. 15, 4:23 p.m. ET): Per Hughes, head coach Aaron Glenn confirmed that Cooper (along with quarterback Geno Smith) is dealing with an ankle injury and that more testing will be required to determine if it's a "high or low" situation.
Update #1 (Nov. 15, 2:51 p.m. ET): Cooper has officially been ruled out of Sunday's game , according to NFL insider Mike Garafolo.
As seen in the video above, Cooper's outlook appeared grim the second multiple players landed on him. He seemingly struggled to put weight on it, which eventually led to the Jets confirming that he'd be questionable to return with an ankle injury.
Omar Cooper Jr. is questionable to return with an ankle injury
Considering that Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell have also been dealing with injuries this season, the last thing the Jets need is for Cooper to be out long-term. The Indiana product had just played a season-high 54 offensive snaps against the Chiefs in Week 9, only to be limited to just one passing route before being forced to leave against the Bills.
That said, Cooper still hasn't been ruled out at the time of writing, making it crucial for Jets fans to stay locked in for each of the upcoming updates on Sunday and beyond.
Although he oozes talent, it's hard to ignore Cooper's history with the injury bug—especially after his latest issue.
Injuries have been an obstacle for Cooper dating back to high school, when he tore his ACL . He also occasionally dealt with ankle issues during his time with the Hoosiers, including when he missed three games in 2023.
Much to everyone's dismay, Cooper has continued to miss time at the pro level. After making an impressive 30-yard catch in his NFL debut against the Titans, Cooper suffered a high-ankle sprain that forced him to miss four games. Back-to-back 100-yard performances after getting off the injured reserve left Jets fans excited about his outlook, but it seems like his promising rookie year will likely be on pause again.
Before Sunday's exit, Cooper was up to 306 receiving yards and two touchdowns on 20 catches in five games.
Assuming that Cooper misses any time, the Jets will continue looking to Wilson and Mitchell as their top wide receivers. The dynamic duo is capable of flipping any game on its head, which means any success will hinge on quarterback Geno Smith's ability to get them the ball. Tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor have also proven they can step up.
It'd also be nice to see Isaiah Williams step up during Cooper's potential absence. The veteran WR has still been solid as a returner; however, his receiving numbers have left much to be desired this season. The same could be said for fellow elder-statesman wideout Tim Patrick, who was a healthy scratch on Sunday.
Cooper's injury could also mean more opportunities for UDFA WR Malik McClain, who hadn't received a target before Week 10. There's also a chance that New York could elevate one of Sterling Shepard, Jamaal Pritchett or Joseph Manjack IV off the practice squad.

title: Kracz: 5 Things Eagles Fans Should Know as the Bye Week Ends
full_text:
The Week 10 action is officially over, so now is the perfect time to catch up with the Eagles as they come out of their bye week . Here are five things that every Philadelphia fan must know heading into Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season.
When we last saw quarterback Joe Milton, he was sacked seven times while completing just 53 percent of his 34 passes in a 19-11 home loss to the Giants. Not great, but he wasn’t ready after being here for just three weeks. He made plays with his legs, though, and led the team in rushing with 64 yards on nine carries.
Milton will likely get the start on Sunday against the Steelers. Still, Sirianni could always change his mind on Wednesday, as he did when he infamously said, "Tanner's our guy," then benched McKee for Milton just days before the Eagles hosted the Giants.
This is what Sirianni said about Milton after losing to New York:
Still, Milton's fate is tied to the whims of his head coach.
The QB was asked how he would spend the bye week. He said he would probably take two days off, then get back to learning the Eagles’ system.
“I just want to be better,” he said. “We want to be better as a team.”
The Eagles went three-and-out and punted three times to start the second half, allowing the Giants to take control.
It’s not the first time the offense has been so inept for long stretches in games this year. In fact, offensive coordinator Sean Mannion’s unit has gone three-and-out on 43% of its offensive possessions, which is the highest rate of any team in the last three seasons and the highest rate for any Eagles team in the 21st century.
The Eagles filled two of the four openings on their 53-man roster, adding offensive lineman John Ojukwu and tight end Zach Ertz on Monday. Expect Ertz to make his march to the franchise record for most catches in an Eagles career. He needs eight more to break the mark of 589 set by Harold Carmichael from 1971-1983. In a lost season, at least it’s something.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
The flip side is what happens with developmental second-round pick Eli Stowers. The rookie tight end got just seven snaps against the Giants.
The hole in the NFC East didn’t get much deeper for them during their week off, with the first-place Giants losing and the Cowboys stumbling again in Week 10. Still, the hole was already plenty deep enough to entertain any thoughts about making a late push to the top.
At 2-7 and incapable of winning a game since Sept. 20, Philadelphia is four games behind New York (5-3-1) in the loss column and entrenched in last place in the division.
It was a stunning move to see general manager Howie Roseman move on from Jordan Davis , a defensive tackle that he just opened the vault for in the offseason, but the return of a first-round pick next year and a second in 2028 was too great to pass up.
As for Arnold Ebiketie, the Eagles thought they had a deal done with the Bengals to get a sixth-round pick next year, but Cincinnati messed up and had to back out . So, it might be a tad awkward for the outside linebacker when he shows up in the locker room.

title: T.J. Paganetti Reunion Could Shed Light on Eagles' Mindset as They Return From Bye
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — As they return from their bye week , the Eagles are bringing back T.J. Paganetti in a consulting role, a league source confirmed to Sports Illustrated .
The move mirrors previous outside voices the organization has brought in during the Nick Sirianni era, including Jim Bob Cooter in 2021 and Marcus Brady in 2022, not to mention Vic Fangio during the run-up to Super Bowl LVII.
Paganetti’s expertise is in offensive concepts—particularly the run game. Sirianni will speak on Wednesday and could offer more clarity on the role Paganetti will provide for the struggling 2-7 Eagles.
Although Paganetti’s institutional knowledge makes him a logical addition at a moment of clear offensive regression, the organization has used consultants in varying, sometimes unconventional ways.
For instance, Brady, a former offensive coordinator in Indianapolis and the current passing game coordinator in Baltimore, helped advise the defense in 2022 while Fangio offered up his defensive expertise to the offense before the Super Bowl that same season.
Paganetti held a variety of roles across his first stint with the Eagles from 2017 to 2024. He began as offensive quality control and assistant offensive line coach (2017-18) under Jeff Stoutland, then moved to assistant running backs coach (2019-20).
Under Sirianni, he first returned to quality control (2021-22) before being promoted to run game specialist/assistant tight ends coach in 2023 and run game specialist/assistant offensive line coach in 2024, where he again aided Stoutland. He was part of both Super Bowl championship staffs (LII and LIX) and left after the Super Bowl LIX win to become Kellen Moore’s run game coordinator with the New Orleans Saints.
Paganetti was later fired by the Saints earlier this month amid their own ground-game struggles earlier this season.
The timing is hard to ignore. The Eagles entered their bye week with all eyes on the offensive coaching staff and whether there would be any changes.
The organization went into the season intent on better marrying the running and passing games under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. That meant moving on from  Stoutland in favor of Chris Kuper (offensive line) and Ryan Mahaffey (run game coordinator/tight ends).
The shift has not produced the desired results . Philadelphia is currently mired in a seven-game skid, with the offense ranked near the bottom of the league and the line and run game a far cry from the record-setting 2024 unit that featured Paganetti in a specialized run-game role.
What’s somewhat strange—and perhaps telling—is the philosophical contrast between the two different ground game approaches.
Stoutland’s philosophy emphasized physical, vertical displacement, power-based downhill schemes, and a culture of technique, fundamentals and player development that turned the Eagles’ line into a sustained strength from the famed and marketed “Stoutland University.”
Mannion’s system, drawing more from zone-heavy influences, prioritizes lateral movement, wide-zone concepts, and better integration with the passing game. The personnel and teaching styles have not aligned cleanly this season, and the on-field product has reflected that disconnect.
Bringing back a Stoutland loyalist—even in a consultancy capacity—could be viewed as raising the white flag on the full transition.
At minimum, it reads as a concession that some of the old running-game principles that powered the Eagles’ previous sustained success need to be reintroduced.
Whether Paganetti can meaningfully influence scheme, technique, or messaging from a consultancy role is unlikely, but it remains to be seen. That said, the organization has at least signaled that the current run-game direction is not working as constructed.
With the season already largely lost and Jalen Hurts sidelined , the Eagles' focus seems to have shifted toward stabilization and identifying what elements of the one-time successful run-game identity are worth preserving.

title: McMullen: What Eagles’ Latest Flurry of Moves Could Mean Coming Out of the Bye Week
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — The Eagles will get back to work this week after a bye in which they already let go of two reserves who didn’t fit into their 2027 plans when they waived wide receiver Hollywood Brown and offensive tackle Fred Johnson .
Add that to the recent trade of nose tackle Jordan Davis to Jacksonville, and the release of running back Jayden Blue and general manager Howie Roseman currently has four open 53-man roster spots to play with.
Roseman already filled two spots by elevating veteran tight end Zach Ertz and tackle John Ojukwu from the practice squad on Monday, and could have foreshadowed a third by staring the practice window of running back Will Shipley, who has been sidelined with a partial plantar fascia tear suffered in the London loss against the Jaguars.
We have signed TE Zach Ertz and T John Ojukwu to the active roster and opened the practice window for RB Will Shipley. We also signed RB Jaydon Blue, LB Chance Campbell, and TE Hayden Rucci to the practice squad and released DB Shaun Wade from the unit. pic.twitter.com/CXy6mv1qm9
Blue was brought back to the practice squad Monday, as was linebacker Chance Campbell and tight end Hayden Rucci, an in-line blocking option which has been a problem.
All of the movement could just be the start of a continued significant churn that could mean opportunities for others, be it inside or outside the Jefferson Health Training Complex. In fact, Roseman, who has a history of trying to win outside the margins, could be opening up a larger in-season roster-building lever by scanning  the practice squads of other teams in order to find younger players with upside and a cost-effective short-term future.
Brown and Johnson weren’t playing meaningful roles this season, and neither was going to be part of the long-term picture moving forward.
Brown caught five passes for 63 yards. Johnson played 24 snaps. With DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks expected back after the bye, and with younger options already getting looks on the offensive line, the Eagles made a practical decision.
The Eagles cleared the space, shed some salary, and seemingly accepted the reality of a 2-7 season that has long since slipped out of contention despite the realization that the rest of the woeful NFC East refuses to run away.
The trend could continue especially is the losing continues with veterans like Jonathan Jones, Elijah Moore, Kenny Moore, A.J. Epenesa and Arnold Ebiketie, who all fit the profile of aging or short-term players unlikely to be part of the 2027 core.
The Eagles already planned to move Ebiketie to Cincinnati for a 2027 sixth-round pick before the dysfunctional Bengals needed compensatory pick expert Nick Korte to explain how that deal would have cost them a third-rounder next April.
Obvious correction here: the Bengals gave up a regular 6th rounder--they did not gain one. The main point is of course about the 3rd round compensatory pick that this trade would cancel out. https://t.co/7Zjn5WK6NQ
Jones is 33 and has been limited by injury. Moore is 31 and was a midseason addition for depth while Epenesa has played sparingly behind a group of younger edge rushers. None of them projects as a building block for next year.
At 2-7, the Eagles should continue to be realistic about this season. Last Friday’s moves indicate that Roseman and the front office has already shown it is willing to make those calls so why not continue it?
At least, if there are viable options with potential that spans years instead of weeks.

title: 3-Round Eagles Midseason 2027 Mock Draft: Philly Casts a Wide Net to Address Several Needs
full_text:
As the Eagles come out of their Week 10 bye, it's hard not to think about the future. A 2-7 record upon their return has Philadelphia fans more focused on the possibilities that the 2027 NFL Draft could bring rather than the remaining regular-season schedule, especially after general manager Howie Roseman added some capital before last week's trade deadline .
According to Spotrac, the Eagles are on track to have nine picks in each of the next two drafts , giving Roseman & Co. plenty of opportunities to build for the future. The possibilities become even more exciting when accounting for the fact that Philadelphia will own two first-rounders in April thanks to the Jordan Davis trade with Jacksonville.
Eagles' current selections
That said, the midway of the 2026 season is the perfect time for a mock draft, so let's dive into what the first three rounds of the annual event could look like for the Eagles in April.
Rostering an elite offensive line played a key role in the Eagles' success over the last decade. The unit took a hit this season, with Lane Johnson retiring and Cam Jurgens traded to the Ravens—and that's without even mentioning that Landon Dickerson isn't getting any younger.
With that in mind, assuming they have the fifth overall pick, drafting Texas's Trevor Goosby is a no-brainer decision for the Eagles.
The Ohio State pass rush wasn’t great… but Trevor Goosby and Melvin Siani are also EXTREMELY good Just 2 pressures allowed combined between them against in Texas’s huge win over the Buckeyes pic.twitter.com/YlyiAgstFV
Standing 6'7" and weighing 312 lbs, Goosby is the type of behemoth blocker that can anchor Philadelphia's O-line for years to come. He's an athletic specimen who knows how to be in the right place at the right time, which is why he's allowed only three sacks across 1,571 offensive snaps , according to Pro Football Focus , since joining the Longhorns in 2023.
Goosby suffered a season-ending knee injury in October; however, he's expected to make a full recovery , per ESPN 's Pete Thamel.
Coming out of their bye week, the Eagles are tied for the fourth-fewest sacks (16) while owning the PFF's fifth-worst pass-rush grade (61.9).
In other words, drafting a promising pass rusher should be a priority early in the 2027 draft, which could lead Philadelphia to draft Alabama's Yhonzae Pierre. Since 2021, the Eagles have drafted four Crimson Tide products in the first three rounds, including linebacker Jihaad Campbell (31st overall in 2025).
After not drafting anyone from Alabama last year, resuming the trend of adding Pierre to defensive coordinator Vic Fangio's unit makes too much sense to ignore. The 22-year-old disruptor has improved with each passing season in the SEC, and the 2026 campaign isn't an exception, as he currently owns career-high PFF grades when it comes to :
Pierre isn't perfect, as he still occasionally misses tackles, but it's hard to ignore the 32 pressures (five sacks) he's racked up. He's also steadily improved in coverage, allowing only a 42.9% completion rate and an 11.3 passer rating on seven targets so far. It isn't a huge sample size, but it's notable after allowing 10-of-12 passes (83.3%) for 99 yards and a 101.0 passer rating last season.
Imagine if the Eagles can mold him into their next defensive great?
It's hard to say what the future will hold for Jalen Hurts. The Eagles lost their franchise QB for the season to blood clots last month, and while fans would love nothing more than to see Hurts make a full recovery, there's at least a possibility that he won't suit up for Philadelphia again . And if he does, he might not be the same player.
Whether he's under center in 2027 or not, the Eagles must prepare for a Hurts-less future eventually, which could lead them to draft UCLA's Nico Iamaleava on Day 2. On Saturday, I wrote about how Iamaleava could be a second-round target for Philadelphia , especially since he could become the same type of dual-threat fans are used to in Hurts.
Unlike Goosby, Iamaleava reportedly plans to return to UCLA after a season-ending injury, which was an ACL tear. We're at a point in modern medicine where that injury isn't as big an issue anymore, so it shouldn't deter the Eagles from ignoring what they could have with Iamaleava if his plans change.
There's a good chance that the Eagles' tight end room will have some vacancies to fill this offseason. As it stands, rookie Eli Stowers is the only TE Philadelphia has under contract for 2027, with Dallas Goedert, Grant Calcaterra, and Johnny Mundt all set to become unrestricted free agents in March.
Although the Eagles could re-sign any combination of them, it wouldn't hurt to add someone like Texas Tech TE Terrance Carter Jr. through the draft.
Carter is the kind of scoring machine most NFL coaches would love to inject into their offenses. He scored seven touchdowns on 76 catches across 25 games with Louisiana in 2023 and 2024 before transferring to Texas Tech the following season. That move proved to be the right call, as Carter has amassed 922 yards and 10 TDs on 82 catches since the start of 2025, meaning he's found pay dirt on 12.2% of his receptions.
Texas Tech’s offense is at its best when Terrance Carter Jr. is involved. One of the best TEs in the country after the catch. Carter has averaged 6.9 YAC per reception for his career pic.twitter.com/TKhkmIkvYK
He's known for his pass-catching, but Carter can contribute as a blocker, too. He's up to 65.2 run-block and 59.1 pass protection grades on PFF and has yet to surrender a sack throughout his five-year collegiate run.
Even if they return, Goedert and Calcaterra aren't getting any younger. It's time to invest in the future, and a TE room that's built around Carter and Stowers could help fuel the Eagles' offensive success for years to come.

title: Howie Roseman's Miami Visit Is Creating Eagles Buzz It Might Not Deserve
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — Eagles general manager Howie Roseman’s Miami-Duke visit created the expected noise. The calendar, family context and the broader quarterback picture for the Eagles make it more routine than it looked.
The video clip went viral pretty quickly: Philadelphia’s general manager on the field before Miami hosted Duke, briefly greeting Hurricanes quarterback Darian Mensah.
"Bring him to Philly!" Philadelphia Eagles GM Howie Roseman a little pregame love for Canes QB Darian Mensah @WPLGLocal10 pic.twitter.com/QkhiiNuepN
For a team that has struggled , sits with Jalen Hurts sidelined for the season by blood clots and is projected to hold significant 2027 draft capital (including a potential top-five pick and another later in the round, any Roseman-QB interaction was going to generate some “bring him to Philly” reactions.
The timing amplified it, but the context points more to business as usual. The Eagles are on their bye week , the trade deadline has passed, and Roseman has more time than he typically has in mid-November.
More significantly, Roseman’s oldest son, Jake, attends Duke and works with the Blue Devils’ football program. That family visit is the far more likely reason why the Miami-Duke game made logistical sense during the bye.
Mensah himself was the starting QB at Duke in 2025 before transferring to Miami (a move that involved an NIL dispute that was later settled). Roseman was hardly the only NFL representative in the building for a high-profile ACC game—scouts from several other teams were present—but the personal tie to Duke and the time Roseman has with the Eagles off this week are the clearest reasons he was there in person.
None of that means Mensah falls outside the Eagles’ evaluation of quarterbacks when the position could top Roseman's wanted list next April. He is a productive quarterback who has put up elite numbers at Miami after earlier stops at Tulane and Duke. He will be on the board for teams that need a signal-caller in the first round. The same is true of other names that most personnel evaluators currently place ahead of Mensah.
Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker continues to draw the strongest “upside” comments. The former walk-on has the physical tools, production, and arm talent that keep him at or near the top of many 2027 quarterback rankings. Notre Dame’s C.J. Carr is viewed as the most advanced processor of the group, according to multiple personnel evaluators who spoke to Eagles On SI .
Carr is accurate, comfortable with pre-snap manipulation, and further along in the mental side of the position than most of his peers. Texas’s Arch Manning still carries the pedigree and the traits that made him a high-profile prospect, even as his tape this season has been more uneven than some of the others.
Roseman’s job is to uncover as much information as possible with all those possibilities.
A pregame conversation with Mensah, against the backdrop of a son at Duke, does not lock the Eagles into (or out of) any particular quarterback plan.
It is one hardly-significant data point in a process that will also include Mestemaker’s high-ceiling flashes, Carr’s processing, and Manning’s pedigree.
With Hurts’s recovery timeline unclear and the Eagles' roster in flux, that evaluation work on Mensah and others who participated in the Hurricanes-Blue Devils matchup is simply part of the job—no more dramatic, and no less necessary, despite the way it might have looked to the uninitiated on a bye-week Saturday in South Florida.

title: Fred Johnson's Release Underscores the Eagles' Personal Gong Show
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA, P.A. — For younger readers, "The Gong Show" was a somewhat iconic television game show from the 1970s in which often bizarre, eccentric and untrained amateur contestants performed on stage while a panel of three celebrity judges watched.
If a judge disliked an act, they would strike a massive brass gong with a wooden mallet to abruptly end the performance.
The always-interesting Fred Johnson recently introduced the percussion instrument into the Eagles' locker room to liven things up during what’s turned into a seven-game skid for an organization not used to losing.
Turns out Johnson’s gong had a shorter shelf life than A.J. Dillon’s infamous positivity bunny.
The big man eventually moved the gong into the offensive line room, but now both Johnson and his new toy will be filing a change of address form .
The last figurative clang of Johnson’s gong signaled the Eagles' waiving of a pair of veteran offensive players Friday: wide receiver Hollywood Brown and Johnson, the team’s proven swing tackle.
We have waived WR Marquise Brown and T Fred Johnson. pic.twitter.com/S4ieutMSfU
Neither player figured into the organization’s 2027 plans, so the decisions highlight the end of any realistic push for the 2026 postseason and a clear shift toward the continued evaluation of younger players who have an opportunity to be part of the solution moving forward.
The actual reasons for moving on are slightly different. With starting receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) set to return from injuries after the Eagles’ bye week, there wasn’t going to be much playing time for Brown.
An NFL source confirmed to Eagles On SI that Brown wanted to move on, and Philadelphia agreed after working out a non-injury settlement . In other words, Brown agreed to give back some of the $5 million he was guaranteed back in March for the opportunity to seek more playing time elsewhere, perhaps with a playoff contender.
Johnson, 29, is a little bit different. He has been a reliable swing tackle and backup for the Eagles in recent seasons and has garnered plenty of playing time since first joining the organization in late 2022.
Johnson contributed during the Super Bowl LIX-winning 2024 campaign (primarily filling in at left tackle for an injured Jordan Mailata) and logged a career-high 626 regular-season snaps in 2025 while starting nine games, mostly in relief of Lane Johnson.
After the Super Bowl season, Johnson left in free agency for an opportunity to compete for a starting job in Jacksonville. That didn’t work out, and the Eagles sent a seventh-round pick to the Jags to get him back just before the start of the 2025 season.
If it were a strict meritocracy, Johnson likely would have taken over at right tackle after Lane Johnson’s in-season retirement. Instead, the Eagles went with upside, inserting third-round rookie Markel Bell.
Fred Johnson appeared in seven games this season with only 24 offensive snaps, many of them as an extra tight end in a jumbo package.
The Eagles entered their bye week at 2-7 , last in the NFC East and mired in a seven-game skid. The team’s playoff odds have effectively evaporated, even in a weak NFL East.
In that context, cutting a veteran with no long-term roster value—and no trade value after the deadline—frees a spot on the 53-man roster while the evaluation of Bell continues.
These moves fit a broader pattern of roster pruning during the downtime of the bye. Earlier in the week, the Eagles also waived running back Jaydon Blue and traded defensive tackle Jordan Davis , opening multiple spots.
The organization can now promote or claim developmental players from practice squads. In-house, John Ojukwu, Kiran Amegadjie and Evan Neal could factor in as swing-tackle options behind Mailata and Bell.
For Johnson, the departure closes a productive chapter in Philadelphia. He took to Instagram after the news with a simple thank-you to the city , posting a photo from the Super Bowl celebration.
The Eagles return to action on Nov. 22 against the Steelers. By then, the roster will reflect a more explicit developmental priority—an acknowledgment that the corner on 2026 has been turned and the focus has shifted primarily to the future.
Essentially, the Eagles' 2026 season just got gonged.

title: 3 Eagles Who Should Barely See the Field After the Bye Week
full_text:
The Eagles have proven that things change on a dime in the NFL. Philadelphia entered the season with Super Bowl hopes, but enters its bye week with the worst record in the NFC (2-7). A team that has been focused on hoisting the Lombardi Trophy now needs to shift toward planning for the future .
There's been a lot of new faces wearing midnight green. That'll happen when the starting quarterback goes down, a Pro Bowl offensive lineman retires, and a star defensive tackle is traded . The Eagles have an opportunity to retool by focusing on youth and development over the final eight games.
That means decreasing their reliance on short-term veterans. Here's a look at three Eagles who stick out.
The Eagles had agreed to trade defensive end Arnold Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a sixth-round pick. That was until Cincinnati backed out when they determined the deal would result in a lost compensatory pick. Ebiketie will remain in Philly before entering free agency at the end of the season.
The fact that the Eagles were ready to part ways with Ebiketie shows he doesn't fit into their 2027 plans. The 27-year-old has failed to make much of an impact, posting 25 tackles and two quarterback hits in nine games (48% of the defensive snaps and 37% of the special teams snaps).
Shrinking Ebiketie's role in the defensive end rotation would allow rookie Keyshawn James-Newby to play increased snaps . The seventh-round pick flashed with two pressures in 20 pass-rush snaps in Week 6. James-Newby's 9.0 sacks with New Mexico in 2025 led the Mountain West Conference.
Cornerback Kenny Moore II was not expected to take on a major role in Philly's secondary when he was signed in September. That was before Michael Carter II's abdominal injury. Moore has stepped in at safety as of late, playing at least 48% of the defensive snaps in four of the Eagles' past five games.
The increase in snaps was simply injury-fueled, though. Moore has struggled in pass coverage, allowing a 158.7 passer rating when targeted. The former Pro Bowler was picked on for an eight-yard touchdown, a 30-yard completion, and a 20-yard completion during a Week 8 loss to Washington.
Moore is 31 and playing on a one-year deal. He should stay on the sideline once Carter returns. The second half of the season is also a chance for the Eagles to see what rookie safety Cole Wisniewski can add to the mix. The sixth-round pick has been a hard-hitting tackler on special teams.
The Eagles didn't even wait until the bye week to bench quarterback Tanner McKee in favor of Joe Milton, who had been in Philly for less than a month. This comes after Andy Dalton beat McKee for the backup QB spot in training camp. The franchise clearly doesn't view McKee as a long-term option.
It's a harsh reality for someone who has been on the roster since 2023. McKee was inconsistent in his three starts this campaign, completing 72 of his 114 passes (63.2%) for 638 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions. The Eagles averaged a disappointing 15.0 points across those three contests.
"The Eagles benched Tanner McKee way too soon!" They went with Joe Milton for reasons like this. He's a dynamic athlete and behind this OL, this type of escapability is needed. This led to the Eagles third first quarter TD of the season. #Eagles pic.twitter.com/QV2BR5wiaw
The final eight games of the season should be treated as a tryout for Milton to earn a roster spot in 2027. If he plays well, he could be Jalen Hurts's backup. If he plays poorly, the Eagles could cut bait. It'll be up to Philly's coaching staff to make the most of Milton's strong arm and scrambling abilities.

title: 3 Sneaky QB Prospects the Eagles Should Already Be Eyeing in the 2027 NFL Draft
full_text:
The Eagles' ongoing losing streak will remain where it is for now as they take a breather during a much-needed bye in Week 10. Seven consecutive losses following a 2-0 start have sucked the oxygen right out of the room in Philadelphia, and a quiet trade deadline performance further hammered home that there won't be much to celebrate this season .
With the halfway point of the 2026 season here, it's time for Eagles fans to start thinking about the future—whether that's potential offseason departures or free agency signings . Some folks are even thinking about the 2027 NFL Draft, where the Eagles' selections will happen earlier than they're used to.
That said, drafting a potential quarterback could be on general manager Howie Roseman's radar in April. Questions surround Jalen Hurts's outlook after blood clots knocked him out of the current season , and it's safe to say that Joe Milton, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton have a long way to go toward proving their long-term value.
Even if Hurts makes a full recovery, the Eagles would be wise to start thinking about the future. If Philadelphia wants to use its upcoming first-rounder on another position, there are still at least three sneaky QB prospects Roseman & Co. should consider on Day 2.
Hurts's mobility is one aspect that helps make him so great, so no one would be surprised if head coach Nick Sirianni wants his next franchise QB to have a similar trait. That's why UCLA's Nico Iamaleava could be on the Eagles' radar once the second round begins.
Standing 6'5" and weighing 215 lbs, Iamaleava boasts the size and athleticism that NFL coaches love. He's displayed a well-rounded game during his time at UCLA and Tennessee, completing 521-of-818 passes (63.7%) for 5,840 passing yards and 38 touchdowns to 16 interceptions while converting 283 carries into 1,078 rushing yards (3.8 per attempt) and 11 TDs.
Nico Iamaleava at his best is a top 3 qb in college football pic.twitter.com/S3pUYq4b01
Unfortunately, Iamaleava's 2026 campaign ended last month when he tore his ACL in a 17-15 win over Oregon, ending his final collegiate season. That said, medicine has come a long way, and there's no reason to believe that Iamaleava can't be a franchise QB in the NFL one day. If anything, his season-ending injury might help him fall to the Eagles on Day 2, depending on where they draft.
One season after leading the Big Ten in passing yards (3,711), yards per completion (14.0) and passing yards per game (285.5) en route to third-team honors, it's safe to say Jayden Maiava picked up from where he left off.
The USC product currently paces the conference with 198 completions, 2,524 passing yards and 20 TDs through nine starts. He's thrown for multiple touchdowns in six of his nine appearances, which includes a career-best five-TD game against Louisiana back on Sept. 12.
Jayden Maiava is quietly one of the most efficient QBs in the country 👀 ▫️ 86.5 PFF Short Passing Grade (#1 FBS) ▫️ 2,525 Pass Yards (#1 Big Ten, #10 FBS) ▫️ 20 Pass TDs (#1 Big Ten) ▫️ 1.0% Turnover-Worthy Play Rate vs No Blitz (#3 FBS) He’s no longer just the gunslinger,… pic.twitter.com/ZTeQRFhOtD
Maiava isn't without his flaws, which is why he's a projected second-round pick in most mock drafts. His play sometimes drifts into sloppy territory when he isn't completely focused, which can lead to turnovers (one interception in the first four games vs. four INTs in the last five). And, unlike Iamaleava, Maiava isn't a mobile threat, as proven by his averaging 2.4 yards on 173 carries (although he has scored 15 rushing TDs).
The offensive line has gone through injuries and departures this season, but Sirianni and his coaches know how to protect a quarterback when the pieces are there. If the Eagles can recreate that magic, Maiava is the perfect pocket passer to take advantage of that protection—especially with the weapons he'd have at his disposal (DeVonta Smith, Saquon Barkley, Eli Stowers, etc.).
Dante Moore is yet another collegiate QB whose season is lost, having sustained a season-ending concussion in September . That said, the Eagles shouldn't let any concerns keep them from drafting the Oregon product.
After all, Moore has the release and pocket presence that NFL coaches admire. His lack of mobility might be a red flag to some, but that's negligible when considering what he can accomplish without his legs being a factor. Moore racked up 39 TDs (to 10 INTs) and 4,491 passing yards in 19 games for the Ducks over the last two seasons, completing 71.4% of passes along the way. He even boasted a 9-0 TD-INT ratio before his current campaign ended, illustrating how efficient he can be.
Let's also not forget that there was a time when Moore was projected to be the No. 2 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , only to return to Oregon for another season. That potential doesn't just fizzle away overnight, even if this season hasn't gone as planned. The Eagles could be big winners if they can grab Moore and tap into that potential, and other QB-needy teams passing on him might further motivate him to prove the doubters wrong.
Throw in the fact that Hurts could take him under his wing to get him to use his feet more often, and the Eagles have every reason to take a swing on Moore next spring.

title: Eagles Have Nothing to Lose by Giving One Rookie a Sink-or-Swim Test Moving Forward
full_text:
With a losing season almost a guarantee at this point , it's time to start thinking about the future in Philadelphia.
The Eagles used a second-round pick in the 2026 NFL trade to select tight end Eli Stowers from Vanderbilt. It was a relatively high pick for a tight end, but the Eagles clearly viewed Stowers as the potential future of the position in Philadelphia.
Unfortunately, Stowers experienced a slow start to his Eagles tenure. He struggled throughout training camp and was then sidelined for an extended period at the start of the season due to a combination of hamstring and quad injuries.
Stowers finally made his Eagles debut in Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday Night Football. He didn't have any catches in the game, but at least he made it onto the field, which was a dream come true for the Texas native. “It’s a dream come true just to be out there, working, getting better," Stowers said after the game. "Just to be out on the field was a blessing.”
Stowers followed his debut with a three-reception, 53-yard performance against the Washington Commanders in Week 8, then went without a reception again in Week 9 against the Giants.
The Eagles now have eight games remaining in the current campaign, and with their playoff hopes already dashed, getting increased on-field opportunity for some unproven young players should be a top priority for Philly, and Stowers should be at the top of that list.
The Eagles simply need to see whether he is the future of the TE position, and the only way to do that is by throwing him into the deep end.
Despite speculation that they would, the Eagles didn't trade veteran tight end Dallas Goedert before Tuesday's trade deadline, and there's even a chance that he could be back in Philly next season . He's also 31 years old, so the organization needs to identify a succession plan at the position. The Eagles obviously know what they have in Goedert, and with little to play for in terms of a postseason perspective, the team should let Stowers eat into a large chunk of Goedert's playing time moving forward.
Second week in a row we are seeing Eli Stowers (No. 87) give this kind of effort blocking a CB Baby steps! pic.twitter.com/l5FhR3fGRI
The Eagles will have to make decisions regarding the TE position this offseason. Should they bring back Goedert? Should they look to add another TE in free agency? Should they draft a TE again? The front office won't be able to answer these questions properly unless they see a larger sample size from Sowers—both in the blocking and pass-catching departments.
Whenever Stowers does see the field for Philly, his aim is to be as impactful as possible.
“ Every single play there’s something that you can do to help the offense be successful ,” Stowers said earlier this month (h/t NBC Sports Philadelphia ). “Everybody’s got a job on every single play and so it’s every single rep. How can you be intentional about what your job is? Whether it’s getting open, catching the ball, blocking for somebody, running off for somebody. How can you do that to the best of your abilities? That’s what I try to do.”
Stowers seeing the field more over the final two months of the season will be beneficial for a couple of reasons. First, it will let him gain some much-needed experience in some relatively low-stakes games. It will also provide the organization with an excellent opportunity to evaluate him—and the tight end position as a whole—heading into the offseason.

title: What Fred Johnson & Hollywood Brown's Releases Say About the Eagles’ Plans Moving Forward
full_text:
There could be tumbleweeds blowing through the Eagles' locker room next week. That’s only a slight exaggeration, but there will be plenty of vacant lockers after some roster destruction during the bye week.
The latest move involved the release of veteran swing tackle and sometimes guard Fred Johnson on Friday. That came on the heels of the release of receiver Hollywood Brown , which came on the heels of the release of running back Jaydon Blue earlier in the week. Combine that with the trade of Jordan Davis, and the Eagles have four open roster spots.
The #Eagles are releasing veteran OT Fred Johnson, source says. He's been with the team since 2023. pic.twitter.com/y3Ln9Jm8kN
Cutting Blue signifies that Tank Bigsby and/or Will Shipley could be returning in time for their game against the Steelers on Nov. 22. Bigsby has been on injured reserve since Oct. 6, when a core muscle injury sidelined him. Shipley has been on IR since Oct. 16 with a partial tear of the plantar fascia in his foot. Both have missed the required four games.
As for the release of Brown, the Eagles are likely to get both DeVonta Smith and Tay Wicks back after the bye. Smith has played in just four games this season while battling a hamstring injury, and Wicks has missed three straight games with an ankle injury.
Neither player was placed on IR, so they can return at any time.
Brown wore the number 0, which has become a jinx of sorts since the NFL allowed that number to be worn. Nobody who has worn it since has lasted more than a year. Eagles who wore it previous to Brown are:
Johnson had been with the Eagles for nearly four seasons. He played in six games this year, but played in all 17 games in his previous three years with the team, making 14 starts.
His release signals the Eagles’ readiness to turn to younger players on the offensive line. There is an intriguing prospect on the practice squad who could be summoned. That is Yale’s Kiran Amegadjie, who is 6'5" and 326 lbs. John Ojukwu could also be a possibility.
The Eagles may not be done unloading veterans, either, as they transition to a team that wants to see the younger players play.
Safety Marcus Epps could be in jeopardy, with the possibility that seventh-round pick Cole Wisnieski could see time. Also, the Eagles could release Arnold Ebiketie and/or A.J. Epenesa and turn to seventh-round pick Keyshawn James-Newby. The Eagles thought they had a deal to trade Ebiketie to the Bengals at the trade deadline, but the Bengals backed out.
It might not even be a surprise if the Eagles give Uar Bernard and Josh Weru opportunities over the final eight games.
