title: Steelers Have QB Problem Aaron Rodgers Can't Solve
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers possess a laundry list of problems, many of which were revealed during a 38-18 butt-whooping at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals.
On both sides of the ball, the Steelers were "decisively beaten," head coach Mike McCarthy said postgame. The defense was unable to "settle down," according to inside linebacker Patrick Queen, and that shakiness allowed Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow to move the ball at will and score 38 points.
On offense, it was a silent day for the team's top weapon and running back, Jaylen Warren. Left guard Mason McCormick sustained an ankle injury that appears to be serious and possibly long-term. Wide receiver DK Metcalf ended his five-game touchdown drought, but he once again failed to be a difference-maker on the outside.
All that included, and the list of issues the Steelers must address is overwhelming. Unfortunately, that list is not complete unless it includes quarterback Aaron Rodgers. After beginning the year playing like a solid game-managing quarterback, the soon-to-be 43-year-old QB's play on the field doesn't align with the winning football he and the Steelers claim to be pursuing.
Aaron Rodgers is an undisputed, first-ballot Hall of Fame candidate when the time comes.
Even the greatest in league history eventually lose it, and the decline of Rodgers has been ignored for far too long. The version the Steelers brought to Pittsburgh was obviously not Rodgers in his prime, but this season appears to be a very clear regression for the four-time NFL MVP.
This regression is most evident on throws beyond 10 yards. Rodgers will go down as one of the best pure passers in NFL history, capable of locating a pass with pinpoint accuracy.
That description is not anywhere close to applicable to the current version of Rodgers. He's completed less than 60% of his passing attempts five times in nine starts, and on the season he has a 60.8% completion percentage. The numbers just get worse the farther downfield Rodgers attempts to throw the ball.
Rodgers has attempted 52 passes between 10 and 19 yards. He's completed 24 of those attempts for a 46.2% completion percentage. That ranks 42nd among all quarterbacks with at least one dropback in 2026, according to SumerSports .
For passes 20 yards or greater, it's even worse. He's attempted 44 passes of 20 yards or more, but he's only completed nine passes. His 20.5% completion percentage ranks 43rd in the NFL among all quarterbacks with at least one dropback this season.
Despite that, the Steelers remain overreliant on Rodgers having the ball in his hands. He's attempted 30 passes or more seven times in nine contests. He and Metcalf continue to create nothing on offense, but the offense won't stop trying to cram a square peg into a round hole.
Right now, Rodgers is on pace to have one of the worst statistical seasons of his NFL career. Sure, he doesn't care about individual statistics, he only cares about ending his final year on the right note.
But it will be very, very hard to end Rodgers' Hall of Fame career on the right note, the way he has been and continues to play.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Still a Chance? Steelers’ Mike McCarthy Not Ruling Out Mason McCormick Return
full_text:
Pittsburgh Steelers left guard Mason McCormick went down with a scary-looking injury late in the second quarter of the team's 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10.
An air cast was placed on McCormick's right leg, and he was carted off to the locker room from there. Despite the circumstances and long-term outlook appearing grim in the moment, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy did not rule out the possibility of the 26-year-old making his way back onto the field this season while stating that the hope is that the "good news continues" despite him admitting that he suffered a "significant injury" and that there isn't a concrete diagnosis yet.
"Just working through the information gathering," McCarthy said during his weekly press conference. "Hopefully some good news continues. I just think any time you have a significant injury, it's important to get all the information. So, obviously, sitting with him last night, he's got a great attitude and he'll tackle it like he does everything else. But yea, I don't have anything where I can really put a number on it or what the final diagnosis is."
After a demoralizing defeat like the one they were dealt at the hands of the Bengals, Pittsburgh has to focus on wiping its hands clean of that performance and moving on without letting things snowball.
McCormick's injury was, and is, a huge blow, especially considering he's viewed as the heart and soul of a young offensive line that's really gelled ever since Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor entered the starting lineup at right guard and right tackle, respectively, in Week 3.
A fourth-round selection in the 2024 NFL Draft, McCormick has exceeded all expectations and played at a rather high level for the Steelers, whether it be at left or right guard over his first three seasons in the league.
He's helped set the tone in the run game, and he's also held up well as a pass blocker, making him a well-rounded piece up front for Pittsburgh.
Seeing an impact player like McCormick go down with a significant injury is incredibly disheartening, and losing him for the remainder of the campaign would make the Steelers' entire operation on offense run rougher.
If there's real hope of a positive update on McCormick's status though, as McCarthy alluded to, that's the kind of news the entire team could rally around and really benefit from as they move on from their loss to Cincinnati.
There's no telling what the long-term outlook for McCormick is, but any positive developments would be such a huge boost for Pittsburgh.
Spencer Anderson finished out the contest against Cincinnati at left guard, logging 40 snaps at the position (per Pro Football Focus ) and is the favorite to remain in that role moving forward this season.
Anderson was named the starting right guard to open the year but was replaced by Hoffman in Week 3 as previously mentioned.
Part of the reasoning for Anderson being benched was the fact that he suffered a bone break in his leg during Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, though he also allowed a sack and five pressures in pass protection before being supplanted by Hoffman.
The 2023 seventh-round pick played over 400 snaps at left guard for the Steelers between the 2024 and 2025 campaigns, so having him fill in there once again is the team's likeliest course of action for as long as McCormick is out.
Third-round rookie Gennings Dunker is another potential candidate to earn playing time at left guard, though he's resided on the reserve/injured list since Week 3 with an MCL sprain.
Dunker was initially expected to remain out for four-to-six weeks, and since he's now at the end of that timeline, perhaps he could return in the not-so-distant future. McCarthy told reporters that Dunker returning from IR is "definitely part of the conversation" as well.
Backup center Ryan McCollum has played just four regular season snaps at guard throughout his career, though he has logged a total of 115 snaps at the position in the preseason since entering the league in 2021 ( per PFF ) and could probably play there in an absolute pinch for Pittsburgh.
Doug Nester and Steven Jones could also be called upon from the practice squad in some fashion as depth options at guard too, likely as game day elevations somewhere down the line.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Should Consider Rookie Guard When Healthy
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers lost one of their most important players on offense during their Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals.
The Steelers were absolutely routed by their AFC North rivals, but the sting of losing to the Bengals paled in comparison to the pain of losing starting left guard Mason McCormick. The third-year guard was carted off the field in the first half of the game after suffering what appeared to be a serious ankle injury.
Fourth-year offensive lineman Spencer Anderson replaced McCormick for the rest of their Week 10 contest, but it's unclear if he will be the starting left guard moving forward. Pressed for options, the Steelers may have to consider rookie guard Gennings Dunker when he returns from injury.
The Steelers are in a difficult position following McCormick's injury. The ugly reality is that they don't have another interior offensive lineman who can play at the level McCormick can, so it becomes a matter of how Pittsburgh can manage his absence.
The best part of the Steelers' offense this year has been their running game. Running back Jaylen Warren is having the best season of his NFL career, and a large reason for that is because of the offensive line's play.
While Dunker has never played an NFL snap in the regular season, he was given plenty of opportunity during the preseason. A former tackle in the NCAA, Dunker is a work in progress, but he stood out in one area.
That area was run-blocking. While pass-rush overwhelmed the first-year guard, his ferocious mentality and huge frame were an asset in the run game.
And that's what makes him a viable option for the Steelers moving forward. The offense has to sustain their success on the ground, and finding their way back to that after losing McCormick will be even more challenging.
Dunker isn't a guarantee, but he does provide optimism and excitement.
The Steelers are very high on Dunker, but the start of his NFL career hasn't gone according to plan. The organization placed him on the Injured Reserve just ahead of their Week 3 contest against the Bengals, following an MCL sprain he suffered in practice.
Now preparing for their Week 11 opponent, the Philadelphia Eagles, Dunker is eligible to come off of the IR. It's just a matter of when that will happen.
He's made progress in recent weeks, which is an encouraging sign. In practice ahead of their Week 8 game against the Cleveland Browns and Week 10 game in Cincinnati, Dunker has been working with the rest of the injured players in a limited capacity. Stretching and light jogging don't sound like exciting activities, but for the rookie, it's a huge step forward.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Can Steelers Ever Get Out of DK Metcalf Contract?
full_text:
Another week, another disappointing outing from DK Metcalf for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The 28-year-old was nowhere to be found early in the Steelers' blowout 38-18 loss at the hands of the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football in Week 10. Metcalf once again failed to create separation, and on the one occasion he could've created an explosive play with a little under five minutes left during the second quarter, he dropped what would've been right around a 30-yard gain with Jordan Battle in coverage.
While Battle bailed Metcalf out with a taunting penalty before the latter came alive with 54 yards and a touchdown during garbage time in the fourth quarter, it wasn't nearly enough to completely rectify all of the issues currently ongoing with the veteran wide receiver .
Metcalf has not lived up to his four-year, $132 million deal with Pittsburgh, which he signed after arriving in a trade from the Seattle Seahawks in March 2025. Not only that, but the contract looks like a complete albatross and is up there among the worst in the league.
Is there any path for the Steelers to get out of that deal, however?
Pittsburgh restructured Metcalf's contract this past offseason in order to free up almost $18 million in cap space.
As a result, $23.7 million of his salary for the 2026 campaign was converted into a signing bonus and his salary cap charge was lowered by $17.775 million while simultaneously raising his cap charge in future seasons by $5.925 million per year (per Over the Cap ).
Metcalf is also due a $6.5 million roster cut on the fifth day of the 2027 league year and a $5 million roster bonus on the fifth day of the league year in both 2028 and 2029.
Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap).
Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money.
Should they look to cut or trade him in 2028, the dead money would remain the same while the cap savings would jump to $28 million before leaping once again to $35.5 million in 2029.
Parting ways with a player of Metcalf's magnitude might not be popular in the locker room, and it could also send the wrong message.
The Steelers traded a 2025 second-round pick and a 2025 seventh-rounder in exchange for Metcalf and a 2025 sixth-rounder. That's a rather considerable haul, and the organization could be wary of cutting their losses just two years into his tenure.
Still, if Metcalf doesn't turn things around this season, the idea of moving on from him has to at least be weighed.
His decline, most notably in terms of drops and the inability to win downfield, has come as a surprise. Pittsburgh thought it was getting a true No. 1 receiver, and instead, he's playing at replacement level in 2026.
As such, finding a taker for his contract will prove to be difficult. In fact, the Steelers might have to attach a pick just to find a suitable trade.
Releasing Metcalf feels far more probable than sending him elsewhere, but doing so comes with complications as well due to the dead money involved.
There is an avenue to move on from Metcalf, and if Pittsburgh is desperate enough it could theoretically happen next offseason even if it's not overly logical. As of right now, however, it's likely that he'll remain on the team's roster in 2027 despite the fact that he's lost a step, has provided little value this season and is on pace for 816 yards over 17 games, which would be a career low.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Is Steelers Season Over?
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- It's hard to recall a loss as bad as this one for the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Embarrassing doesn't seem to fit how poor of a performance Week 10 was for the Steelers. Their 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals firmly removed them from contention status and put them into a freefall that makes this season feel closer to finished than anything else.
But is it really over? Well, sometimes history repeats itself, and if that's the case, this year is going to be really disappointing.
The last time the Steelers gave up more than 38 points was Nov. 28, 2021 -- at Cincinnati (41-10)
The last time the Steelers gave up more than 38 points was Nov. 28, 2021 to the Bengals in a 41-10 loss. While they avoided that mark this time around, the 2021 season ended in familiar fashion.
Head coach Mike Tomlin walked into Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City and told the world to "cut your eyelids off." The Steelers then went on to lose 42-21.
Look, a bad loss coming off of a bye week feels terrible for every fan out there. No one is sitting around smiling, enjoying the loss to the Bengals . The players felt the same way in the locker room, as the mood was gloomy, discouraged and somewhat angry.
But the Steelers are 6-3 and one game behind a team that they beat earlier in the year. So, yes, the Bengals won the second battle, but the war is still split evenly, and that's something to hold onto.
"We're gonna address it here in practice and get after it," Cam Heyward said about the loss. "That's the only way that I know how to get better. There's a lot of ball to be played and I'm looking forward to getting better because of this."
The Steelers will travel to Philadelphia next to take on a 2-7 Eagles team led by Joe Milton. They then have an opportunity to come back, potentially 7-3, and host the Denver Broncos with a shot to re-prove themselves in the AFC.
This team will still play the Jacksonville Jaguars and Baltimore Ravens, twice, and add the Houston Texans, who are fighting for a playoff spot as well.
There's too much football to be played to say this season is finished.
"I've been a part of this league for a long time," Rodgers said. "There are big wins. There are tough losses. So, we'll deal with this appropriately."
Is it bad? Yes. Is it over? Not yet.

title: 6 Losers, 1 Winner From Steelers' Embarrassing Loss to Bengals
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers were flat-out embarrassed from start to finish by the Cincinnati Bengals in a 38-18 loss on Sunday Night Football .
Coming off their Week 9 bye while riding a four-game win streak, the Steelers felt like they had a fair amount of momentum on their side heading into Paycor Stadium in Week 10.
Unfortunately for them, however, the Bengals were also in the midst of a four-game win streak and simply outclassed them by a wide margin in each facet of the game.
Now sitting at 6-3 and a game back of Cincinnati for first place in the AFC North, Pittsburgh has a lot to ponder over and reevaluate before taking on the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11.
With that, here are our winners and losers from one of the Steelers' more lopsided losses in recent memory.
This was arguably the worst Rodgers has looked all season long. The 42-year-old can still move around a bit more than he gets credit for when the pocket starts to collapse, but the lapses in his accuracy, particularly downfield, really showed against the Bengals.
Rodgers never truly looked comfortable until garbage time in the fourth quarter when he threw for a pair of touchdowns before Mason Rudolph came in. That sentiment shows in his 15-of-29 stat line, as he threw for just 143 yards while also starting the contest 0-of-8, which is the first time he had ever done so.
It was déjà vu for Samuel Jr. in this one.
Samuel Jr. had a rough go of it vs. Cincinnati in Week 3, despite Pittsburgh coming away with a 30-27 win, allowing 61 yards and a pair of touchdowns (per Pro Football Focus ) while also taking a backseat to rookie Daylen Everette late in that contest.
On a night where there were plenty of weak links for the Steelers in their rematch with the Bengals, Samuel Jr. was among the team's biggest liabilities. He gave up 134 yards in coverage (per PFF) and was also called for defensive pass interference deep down the field on the first play of the second quarter, which set up Cincinnati's first touchdown of the night.
Wilson has largely been trending up in his third season with Pittsburgh, but his outing against the Bengals really set him back.
While he did lead the Steelers in total tackles with 19, which is his new career-high in a single game and is tied for the most by any player in the NFL this season, that was more so a product of Cincinnati dominating the time of possession battle (35:09 vs. 24:51) and running 65 offensive plays (58 of which came in the first three quarters) than anything else.
Wilson missed three tackles in this contest and allowed 98 yards in coverage on 10 receptions (per PFF ), highlighting just how poor of a performance the 26-year-old turned in.
Once again, Amarius Mims completely shut Watt out.
Watt did not register a single pressure against the Bengals' star right tackle in Week 3, and the same held true this time around as well (per PFF ).
Though Watt's had a resurgence this year with 7.5 sacks, which had already eclipsed his 2025 total of 7.0 sacks over 14 games, he can't disappear against the best tackles the league has to offer if Pittsburgh's defense wants any chance of truly establishing itself as the cream of the crop or even close to it.
If there was any silver lining for the Steelers, it was that Nichols finally got an opportunity and made the most of it as the team took out its starters and turned to its reserves in the fourth quarter.
The 25-year-old had just two carries for six yards over two contests for Pittsburgh coming into this game. On six carries vs. Cincinnati, however, he ran for 43 yards while also adding a catch for two yards.
As is also the case with Rodgers, Metcalf's slight redemption from a numbers perspective with two catches for 54 yards and a touchdown in the fourth quarter when the game was already far out of reach meant next to nothing.
Generating separation remains a chore for Metcalf, and he's failed to haul in throws downfield at an alarming rate for a 28-year-old who is supposed to thrive in that regard while still being in his prime.
Metcalf has been a complete disappointment for the Steelers, and considering he's under contract through the 2029 season while making an average annual salary of $33 million, there might be no way  out for the organization in the near future.
Much like Watt, Highsmith was essentially nonexistent against the Bengals.
The 29-year-old recorded zero pressures ( per PFF ) in a contest for the first time since last season's Wild Card round loss to the Houston Texans. It was also just the third time Highsmith had failed to log a pressure during the regular season since the beginning of the 2021 campaign.

title: Steelers vs. Bengals Takeaways: Season Over?
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Maybe Ja'Marr Chase was right when he said the Pittsburgh Steelers versus Cincinnati Bengals rivalry isn't that strong.
The Steelers move to 6-3 on the season in the most embarrassing fashion, losing 38-18 at Paycor Stadium. This team came into Week 10 red-hot and looking to prove they're the real deal in the AFC and the leaders of the AFC North. They proved the complete opposite of both.
Now, the questions aren't about how far they can go but how low they can fall. This team struggled in every facet of the game. And these takeaways show that.
This is a real stat. Just before the two-minute warning in this game, Aaron Rodgers was 0/7. Joe Burrow was 21/26 for 245 yards and two touchdowns.
Genuinely one of the graphics of all time pic.twitter.com/jvitfuIqw0
The entire Steelers team looked bad in this loss, but none more than Rodgers. Some plays, he was rattled by the pass rusher before the ball was even snapped. Others, he was inaccurate and nearly throwing interceptions. And the cherry on top was him being so worried at times that he would instantly dump it off to a running back for negative yards.
Rodgers still shows he has it, even at 42 years old. But against the Bengals, he was atrocious. Maybe the worst player on the field.
The Steelers desperately need a WR1. Germie Bernard is the closest thing they've got, but he's not good enough yet, and DK Metcalf is not the answer.
Omar Khan's decision not to make a move at the trade deadline will continue to haunt Pittsburgh. Aaron Rodgers doesn't have the weapons and when he finds himself without anyone open, he doesn't always try to extend plays. Most times, actually, he gives up early when no one is open immediately.
This offense is in trouble without someone breaking out. Hopefully, Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. provide enough. If they don't, don't expect this offense to be able to compete against high-powered offenses like Cincinnati's.
At this point, it's hard to justify DK Metcalf playing more snaps than Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. when they return. He adds very little value to this offense and yes, he does draw attention from the defense, but that's only useful if Rodgers can find other open targets.
Metcalf can't even be relied on to catch open passes at this point.
dk metcalf drop pic.twitter.com/zvdq9PczjP
Yes, he finished with two receptions, 54 yards and a touchdown. None of that came until the fourth quarter, when the Steelers were down 31-3.
The offensive and passing-game struggles are not all of his fault, but when you're paid over $30 million a year to be an elite receiver and barely pass as a playable one, the target is going to be on your back.
Metcalf, just plain and simple, isn't very good right now. At times, he's not good at all. And the more fans are reminded of it, the more infuriated they become that the team's WR1 is an overpaid former starter who may not have "it" anymore. And the Steelers desperately need "it."
Asante Samuel Jr.'s return to an NFL starting lineup is impressive. It's great to see him bounce back and overcome a neck injury that nearly ended his career much earlier than it deserved to end. But in Pittsburgh, there are six games a year that don't fit his size or play style, and those are crucial games.
Samuel Jr. just isn't big enough to play against the Bengals. He's not big enough to battle with Tee Higgins, who continues to make it look easy when matched up against him. And for Ja'Marr Chase, no one in the NFL can say they have the upper hand over him, but Samuel Jr. doesn't even come close.
Daylen Everette is going to come with mistakes. Every rookie does. But he has the size to compete in these AFC North showdowns and Pittsburgh needs to test him out. It's not the right answer but it's something. Samuel Jr. just doesn't have it against Cincinnati.
The Steelers lost Mason McCormick to what looked like a significant ankle injury just before halftime. If McCormick is going to miss the remainder of the season, Pittsburgh's offensive line just got significantly worse, and the blow may be their second toughest to overcome.
Zach Frazier and McCormick have been Pittsburgh's best two offensive linemen this season. McCormick, a third-year fourth-round pick, has been playing at a Pro Bowl level. At times, he's been their most reliable player up front, and as the group has continued to grow together, he's been a key piece in that foundation.
The offensive line took a clear step backward against the Bengals. Now they need to navigate without one of their best players, and all of a sudden, the problems feel overwhelming for this offense.
Well, at least for now, you can put those Pittsburgh Steelers Super Bowl dreams to bed. This team is a big of a "pretender" as they come. This season, they've played two teams in the AFC playoff race on the road, and both times, they've lost in blowouts.
This team is just not serious when it comes to competing with high-powered offenses. They can't keep up in the secondary and their offense has zero juice when Jaylen Warren isn't rushing for 100 yards.
You remove the superpower of No. 30 and this entire team shuts down. And their four-game winning streak was impressive, but it was tight games against losing teams. That's not going to translate to real competition.
This season isn't over yet. But it doesn't look bright as the second-half is only going to get harder.

title: Steelers' Mason McCormick Suffers Ankle Injury Against Bengals
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers' first half against the Cincinnati Bengals was a total disaster, but the worst moment came when one of their top offensive lineman suffered a serious-looking injury. Coming out of their bye week, the Steelers had the chance to send a message to the Bengals, the division and the rest of the AFC.
Instead, the Steelers completely stumbled out of the gate. Quarterback Aaron Rodgers missed the first eight passes he attempted, and the run game was stifled by the Bengals' defense. Their offense failed to match Cincinnati's productivity in the first half, punting on each of their first three drives.
Toward the end of the first half, the Steelers began to find life on offense. That's when starting left guard Mason McCormick went down with what appeared to be a right ankle injury. While trying to keep a Bengals defensive lineman out of Rodgers' face, McCormick
He looked to be in serious distress after the play, and medical trainers tended to him on the field. After placing an aircast on the injured leg, the medical staff carted him off the field. Most of the Steelers roster came to greet him and give well wishes to the starting guard before he exited the field.  Shortly after McCormick was taken off the field, the Steelers ruled him out for the game.
Mason McCormick ruled OUT with an ankle injury
Without McCormick in the left guard position, the Steelers' offensive line takes a serious blow. McCormick has been arguably the top lineman in Pittsburgh this season, and he's been a crucial piece in the team's success on the ground.
With the third-year guard out, the Steelers have to turn to their bench. Players like Spencer Anderson have experience at the left guard position, while backup center Ryan McCollum is another option who could step up while McCormick is out.
Anderson has starting experience with the Steelers at multiple positions. He's played across the offensive line, most recently starting the season as the right guard. He was replaced after the team's Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots, and he's been used primarily as an extra lineman in jumbo packages.
McCollum is a player who has plenty of experience and versatility as well. He's the backup center to Zach Frazier, but like Anderson, he can move around the offensive line.
The injury also brings up rookie Gennings Dunker. One of the team's recent third-round picks was placed on Injured Reserve earlier in the season. At the time, it was a tough development, but something the o-line could withstand. Now that McCormick is out for potentially a long time, the Steelers ' lack of depth at guard is becoming a problem in a hurry.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Offense Gets Their Tight End Against Bengals
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers got some good news regarding the availability of one of their top skill position players ahead of a Week 10 clash against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
Tight end Pat Freiermuth, who was added to the injury report and listed as questionable the day before the game with an illness, will be active vs. Cincinnati.
The Steelers appear closer to getting wide receivers Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) back from the reserve/injured list. With both remaining out for the time being, however, Freiermuth's importance to the team's offense remains heightened for a crucial battle between two 6-2 AFC North foes.
Following what was a bit of a lackluster 2025 campaign (486 yards, four touchdowns) for Freiermuth in his first year working with Aaron Rodgers, the hope was that he'd bounce back this season while continuing to build a stronger rapport with the future Hall of Fame quarterback.
Freiermuth was impressive during training camp and began the year on a high note with a  46-yard, one-touchdown performance in Pittsburgh's Week 1 victory over the Atlanta Falcons.
The 28-year-old has largely been inconsistent ever since, however, failing to break the 40-yard mark in a single game from that point on, outside of posting 44 yards and a pair of touchdowns in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts.
All in all, Freiermuth is on pace for 499 yards and nine touchdowns this season, the latter of which would represent a career-high.
He's filled his role admirably and made more of an impact than he did a year ago, though it still feels like he has the potential to take his game up another level.
Simply put, Freiermuth has owned Cincinnati throughout his career.
His 649 yards vs. the Bengals over 11 games is his most against any team by a wide margin, with his 349 yards vs. the Cleveland Browns marking his second-highest total in that regard.
Furthermore, Freiermuth's 111-yard, two-touchdown showing in the Steelers' Week 7 loss to Cincinnati on Thursday Night Football last season was just the second time in franchise history that a tight end finished a game with 100 or more receiving yards and two or more receiving touchdowns.
While he put up just 30 yards in Pittsburgh's Week 3 victory over the Bengals earlier this season, Freiermuth's history against Cincinnati should inspire some confidence that he can turn in another standout performance in primetime at Paycor Stadium.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers’ DeShon Elliott Suffers Pregame Injury, Out Against Bengals
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers have lost a key piece of their secondary for a monumental Week 10 showdown against the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday Night Football.
According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, safety DeShon Elliott suffered a knee injury during pregame warm-ups at Paycor Stadium and has been ruled out vs. Cincinnati as a result.
Steelers S Deshon Elliott injured his knee during the pregame and has been ruled out for tonight’s game vs. Cincinnati.
Elliott was listed on the injury report this week with an ankle injury, though he was a full participant on both November 12 and 13 after initially being limited on November 11, and thus was not listed with a game designation.
Having to face an explosive Bengals passing offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow as well as the star wide receiver duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins now becomes much tougher of a task for Pittsburgh without Elliott on the field.
The Steelers, though, were able to at least hold Cincinnati in check to an extent during their first meeting this season, which resulted in a 30-27 victory for the black and gold at Acrisure Stadium in Week 3. Elliott was not active for that contest either, while residing on the reserve/injured list to open the year after going down with a season-ending knee/hamstring injury in Week 8 of the 2025 campaign.
Jaquan Brisker, Robert Spears-Jennings and Jalen Ramsey now become all the more important for the Steelers now that Elliott will be sidelined against the Bengals.
It's not unfamiliar territory for that trio, as Elliott has only appeared in two games and played 43 defensive snaps since being activated from IR ahead of Pittsburgh's Week 7 game against the New Orleans Saints in Paris.
Holding up in coverage as a group on the back end of the defense against the likes of Chase and Higgins would've been a big ask even with Elliott on the field, though, and being down a veteran like that could have reverberating effects when facing a passing offense that averages the most yards per game (285.5) in the league.
Where the Steelers' safeties shouldn't have much of an issue holding down the fort, however, is against the Bengals' run game.
Cincinnati is averaging just 85.6 rushing yards per contest, which was the third-lowest mark in the NFL entering the day, while Pittsburgh allows the third-fewest yards on the ground per game at 83.9.
The likes of Ramsey, Brisker and Spears-Jennings are all capable of stepping up from the second level of the defense and making plays against the run, and with a favorable matchup in that regard vs. the Bengals, the Steelers shouldn't feel the loss of Elliott as much as they will in coverage.

title: Tory Horton May Have Earned Larger Seahawks Role After Raiders Game
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks dominated on defense and were outstanding on offense, especially in the third quarter against the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 10 victory . Still, it was a special teams play that might have sealed the deal going into the bye week.
With just 2:04 left to go in the game , the Raiders kicked off to the Seahawks after knocking down a field goal to make it a one-score game. The Seahawks knew that a touchback would result in an additional time stoppage, so they wanted to avoid this at all costs. That prompted wide receiver Tory Horton to make arguably the biggest special teams play of the season.
The effort by the Seahawks special teams to prevent the touchback and keep the clock running 👏 SEAvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YF6eTRh4gs
"It kind of bounced off my hands and I kind of just like drifted out of bounds," Horton said via the team's website.
"So, kind of just pointed at Sheed (Rashid Shaheed) to pick the ball up and return it. Just wanted to just keep the ball in play. I wish I caught it with one hand, but that's a pretty hard catch to do with the ball and go inflight like that. So I was still happy that Shaheed recognized the ball was in play and picked it up after I told them and just happy that we got it under 2 minutes."
Going into the contest, Horton wasn't even supposed to be in that position to begin with. However, circumstances changed throughout the game, and that forced Horton into that situation.
"It was a tremendous play," head coach Mike Macdonald added after the game.
"Tory's actually trying to catch that ball, albeit with one hand. Just an incredible play. With George Holani going down, we had to take JD (Jadarian Price) off of kickoff returns, so those are guys that haven't necessarily practiced (kick return) a bunch in a while, especially with this game plan. So to be able to step in and be able to execute some of those critical situations is some great stuff by them, great job by our coaches, and it really helped us close the game out."
Knowing that Horton wasn't even supposed to be in that position but made a play on the fly in a crucial situation that normally doesn't pop up is exactly how the Seahawks want to identify themselves. They have a next-man-up mentality that places importance on all 70 players on the main roster and practice squad, giving them moments to shine like this.
This identity helped carry the Seahawks to the Super Bowl last season, and it is what has them on pace to go all the way once again. It's going to take more plays like this after the bye, but this is a sign that the Seahawks are getting ready to make a run.
The Seahawks will return after the bye week to take on the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 29. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:25 p.m. PT inside Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Fans can watch the game on FOX or stream it on the FOX One app.

title: NFL Playoff Picture: Where Are Seahawks Going Into Bye Week?
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are still in the win column after beating the Las Vegas Raiders 21-13 in their Week 10 matchup.
The victory allows them to keep pace in a crowded NFC playoff race that has five teams that are above .500 fighting for three spots. Here's a look at the NFC playoff picture following Week 10.
1. San Francisco 49ers (8-1) — NFC West Leader 2. Detroit Lions (7-2) — NFC North Leader 3. New York Giants (5-3-1) — NFC East Leader 4. Carolina Panthers (4-5) — NFC South Leader 5. Minnesota Vikings (7-2) — Wild Card 1 6. Chicago Bears (7-2) — Wild Card 2 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) — Wild Card 3 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (4-6) 11. Washington Commanders (3-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) 13. New Orleans Saints (3-6) 14. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 15. Arizona Cardinals (3-7) 16. Philadelphia Eagles (2-7)
The entire NFC North sits above .500, and all four are in the playoff picture. The Minnesota Vikings' win pushes the Green Bay Packers into a tie with Seattle and the Los Angeles Rams, who beat the Arizona Cardinals by multiple scores.
The NFC North is likely going to beat up on each other to the point where at least one team will not be in the playoff picture by season's end. The Vikings are 3-1 in the division, while the Packers are 1-3. The Detroit Lions are 2-0, while the Bears are 0-2. There are plenty of games left between now and the end of the season, and that could make a massive difference in the grand scheme of things.
If one of the NFC North teams falls by the wayside, it opens up a spot for the Seahawks or Rams, who are both 6-4 and fighting for likely one wild card spot. The two teams won't meet until Week 16 of the season, which could be an early start for the playoffs. That means the Seahawks only have four games between now and then to enhance their positioning and get ready for when the games truly start to count.
The Seahawks' next game is on Sunday, November 29, against the San Francisco 49ers. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:25 pm PT inside Levi Stadium in Santa Clara. Fans can watch the game on Fox or stream it on the Fox One app.

title: Mike Macdonald Just Ended the Seahawks QB Controversy
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going into the bye week after a pair of big wins from backup quarterback Drew Lock.
Lock is 3-0 as the Seahawks starter this season, which is the same amount of wins Darnold has as the team's starter. This includes Darnold's start in Week 1 against the New England Patriots when he was substituted out of the game due to a glute injury for Lock.
Darnold's struggles and Lock's success could lead many to believe a quarterback change is on the horizon. However, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald shut down the possibility of switching things up when the team returns to the field in Week 12.
"Yeah, I'd say we're really optimistic that he's going to be able to get a full week's worth of work and be able to play against San Fran," Macdonald said of Darnold via Seattle Sports 710 AM.
Mike Macdonald on @SeattleSports on if they think Darnold will be able to practice next week... "Yeah, I'd say we're really optimistic that he's going to be able to get a full week's worth of work and be able to play against San Fran."
Darnold has struggled with interceptions this season, throwing nine in seven games with the team. That has been the primary issue the Seahawks have dealt with in games where Darnold is under center. However, the Seahawks believe he still provides them with the best chance of winning moving forward.
So far this season, Lock has thrown 93 passes without an interception. He has seven touchdowns as well, including two against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10. However, Lock did fumble the ball twice, which could part of the reason they aren't making a change.
The Seahawks should be basing this decision on what has happened this season rather than what happened last year. Darnold was brilliant last season, and winning a Super Bowl shouldn't go unnoticed. However, he has not performed at the same level this season as he did in 2025. Lock has been strong in his absence, which does warrant some consideration for a change.
The Seahawks have to hope that McDonald and the coaching staff are making this decision for the right reasons. It isn't about what has happened in the past, but rather about who puts the team in the best position to win in the future. Lock has shown that he can lead the team to a win more often than Darnold.
While that shouldn't be the only reason behind the decision, it should be under consideration as the team prepares for the home stretch.

title: Seahawks Run Game vs. Raiders Proves Not Trading for Jonathan Taylor Was Smart
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are feeling pretty good about themselves after a 21-13 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 inside Allegiant Stadium.
In the win, the Seahawks had their best game on the ground to date. It has been an inconsistent issue throughout the season, but it all came together against the Raiders . It proves that their decision not to trade for Indianapolis Colts star Jonathan Taylor was the right one.
In the win against the Raiders, Zach Charbonnet led the backfield with 20 carries for 94 yards. Meanwhile, rookie first-round pick Jadarian Price ran the ball nine times for 36 yards and a touchdown, proving that there was a solid one-two punch in the running back room.
"We were hoping to take another step in the run game today [and] I thought we did," head coach Mike Macdonald said postgame via the team's website.
Price spoke about how the committee approach the team is taking is infectious and how each of them is making each other better.
"We've been doing a pretty good job," Price said via the team's website. "Watching Charbs (Zach Charbonnet) go out there and make guys miss, break tackles and stuff like that, it makes you want to go out there and do the same. I like where our offense is heading."
The trade deadline last week sent the league into a frenzy as multiple blockbuster deals were consummated. Taylor was one of the big names discussed as the Colts went into a fire sale, which included a deal with the Seahawks for offensive lineman Quenton Nelson . Ultimately, the Seahawks chose not to trade for Taylor, or any available running back for that matter.
Taylor stuck with the Colts and ran the ball 16 times for 83 yards in a 24-22 win against the Miami Dolphins.
While a Taylor trade would have made sense by improving one of Seattle's weak spots, the team ultimately concluded that the lack of run-game production had to do with injuries to Price and Charbonnet. Earlier in the season, it took them a few weeks to get some momentum, but now that they have both been active for the past three games, the Seahawks have an established plan moving forward.

title: Hanich Panic Meter: Seahawks' JSN Could Break Single Season Record
full_text:
In just two years, Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba became a No. 1 pass-catcher. Just one year late last season, JSN became a superstar and became the league’s offensive player of the year. He might finish up his fourth season with one of the most legendary achievements.
​ JSN, once again, played like the elite player he is and became the Seahawks’ offense to help Seattle win 21-13 at the Las Vegas Raiders. He caught eight receptions for 171 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Raiders. Just like he was last season, JSN is on pace to break Calvin Johnson’s single-season record of 1,964 yards set in 2012. There is a great chance he may accomplish it in 16 games as opposed to 17 games.
​Through 10 games this season, JSN has caught 79 receptions for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns. He is only 758 yards away from breaking Johnson’s record. For JSN to break the record, he would have to average 108.3 yards in each of the remaining seven games. To break the record in the same 16-game timeframe as Johnson, JSN would have to average 126.4 yards in each of the remaining six games,
​He has accounted for at least 100 yards in eight of the ten games this season. It doesn’t matter if it’s Sam Darnold or Drew Lock throwing him the ball; he finds a way to open. He has 721 receiving yards from Darnold and 486 in nearly four games from Lock. He is easily a solid path to be named offensive player of the year for a second consecutive season and, possibly, league MVP if the award were quarterback-focused.
​JSN was on pace to break Johnson’s all-time receiving record last season. Through 11 games last season, JSN caught 80 receptions for 1,313 yards and seven touchdowns. This meant he only had 652 more yards in the remaining six games to break the record. It was at that point, there was some offensive fatigue and the running game had to be re-established. JSN would only account for 480 yards during the final games to finish with 1,793 yards.
​Last season, it seemed like it was a surprise that JSN was so elite at creating enough separation and making big plays after the catch with his speed and elusiveness. This season, despite being mentioned as one of the top receivers in the league, he is still getting open so much. He has a great feel with either Darnold or Lock throwing him the ball . It seems like no matter how many times the opposing defenses game plan around him, JSN still finds ways to get open.

title: 3 Observations in Seahawks Week 10 Win vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are kicking their feet back after a 21-13 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 10 action inside Allegiant Stadium.
The Seahawks needed to take care of business before their bye week, and they did just that. Their matchup against Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza proved exactly why the Seahawks have the top defense in the league and propelled them to victory.
Here's a look at three observations from the matchup.
Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued to flex his dominance this season. He added 8 catches for 171 yards and a touchdown to his league-leading total, which puts him on pace to be the first player in league history to have over 2,000 receiving yards in a season.
Smith-Njigba was responsible for all but 61 of the team's passing yards, which shows the difference between him and the rest of Seattle's receiving core. The Seahawks would greatly benefit from having another receiver to take some attention off of him. Even though Cooper Kupp had a touchdown, it's not enough.
Ultimately, the Seahawks still won the game, and they will take it at this point. If he were to miss any time due to injury, it would be season-altering and the offense would struggle mightily.
Luckily for the Seahawks, they have the top defense in the league, and they made Mendoza look like a rookie in Week 10. The Seahawks surrendered just 163 total yards of offense, which will improve their average going into their bye week. The Seahawks sacked Mendoza six times during the afternoon, including two from cornerback Devon Witherspoon.
As long as the offense can take care of the football and score on a couple of drives throughout the game, the Seahawks will have a chance to be any team in the back half of the season and playoffs.
Drew Lock is now 3-0 as the Seahawks' starting quarterback this season. That could spark a debate during the bye week about whether he should be the permanent QB1 over Sam Darnold, who has struggled to take care of the football this season. Darnold's nine interceptions in seven games are an issue that Seattle's offense has been dealing with all year.
Lock has been playing well enough to spark some small whispers of conversation, but his two fumbles today likely will hand the ball back to Darnold when he is healthy and ready to go.
There is reason to believe Darnold will be available for Week 12 against the San Francisco 49ers. If he is, Seattle will have to make a big decision between the two. Outside of the fumbles, Lock was surgical against the Raiders, but if turnovers are the biggest issue for the quarterback and both of them have struggled in that department, the team might as well stick with the default, which is Darnold.

title: Seahawks' Jaxon Smith-Njigba Criticizes Controversial OPI Call vs. Raiders
full_text:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba got off to a slow start against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, but he nearly got going much earlier if not for a questionable offensive pass interference call.
In the first quarter, Smith-Njigba was flagged for pushing off Raiders cornerback Eric Stokes on a 29-yard catch-and-run touchdown. While subjective, of course, his arm extension was pretty minimal by NFL standards, but Stokes fell at the top of the route. That is likely what drew the flag, in conjunction with the small push.
When asked postgame whether he disagreed with the call, Smith-Njigba gave his honest thoughts.
OPI on JSN pic.twitter.com/QOsXFrFI2K
“Yeah, definitely. It didn’t feel like I pushed off at all,” Smith-Njigba said. “We had some hand battling; I tend to snap off pretty quick, and he fell. That’s kind of my perspective of it. Refs are human; it sucks that they go out there and make mistakes, but it happens.”
It was similar to a play that Smith-Njigba was flagged for in the Seahawks’ Week 8 Monday night loss to the Chicago Bears. The refs appear to be cracking down on his push-offs, in particular, especially as Smith-Njigba continues to dominate NFL defenses across the league.
“It’s always the next-play mentality,” Smith-Njigba said. “You can’t sulk in the bad stuff or the good stuff. I just try to lock in every single play. That’s our mission on offense: No matter what, just keep pushing. So, definitely proud of my guys and how we went out there and fought today.”
Oh damn, surprised they called that on JSN pic.twitter.com/NvFHtA7KW2
Smith-Njigba had just 11 receiving yards in the first half before exploding for 144 yards and a touchdown in the third quarter alone. He finished the game with eight catches for 171 yards and the score.
The Seahawks superstar is still on pace to break the all-time single-season receiving record with 79 catches for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns through 10 games. He is slightly ahead of his 10-game pace from 2025 and is currently projected to total 134 catches, 2,051 yards and 20 touchdowns by the end of the season.
If he continues at the current pace, Smith-Njigba will beat Calvin Johnson’s 2012 record of 1,964 receiving yards in a single season. Opponents haven’t found a way to shut him down, and Sunday’s game proved that he isn’t slowing down anytime soon.

title: Seahawks 'Not Sure' About Injury Severity to Abe Lucas, George Holani
full_text:
Already banged up, the Seattle Seahawks unfortunately didn’t get out of their Week 10 win against the Las Vegas Raiders without new injuries.
Starting right tackle Abraham Lucas exited the game early and did not return after running back George Holani had already left . Defensive tackle Jarran Reed also exited the game and was ruled doubtful to return, but he did go back into the game.
Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said after the game that he is unsure of the severity of both Lucas and Holani’s injuries. He did confirm that Lucas has an ankle sprain.
“Abe is an ankle; to what degree, we’re not sure,” Macdonald said. “George is a knee; to what degree, we’re not sure.”
Backup tackle Bobby Hart finished the game for the Seahawks at right tackle, adding a third replacement to an offensive line that was already missing starting left tackle Charles Cross and left guard Quenton Nelson.
Surprisingly, even with that many changes up front, Seattle totaled 150 rushing yards — its third-most of the season — and protected backup quarterback Drew Lock well enough that he completed 14 of 17 passes for 240 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions.
At running back, the Seahawks only had Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price available for the rest of the game. Holani was the third running back, but luckily he wasn’t needed in the win.
Macdonald wouldn’t commit to a potential post-bye-week plan for the offensive line if Lucas is forced to miss time. Cross has already missed three games and could return after the bye, which would likely lead to Josh Jones moving to the right side if Lucas is out.
“I’m not sure what we’d do … We’ll see how serious it is with Abe, and then we’ll put a plan together, and I’ll fill you guys in when we make that decision,” Macdonald added.
The Seahawks were already missing defensive lineman Leonard Williams, quarterback Sam Darnold, backup running back Emanuel Wilson, Cross and Nelson entering the game. The hope now is that most of those players will be able to return when the Seahawks face the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, Nov. 29.
Macdonald said the team will be off until Monday, Nov. 23, when they return from the bye.

title: 3 Winners, 1 Loser in Seahawks Victory vs. Raiders
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are celebrating after a 21-13 victory against the Las Vegas Raiders inside Allegiant Stadium in Week 10.
The Seahawks started off rough, giving up a touchdown early to rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in his first career start , but they settled down and kept them out of the end zone for the remainder of the game.
Here's a look at the winners and losers from the matchup.
Jaxon Smith-Njigba continued to establish himself as the league's best wide receiver. He added to his league lead in receiving yards with 171 on eight catches and a 71-yard touchdown that was arguably the play of the day.
Drew Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba is looking like a dangerous connection 👀 CBS | Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/6hXecLdtM6
Smith-Njigba's presence in the offense shakes everything up for the Seahawks and they wouldn't be the same without him on the field.
Sharpe had another strong week as the team's RB1. He ran the ball 20 times for 94 yards, giving them a strong presence on the ground against the league's worst run defense. Making sure the run game was established was an important part of Seattle's game plan going into the week, and Sharpe helped execute that to a tee.
Rookie Jadarian Price found the end zone as well, which means the Seahawks' vision of having a reliable running back room with depth is reigning true.
Star cornerback Devon Witherspoon had a strong performance against the Raiders. No receiver had more than 22 yards during the game, apart from running back Ashton Jeanty, who led the way with four catches for 46 yards.
Witherspoon had a pair of sacks, which added up to six for the team in the game. He proved why the Seahawks made him the league's highest-paid cornerback during the offseason.
Drew Lock had a solid game, recording 240 passing yards and 20 rushing yards. He completed 14 of 17 passes and connected on a pair of touchdowns: one to JSN and the other to Cooper Kupp.
Lock did fumble the ball twice, including once on the team's opening possession, which has been an issue for the offense throughout the season. Limiting these turnovers is what will turn Seattle from good to great. Had these turnovers not happened, the argument for Lock to start after the bye week would have been stronger. However, it might not be the case.

title: Jarran Reed Injury Update: Seahawks Defensive Tackle Leaves in Second
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are getting dismantled one player at a time today. George Holani was minor enough to be barely noticed, Abraham Lucas hasn’t played well this season, but now, things are getting dire. Jarran Reed left the game with a toe injury, and as of this article hasn’t yet returned, with his return being labeled Doubtful by the team already.
This injury is a disaster for the Seahawks, who are already without Leonard Williams and have not played the run especially well so far today. Byron Murphy will have to do all the heavy lifting on the interior now, and Rylie Mills now has to play a lot. Brandon Pili might be able to fill some gaps, but this is much too thin for the Seahawks defense to be itself.
Combined with the other injuries the Seahawks have right now, you have to wonder if it's just becoming too tall of a task to win against even a team as deeply flawed as the Raiders. With Mills on the field, the Raiders are going to pound the run and take away Seattle's opportunity to force Mendoza to make mistakes. And beyond this game, well, at least it's the bye week.
Rylie Mills and Brandon Pili are the names to watch right now, as they're going to see a lot of action in this second half. Mills has been very poor so far this season, especially holding up against the run, so asking him to play in a competitive game is very risky. He's also been a relative no-show as a pass rusher, so there's no  particular upside to Mills getting more reps right now.
Pili is a little more stout, able to hold his ground against the run, but he's most certainly nothing special as far as an NFL player goes. However, this team should have expected Jarran Reed to not make it through the entire 17 game season at his age, especially with him still taking quite a few snaps. Now they just have to get Leonard Williams back to be able to survive it.
Reed has been solid and effective this season, making big contributions to the NFL's top run defense. Obviously, his age shows up on occasion, but he remains an important part of this defense as well as a great leader in the locker room. His absence will be felt as they try to punch in a second half comeback win. Again, at least we have a bye week, so at least he has extra time to get back.

title: 3 Overreactions to 49ers' Stressful Win Against Cowboys
full_text:
It was a game that was much tougher to win than expected, but the San Francisco 49ers got the job done against the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40.
However, because the game was a stressful win, there are few overreactions to unpack. Here are my three overreactions from the 49ers' Week 10 win against the Cowboys.
Dak Prescott lit up the 49ers, and how couldn't he? There was no pass rush to bother him throughout the game. Prescott was extremely comfortable on nearly every dropback. He was only pressured 16 times, for a 29.6% pressure rate.
A defensive front with Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner, and Osa Odighizuwa, that is pitiful. They need to be a lot better than that if they want to avoid giving up 40 points in a game. But this has happened for the second straight game.
The 49ers' pass rush wasn't a significant factor against the Las Vegas Raiders either. For a team with Super Bowl aspirations, this must improve. They will not win the Super Bowl without an effective pass rush. This is a concern until proven otherwise.
If Brock Purdy hadn't put on his superhero cape , the 49ers would've lost to the Cowboys. He was amazing in this game and strengthened his MVP case.
However, the fact that the 49ers needed him to play at such a level for them to beat the Cowboys, who are no better than average, is concerning.
Is this what the 49ers need to win games? Does Purdy have to perform at an incredible level every game? Given their ineffective pass rush, it may be true, but it's unfair unless others pick up the slack.
The only bright side to that is it would exponentially help his MVP case since Purdy will be the driving force of the 49ers' success while overcoming other weak areas.
Is the 49ers' offensive line declining after their hot start to the season? They just made the Cowboys' defensive front look like a top-five unit. Purdy was sacked five times and pressured 12 times on 35 dropbacks.
It's the highest pressure rate (34.3%) he's faced since Week 5 against the Seattle Seahawks. It's one thing to have a difficult time against Seattle, but the Cowboys? It was a concerning performance by the 49ers' offensive line.
Maybe it was just one game slide, with the Cowboys extra motivated. But the offensive line could be leaking oil, and it's not going to get better next week against the vaunted Minnesota Vikings defense.

title: 9 Winners and Losers From 49ers' Week 10 Win Over Cowboys
full_text:
Defeating the Dallas Cowboys was way more stressful than it needed to be for the San Francisco 49ers . It went down to the wire before they sealed the deal in a 46-40 win.
Several 49ers stood out positively in this game as winners, while a few others were negatives. Let's take a look at the winners and losers from the 49ers' Week 10 win over the Cowboys.
Someone hand Brock Purdy a top hat and a wand because he looked like a magician against the Cowboys. The 49ers needed him to be, or they would've lost.
Purdy strengthened his MVP case with his immaculate performance, completing 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards (career-high), three touchdowns, and no turnovers. He did all of that despite a bunch of pressure in his face throughout the game.
Another elite 49ers performer was Christian McCaffrey. He tallied three touchdowns and 223 scrimmage yards. But his most impressive work was his two touchdown catches and runs that made history.
McCaffrey caught a 74-yard and a 66-yard touchdown pass, becoming the first running back in NFL history to have multiple receiving touchdowns of at least 65 yards in a game. Have yourself a day, McCaffrey.
Running 20 routes and catching five passes for 61 yards probably isn't what the 49ers had in mind for Keenan Allen in this game. But that's exactly what he did, and they needed it.
Allen's contributions helped sustain drives and kept the passing game flowing. The 49ers needed a wide receiver who could separate with Mike Evans out. Allen has answered that need.
What a breakout game for rookie Kaelon Black. He's a tough running back to bring down, as shown by his 25-yard touchdown run. This kind of performance has been brewing since Week 7.
His numbers may not be that impressive (11 rushes for 53 yards), but his impact is as clear as day. He's been a solid addition to the 49ers' offense.
He only reeled in two catches for 49 yards, but make no mistake. Watkins is a winner from this game. It's another example of how he's becoming a key offensive player. Whenever he gets his chances, he makes the most of them. He continues to be rewarded.
It was an extremely rough game for Deommodore Lenoir. The Cowboys made a point of picking on him in coverage. Lenoir was targeted 16 times, allowing 10 catches for 134 yards and three touchdowns.
George Pickens outclassed him. I'm sure playing with compromised health hindered Lenoir, so he gets credit for toughing it out. Still, he was demolished. It was by far the worst game of his NFL career.
One of the touchdowns Lenoir allowed could've been avoided had Marques Sigle not abandoned his zone. The 49ers were in quarters coverage, so Sigle had a deep quarter zone.
Yet for some reason, he charged downhill within seconds of the ball being snapped. It seems he bit on the play action, which was foolish. He left Lenoir on the island with Pickens, who scored where Sigle should've been in his zone.
It felt like on almost every pass attempt, Connor Cobly was being driven back. He was having a difficult time holding his own. The entire offensive line wasn't playing up to par, which is why Purdy was sacked five times. But Colby's struggles stood out the most, as usual.
The 49ers' pass rush was their most pitiful performance in this game. They were ineffective for the second consecutive game. Except this time, they were downright nonexistent. Dak Prescott was pressured only 16 times on his 54 dropbacks.
A pass rush led by Nick Bosa, DeForest Buckner, and Osa Odighizuwa must be better. It needs to be better. That's enough talent to make an impact. They don't need to pop off for five sacks or more a game, but it can't be as poor as it was in this game.

title: What We Learned About the 49ers in their Win Over the Dallas Cowboys
full_text:
The 49ers just won another game , and now their record is 8-1. Give them credit.
Their offense seems unstoppable even without Mike Evans, thanks to the addition of Keenan Allen, the return of Deebo Samuel, and the emergence of Kaelon Black and Jordan Watkins, not to mention the MVP-caliber play from Brock Purdy and brilliant coaching from Kyle Shanahan.
The 49ers scored a whopping 46 points in Dallas. And yet, they won by only six points, which is alarming because the offense didn't turn the ball over. It was close to flawless. The defense simply stunk, particularly when it came to stopping the pass.
Through 10 weeks this season, the 49ers have one of the best run defenses in the NFL. It's giving up just 3.4 yards per carry, which is tied with Seattle for the lowest mark in the league. Plus, the 49ers have given up just four rushing touchdowns all season. Impressive.
But, the pass defense has been putrid in every way. On Sunday, the 49ers gave up 343 yards and 5 touchdown passes to Dak Prescott, who's mediocre. A few weeks earlier, the 49ers gave up three touchdown passes to Michael Penix Jr., who's subpar.
In the past three games, the 49ers defense has recorded just one sack, and that was when Dak Prescott jogged out of bounds for no gain. For the season, the 49ers average just 1.8 sacks per game, which ranks tied for fourth-worst in the league.
Part of the problem is Nick Bosa. He simply hasn't produced this season, and moves with a noticeable limp on the field. Not surprising, considering he's had three ACL tears in his career. On most plays, the offensive tackle pushes him past the quarterback with ease. And he's still the best edge rusher on the team.
Then, there are the cornerbacks.
Renardo Green is good, but injured, and hasn't finished either of the 49ers' past two games. Deommodore Lenoir also is injured and has given up a passer rating of 105.7 this season. And Upton Stout is knicked up all the time and has allowed a passer rating of 116. These guys play such soft coverage, the pass rush doesn't have much time to sack the quarterback.
And then there's safety Ji'Ayir Brown, who has given up a passer rating of 105.9 this season. He's not injured -- he's just bad. No excuses for him.
Which means the 49ers can't cover or sack the quarterback. That's a terrible combination for a team that has Super Bowl aspirations.
So far, the 49ers' big trade deadline addition, DeForest Buckner, hasn't improved the defense at all. Which means they need to hope that Nick Bosa becomes Nick Bosa again. Right now, he's Rick Bosa -- a complete impostor.
In addition, the 49ers need veteran cornerback Nate Hobbs to get healthy and play well right away, something he hasn't been able to do all year.
Fortunately for the 49ers, they have what seems to be an all-time great offense. But if they fail to win the Super Bowl yet again, you can point directly at the defense and the general manager who built it.

title: The Craziest Stats From the 49ers' 46-40 Victory vs Cowboys
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers' 46-40 victory over the Dallas Cowboys was an enthralling spectacle.
A win is a win, even if it was closer than it should've been. With 86 points scored between the two sides, it was also the highest-scoring game in the history of this particular fixture.
If you think that's a crazy statistic, think again. Here are three of the craziest stats from the matchup. All stats are extracted from the 49ers' post-game notes .
Scoring 46 points is no small feat. With six touchdowns, five successful PATs, a two-point conversion and a field goal, the 49ers' offense registered 584 total yards – an incredible display.
It's no surprise that this was a season high, but what's remarkable is that it was also the most ever recorded by a visiting team against the Cowboys.
Per StatMuse , Dallas has played 547 total games on their home turf, including the regular season and the playoffs. The 49ers have achieved something completely unprecedented.
A more unusual statistic, but thanks to Christian McCaffrey's 74-yard touchdown reception and Deebo Samuel's 70-yard rushing touchdown, the 49ers achieved this feat for just the fifth time in franchise history.
Notably, this was the first time this century, with the previous occurrence dating back to Week 13 of the 1998 season, when running back Garrison Hearst and wide receiver Terrell Owens achieved the feat.
McCaffrey and the record books are a familiar duo by now, and last week was another reminder of why . This time around against Dallas, he recorded 161 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, 62 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown, becoming the first player in NFL history to achieve that combination in a single game.
It's a bonkers statistic, but it's hardly surprising at this point. He always finds a way of adding his name to the record book.
Also, he's now just one game behind newly inducted Hall of Famer Roger Craig for the most games in franchise history with at least 50 rushing yards and 50 receiving yards. McCaffrey has 16, while Craig has 17.
With 13 total touchdowns from nine games so far this season, McCaffrey became just the fifth running back in NFL history to record at least 12 touchdowns in six different seasons.
LaDainian Tomlinson leads with eight seasons, Derrick Henry and Emmitt Smith have seven, and Marcus Allen is equal with McCaffrey with six.

title: 49ers Coach Gets Candid About Keenan Allen Debut
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers debut of Keenan Allen could not have gone better for the team. It is hard to incorporate a new receiver into the mix, especially in the middle of the week. So, Allen catching five passes for 61 yards in his first game with the team is a good sign of things to come.
Head coach Kyle Shanahan made it clear he was happy with the performance .
“We involved him in a lot of stuff, and you never know how the coverages are going to go and stuff, but I thought he did a hell of a job,” said Shanahan after the game.
Shanahan noted that the team did not have many restrictions for Allen in his debut. The plan was to let him play as much as he could handle or understand in the playbook.
The 49ers coach admitted that Allen did not play in two-minute situations because he did not pick up the playbook that fast yet. Aside from that, the team let him take on a full snap share.
“We never just said it was just these plays,” admitted Shanahan on the game plan this week. “You know, we knew to be smart with him, but we told him to try to learn everything. The stuff in the game plan, he told us he had down on Saturday, and he felt good with all that stuff.”
Allen averaged a season-high 2.9 yards per route run in the win. It was the most efficient game of his season.
The 34-year-old veteran said that he leaned on his experience of being a player who can be quarterback-friendly. He did what he knows quarterbacks like, and Brock Purdy found him.
“Just be quarterback-friendly, be an outlet,” said Allen . “Always try to be in his vision, and give him all the, you know, be able to make a play. As I said, he's tried to stay in his vision.”
All of a sudden, the 49ers wide receiver corps looks much better. Allen entered the room, and Deebo Samuel returned from injury. Demarcus Robinson was in his second game back from injury, but he only needed to be depth.
That is because second-year receiver Jordan Watkins has ascended into a starter. This is with their supposed top two pass catchers, Mike Evans and De’Zhaun Stribling out with injuries. We will see how things shake up once those two come back and Allen gets more comfortable.

title: Why the Win vs. Cowboys Could Be Brock Purdy's Best Game with the 49ers
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers defeated their historic rivals, the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40 at AT&T Stadium to improve their record to 8-1.
Brock Purdy threw three passing touchdowns, two to Christian McCaffrey and one to Deebo Samuel, while McCaffrey, Samuel and rookie Kaelon Black each added a rushing touchdown.
Their performances were simply sublime across the board , with all of San Francisco's offensive weapons contributing. However, Purdy was the focal point, making a compelling case for this being his best performance since taking the job as the 49ers' starting quarterback.
Purdy finished 22-of-28, passing for 389 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions, despite taking five sacks. A 154.5 passer rating. Not quite a perfect rating, but an exceptional one nonetheless.
In addition, according to Next Gen Stats Purdy completed all four of his scramble pass attempts for 135 yards and a touchdown, tying Patrick Mahomes (2018) and Josh Allen (2024) for the most scramble passing yards in a game since 2018.
Plus, on a play that resulted in a Samuel touchdown, Purdy even took on the role of a fullback, helping with a crucial block to help make the score possible.
The manner of the performance is what makes this such a strong contender for Purdy's best game in red and gold. When he wasn't being sacked, his efficiency was almost faultless.
He compensated for cracks in the offensive line, scrambled brilliantly and remained remarkably calm and composed throughout despite the hits. These are the qualities of an elite quarterback.
I've never doubted Purdy's ability, but the overall manner of this performance was particularly impressive. With the 49ers' defence conceding 40 points, the pressure on the offense to keep delivering was immense. For Purdy to maintain such a high standard throughout is simply remarkable.
To produce a performance like this against the franchise's biggest non-divisional rivals only adds to its significance. Purdy clearly relishes the big occasion, and against a rivalry that has stood for decades, this was far from the first time he has risen to the challenge against the Cowboys. He's now 4-0 and remains unbeaten.
With every passing week, he continues to impress in more ways. He constantly strives to improve, with no distractions beyond his own development and that of his team, and almost always delivers in the face of adversity .
He's looking like the frontrunner for this year's MVP . But what matters more to him is winning football games.

title: 5 49ers Who Saw Their Stock Soar in Week 10
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers squeezed out a win in an offensive explosion against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10. Which players stepped up the most in the win?
The question entering the game was what the team would do at receiver with the addition of Keenan Allen and the return of Deebo Samuel. The two veterans were almost certain to impact Jordan Watkins, but the second-year receiver has been making a case to see the field more.
The results in Week 10 were Watkins leading the team in snaps and hauling in two catches for 49 yards. This was a good performance. It will be hard to take him off of the field when Mike Evans is back.
Allen is exactly what the team needed to complete the offense. He came in this week and hardly knew the playbook. Still, he hauled in five passes for 61 yards in the win. The 49ers have not had a possession slot to take on routes over the short middle of the field. They might have finally found one. It looked like he acclimated quickly and will be a nice addition.
Samuel just returned from a hamstring injury in Week 10. He ended up leading the 49ers in rushing with 78 yards and a touchdown. He also added three receptions for 31 yards and a touchdown. His impact in all areas of the field is valuable and was seen in Week 10.
The 49ers have had a three-man rotation at safety over the past two weeks. Mustapha has led the way between the three in the past two games in snaps. He has also been the most impactful player of the three safeties.
He was benched earlier in the year because he was not healthy. However, once he took the field, it has been impossible to take him off. He has to be a full-time starter next week.
Williams has 1.5 sacks and eight pressures in his first five games back from an ACL injury. Last year he had one sack and 19 pressures in nine games. He had four pressures and added half of a sack with Dre Greenlaw in the 49ers' win over the Cowboys. He was their best defensive threat up front. The 49ers need him to continue to progress.
